title: Corneal enzymatic digestion resistance in the presence of oestradiol and oestradiol plus selective tissue oestrogenic activity regulators (STEAR).
summary: This ex vivo study tested how β-oestradiol and the selective tissue oestrogenic activity regulator tibolone affect corneal resistance to enzymatic digestion using porcine corneal buttons exposed to collagenase A. Oestradiol significantly reduced digestion resistance compared with controls, and the combination with tibolone further decreased resistance (means ± SD: control 31.38±2.03 h; oestradiol 27.25±1.84 h; oestradiol+tibolone 22.38±2.47 h; all p<0.01).

title: Intraparenchymal Enzyme Injections in Islet Isolations With Incomplete Ductal Perfusion of Enzymes.
summary: This letter describes the use of intraparenchymal injections (IPI) of digestive enzymes to overcome incomplete ductal perfusion during human pancreatic islet isolation. In observational data from 279 consecutive isolations, IPI improved digestion (notably in ARC procedures and TPIAT cases) and supported sufficient islet yields even when ductal cannulation was impossible in some autologous cases.

title: Dual Proteomics Strategies to Dissect and Quantify the Components of Nine Medically Important African Snake Venoms.
summary: This study applies a dual proteomics workflow combining Multi-Enzymatic Limited Digestion (MELD) and trypsin-only digestion, integrated with species-specific venom gland transcriptomes, to comprehensively characterize and relatively quantify toxin families in nine African snake venoms (five Dendroaspis and four Echis). The work reveals genus-specific toxin dominance (3FTxs/vKunitz in Dendroaspis; SVMPs/PLA2s in Echis), identifies rare components (e.g., hyaluronidases, renin-like proteases), and validates MELD as a reproducible method for deep venomics profiling.

title: Homogenization of Northern Belgian landscapes through centuries of reclamation, agricultural transition, and urbanization.
summary: The study uses deep learning-based GeoAI to segment and harmonize three series of historical maps (1774, 1873, 1969) plus a 2022 dataset to quantify long-term land-use change across northern Belgium, revealing three sequential drivers: reclamation (1774–1873), agricultural transition (1873–1969), and urbanization (1969–2022). These shifts weakened the association between land use and soils and increased interspersion, culminating in homogenized peri-urban landscapes despite high segmentation accuracies for historical maps.

title: Perihematomal changes in glucose metabolism and cell counts in the rat collagenase model for intracerebral hemorrhage.
summary: In a rat collagenase model of intracerebral hemorrhage, the authors combined longitudinal [18F]FDG PET and diffusion-weighted MRI with stereological immunohistochemistry to characterize perihematomal changes. They observed early perihematomal hypometabolism and increased diffusion, most prominently in piriform cortex and basal ganglia, that partially normalized by day 7, whereas reduced neuronal counts and increased glial cells persisted and did not correlate with metabolic recovery.

title: Amylase trypsin inhibitors activation of toll-like receptor 4 revisited: The dominance of lipopolysaccharides contamination.
summary: The study isolated an amylase trypsin inhibitor (ATI)-enriched fraction from wheat flour and tested its ability to activate TLR4 signaling using HEK-Blue hTLR4 reporter cells while controlling for lipopolysaccharide (LPS) contamination. Results showed that TLR4 activation was predominantly driven by LPS: polymyxin B blocked the signal, Proteinase K digestion of proteins did not reduce it, and mild heating increased detectable LPS and TLR4 activation, challenging the notion that ATIs directly activate TLR4.

title: Urbanization and genetic homogenization in the medieval Low Countries revealed through a ten-century paleogenomic study of the city of Sint-Truiden.
summary: This paleogenomic study sequenced 372 low-coverage genomes (332 imputed) from 8th–18th century burials in Sint-Truiden (Belgium) and found that an initially heterogeneous medieval population—featuring migrants with Irish/Scottish-like ancestry—gradually homogenized via prolonged local admixture between Gaulish and Germanic ancestries to resemble modern Limburg. Despite detecting fourteenth‑century Yersinia pestis and other pathogens, the authors found no genome‑wide signal of selection in immunity genes across the Black Death horizon, while microgeographic differences in ancestry and relatedness within the cemetery reflected social and spatial structure tied to the abbey and parish contexts.

title: Mass Spectrometric Fingerprinting to Detect Fraud and Herbal Adulteration in Plant Food Supplements.
summary: The study develops and validates an LC–HRMS fingerprinting approach coupled with chemometrics (PLS-DA) to detect regulated and prohibited plants in complex plant food supplements, focusing on slimming products. Using optimized Q-ToF MS methods, data compression, and modeling, the approach achieved high classification accuracy and was applied to 10 real-world illegal samples, revealing undeclared botanicals and highlighting the need for stronger market surveillance; MS outperformed DAD and offered no practical advantage to fused DAD–MS models.

title: Flow Cytometric Analysis and Sorting of Murine Enteric Nervous System Cells: An Optimized Protocol.
summary: This study presents an optimized FACS-based protocol to isolate viable enteric nervous system (ENS) cells from mouse colon, identifying CD56 and CD24 as robust markers and demonstrating neuronal enrichment in a CD56/CD24TIP subpopulation. A 30-minute Liberase-based dissociation using gentle mechanical processing improved viability and yield over collagenase/dispase methods, with ENS identity validated by TUBB3, SOX10, ELAVL4, and RT-qPCR, and sorting/culture performed on BD S8 FACS Discover and BD FACS Aria III.

title: Establishment of patient-derived 3D in vitro models of sarcomas: literature review and guidelines on behalf of the FORTRESS working group.
summary: This review by the FORTRESS working group surveys patient-derived 3D in vitro sarcoma models (tumoroids), summarizing current methods, success rates, characterization standards, and applications across soft tissue and bone sarcoma subtypes. It proposes practical guidelines for tissue processing, culture conditions, validation, biobanking, and use in drug and radiotherapy testing, highlighting the need for collaborative protocol sharing and standardized characterization to advance translational research.

title: Blood collection tubes with protease inhibitors to prevent falsely high renin concentrations due to cryoactivation.
summary: This study evaluated how storage temperature and the use of protease-inhibitor blood collection tubes affect renin cryoactivation and the aldosterone-to-renin ratio (ARR), and whether a 2-hour 37°C incubation can reverse cryoactivation. Renin remained stable at −80°C but increased at +4°C and especially −20°C; a 37°C, 2-hour incubation reversed the increase only in samples collected in trypsin inhibitor or protease inhibitor cocktail tubes, while ARR was markedly lowered by −20°C storage due to falsely high renin.

title: Evaluation of metatranscriptomic sequencing protocols to obtain full-length RNA virus genomes from mammalian tissues.
summary: This study compares two metatranscriptomic workflows for recovering full-length RNA virus genomes from mammalian tissues and finds that an optimized homogenization/RNA purification with rRNA depletion (Method B) markedly improves RNA yield, integrity, and viral genome recovery over a viral enrichment/SPIA approach (Method A). Method B enabled assembly of four complete rodent hepacivirus genomes with reduced host background, while Method A favored recovery of polyadenylated paramyxoviruses but yielded fragmented hepacivirus genomes.

title: A Century of Shifting Native Species-Accumulation Curves Reveals Long-Term Biodiversity Loss.
summary: Using nearly a century of Dutch vegetation-plot data, the authors show that species-accumulation curves have flattened over time, indicating long-term biodiversity loss driven by habitat degradation and spatial homogenization. While grassland biodiversity shows partial recovery and protected areas tend to stabilize trends, forest biodiversity continues to decline, underscoring the need to pair protected-area expansion with large-scale habitat restoration and improved management.

title: Rapid Colonisation of Synanthropic Stone Martens in a Highly Urbanised Region: Insights From Temporal and Spatial Analysis.
crm_level_1: Research Institute for Nature and Forest (INBO)
summary: This study used genotyping-by-sequencing of 5536 SNPs from 376 stone martens collected across Flanders (Belgium) between 1995 and 2013 to reconstruct rapid recolonisation dynamics in a highly urbanised landscape. Results revealed multiple source lineages, increasing genetic patch size over time, and strong effects of motorways (and to a lesser extent other urban features) in shaping gene flow, with persistent differentiation between eastern and western populations despite some admixture.

title: A prospective evaluation of the inoculation of homogenised tissue and bone biopsies in blood culture bottles for the diagnosis of orthopaedic-device-related infections.
summary: This prospective study compared inoculation of homogenized bone and tissue biopsies from suspected fracture-related or periprosthetic joint infections into BacT/ALERT VIRTUO blood culture bottles versus conventional Wilkins–Chalgren enrichment broth. The blood culture bottle method showed similar sensitivity but significantly higher specificity and markedly faster time to positivity, with 14 days required to reliably detect Cutibacterium acnes.

title: Wallpaper Group-Based Mechanical Metamaterials: Dataset Including Mechanical Responses.
summary: This article introduces a large open dataset of 2D mechanical metamaterial microstructures that span all 17 wallpaper symmetry groups, paired with finite-strain, buckling-inclusive mechanical responses computed via computational homogenization. Geometries are created by a periodic graph plus Bézier-curve method and simulated under diverse loading paths, totaling 1,020 designs and 12,240 trajectories for machine learning and symmetry–property studies.

title: Animal Models of Laryngopharyngeal Reflux Disease: A Systematic Review of Mucosal Changes and Voice Disorders.
summary: This systematic review synthesizes findings from 19 animal model studies showing that exposure of laryngeal tissues to acidic refluxate—especially pepsin—induces inflammatory infiltrates, epithelial disruption, intercellular space dilation, and other mucosal injuries that could underlie voice changes. Translational relevance is limited by heterogeneity of models and key differences from human LPRD (e.g., liquid acidic exposures in supine quadrupeds vs mostly weakly acidic/alkaline gaseous events in upright humans).

title: A practical CD90.2-based FACS strategy for obtaining Schwann cell-enriched cultures from adult mouse nerves.
summary: The study presents a negative-selection FACS workflow using CD90.2 (Thy-1.2) to deplete fibroblasts and obtain highly enriched primary Schwann cell populations from adult mouse sciatic nerves and brachial plexuses. This approach preserves Schwann cell surface epitopes and physiology, yields >97% purity after a brief recovery culture, and is validated by qPCR, western blot, and immunocytochemistry.

title: Decoupling mechanical and morphometric properties in meta-biomaterials.
summary: This study presents a general framework to decouple mechanical and morphometric properties in non-stochastic 3D meta-biomaterials using high-throughput numerical homogenization (44,837 simulations) and multi-objective optimization, successfully isolating Poisson’s ratio and relative mass density with low deviations in other properties. Optimized designs were fabricated via PolyJet and two-photon polymerization and validated experimentally for effective elastic modulus, Poisson’s ratio, and permeability, enabling independent tuning of scaffold properties for mechanobiology and tissue engineering applications.

title: Miniaturization of the QuEChERS method in fruits and vegetables without cryogenic milling: approach to greener analysis of pesticide residues.
summary: This study shows that the QuEChERS pesticide residue method can be miniaturized to analytical test portions as small as 0.5 g for spinach, orange, and red grape using ambient (non-cryogenic) comminution, with acceptable variability when appropriate homogenization is applied. One-step chopping sufficed for spinach and orange, whereas red grape benefited from a second Ultra-Turrax homogenization; miniaturization improved greenness (AGREE score) though slightly reduced recoveries were observed for some polar analytes and with bead-mill extraction.

title: Predictive Value of Digestive Enzymes in Patients With Reflux-Induced Chronic Cough.
summary: This prospective controlled study in 104 adults with objectively confirmed laryngopharyngeal reflux disease assessed salivary digestive enzymes and their relationship to reflux-related chronic cough. Patients with chronic cough had greater symptom burden and improvements after therapy, with salivary elastase correlating with cough presence and symptom severity and bile salts correlating with quality-of-life impact, suggesting these biomarkers may help predict clinical findings.

title: Pathogenic IgG from long COVID patients with neurological sequelae triggers sensitive but not cognitive impairments upon transfer into mice.
summary: Purified IgG from long COVID patients with neurological symptoms induced transient mechanical allodynia and pain-related facial grimacing in mice without affecting cognitive, anxiety, or depressive-like behaviors, and these effects were abolished by IgG depletion or papain digestion. Transferred human IgG localized to mouse dorsal root ganglion sensory neurons (not CNS parenchyma) without evidence of microgliosis or astrogliosis, and a targeted autoantigen screen did not reveal a consistent autoreactivity signature across patients.

title: Unipept in 2024: Expanding Metaproteomics Analysis with Support for Missed Cleavages and Semitryptic and Nontryptic Peptides.
summary: This paper presents Unipept 6.0, a major update that replaces a relational database with a Sparse Suffix Array (SSA) index to support fast matching of semi-tryptic, non-tryptic, and missed-cleavage peptides and on-the-fly functional/taxonomic annotation. Benchmarks on SIHUMIx peptides show similar accuracy to prior versions but up to ~70× faster performance for missed-cleavage handling, with an API rewritten in Rust and memory-optimized indexing usable across the Unipept ecosystem.

title: Role of Klhl14 in senescence and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition via TGF-β modulation.
summary: This study shows that the E3-ubiquitin ligase adaptor KLHL14 maintains thyroid epithelial identity and growth, and that its knockdown in mouse and human thyroid organoids induces a combined senescence and EMT-like program via activation of TGF-β signaling. Pharmacologic inhibition of TGF-β reverses growth impairment and molecular senescence/EMT markers, and interactome analysis suggests KLHL14 interfaces with regulators within the TGF-β pathway, indicating a bidirectional regulatory axis.

title: Reversing vegetable biodiversity loss to diversify diets.
summary: This Perspective argues that reversing the loss of vegetable biodiversity is essential to close global dietary gaps, improve nutrition, and build climate-resilient food systems. It proposes a four-part agenda—secure, harness, promote, and integrate vegetable biodiversity—illustrated with regional roadmaps and an African pilot that links conservation, breeding, school meals, and policy to diversify diets.

title: From microstructure to mechanics: A multi-constituent micro-scale computational model of arterial tissue.
summary: The study presents a microstructure-informed representative volume element (RVE) model of porcine aortic media that explicitly includes elastic lamellae, elastin fibers, collagen fibers, and smooth muscle cells, with geometry derived from multi-modal imaging and mechanics assigned from literature. Using finite elements with embedded elements and periodic boundary conditions, the model is verified for size and mesh convergence, validated against porcine uniaxial tests, subjected to sensitivity analyses, and used to quantify constituent contributions and derive GOH parameters across different microstructures.

title: Serine protease-driven entry and S2 ' cleavage flexibility of feline coronavirus during feline enterocyte infections.
summary: This study shows that feline coronavirus (FCoV) exploits intestinal serine proteases—trypsin, chymotrypsin, elastase—and membrane-bound TMPRSS2/TMPRSS11D to cleave and activate spike at S2′ (and flanking alternative sites), enabling enterocyte infection and syncytia formation, with acidic pH also required. Serine protease inhibitors strongly reduce infection, cleavage mapping confirms flexible S2′ activation (including compensatory sites when S2′ is mutated), and feline colonic contents provide endogenous serine protease activity consistent with these findings.

title: Accuracy and Clinical Findings of Saliva Digestive Biomarkers in Laryngopharyngeal Reflux Disease.
summary: This prospective controlled study assessed multiple salivary digestive biomarkers in 123 patients with laryngopharyngeal reflux disease (LPRD) versus 48 controls, using 24-hour hypopharyngeal-esophageal multichannel intraluminal impedance-pH (HEMII-pH) as the diagnostic reference. Salivary cholesterol showed outstanding diagnostic performance (AUC 0.989; threshold <2.05 mg/dL), elastase performed moderately (AUC 0.811), and combining salivary pH with clinical scores yielded high accuracy, positioning cholesterol, elastase, and salivary pH as promising non-invasive LPRD biomarkers.

title: Comparative proteomic analysis reveals functional and evolutionary diversity in five Montivipera snake venoms.
summary: The study provides a comprehensive proteomic characterization of venoms from five Montivipera species (bornmuelleri, bulgardaghica, xanthina, raddei, albizona) and Macrovipera lebetina ssp., integrating SDS-PAGE, RP-HPLC, and shotgun proteomics with both trypsin and multi-enzymatic limited digestion (MELD). It identifies 129–179 proteins per Montivipera species, confirms conserved major toxin families with species-specific abundance shifts, highlights unusually high svVEGF content across Montivipera, and reveals 39 proteins shared across all five Montivipera venoms, indicating strong interspecific similarity alongside lineage-specific features.

title: Estimating Full Path Lengths and Kinetics from Partial Path Transition Interface Sampling Simulations.
summary: The authors develop a Markov state model framework to reconstruct full path lengths and extract kinetic properties (crossing probabilities, MFPTs, flux, and rate constants) from computationally efficient partial paths generated by REPPTIS. They validate the approach on 1D model potentials and all-atom systems (KCl dissociation and trypsin–benzamidine unbinding), finding excellent agreement with benchmarks except for an underestimated rate in the protein–ligand case.

title: Circulating FGF21 is lower in South Asians compared with Europids with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
summary: This secondary analysis of three clinical trials compared circulating inflammation-related proteins between Dutch South Asians and Europids with type 2 diabetes, using an Olink Target 96 Inflammation panel and ELISA validation for FGF21. Twelve proteins differed between groups, with notably lower FGF21 in South Asians (validated in serum for both sexes), while no difference was seen in healthy lean males without T2DM; the causal role of FGF21 in ethnic T2DM risk remains unresolved.

title: Human Vocal Fold Tissue Modifications Related to Laryngopharyngeal Reflux Disease: A Systematic Review.
summary: This PRISMA-guided systematic review synthesizes evidence from 24 human-focused experimental studies showing that laryngopharyngeal reflux—particularly pepsin exposure—is associated with epithelial barrier disruption, inflammation, oxidative stress, DNA damage, and altered defense molecule expression in laryngeal and vocal fold tissues. The review highlights candidate pathogenic mechanisms and biomarkers while noting methodological heterogeneity and gaps, especially the lack of studies on non-acidic reflux enzymes and standardized diagnostic confirmation with HEMII-pH.

title: Oral enzyme combination therapy reduces systemic inflammation, urinary CTXII and pain in knee osteoarthritis: a proof-of-mechanism, randomised, crossover, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
summary: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial in patients with knee osteoarthritis tested an oral enzyme combination (bromelain, trypsin, rutoside) for 8 weeks and found increased serum α2‑macroglobulin and IL‑10, reduced urinary CTX-II, and improvements in KOOS Pain and Symptoms versus placebo, with good tolerability. The findings suggest systemic anti-inflammatory effects and potential modulation of cartilage turnover by the therapy.

title: Multi-omics analysis reveals distinct gene regulatory mechanisms between primary and organoid-derived human hepatocytes.
summary: This study compares gene regulatory mechanisms in primary human hepatocytes (PHHs) and intrahepatic cholangiocyte organoid (ICO)-derived hepatocyte-like cells using integrated single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq. It finds extensive AP-1 co-occupancy with HNF4A in PHHs and identifies ELF3 as an ICO-specific regulator whose depletion enhances hepatocyte marker expression in differentiated ICOs, highlighting distinct transcriptional control between PHHs and organoid-derived hepatocytes.

title: Ex vivo drug sensitivity profiling to complement molecular profiling in pediatric precision oncology.
crm_level_3: Princess Máxima Center for Pediatric Oncology
summary: This study demonstrates that rapid ex vivo drug sensitivity profiling using PDX-derived tumor cells from pediatric solid tumors is feasible within 14 days, reproducible across two institutes, and identifies actionable drug hits for the vast majority of cases. Genomic alterations alone poorly predicted drug response, while transcriptomic features and ex vivo screening together refined treatment selection and broadened therapeutic options, supporting integration into precision oncology diagnostics.

title: Canine organoids: state-of-the-art, translation potential for human medicine and plea for standardization.
summary: This review synthesizes the state-of-the-art on canine organoids and tumoroids, their translational potential to human medicine, and a meta-analysis of 41 studies that reveals substantial variability and reporting gaps in culture methods. The authors advocate for methodological standardization and propose a practical, cross-tissue baseline protocol to improve reproducibility and application in veterinary and human research, particularly oncology.

title: Integration of lymphatic vasculature to a human lymph node-on-chip enhances physiological immune properties.
summary: The authors developed a human lymph node-on-chip that integrates a perfused lymphatic endothelial cell-lined channel created via a sacrificial-print approach in a HUMIMIC Chip2 device, yielding a metabolically stable model under flow. Incorporation of lymphatics induced LN-like LEC phenotypes (e.g., ACKR4 and CCL21 expression), increased lymphocyte—especially B cell—numbers, compartmentalized secretion of IL-7 and CCL21, and closer immune-cell clustering, indicating enhanced physiological immune properties.

title: Comparison of air-liquid interface transwell and airway organoid models for human respiratory virus infection studies.
crm_level_1: National Institute for Public Health and the Environment (RIVM)
summary: This study harmonized key experimental parameters across three labs to compare a primary human bronchial epithelial air–liquid interface (ALI) transwell model and two adult stem cell–derived airway organoid models for influenza A/H1N1 infection. All models showed similar differentiated cell types, viral growth kinetics, antiviral cytokine profiles, and serum-mediated neutralization, supporting their comparability and utility for respiratory virus research and preclinical vaccine studies.

title: Progression to fibrosis and hepatocellular carcinoma in DEN CCl4 liver mice, is associated with macrophage and striking regulatory T cells infiltration.
summary: Using a DEN-CCl4 mouse model that progresses from fibrosis to hepatocellular carcinoma, the study maps immune-cell composition and spatial distribution by multiplex immunofluorescence and flow cytometry. It finds marked increases of infiltrating macrophages and regulatory T cells—especially at the invasive margin and non-tumor fibrotic regions—while CD8+ T cells do not rise, recapitulating immunosuppressive features of human HCC.

title: Functional organotypic human lymph node model with native immune cells benefits from fibroblastic reticular cell enrichment.
summary: The authors developed an organotypic 3D human lymph node hydrogel model incorporating native lymph node immune cells and donor-matched ex vivo cultured fibroblastic reticular cells (FRCs). FRC enrichment improved immune cell viability (notably B cells), shifted subset composition and cytokine/chemokine milieu (e.g., BAFF, CXCL12, CCL19, IL-6), and constrained T cell expansion while still permitting activation by anti-CD3 or allogeneic dendritic cells, thus capturing key lymph node functions.

title: Blood and tissue HIV-1 reservoirs display plasticity and lack of compartmentalization in virally suppressed people.
summary: In ART-suppressed people living with HIV, translation-competent reservoir cells show distinct phenotypes in blood versus lymph nodes, with blood p24+ cells enriched for GZMA and effector memory features, while lymph node p24+ cells are mainly central/transitional memory and frequently CXCR5+, with no enrichment in germinal center Tfh cells. Near full-length sequencing across matched blood, lymph nodes, and gut reveals widespread clonal overlap without compartmentalization, indicating reservoir clones persist and disseminate across tissues without evidence for ongoing replication under therapy.

title: Synchronizing the Osteochondral Regeneration Process through Spatial Patterning of Stable and Hypertrophic Cartilage Organoids.
crm_level_3: Prometheus the Translational Division of Skeletal Tissue Engineering
summary: This study presents a scaffold-free, zonated osteochondral implant created by spatially assembling iPSC-derived chondrocyte (iChon) organoids with hypertrophic cartilage organoids from human periosteum-derived cells (hPDC), yielding distinct chondral and osteo-like zones that self-organize an interface. In a rat full-thickness osteochondral defect model, iChon+hPDC assembloids promoted hyaline-like cartilage repair with partial restoration of collagen anisotropy and ongoing subchondral remodeling, outperforming hAC+hPDC and defect-only controls.

title: Impact of treatment history on drug resistance of metastatic colorectal cancer organoids.
summary: This study compared 35 patient-derived metastatic colorectal cancer organoids (PDOs) from chemonaive and pretreated patients to assess how prior therapy shapes tumor genomics, transcriptomics, and drug resistance. Pretreated PDOs showed higher mutational load and chemotherapy-associated signatures; oxaliplatin resistance was stably maintained via tumor cell-intrinsic transcriptional programs (including ZNF300/TGM2 and Hedgehog enrichment), whereas irinotecan resistance associated with deep deletions at common fragile sites and specific signatures, and 5-FU/SN-38 resistance was only partly captured.

title: Re-reply to Sabbagh et al.
summary: This correspondence clarifies that the authors advocate analyzing DNA from uncultured mesenchymal core (MC) and cytotrophoblast (CTB) from chorionic villi separately, rather than using MC cultures or mixed villi, to improve accuracy in diagnosing confined placental mosaicism (CPM) and related prenatal findings. They outline rapid enzymatic dissociation (trypsin, then collagenase for MC) enabling immediate DNA testing and recommend SNP-array-based approaches for mosaicism and UPD detection, with an MC back-up culture only as needed.

title: Parkinson's disease-associated PINK1 loss disrupts ensheathing glia and causes dopaminergic neuron synapse loss.
summary: Using Drosophila Pink1 loss-of-function models, the study shows that Pink1-deficient neurons trigger a non–cell-autonomous, injury-like activation of ensheathing glia, which in turn becomes essential to preserve neuronal function and dopaminergic synapse integrity. Targeted downregulation of vesicle trafficking genes Vps35 and Vps13 specifically in ensheathing glia rescues visual circuit transmission defects and prevents age-dependent dopaminergic synapse loss, highlighting glial trafficking pathways as therapeutic entry points in Parkinson’s disease.

title: Protocol for measuring cellular energetics through noncanonical amino acid tagging in human peripheral blood and murine tissue immune cells.
summary: This STAR Protocol describes CENCAT, a flow cytometry-based method that quantifies cellular energetics by measuring protein synthesis via incorporation of a noncanonical amino acid (β-ethynylserine) under metabolic inhibition, enabling immunometabolic profiling in human PBMCs and murine tissue-resident immune cells. It details sample isolation, tissue digestion, βES incorporation, CuAAC click chemistry, immunostaining, and data analysis to compute glucose and mitochondrial dependence with low cell input requirements.

title: MHC1-TIP enables single-tube multimodal immunopeptidome profiling and uncovers intratumoral heterogeneity in antigen presentation.
summary: The study introduces MHC1-TIP, a single-tube, low-input, mild-acid-elution immunopeptidomics workflow that enables quantitative, multimodal profiling of MHC-I ligands alongside the proteome from the same sample. Applying MHC1-TIP to human cell lines, patient-derived organoids, and sub-milligram renal cell carcinoma fragments revealed extensive intratumoral heterogeneity in antigen presentation that is largely decoupled from source protein expression.

title: Optimized culturing yields high success rates and preserves molecular heterogeneity, enabling personalized screening for high-grade gliomas.
summary: This study presents an optimized protocol to establish patient-derived glioma stem-like cell cultures from high-grade glioma using both traditional resections and ultrasonic aspiration, and both single-cell and multicellular fragment starts, achieving up to a 96% combined success rate. Cultures retained genetic and transcriptomic heterogeneity (particularly from ultrasonic aspirates), and enabled personalized screening of 20 anticancer agents within a clinically relevant four-week window for most cases.

title: C9orf72 hexanucleotide repeat expansions impair microglial response in ALS.
summary: This study shows that C9orf72 hexanucleotide repeat expansions reduce C9orf72 expression in human microglia and blunt their transition into reactive (DAM/HLA) states, with prominent defects in endolysosomal pathways, compared to sporadic ALS. Findings were validated in xenografted human iPSC-derived microglia and in vitro, and extended to astrocytes showing a similarly diminished reactive response, alongside an atlas of dysregulated microglia–astrocyte ligand–receptor interactions in ALS.

title: Visualization of F-Actin Through Expansion Microscopy (ExM) with Trifunctional Linker-Conjugated Phalloidin.
summary: This Bio-protocol describes an expansion microscopy workflow for high-resolution visualization of F-actin using a trifunctional linker–conjugated phalloidin (TRITON/Actin-ExM), enabling efficient gel anchoring and strong signal retention. Using HeLa cells, the method combines AcX-based anchoring, hydrogel embedding and polymerization, proteinase K homogenization, and 4× swelling to achieve ~70 nm effective resolution on a standard confocal microscope.

title: Animal-free edible scaffolds from soy protein isolate for the scalable production of cultured meat.
summary: This study develops fully plant-based, edible soy protein isolate (SPI) films and microcarriers that support adhesion, proliferation, and differentiation of bovine myoblasts, including in suspension bioreactors. Proteomics and peptidomics show SPI processing exposes and releases cell-adhesive peptides (e.g., RGD-, LDV-containing), enabling serum-free attachment and suggesting SPI-derived components can partially replace serum functions.

title: Reconstructed Human Skin Models to Study Superficial and Deep Skin Wound Healing In Vitro.
summary: This study presents human reconstructed skin wound models that include dermal fibroblasts, adipose stromal cells (ASCs), and ASC-derived adipocytes to mimic superficial and deep wounds in vitro. Deep wounds with adipocytes exhibited delayed re-epithelialization, increased contraction, and higher α-SMA expression indicative of early scarring, while ASC-only wound beds improved re-epithelialization but still showed elevated α-SMA, alongside distinct cytokine profiles such as reduced leptin.

title: Regulation between LRRK2 and PP2A signaling in cellular models of Parkinson's disease.
summary: This study uncovers a bidirectional regulatory loop between LRRK2 and PP2A: PP2A dephosphorylates LRRK2 at T1503 within the RocCOR domain to destabilize dimers and reduce kinase activity, while LRRK2 phosphorylates the PP2A catalytic subunit PPP2CA at T304 to diminish its C-terminal methylation, impair holoenzyme assembly, and reduce phosphatase activity. Wild-type PPP2CA protects primary mouse cortical neurons from G2019S-LRRK2-induced toxicity, whereas a PPP2CA-T304A mutant does not, highlighting therapeutic potential in boosting PP2A complex formation/activity in Parkinson’s disease.

title: The pentose phosphate pathway controls oxidative protein folding and prevents ferroptosis in chondrocytes.
summary: This study shows that the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway (PPP), via G6PDH-dependent NADPH production, is essential for maintaining ER redox balance to support oxidative protein folding and prevent ferroptosis in hypoxic, differentiating growth plate chondrocytes. Genetic deletion of G6PDH in mouse chondrocytes preserved proliferation through non-oxidative PPP rewiring but reduced NADPH and GSH recycling, triggering ER stress, proteasome/lysosome activation, lipid peroxidation, ferroptosis, and impaired collagen matrix properties, all of which were rescued by glutathione or NAC supplementation.

title: Lymphoma-on-chip model reveals that lymph node stromal cells promote diffuse large B-cell lymphoma survival and migration.
summary: The study presents a human lymphoma-on-chip that integrates a lymphatic vessel lined with primary lymphatic endothelial cells and a collagen hydrogel containing diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) cells and fibroblastic reticular cells (FRCs). Using this system, the authors show that FRCs promote DLBCL survival and directed migration toward lymphatic vessels and that DLBCL cells increase lymphatic vessel permeability, further enhanced by FRCs.

title: Enhanced MHC Class-II Expression in Fibroblastic Reticular Cells Associates with Maturation.
summary: This study shows that lymph node fibroblastic reticular cells (FRCs), particularly T-cell zone reticular cells (TRCs), exhibit enhanced MHC class II expression that increases along a maturation trajectory, suggesting a key role in peripheral tolerance. Combining scRNA-seq with surface protein measurements in mouse and human lymph nodes, the authors identify BST1+CD200+/neg (mouse) and BST1+CD200+ (human) FRCs as the most MHC-II–expressing subsets, highlighting them as potential therapeutic targets in autoimmunity.

title: Emergence of oncofetal plasticity is ubiquitous in early colorectal cancers.
summary: This study shows that metastasis-associated oncofetal cell states are already induced at the earliest invasive fronts of human T1 colorectal cancers and are ubiquitous even in non-metastatic cases, implying additional bottlenecks such as immune evasion. Using multiregional organoids, bulk and single-cell spatial transcriptomics, and cocultures, the authors demonstrate that trophocyte-like cancer-associated fibroblasts in the submucosa drive oncofetal plasticity via TGFβ and prostaglandin signaling rather than tumor-intrinsic genetics.

title: Distinct Fecal Proteolytic Activity in Zoo Animals with Different Feeding Strategies.
summary: This study measured fecal proteolytic activity across zoo mammals with different feeding strategies and found significantly higher activity in carnivores and omnivores compared with herbivores. Inhibitor profiling indicated that trypsin-like serine proteases account for most activity, suggesting diet strongly influences intestinal protease profiles.

title: Human gut M cells resemble dendritic cells and present gluten antigen.
summary: The study establishes a human intestinal organoid model that robustly generates M cells, maps their differentiation trajectory (SPIB+ICAM2− to SPIB+ICAM2+GP2+), and shows they constitutively express MHC-II and dendritic cell-like programs, unlike mouse M cells. Human M cells process and present gluten antigens (including via TGM2-mediated deamidation) to CD4+ T cells in HLA-DQ2.5–restricted assays, implicating M cells as professional antigen-presenting cells relevant to celiac disease.

title: Advancing in vitro vascular wall modelling using digital light processing to study hyperglycemia-driven cell changes.
summary: The study developed and characterized digital light processing (DLP)-printed acrylate-endcapped urethane-PEG (AUP2PEG) scaffolds coated with gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) or atelocollagen to support equine endothelial cells (EC) and mesenchymal stromal cells (MSC) and model hyperglycemia-induced vascular changes. GelMA coatings yielded uniform, cytocompatible surfaces that supported EC/MSC growth and MSC trilineage differentiation, and high-glucose culture reduced EC viability on the scaffolds while MSC were comparatively resilient over the short term.

title: Preventing MALT1-mediated CYLD cleavage induces intestinal dysbiosis and reduces EAE severity.
summary: The study generated CYLD(R321A) knock-in mice expressing a MALT1 cleavage-resistant CYLD to dissect substrate-specific roles of MALT1 protease activity in vivo. These mice showed normal lymphocyte development and signaling but displayed altered gut microbiota and reduced EAE severity, indicating that preventing CYLD cleavage modulates neuroinflammation and microbiota without causing broad immune defects, supporting substrate-specific MALT1 targeting as a therapeutic strategy.

title: Antibacterial activity and cytotoxicity of tricalcium silicate-based cements with different antibacterial additives.
summary: This in vitro study evaluated the antibacterial activity and cytotoxicity of a tricalcium silicate-based cement (TCS) enhanced with five antibacterial additives (benzalkonium chloride, cetrimide, titanium oxide, zinc oxide, and stannous fluoride) across multiple concentrations. Benzalkonium chloride provided the strongest antibacterial effect but with increased cytotoxicity at higher doses, and TCS with 1% BAC achieved the best balance of antibacterial efficacy and cell compatibility on fibroblasts and human dental pulp stem cells (hDPSCs).

title: CD8+ T cells drive myofibroblast activation and contraction via JAK/STAT3 and TGFβ signaling.
summary: In a 3D collagen hydrogel model, CD8+ T cells more potently than CD4+ T cells drive human skin myofibroblast activation and contraction via cytokine-mediated JAK/STAT3 and TGF-beta signaling rather than cytotoxicity. Pharmacologic inhibition with tofacitinib (JAK/STAT3) and SB-505124 (TGF-beta receptor) additively blocked myofibroblast activation and gel contraction, suggesting a dual-targeting antifibrotic strategy.

title: Fibroblast-derived osteoglycin promotes epithelial cell repair.
summary: Using a proteomics-guided screen of the lung fibroblast secretome, the authors identify osteoglycin (OGN) as a key pro-regenerative factor that enhances alveolar epithelial organoid formation, boosts antioxidant and growth-factor signaling programs, and is reduced by cigarette smoke exposure. An active OGN fragment (LRR4–7) recapitulates full-length activity, attenuates elastase-induced injury in precision-cut lung slices, and improves lung function in a mouse injury model, highlighting a therapeutic candidate for COPD.

title: Differential biomarker expression of blood and lymphatic vasculature in multi-organ-chips.
summary: This study isolates and expands human dermal blood and lymphatic endothelial cells (BECs/LECs), endothelializes multi-organ-chips, and examines how blood- versus lymph-like flow and TNFα-driven inflammation affect their morphology, identity, and secretome. Flow altered morphology (alignment and junction tightening under blood flow), but not lineage identity or most secreted biomarkers; LEC CCL21 expression was restored by flow and suppressed by TNFα, and LECs showed a stronger inflammatory secretory response than BECs.

title: Stepwise Differentiation of Mouse Embryonic Stem Cells Into Murine Blood Vessel Organoids With Endothelial Lineage Tracing for Quality Control.
summary: This Bio-protocol describes a robust, stepwise method to differentiate feeder-dependent mouse embryonic stem cells into murine blood vessel organoids with an endothelial VE-cadherin lineage-tracing module for quantitative quality control. The workflow yields ~100 organoids per run across several mouse genetic backgrounds and supports functional assays, genetic manipulation, and in vivo validation after syngeneic grafting.

title: Biocomposites of Enzymes and Covalent Organic Frameworks: A Novel Family of Heterogenous Biocatalysis.
summary: This review synthesizes the state of the art in immobilizing enzymes within covalent organic frameworks (COFs), covering post-synthetic adsorption and covalent attachment, direct encapsulation via hard/soft templates, and biocompatible in situ assembly. It analyzes how COF chemistry, pore architecture, linkages, and process conditions govern enzyme loading, activity, stability, and applications in biocatalysis, photoenzymatic catalysis, sensing, chiral resolution, and stimuli‑responsive release, while outlining challenges and future directions.

title: Intrinsic resistance to RAS inhibitors is driven by dysregulation of KRAS degradation.
crm_level_3: VIB-KU Leuven Center for Cancer Biology
summary: The study shows that elevated wild-type KRAS protein, caused by impaired LZTR1-mediated degradation or by pharmacologic RAS inhibition, drives intrinsic resistance to RAS-targeted therapies in KRAS-mutant lung adenocarcinoma by activating the mTOR/HIF1α axis via lysosomal recruitment of the SLC3A2/SLC7A5 amino acid transporter. Co-inhibition of mTOR or LAT1 (SLC7A5) with dactolisib or JPH203 restores sensitivity to KRAS inhibitors in vitro and in vivo, suggesting combination strategies to overcome resistance associated with LZTR1 loss common in KRAS-mutant LUAD.

title: A versatile mouse model to advance human microglia transplantation research in neurodegenerative diseases.
crm_level_3: VIB Center for Brain and Disease Research and Department of Neurosciences
summary: The study introduces hCSF1Bdes, a new immune-deficient mouse line (Rag2−/− with human CSF1 knock-in) that supports robust engraftment of iPSC/ESC-derived human microglia without requiring Il2rg deficiency, and makes the model broadly accessible for academia and industry. Transplanted human microglia widely colonize the brain, remain homeostatic in control mice, and mount multipronged DAM/HLA/CRM transcriptional and protein responses to amyloid-β plaques when crossed to Alzheimer’s AppSAA knock-in mice.

title: Osteosarcoma 3D patient derived cultures to test genome-informed personalized treatment options: a feasibility study.
summary: This feasibility study established patient-derived 3D osteosarcoma cultures directly from resection tissue to test genome-informed therapies, achieving long-term expansion in 1 of 7 cases (14%). The successful line (L6565) retained tumour genetics (KRAS mutation, homozygous CDKN2A loss), showed sensitivity to the CDK4/6 inhibitor palbociclib, and demonstrated model-dependent variability in drug response across 2D, spheroid, hydrogel, and ‘microsarc’ formats.

title: High-Calorie Diet Consumption Induces Lac-Phe Changes in the Brain in a Time-of-Day Manner Independent of Exercise.
summary: In male Wistar rats, brain Lac-Phe levels in hypothalamus and cortex fluctuate across the 24-hour light/dark cycle and are elevated by high-calorie diet intake independently of exercise. Microglia express CNDP2 and show time-of-day variation in SLC16A1 expression, suggesting microglial involvement in brain Lac-Phe production and regulation.

title: Spike gene variability in porcine epidemic diarrhea virus as a determinant for virulence
summary: Using reverse genetics, the authors engineered live-attenuated PEDV candidates by deleting the spike N-terminal sialic-acid-binding domain (SΔN), deleting ORF3, and/or rearranging S-E-M-N gene order, and evaluated their safety, replication, and immunogenicity in piglets. SΔN recombinants were markedly attenuated in neonates and immunogenic, but maternal vaccination with rPEDV-SΔN did not induce sufficient IgA in sows and failed to protect suckling piglets upon virulent challenge.

title: ATP13A4 gates extracellular polyamine levels to control excitatory synaptogenesis.
