title: The genome sequence of the Hungarian meadow viper, Vipera ursinii rakosiensis (Méhely, 1893).
summary: This Data Note reports a high-quality, chromosome-scale genome assembly for a female Hungarian meadow viper (Vipera ursinii rakosiensis), totaling 1,625 Mb with 19 pseudomolecules (including W and Z) and a complete mitochondrial genome. The assembly, generated using PacBio HiFi long reads and Hi-C data with supporting RNA-Seq, shows strong completeness and accuracy metrics and is openly available in INSDC repositories.

title: Immune counter-evolution: immortalized B cell clones can undergo ex vivo directed evolution to counteract viral escape.
summary: This study uses immortalized human B cell libraries from PBMCs and tonsil tissue to discover SARS-CoV-2-neutralizing antibodies and then applies ex vivo AID-driven directed evolution to enhance breadth and potency against emerging variants. The authors identify a broadly neutralizing RBD-directed antibody (KBA2401), map a conserved epitope, and create a bi-paratopic construct with a non-neutralizing binder (KBA2402) that improves neutralization of recent variants like JN.1 and KP.3.

title: Growth Plate Morphogens as Potential Modulators of Cellular Tissue Remodeling by Annulus Fibrosus Cells.
crm_level_3: Biomedical Engineering Eindhoven University of Technology Eindhoven the Netherlands
summary: This study investigates whether growth plate morphogens modulate annulus fibrosus (AF) cell proliferation and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling using bovine AF cells in 2D screening and a 2.5D platform that preserves native cell morphology. BMP-2, TGF-β1, and FGF-2 elicited robust, distinct transcriptional programs affecting ECM organization and cell-cycle pathways, with BMP-2 promoting cartilage-like ECM, TGF-β1 inducing fibrotic/contractile remodeling, and FGF-2 driving proliferative and collagen turnover signatures, corroborated by increased DNA and sGAG outputs in short-term functional assays.

title: Comparative proteomic analysis of unfermented cocoa beans reveals key metabolic differences between fine-flavor and bulk genotypes.
summary: This study performed a comparative proteomic analysis of unfermented cocoa beans from four Theobroma cacao genotypes (EET19, CCN51, P7, PA121), identifying 2,015 proteins and 198 differentially abundant proteins that distinguish fine-flavor from bulk types. Fine-flavor genotype EET19 showed higher levels of storage proteins, while enzymes related to flavor precursor formation and other pathways varied across genotypes, providing targets for breeding and quality improvement.

title: Faecal amino acids stability: investigating optimal sampling conditions for analysis.
summary: This study assessed how pre-analytical factors—storage temperature and duration, sampling location within stool, freeze–thaw cycles, and the OMNImet GUT device—influence faecal amino acid measurements by targeted LC-MS/MS in healthy donors. Most amino acids were stable across sampling sites and freeze–thaw cycles, storage at −20 °C preserved integrity up to 3 months, 4 °C and 20 °C introduced variability, and the OMNImet GUT device stabilized some amino acids but showed inconsistencies, underscoring the need for standardization.

title: Characterisation of the manchette architecture and its role as transport scaffold using cryo-electron tomography.
summary: Using cryo-electron tomography and proteomics, the study reveals the 3D architecture of the spermatid manchette, showing that the perinuclear ring thickens as the structure elongates and constricts, and directly visualizes dynein–dynactin complexes on manchette microtubules. It also identifies F-actin filaments as both bundles and single filaments intercalating with microtubules and finds little evidence for IFT train-like assemblies, clarifying the manchette’s role as a transport scaffold during spermiogenesis.

title: Multiple sclerosis-associated HLA demarcates EBV-specific CD8+ T cells with an exhausted and brain residency phenotype.
crm_level_1: Erasmus MC, University Medical Center Rotterdam
summary: This study shows that in multiple sclerosis, HLA-B7–restricted EBV-specific CD8+ T cells are largely focused on the latent EBNA3A epitope, exhibit an exhausted phenotype with high co-inhibitory receptor co-expression, and display brain-homing/residency markers (e.g., CXCR3, CD20), being enriched in CNS compartments compared to HLA-A2–restricted cells. Consistently, higher anti-EBV IgG titers were observed in HLA-B7+HLA-A2− patients, and natalizumab treatment restored circulating EBV-specific TEM cells, supporting a model of impaired EBV control and increased CNS infiltration by HLA-B7–restricted CD8+ T cells in MS.

title: Degradation rather than disassembly of necrotic debris is essential to enhance recovery after acute liver injury.
summary: In a mouse model of acetaminophen-induced liver injury, the authors show that necrotic debris contains extracellular DNA, F-actin, histones, complement and fibrin(ogen), and that systemic DNase 1 promotes recovery primarily by degrading DNA and reducing circulating nucleosomes and actin. In contrast, disassembling debris with charged peptides failed to improve outcomes, and enhancing fibrinolysis with tPA worsened injury, indicating that enzymatic degradation (not disassembly) and fibrin encapsulation are key to recovery.

title: High-throughput spheroid-based assay for functional breast cancer precision medicine facilitated by deep learning.
summary: The study presents a high-throughput breast cancer spheroid assay that uses deep learning-based segmentation to quantify treatment response and discriminate between therapy-sensitive and -resistant models. Using patient-derived xenograft (PDX) spheroids, the assay recapitulates expected in vivo responses and reliably distinguishes olaparib-sensitive from -resistant tumors by predicting the fraction of responding spheroids.

title: Harnessing human immune system models to validate NADPH oxidase 1 inhibition as treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma.
summary: The study developed two human immune system (HIS) mouse models—one enriched for human T cells and another for human myeloid cells—orthotopically engrafted with human Hep3B hepatocellular carcinoma to evaluate NADPH oxidase 1 inhibition (NOX1i), and validated findings in ex vivo patient-derived precision-cut tumor slices (PCTS). NOX1i consistently reduced pro-tumorigenic cytokines, adhesion and hypoxia markers, and tumor-promoting immune signatures, with decreased human immune cell infiltration in tumors of the myeloid model, supporting NOX1i as a tumor–immune microenvironment modulator with potential for combination therapy in HCC.

title: Modeling cis-regulatory variation in human brain enhancers across a large Parkinson's Disease cohort.
summary: This study integrates long-read whole-genome sequencing with matched single-nucleus multiome (snATAC-seq and snRNA-seq) from anterior cingulate cortex and substantia nigra of 190 human donors to map cis-regulatory variants that modulate enhancer accessibility, methylation, and gene expression in a cell type-specific manner. By validating 53,841 enhancer variants via caQTL and allele-specific chromatin accessibility and leveraging sequence-to-function models (CREsted and scooby/Borzoi), the work prioritizes causal regulatory variants at Parkinson’s disease GWAS loci and links a subset to target genes across brain cell types, including rare dopaminergic neurons.

title: Inflammatory factors released by ACL reconstruction tendon grafts and their potential for macrophage polarization.
summary: Using an ex vivo, statically loaded culture of human semitendinosus tendon grafts, the study found that fresh autografts rapidly release a mixture of pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines and MMPs, whereas frozen or decellularized grafts release far less. Despite these releases, conditioned media generally did not polarize THP-1 macrophages, responses varied markedly between patients, and no age-related effects were observed, suggesting potential benefits of decellularized grafts and the need for personalized rehabilitation strategies.

title: Bioengineering developmentally inspired matrix vesicles as designer nanotherapeutics for bone regeneration.
crm_level_3: Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery & Special Dental Care
summary: The study bioengineers matrix vesicles (MtVs) from human bone marrow mesenchymal stromal cell-derived hypertrophic cartilage microtissues, showing that BMP2 and hypertrophic conditioning increase vesicle yield, ALP activity, calcium binding, and BMP2/VEGF cargo. These MtVs enhance hBMSC proliferation, migration, osteogenesis, and hECFC angiogenesis, with proteomics revealing enrichment of ECM remodeling, mineralization, and angiogenic pathways, supporting their use as tunable nanotherapeutics for endochondral bone regeneration.

title: Assessing Surface Binding Events on Golgi Microsomes Isolated from Cancer Cells by Capillary Electrophoresis.
summary: This study demonstrates the first direct measurement of ligand binding at the surface of Golgi microsomes isolated from cancer cells by integrating partial-filling affinity capillary electrophoresis (ACE) with a refined binding model that accounts for limited target abundance and nonspecific interactions. Using human Caki-1 cell–derived Golgi vesicles containing UGCG, the authors quantify eliglustat binding (KD ≈ 15.5 μM) and validate specificity via competitive displacement by miglustat (KB ≈ 153 μM), establishing ACE as a low-consumption, label-free platform for assessing target engagement in native membrane environments.

title: Pregnancy exacerbates neutrophil responses in murine lungs and alters gut microbiota composition after cigarette smoke exposure.
summary: This study shows that pregnancy amplifies cigarette smoke–induced neutrophil-driven lung inflammation in mice and alters gut microbiota composition and short-chain fatty acid levels, implicating a gut–lung axis. Using BALB/c mice, the authors integrate lung RNA-seq, BALF cell/mediator profiling, and fecal microbiome and SCFA analyses to demonstrate heightened neutrophil chemotaxis pathways and reduced cecal SCFAs in smoke-exposed pregnant dams.

title: GJA5 and ATP1A1 perturbations recapitulate inflammation-related beat irregularities in iPSC-based atrial myocardium tissue model.
summary: This study builds a 3D human iPSC-derived atrial myocardium model (atrial-like cardiomyocytes, cardiac fibroblasts, and macrophages) to uncover how inflammation—specifically M1 macrophage activation—induces reduced contraction, sodium/calcium deficits, and beat irregularity. Mechanistically, combined downregulation of GJA5 (Cx40) and ATP1A1 (Na+/K+ ATPase) reproduced pro-arrhythmic phenotypes in vitro and triggered atrial fibrillation in human whole-atria in silico simulations under stress, even without ectopy.

title: Preliminary Insights into Geographic Variation in Venom Profiles and Functional Activities of Nigerian Snakes, Bitis arietans and Naja nigricollis.
summary: This study compares venom composition and functional activities of Bitis arietans and Naja nigricollis collected from northern (Kaduna) and southern (Ibadan) Nigeria using integrated proteomics (LC–IM–MS/MS, SDS-PAGE) and biochemical assays. It finds preliminary region-associated differences—more serine proteases in southern B. arietans, higher lectins/SVMP isoforms in northern B. arietans, and broadly conserved PLA2/3FTx backbones in N. nigricollis—accompanied by corresponding shifts in enzymatic, fibrinogenolytic, hemolytic, and coagulation activities, while cautioning that conclusions are limited by small, pooled sample sizes.

title: Efficacy of MLN9708 (ixazomib) in experimental autoimmune myasthenia gravis and in anti-AChR producing primary thymic cell cultures from myasthenia gravis patients.
summary: This study evaluates the proteasome inhibitor ixazomib (MLN9708) for depleting autoantibody-producing plasma cells in early-onset myasthenia gravis (EOMG) thymic cell cultures and in a rat model of experimental autoimmune myasthenia gravis (EAMG). Ixazomib (≥30 nM in vitro; 0.35 mg/kg s.c. twice weekly in vivo) markedly reduced plasma cells, total IgG, and pathogenic anti-AChR antibodies, with acceptable tolerability in rats at 0.35 mg/kg and no evidence of sensory neuropathy in the assays used.

title: Pharmacologic Inhibition of Glutamate Dehydrogenase 1 Improves Functional Recovery of Neuromuscular Junctions and Muscle Function in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
summary: This study shows that pharmacologic inhibition of glutamate dehydrogenase 1 (GLUD1) with R162 improves neuromuscular junction structure and function, enhances satellite cell activity, and increases muscle performance in mdx mice, a model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy. The benefits are linked to elevated glutamate availability that boosts acetylcholine release via presynaptic NMDA receptor signaling, require macrophage presence but are not achieved by macrophage-specific GLUD1 deletion alone, and persist beyond treatment cessation without behavioral side effects.

title: Does sex matter in neurons' response to hypoxic stress?
summary: Using primary cortical neuronal networks from male and female newborn Wistar rats, the study modeled ischemic penumbra-like hypoxia on microelectrode arrays and assessed whether neuronal responses differ by sex and whether 17β-estradiol modulates outcomes. Hypoxia similarly depressed activity in both sexes, while estrogen transiently increased network burst rates and shortened burst duration without conferring long-term neuroprotection, and it mainly affected caspase-dependent apoptosis.

title: Close-to-Patient Models for Gastric Cancer: From Patient-Derived Xenograft Towards a Novel Gastric Cancer Mini-Tumor Model.
summary: This study establishes five close-to-patient gastric cancer models—patient-derived organoids (PDOs), a fibroblast–organoid mini-tumor co-culture, organoid-derived xenografts (ODX), and subcutaneous and orthotopic patient-derived xenografts (PDX)—and shows they preserve key histological features, stromal content, HER2 status, and mutational profiles of the parental tumors. The models provide fibroblast-rich, translational platforms for preclinical testing in vitro and in vivo, potentially improving evaluation of therapeutic strategies for gastric cancer.

title: The glucocorticoid receptor is affected by its target ZBTB16 in a dissociated manner.
summary: This study shows that glucocorticoid-induced ZBTB16 modulates glucocorticoid receptor (GR) actions in a dissociated manner: it restrains GR-driven transactivation (e.g., endothelial barrier strengthening and gluconeogenic responses) while promoting GR-mediated transrepression linked to anti-inflammatory effects. Using human endothelial and synovial cells and zebrafish larvae, the authors demonstrate that reducing ZBTB16 enhances GR activation outcomes but blunts GR’s anti-inflammatory repression, identifying ZBTB16 as a conserved intracellular feedback modulator of glucocorticoid action with therapeutic implications.

title: Neurotrophin-3 produced by motor neurons non-cell autonomously regulate the development of pre-motor interneurons in the developing spinal cord.
crm_level_3: Louvain Institute of Biomolecular Science and Technology
summary: The study shows that Onecut transcription factors in spinal motor neurons non-cell autonomously control the differentiation and spatial distribution of premotor interneurons by moderating motor neuron expression of Neurotrophin-3 (Ntf3). Conditional deletion of Ntf3 in motor neurons increased V1/V2 interneuron numbers and mispositioned multiple interneuron classes, leading to coordination deficits, while Onecut loss in motor neurons altered interneuron positioning without broad changes in interneuron numbers.

title: Activated T Cells Break Tumor Immunosuppression by Macrophage Reeducation.
summary: The study identifies hematopoietic prostaglandin D2 synthase (HPGDS) as a defining feature of an immunosuppressive tumor-associated macrophage subset in melanoma, where T-cell activation via TNFα downregulates HPGDS and reduces PGD2 signaling. Genetic or pharmacologic HPGDS inhibition reprograms macrophages, normalizes tumor vessels, enhances CD8+ T-cell recruitment and function, and sensitizes tumors to anti-PD-1 therapy in mice, with supportive data in human samples and patient-derived tumor spheroids.

title: A functional single-cell metabolic survey identifies Elovl1 as a target to enhance CD8+ T cell fitness in solid tumours.
summary: This study performed an in vivo CRISPR/Cas9 metabolic screen combined with single-cell RNA-seq in CD8+ T cells across primary pancreatic tumors and metastatic niches, identifying Elovl1 as a metabolic checkpoint whose inhibition enhances T cell function and synergizes with anti-PD-1 therapy. Mechanistically, Elovl1 loss reduces saturated VLCFAs, destabilizes INSIG1 to activate SREBP2, raises membrane cholesterol and TCR signaling, boosts mitochondrial fitness and fatty acid oxidation, and correlates with better anti-PD-1 responses in patients’ CD8+ TILs.

title: Proteomic profiling of dysbiosis-challenged broilers reveals potential blood biomarkers for intestinal health.
summary: This study used mass spectrometry-based proteomics of blood plasma from broiler chickens in an in vivo dysbiosis model to identify potential blood biomarkers of intestinal inflammation and barrier dysfunction. Dysbiosis led to increased permeability (faecal ovotransferrin, serum iohexol), villus atrophy/crypt hyperplasia, and differential abundance of 25 plasma proteins highlighting immune activation and suppression of extracellular matrix and cell-adhesion pathways, suggesting candidates such as GAL-9, LRG-1, and PSAP.

title: Ferroptosis-armed dendritic cell vaccines for glioma immunotherapy.
summary: This study shows that dendritic cell vaccines loaded with ferroptotic glioma cell lysates elicit strong, tumor-specific immunity that protects and treats intracranial gliomas in mice, enhancing CD8+ T-cell infiltration, activation, and effector-memory formation. The vaccine’s efficacy depends on calreticulin exposure and ATP release during ferroptosis (but not HMGB1–TLR4), is independent of glioma type or ferroptosis inducer, and does not require bacterial adjuvants.

title: Advancing DIA-Based Limited Proteolysis Workflows: Introducing DIA-LiPA.
crm_level_3: VIB UGent Center for Medical Biotechnology
summary: The study benchmarks library-free DIA workflows (DIA-NN and Spectronaut) for limited proteolysis mass spectrometry (LiP-MS) and introduces DIA-LiPA, an analysis pipeline that integrates tryptic and semitryptic precursor data while modeling missingness for structural interpretation. Using rapamycin-treated human HEK293T lysates and a yeast heat-shock dataset, the authors show library-free approaches achieve higher sensitivity and coverage with acceptable FDR control and that DIA-LiPA reproduces known structural signatures and reveals additional regulatory patterns.

title: Soluble multi-epitope protein vaccination leverages antigen availability to drive CD8+ T cell immunity and tumor control.
summary: This study engineered and produced soluble multi-epitope MBP-fused protein vaccines in endotoxin-free E. coli (ClearColi) carrying OVA-derived CD8+ and CD4+ epitopes and showed they prime robust antigen-specific CD8+ T cell responses in vivo, yielding complete prophylactic protection and transient therapeutic control in a B16-OVA melanoma model when adjuvanted with αCD40 and AddaVax. Despite modest in vitro antigen presentation, in vivo vaccination induced proliferative, polyfunctional CD8+ T cells and detectable antibodies, with efficacy hinging on antigen availability and dosing (prime-boost versus single-prime).

title: A subcellular study on reactive oxygen species generation by PFAS in HepG2 cells.
summary: This study examined how various PFAS (PFCAs, PFSAs, and FTOHs) induce reactive oxygen species (ROS) and reduce viability in human HepG2 cells, using antioxidants (quercetin and mito-tempo) to localize ROS sources and assess mechanistic differences by headgroup and chain length. PFAS increased ROS and marginally altered mitochondrial respiration, lysosomal leakage and lipid peroxidation were consequences rather than causes of ROS, and PFOA/PFOS reduced peroxisomal catalase activity; results suggest headgroup-dependent mechanisms with mitochondrial ROS more central for PFCAs than PFSAs.

title: Single-cell transcriptome atlas of male mouse pituitary across postnatal life highlighting its stem cell landscape.
crm_level_3: Tissue Plasticity in Health and Disease
summary: This study builds a single-cell transcriptomic atlas of the male mouse anterior pituitary across neonatal, young-adult, middle-aged, and old stages in healthy and injury conditions, and validates regulatory insights using pituitary stem cell-derived organoids. It uncovers stem cell markers and regulons (KLF5, AP-1), niche interactions (EGF/ERBB, HGF/MET, MDK/PTPRZ1), and an aging-associated inflammatory phenotype, with partial translation to human pituitary datasets.

title: Donor age and breed determine mesenchymal stromal cell characteristics.
summary: This study isolated bovine subcutaneous adipose tissue-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) from Holstein Friesian and Belgian Blue cattle across fetal, calf, and adult ages to assess how donor age and breed influence proliferation, senescence, immunophenotype, and tri-lineage differentiation. Fetal and calf Holstein Friesian MSCs showed superior proliferation (often >30 doublings), Belgian Blue MSCs exhibited stronger osteogenesis, and CD34 expression (higher in calf Holstein Friesian) positively correlated with proliferation but negatively with osteogenesis, underscoring the need to select donors by age/breed for MSC applications.

title: A review of the toxicological effects and allergenic potential of emerging alternative protein sources.
summary: This systematic review evaluates the toxicological effects and allergenic potential of emerging alternative protein sources including legumes (faba bean, mung bean, lentil, black gram, cowpea), quinoa, hemp, leaf proteins (alfalfa, Moringa), microalgae, and duckweeds. It highlights widespread occurrence of antinutritional factors, phytoestrogens, and allergenicity (including cross-reactivity), the limited quantitative data on processing effects, and calls for food-level safety assessments to support a safe protein transition.

title: Tissue-specific mutagenesis from endogenous guanine damage is suppressed by Polκ and DNA repair.
summary: This study shows that the translesion polymerase Polκ suppresses a novel, tissue-specific somatic mutational signature (SBS-Polk) in mouse liver and kidney that arises from endogenous guanine adducts, and that nucleotide excision repair (NER) and an additional transcription-coupled pathway further limit these mutations. Using mouse genetics, organoid WGS/NanoSeq, Xenopus egg extract replication assays, and untargeted DNA adductomics, the authors demonstrate largely error-free Polκ bypass of N2-dG adducts and discover several previously unknown bulky guanine adducts enriched in NER-deficient livers.

title: Identification and functional analysis of putative effector proteins from Diaphorina citri and 'Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus'.
summary: The study integrates transcriptomics of Diaphorina citri heads and proteomics of insect saliva (artificial diet) and phloem exudates from multiple host plants to identify putative effector proteins from both the psyllid vector and ‘Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus’ (CLas). Six candidates (four from D. citri and two Sec-dependent from CLas) modulated flg22-triggered ROS in Nicotiana benthamiana, and psyllid effectors reduced Pseudomonas syringae pv. tabaci growth, indicating roles in manipulating plant defense.

title: Ketogenic diet suppresses colorectal cancer through the gut microbiome long chain fatty acid stearate.
summary: This study shows that a ketogenic diet reduces colonic tumor burden in mouse models of colorectal cancer by reshaping the gut microbiome to increase free stearic acid, which directly induces cancer cell apoptosis and decreases pro-tumorigenic Th17 cells. Microbiome causality was demonstrated via cecal microbial transfer; stearate supplementation alone replicated anti-tumor effects, linking ketogenic diet-induced microbial functional shifts to tumor suppression.

title: Wild bee diversity in the Entre-Sambre-et-Meuse National Park (Belgium).
summary: This study conducted a standardized inventory of wild bees across 32 sites in the Entre-Sambre-et-Meuse National Park (Belgium) from April to August 2025, recording 1,159 specimens representing 102 species, 17 of which are nationally threatened. Calcareous grasslands and lowland hay meadows supported the highest diversity and concentration of threatened taxa, underscoring their conservation importance within the park.

title: Changes to the Autophagy-Related Muscle Proteome Following Short-Term Treatment with Ectoine in the Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Mouse Model mdx.
crm_level_3: Neuromuscular Reference Center and Department of Neurology
summary: This study evaluated how short-term ectoine treatment affects autophagy-related proteins in skeletal muscles of Duchenne muscular dystrophy mdx mice using Western blotting and immunofluorescence. Ectoine modestly altered ATG5, HSP70, LC3 II, SQSTM1 (including Ser366-phosphorylated SQSTM1), and mTOR, significantly improving the LC3 II/SQSTM1 balance in gastrocnemius muscle and increasing LC3 II staining in tibialis anterior, supporting further investigation of ectoine as a supportive therapy for DMD.

title: Verapamil and low-dose anti-mouse thymocyte globulin combination therapy stably reverses recent-onset type 1 diabetes in NOD mice by acting on the beta cell and immune axes.
summary: Combining continuous verapamil with a short course of low-dose rabbit anti-mouse thymocyte globulin (mATG) reversed hyperglycaemia durably in 45% of recent-onset diabetic NOD mice by day 56, outperforming either monotherapy and preserving beta-cell function with higher pancreatic insulin content/volume and reduced severe insulitis. Mechanistically, mATG induced transient lymphodepletion and memory skewing, while the combination increased the Treg:CD8 TEM ratio in pancreatic draining lymph nodes; normoglycaemia associated with reduced beta-cell Txnip expression.

title: Human Myelin Spheres for in Vitro Oligodendrocyte Maturation, Myelination and Neurological Disease Modeling.
summary: The study introduces human Myelin Spheres (MyS), a coculture of hPSC-derived cortical neurons and inducible SOX10 oligodendrocyte precursor cells that generates early and progressively compact myelin as early as six weeks, outperforming neuron-only spheroids. Multimodal analyses (snRNA-seq, lipidomics, TEM, electrophysiology) show MyS oligodendrocytes resemble late fetal-to-adult human profiles, and the platform models lysolecithin-induced demyelination and rabies virus infection.

title: Intrinsic mechanisms and microenvironmental cues fine-tune plasticity of esophageal progenitors.
summary: This study shows that Hedgehog signaling induces esophageal progenitor plasticity by indirectly activating Sox9 via stromal TGF-β signaling and a later BMP input, producing a junction-like keratinocyte state predisposed to metaplasia. It also uncovers a cell-intrinsic COX-2–dependent mechanism that stabilizes SOX9 protein, and demonstrates that COX-2 inhibitors (e.g., ibuprofen, celecoxib) suppress SOX9 and reprogramming in mouse and human models, suggesting pharmacological strategies to modulate epithelial plasticity and prevent metaplasia.

title: Alternatives to animal-derived extracellular matrix hydrogels? An explorative study with HepaRG cells in animal-free hydrogels under static and dynamic culture conditions.
summary: This study reviews commercially available animal-free extracellular matrix hydrogels and evaluates selected candidates (PeptiMatrix, VitroGel, GrowDex, PuraMatrix) against a Matrigel–collagen reference for culturing HepaRG liver cells under static (plates) and dynamic (OrganoPlate) conditions. All animal-free hydrogels supported viable cultures, but hepatic function was generally lower than the animal-derived reference; notably, PeptiMatrix 7.5 mg/mL under flow showed CYP3A4 inducibility, making it a promising non-animal alternative after further optimization.

title: IFN-I signaling enhances salivary gland stem and progenitor cell activity after irradiation.
summary: Using mouse salivary gland organoids, the study shows that proton irradiation, compared with photons, more strongly derepresses transposable elements, leading to cytoplasmic dsRNA accumulation, RIG-I activation, and enhanced IFN-β signaling that boosts Sox9+ stem/progenitor cell self-renewal. While cGAS-STING and mtDNA/ZBP1 contribute to interferon signaling after irradiation, the proton-specific increase is linked to greater loss of H3K9 methylation and heterochromatin regulators, driving TE upregulation.

title: In Vitro Infection Model Using A6 Cells Sets the Stage for Host-Batrachochytrium salamandrivorans Exploration.
summary: The study establishes a Xenopus laevis A6 cell–based in vitro model that reproduces the complete Batrachochytrium salamandrivorans (Bsal) life cycle, including β-galactose–mediated attachment, germ tube–driven host entry independent of actin dynamics, intracellular maturation, host cell death, and pathogen release. Results mirror ex vivo and in vivo salamander skin responses, validating A6 cells as a practical surrogate to dissect host–Bsal interactions and to support future mechanistic and intervention studies.

title: Endometrium-derived organoids from cystic fibrosis patients and mice as new models to study disease-associated endometrial pathobiology.
crm_level_3: Tissue Plasticity in Health and Disease
summary: This study develops and characterizes endometrial organoid models from women with cystic fibrosis (CF) and from a CF mouse model, demonstrating CFTR dysfunction, aberrant hormone responses, and pathway alterations relevant to endometrial biology and fertility. CFTR modulator treatments partially rescue functional defects, and single-cell RNA sequencing of CF mouse uterus reveals epithelial and immune alterations paralleling human CF endometrium, providing complementary platforms to investigate CF-associated endometrial pathobiology.

title: Efficient mucin O-glycan degradation by specific mucin degrading intestinal bacteria: towards understanding enzyme-glycan interactions.
summary: This study compares the mucin O‑glycan–degrading capacities and enzyme specificities of Akkermansia muciniphila, Ruminococcus torques, and Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron grown on porcine gastric mucin, using proteomics and targeted glycan-cleavage assays with HMOs, sulphated glycans, and mucin-derived O‑glycans. Co-cultures and a synthetic community combined the enzymatic repertoires of the individual species to achieve broad and efficient mucin glycan degradation, revealing distinct linkage preferences and a complementary role for B. thetaiotaomicron in sulphate removal.

title: Identification of β4GALNT2 as an anti-hPIV3 factor through genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 library screening.
summary: A genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screen in human cells identified B4GALNT2 as a potent host restriction factor for human parainfluenza virus 3 (hPIV3), while multiple glycosylation genes acted as proviral factors. Mechanistically, β4GALNT2 installs the Sda glycotope on α2-3–sialylated glycans, which disrupts the hPIV3 hemagglutinin-neuraminidase interaction—particularly contacts involving residue W371—thereby reducing receptor binding and infection, with broader but weaker effects on other paramyxoviruses.

title: Discovery of a Novel Sucrose 6F-Phosphate Phosphorylase and Its Application for Isomelezitose Production.
summary: The authors discovered a novel sucrose 6F-phosphate phosphorylase (SphSPP) from Sphaerochaeta globosa and used it to synthesize the rare trisaccharide isomelezitose from sucrose and isomaltulose, achieving 68 g of >99% purity at 1 L scale. Isomelezitose showed limited digestibility, about 27% relative sweetness to sucrose, and physicochemical properties similar to sucrose, supporting its potential as a low-calorie food ingredient.

title: Tracking the emergence of the Upper Palaeolithic in western Asia and Europe: A Multiple Correspondence Analysis of Protoaurignacian and Southern Ahmarian lithics.
summary: This study applies Multiple Correspondence Analysis to attribute-level data from Early Upper Paleolithic lithic blanks (Protoaurignacian and Southern Ahmarian) from Jordan, Romania, Italy, and France, and compares them to an Iberian Solutrean control to evaluate technological variability and similarities. Results show EUP assemblages cluster together and emphasize bladelet-focused production with shared platform/convexity traits distinct from Solutrean, while retouch on bladelets displays regional idiosyncrasies and supports the heuristic value of the 12 mm blade–bladelet threshold.

title: Changes in bone characteristics precede serum mineral deterioration in a mouse model of early stage chronic kidney disease.
summary: Using Col4a3−/− mice as a progressive chronic kidney disease (CKD) model, the study shows that early CKD evokes hormonal changes (↑FGF23, ↑PTH, ↓1,25(OH)2D3) that preserve normal serum calcium and phosphate and maintain intestinal calcium absorption and renal calcium handling. Despite stable serum minerals, bone loss emerges early—driven by reduced osteoblast number/activity and increased bone marrow adiposity—preceding overt serum mineral deterioration.

title: Age-dependent development and microarchitecture of the osteochondral unit of the humeral head in harbour porpoises (Phocoena phocoena).
summary: This study characterizes age-dependent microarchitectural development of the humeral head osteochondral unit in harbour porpoises, showing that neonates lack a calcified cartilage layer and subchondral bone plate, juveniles display early zonation and incipient calcification, and adults exhibit a fully layered cartilage with arcade-like collagen, an irregular calcified cartilage layer, and a subchondral bone plate. The delayed maturation and irregular cartilage–bone interface relative to terrestrial mammals are attributed to differing aquatic loading, with biochemical trends showing decreased DNA and increased GAG and collagen with age.

title: Production of recombinant IgA1 with defined mucin-type O-glycans in Nicotiana tabacum BY-2 cells.
crm_level_3: Louvain Institute of Biomolecular Science and Technology (LIBST)
summary: The authors engineered Nicotiana tabacum BY-2 suspension cells to install mucin-type O-glycosylation and produce recombinant human IgA1 with defined Core 1 O-glycans in the hinge region by expressing human GalNAcT2 and Drosophila C1GalT1. Lectin blotting and LC-MS/MS confirmed efficient hinge O-glycosylation with strong reduction of plant-specific Hyp/pentose modifications and human-like complex N-glycans at N263, yielding secreted IgA1 without loss of thermal stability.

title: Single-domain antibodies directed against hemagglutinin and neuraminidase protect against influenza B viruses.
summary: The study reports llama-derived single-domain antibodies (VHHs) that broadly neutralize influenza B by targeting conserved epitopes on hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA), with cryo-EM structures revealing a quaternary HA stem epitope and an NA active-site epitope. Bispecific and multivalent formats enhanced potency and breadth, and Fc-fused VHHs fully protected mice from lethal influenza B challenge, including activity against an oseltamivir-resistant NA variant.

title: Modulating Protein Glycation in Skim Milk Powder via Low Humidity Dry Heating to Improve Its Heat-Stabilizing Properties.
summary: The study shows that dry heating skim milk powder (SMP) under very low humidity (<10% RH) at 80–120 °C modulates the Maillard reaction to enhance heat stability while minimizing browning and loss of solubility. A 10 min treatment at 120 °C produced SMP that yielded sterilized recombined filled evaporated milk with markedly reduced droplet size and viscosity, limited HMF/carbonyl formation, and preserved protein solubility and sulfhydryl content compared to controls or longer treatments.

title: Proximal partners of the organellar N-terminal acetyltransferase NAA60: insights into Golgi structure and transmembrane protein topology.
summary: This study used proximity-dependent biotinylation (BioID) to map proteins near the Golgi-localized N-terminal acetyltransferase NAA60, revealing >100 proximal partners enriched in medial/trans-Golgi factors (golgins, GRASPs, Rabs, SNAREs) and yielding peptide-level topology information for transmembrane proteins. Electron microscopy of NAA60 knockout cells showed shortened Golgi cisternae and increased vesiculation, supporting a role for NAA60 and its neighbors in maintaining Golgi integrity and organization.

title: Label free quantitative proteomic analysis reveals the physiological and biochemical responses of Arabidopsis thaliana to cinnamon essential oil.
summary: This study used label-free quantitative proteomics to profile the rapid proteome response of Arabidopsis thaliana leaves to a 6% cinnamon essential oil (CEO) emulsion, revealing 325 differentially accumulated proteins just 1 hour after treatment. CEO strongly suppressed photosynthesis- and membrane-associated proteins while increasing stress-response proteins, consistent with rapid desiccation and damage observed phenotypically.

title: Fusion of Complement Fragment C3d Enhances Germinal Center Responses to HIV-1 Envelope Glycoproteins.
summary: The study shows that fusing complement fragment C3d to the HIV-1 ConM SOSIP Env trimer enhances B cell activation, follicular dendritic cell (FDC) antigen capture/retention, early germinal center (GC) formation, and improves neutralization in mice, particularly when combined with the AddaS03 adjuvant. C3d fusion also shifts antibody specificity away from base epitopes toward the V1V2 apex and prolongs antigen display on FDCs up to 56 days, with stronger responses observed in female mice.

title: Autologous profiling reveals inter-patient heterogeneity in Vδ2+γδTIL responses to glioblastoma driven by extracellular matrix-BTN3A axis.
summary: Using a fully autologous platform with matched primary glioblastoma (GB) tumors and patient T cells, the study shows that Vδ2+ γδTILs (but not αβT cells) robustly recognize GB in the presence of pamidronate, with substantial inter-patient heterogeneity driven by both immune-intrinsic factors and tumor BTN2A1/BTN3A ligand availability. Transcriptomic and functional analyses implicate an extracellular matrix–BTN3A axis (notably LAMA5, TGFB1, and ITGA3) in modulating ligand accessibility and Vδ2+ γδT cell activity, suggesting therapeutic strategies to enhance recognition by targeting this axis.

title: Rough microsomes isolated from snap-frozen canine pancreatic tissue retain their co-translational translocation functionality.
summary: The study shows that rough microsomes isolated from snap-frozen canine pancreatic tissue retain essential endoplasmic reticulum functions for co-translational translocation, including signal peptide cleavage and N-linked glycosylation. These microsomes supported in vitro translocation of model substrates and remained sensitive to the Sec61 inhibitor CADA, providing a practical alternative to fresh tissue for ER translocation research.

title: Trub1-mediated pseudouridylation is dispensable for immune cell development and homeostasis.
summary: The study generated conditional and global Trub1-deficient mice to test whether Trub1-mediated RNA pseudouridylation is required for immune cell development, homeostasis, or function. Despite identifying Trub1-dependent Ψ55 in multiple mouse mitochondrial tRNAs, the authors found no significant impact of Trub1 loss on T, B, NK, or myeloid cells at steady state or in influenza infection and MC38 tumor models, suggesting functional redundancy or overestimation of Trub1’s mRNA role.

title: Small round cell sarcoma tumoroid biobank reveals CIC::DUX4 sarcoma vulnerability to MCL-1 inhibition.
crm_level_3: Princess Máxima Center for Pediatric Oncology
summary: The authors establish a living biobank of long-term patient-derived tumoroids from pediatric small round cell sarcomas (Ewing sarcoma, CIC::DUX4 sarcoma, and BCOR-rearranged sarcoma) that retain histologic, genomic, and transcriptomic hallmarks and tumor heterogeneity across disease stages. Drug screening reveals entity-specific sensitivities, notably a strong vulnerability of CIC::DUX4 tumoroids to MCL-1 inhibitors, highlighting potential targeted therapies for this hard-to-treat subgroup.

title: Comprehensive analysis of blood proteome response to necrotic enteritis in broiler chicken.
summary: This study profiled the blood plasma proteome of broiler chickens across a spectrum of necrotic enteritis severity using DIA LC–MS/MS, identifying 63 differentially abundant proteins out of 412 quantified. Regulated proteins mapped to complement activation, acute phase response, and extracellular matrix/basement membrane remodeling, revealing candidate biomarkers and insights into host-pathogen interactions.

title: Integrin β1 Demarks Precursors of Brain-Residing Antibody-Secreting Cells in Multiple Sclerosis.
summary: Using single-cell RNA-seq and functional assays, the study identifies integrin β1 (CD29) as a defining marker of CXCR3+ memory B cells that preferentially transmigrate across brain endothelium and differentiate into IgG-producing antibody-secreting cells (ASCs), with CD29/CXCR3 coexpression being a dominant feature of ASCs in MS CNS compartments. Therapeutically, natalizumab reduces CD29 on circulating CXCR3+ memory B cells, and after cladribine, reduced CD29 on repopulating CXCR3+ memory B cells associates with absence of early disease activity, nominating CD29 as a potential theragnostic biomarker in MS.

title: Fibroblast-derived matrix human skin equivalents reveal distinct roles for papillary and reticular fibroblasts in human skin barrier integrity and aging.
summary: The study builds fibroblast-derived matrix human skin equivalents with either papillary or reticular fibroblasts to dissect their roles in epidermal differentiation and lipid barrier organization. Papillary fibroblast models show superior epidermal maturation, ceramide profiles closer to native skin, longer LPP repeat distances, and lower TEWL, whereas reticular fibroblast models display an aged-like phenotype with altered ceramide composition, shorter average chain lengths, increased monounsaturation, and impaired barrier function.

title: The Modified Canine Groove Model of Osteoarthritis.
summary: This study introduces a modified canine groove model of osteoarthritis that creates two full-thickness cartilage grooves per femoral condyle using a 3 mm biopsy punch, and compares it to the original superficial-grooving model. Both models produced mild, slowly progressive OA features without significant gait changes; the modified model showed slightly less macroscopic cartilage damage and synovial inflammation, making it suitable for evaluating cartilage repair strategies such as scaffold implantation.

title: Unravelling the cellular sources and location of IL-17A production during a Giardia infection.
summary: This study maps the cellular and anatomical sources of IL-17A during Giardia muris infection in mice, showing that CD4+ T helper cells in the small intestinal lamina propria are the predominant producers of IL-17A. A minor IL-17A contribution arises from MHC-II+CD11c+ innate antigen-presenting cells with a macrophage-like phenotype, while T cell–deficient mice exhibit severely blunted IL-17A responses and fail to clear infection.

title: Functional Characterization of Glycated Peptide Aggregates in Whey Protein Hydrolysates.
summary: The study characterizes whey protein hydrolysates (WPHs) and their size fractions, showing that partially hydrolyzed WPH1 contains >100 kDa glycated aggregates (CML-positive) that bind sRAGE, trigger pro-inflammatory cytokine release in THP-1-derived macrophages, and induce IgE-dependent basophil degranulation. In contrast, extensively hydrolyzed and filtered WPH2 lacks high–molecular-weight aggregates, exhibits minimal sRAGE binding and cytokine induction, and shows little basophil activation, underscoring safety/functionality differences among hydrolysate formulas.

title: The amino acid composition of commercially available vegan meat and dairy analogues.
summary: This study measured the amino acid profiles of 40 commercially available vegan meat and dairy analogues in the Netherlands and compared them with FAO amino acid requirements and animal-based counterparts. Most analogues had lower protein and essential amino acid contents—particularly methionine and often lysine—than animal products, with considerable variability across products and minimal change after typical heat preparation in a tested case.

title: The genome sequence of the common sole, Solea solea (Linnaeus, 1758).
summary: This data note presents a chromosome-scale reference genome for the common sole (Solea solea), assembled from PacBio HiFi long reads scaffolded with Hi-C to 21 chromosomal pseudomolecules, plus a complete mitochondrial genome. The 643.8 Mb assembly (BUSCO 98.3% complete) is annotated with 21,646 protein-coding genes and all raw data and assemblies are publicly available.

title: Distinct tumor immune microenvironmental landscapes drive divergent immunotherapy responses in glioblastoma.
summary: This study defines three functional tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) subtypes in glioblastoma—TIME-low, TIME-med, and TIME-high—using single-cell/nucleus RNA sequencing and spatial proteomics, and shows they have distinct vascular-immune landscapes. Subtype-matched murine models reveal divergent responses to immunotherapies: TIME-med responds best, TIME-low shows transient benefit to anti-angiogenic checkpoint blockade with adaptive myeloid suppression, and TIME-high is largely resistant and worsened by CD40 agonism but can be partially sensitized by adding PI3Kγ/δ inhibition to anti-angiogenic ICB.

title: Regulatory grammar in human promoters uncovered by MPRA-based deep learning.
summary: This study presents PARM, a lightweight deep-learning model trained on promoter-focused massively parallel reporter assays (MPRAs) to predict autonomous human promoter activity, design synthetic promoters, and infer functional transcription factor (TF) regulatory grammar across cell types and stimuli. Using economical promoter-capture MPRA libraries and validation in multiple human cell lines and a colorectal cancer organoid, PARM maps activating and repressive TF motif activities, positional preferences, and context-specific rewiring under heat shock, TP53 activation, and PMA treatment, with experimental confirmation via mutagenesis and motif-insertion MPRAs and proteomics.

title: Food hydrocolloids κ-carrageenan and xanthan gum in processed red meat modify gut health in rats.
summary: This study examined how adding 1% κ-carrageenan or xanthan gum to processed pork affects protein digestibility, microbiota, oxidative stress, and inflammatory pathways using in vitro digestion/fermentation and a 21-day rat feeding trial. Xanthan gum reduced in vitro protein digestibility and increased protein fermentation metabolites, while in vivo both hydrocolloids reshaped colonic microbiota and were associated with down-regulation of colonic inflammatory pathways; κ-carrageenan reduced lipid oxidation in stomach contents and xanthan gum lowered plasma and colonic TBARS.

title: Bcl-xL blockade targets neutrophils and synergizes with chemotherapy in lung squamous cell carcinoma.
summary: In a mouse model of lung squamous cell carcinoma (SNL), tumor-associated neutrophils (TANs) exhibit prolonged survival and elevated Bcl-xL, but Bcl-xL inhibition alone does not slow tumor growth. Chemotherapy (carboplatin + paclitaxel) induces systemic neutrophilia and raises Bcl-xL in TANs, and combining Bcl-xL blockade with chemotherapy reduces Bcl-xL-high TANs and synergistically suppresses tumor progression.

title: Three-Dimensional Bioprinting of Regenerative Cartilage Constructs with Directional Ionically Derived Stiffness Gradients.
summary: This study presents a simple directional ionic crosslinking strategy to 3D bioprint alginate-based cartilage constructs with through-thickness stiffness gradients using a single biomaterial and concentration. Human chondrocytes remained viable for 28 days, and the softer region of the gradient promoted higher cell density and sulfated glycosaminoglycan deposition compared to the stiffer region.

title: Evaluating single-cell ATAC-seq atlasing technologies using sequence-to-function modeling.
crm_level_1: VIB Center for AI & Computational Biology
summary: The study introduces HyDrop v2, an improved open-source droplet-based scATAC-seq platform, and benchmarks it against commercial (10x Genomics) and plate-based (sciATAC) methods for training sequence-to-function deep learning models in mouse motor cortex and Drosophila embryos. They show that models trained on HyDrop v2 data perform comparably to commercial data for enhancer prediction, motif/footprint discovery, and sequence explainability, with cell number outweighing read depth and with substantial cost advantages for large atlases.

title: Park7 deletion leads to sex-specific transcriptome changes involving NRF2-CYP1B1 axis in mouse midbrain astrocytes.
summary: The study shows that loss of Park7 (DJ-1) causes pronounced, male-specific transcriptomic changes in mouse ventral midbrain, characterized by reduced NRF2 signaling and downregulation of EMT, extracellular matrix, and focal adhesion gene programs, prominently in astrocytes. These alterations involve the NRF2–CYP1B1 axis, are recapitulated by Park7/Nfe2l2/Cyp1b1 knockdown in primary male astrocytes and observed in male human iPSC-derived astrocytes with PARK7 mutation, suggesting sex-specific vulnerability to DJ-1 loss.

title: The role of Nrf2 in thyroid maturation and hormone synthesis in vertebrate models.
summary: This study shows that the oxidative-stress regulator Nrf2 is required for thyroid functional maturation across vertebrate models: zebrafish embryos lacking nrf2a develop a hyperplastic, nonfunctional thyroid with defective hormone production, and mouse ESC-derived thyroid organoids lacking Nrf2 fail to produce sufficient thyroglobulin and show impaired folliculogenesis. Multi-omics analysis of organoids links Nrf2 loss to reduced chromatin accessibility at the Tg locus and compensatory activation of AP-1/STAT networks, indicating distinct proximate causes of dyshormonogenesis in fish (iodination defect) versus mammalian organoids (reduced Tg expression).

title: AQP7 deficiency drives adipose tissue remodeling and disrupts homeostasis.
summary: This study shows that reduced AQP7 expression in human adipose tissue correlates with higher BMI and that Aqp7-deficient mice develop visceral adiposity, adipocyte hypertrophy, inflammation, fibrosis, and impaired peritoneal transport, which are exacerbated by high-glucose exposure. Mechanistically, AQP7 loss disrupts adipogenesis and adipocyte function and shifts the adipocyte secretome toward pro-fibrotic and pro-inflammatory signaling that activates fibroblasts and alters tissue remodeling.

title: Comparison of culture media supplements identifies serum components in self-reported serum-free preparations.
summary: The study compared seven self-declared serum-free media (SFM), five human platelet lysates (hPL), and fetal bovine serum (FBS) for mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) expansion, biochemical content, and cost, revealing that two SFMs contained human blood-derived components (MPO, glycocalicin, fibrinogen) and should be reclassified as hPL-like. Overall, most SFMs supported MSC growth but were costlier than hPL, growth factor content did not predict growth performance, and hPL provided the best cost-performance balance.

title: Sodium-myo-inositol cotransporter-1, SMIT1, promotes cardiac hypertrophy and fibrosis induced by pressure overload in mice.
summary: This study shows that the sodium–myo-inositol cotransporter SMIT1 drives pathological cardiac hypertrophy and fibrosis by promoting an IP3/Ca2+-dependent pro‑hypertrophic signaling program in cardiomyocytes during pressure overload. Deleting SMIT1 in mice protects against TAC-induced left ventricular dysfunction, hypertrophy, and fibrosis, via reduced intracellular Na+/Ca2+ loading, altered SR Ca2+ content, blunted NFAT activation, and preservation of the anti-hypertrophic effector Carabin.

title: Infectivity of amphibian chytrid fungi requires metalloprotease-driven spore development and germ tube formation.
summary: This study shows that chytrid fungal zoospores (Bd and Bsal) rapidly secrete metalloproteases that are essential for the transition from attachment to germ tube formation and early spore development, which underpin infectivity. Inhibiting metalloproteases with 1,10-phenanthroline stalls germ tube outgrowth and development in vitro and reduces Bsal colonization of amphibian skin ex vivo at higher doses, with partial rescue by divalent cations indicating metal dependence, especially in Bsal.

title: The pro-inflammatory cytokines IFN-α and TNF-α inhibit organoid-derived extravillous trophoblast invasion.
summary: Using human trophoblast stem cell–derived organoids and first‑trimester tissues, the study shows that IFN‑α and TNF‑α directly impair extravillous trophoblast (EVT) invasion without blocking EVT differentiation, with IFN‑α exerting the strongest effect in both Matrigel and decidua co‑culture assays. Transcriptomic profiling of FACS‑isolated HLA‑G+ EVTs revealed interferon response activation and alterations in EMT, glycolysis, hypoxia, KRAS, and MYC pathways that likely underlie reduced invasiveness.

title: Convergence in Symbiont-Induced Plant-Mediated Responses to Herbivory: Cascading Effects for Foraging Parasitoids.
summary: The study shows that polydnaviruses associated with parasitoid wasps (bracoviruses in Cotesia glomerata and ichnoviruses in Hyposoter ebeninus) induce changes in caterpillar regurgitant that alter Brassica plant volatile emissions, enabling parasitoids to discriminate against hosts previously parasitized by conspecifics. These symbiont-induced, plant-mediated effects create convergent ecological outcomes across trophic levels despite the viruses’ independent evolutionary origins.

title: Potential of Homopolysaccharide-Producing Starter Cultures in the Fermentation of Coconut Yoghurt Alternatives Enriched with Pea Protein Isolate.
summary: This study evaluated a homopolysaccharide (dextran)-producing Latilactobacillus sakei (strain 1.411) to improve texture and stability of coconut milk-based, pea protein-enriched yogurt analogues, comparing it to a non-EPS-producing L. sakei control with similar acidification. Higher sucrose (5% w/w) boosted in situ EPS yields, which, together with pea protein and/or tapioca starch, increased firmness, reduced syneresis, and enhanced perceived thickness during storage, as confirmed by HPLC-quantified EPS, rheology, syneresis tests, and sensory assessment.

title: The Alzheimer's therapeutic Lecanemab attenuates Aβ pathology by inducing an amyloid-clearing program in microglia.
crm_level_3: Centre for Brain and Disease Research
summary: Using human microglia xenografted into Alzheimer’s model mice, the study shows that Lecanemab clears amyloid plaques by engaging microglial Fc receptors to enhance phagocytosis, lysosomal degradation, and antigen presentation, thereby reducing plaques and neuritic damage. Fc-silenced Lecanemab or microglia deficiency abolishes these effects, and single-cell/spatial transcriptomics identify an Fc-dependent program featuring SPP1/osteopontin as a key mediator of amyloid clearance.

title: Vacuolar iron export alters the synergy between doxycycline and fluconazole by affecting cidal ROS levels in Candida albicans
summary: This study shows that vacuolar iron export via the transporter Smf3 controls mitochondrial ROS levels that determine the synergy between doxycycline and fluconazole in Candida albicans, with SMF3 deletion abolishing synergy with iron chelators and elevating ROS under fluconazole. Mitochondria-enriched proteomics revealed iron-utilization changes under fluconazole, SOD2 overexpression reduced ROS and restored synergy in smf3Δ/Δ, and anaerobic conditions eliminated both synergy and fungicidal activity, indicating ROS driven by restricted vacuolar iron access underlies the combination’s effect.
