title: STAT1 drives the immune landscape of murine Toll-like receptor 9-induced liver inflammation.
summary: Using a murine model of repeated TLR9 stimulation, the authors show that type I and II interferon-driven STAT1 activation orchestrates systemic and liver inflammation, with expansion of cycling CD8+ T cells, cDC2s, and monocytes transitioning to inflammatory macrophages. STAT1 deficiency or dual blockade of type I and II IFNs protects mice from these features, and human datasets show concordant IFN-STAT1 signatures, supporting JAK1/2 or direct STAT1 targeting for cytokine storm-related liver disease.

title: Plasma proteome analysis of rheumatic patients reveals differences in fingerprints based on cardiovascular history: a pilot study.
summary: This pilot plasma proteomics study compared rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients with and without cardiovascular events (CVEs) using depletion-based LC–MS/MS and found extensive differences in protein abundances, including a pre-event signature that distinguished RA patients who later experienced CVEs (AUC ~0.72). The findings suggest that plasma protein fingerprints preceding CVEs may help predict cardiovascular risk in RA, though validation in larger cohorts is needed.

title: The farnesoid X receptor activates transcription independently of RXR at non-canonical response elements.
summary: This study shows that the farnesoid X receptor isoform α2 (FXRα2) can bind and activate transcription from non-canonical ER-2 response elements independently of RXR, while RXR promotes FXR binding and activation at canonical IR-1 motifs. An RXR-heterodimerization–deficient FXRα2 mutant (L434R) retains ER-2 binding and activation, and transcriptomic analyses reveal that RXR acts as a molecular switch that enhances IR-1-driven and inhibits ER-2-driven FXRα2 programs, particularly those linked to lipid metabolism and ammonia detoxification.

title: Fungal immunomodulatory proteins skew macrophages towards a pro-inflammatory and tumour inhibitory phenotype.
summary: This study shows that a recombinant fungal immunomodulatory protein from Nectria haematococca (rFIP-nha) reprograms THP-1-derived M2 macrophages toward a pro-inflammatory, tumor-inhibitory phenotype, increasing IL-12/IL-10 ratios and shifting surface markers while reducing phagocytosis. In co-culture with human A549 lung cancer cells, rFIP-nha-treated M2 macrophages and rFIP-nha itself synergistically reduced tumor cell proliferation and increased cell death, indicating dual direct and macrophage-mediated anti-tumor effects independent of rFIP-nha glycosylation state.

title: Dietary 3'-sialyllactose reduces sensitization and type 2 inflammation in a house dust mite induced acute allergic asthma model.
summary: This study tested dietary 3′- and 6′-sialyllactose (HMOS) in a murine house dust mite (HDM) model of acute allergic asthma and found that 0.5% 3′SL, 0.1% 6′SL, and 0.5% 6′SL reduced methacholine-induced airway hyperresponsiveness. 3′SL (especially 0.5%) increased cecal SCFAs and lowered HDM-specific IgE and mast cell degranulation, while 0.5% 6′SL increased eosinophilic inflammation despite reduced airway resistance; both HMOS lowered BALF macrophage influx and modulated lung cytokines toward less type 2 signaling.

title: Advancing Biofilm Removal: Evaluating Electrolytic Methods for Decontaminating Dental Implants In Vitro.
summary: This in vitro study compared two electrolytic systems (GalvoSurge and X-Implant) with chlorhexidine and Terramycin for decontaminating multispecies oral biofilms grown on titanium dental implants. GalvoSurge significantly reduced viable biofilm comparable to chlorhexidine and Terramycin, while X-Implant showed minimal effect, as quantified by v-qPCR and confirmed by SEM/CLSM imaging.

title: Effects of screw configuration and interfacial properties on oil incorporation in high moisture extrusion.
crm_level_3: Physics and Physical Chemistry of Foods
summary: This study examines how twin-screw extruder screw configuration (1 vs. 4 kneading discs) and emulsion interfacial properties (using potato or pea protein emulsifiers) influence oil retention and texture in high-moisture extrusion of soy-based meat analogues. Fewer kneading discs reduced mechanical energy input, oil leakage, and wedge length while increasing stiffness, and emulsions with stiffer interfaces generally produced stiffer doughs but could increase oil leakage under high shear.

title: Using BONCAT to dissect the proteome of S. aureus persisters
crm_level_3: Leiden Institute of Chemistry and The Institute of Chemical Immunology
summary: This study applied BONCAT labeling with L-azidohomoalanine and click-chemistry pulldown to selectively retrieve and quantify newly synthesized proteins from rare Staphylococcus aureus persister cells formed under high-dose oxacillin or moxifloxacin exposure. Label-free LC-MS proteomics revealed broad, largely strain- and antibiotic-specific remodeling of translation, cell-wall stress responses (notably VraTSR), and metabolic downshifts during persistence and recovery, establishing BONCAT as a sensitive method to dissect persister proteomes without cell sorting.

title: An unexpected role of CLASP1 in radiation response and S-phase regulation of head and neck cancer cells.
summary: A genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 knockout screen in an HPV-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma cell line (UM-SCC-11B) identified DNA repair genes and, unexpectedly, microtubule-associated genes—most notably CLASP1—as modulators of radiosensitivity. Validations showed that loss of CLASP1 sensitizes cells to ionizing radiation and etoposide, impairs S-phase progression and replication fork speed, and increases radiation-induced chromosomal breaks, implicating CLASP1 in protecting against DNA damage during replication.

title: Unveiling Mucorales infections: A cutting-edge longitudinal imaging approach for real-time infection and host-response monitoring in Galleria mellonella and mouse models.
summary: This study develops codon-optimized bioluminescent Mucor lusitanicus reporter strains and integrates longitudinal bioluminescence imaging with micro-CT to monitor fungal burden and host responses in Galleria mellonella and neutropenic mouse models of mucormycosis. The approach enables real-time, noninvasive assessment of infection dynamics and pathology, overcoming limitations of endpoint CFU-based methods and establishing a platform for antifungal and pathogenesis research.

title: Phase field modelling of fracturing in frozen foods.
summary: This computational study applies the fracture phase field method to simulate freezing-induced cracking in par-fried French fries, treating fries as a composite of a starch matrix with ice inclusions and coupling heat transfer, ice formation, and elastic-brittle mechanics. Simulations predict microdamage localized at the crust–core interface and reproduce experimental trends with freezing temperature and crust thickness; macroscopic cracking only appears under unrealistically low ice fracture energies, supporting the method’s suitability for investigating fracture in frozen foods.

title: APOE deficiency inhibits amyloid-facilitated (A) tau pathology (T) and neurodegeneration (N), halting progressive ATN pathology in a preclinical model.
summary: Using a robust mouse model that combines amyloid (5xFAD) and tau (TauP301S) pathologies (ATN), the authors show that APOE deficiency markedly suppresses amyloid-facilitated tau pathology and downstream neurodegeneration despite high Aβ burden. Mechanistically, APOE loss reduces dense-core plaque formation and prevents microglial transition from homeostatic to reactive/DAM states, and microglial depletion lowers amyloid-driven tau only in the presence of APOE.

title: Mass Spectrometry Imaging.
summary: The study performed high-resolution proteomic profiling of human iPSC-derived spinal motor neurons carrying ALS mutations (C9ORF72, FUS, TDP-43), revealing mutation-specific and shared dysregulated pathways. Treatment with mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (MSC-EVs) broadly normalized many ALS-associated proteomic changes, supporting MSC-EVs as a potential therapeutic strategy.

title: The genome sequence of an ichneumonid wasp, Polytribax perspicillator (Gravenhorst, 1807).
summary: This data note reports a high-quality, chromosome-level genome assembly of the ichneumonid wasp Polytribax perspicillator generated with PacBio HiFi long reads and Hi-C scaffolding. The 314.21 Mb assembly is scaffolded into eight chromosomal pseudomolecules with a BUSCO completeness of 96.0% and includes a 25.68 kb mitochondrial genome; all data are openly available.

title: Proteomics of post mortem brains in early- and late-onset Alzheimer's disease: Unraveling differential Aβ effects and potential AD biomarkers.
summary: This study analyzed proteomes from 115 post mortem human temporal lobe samples using DIA mass spectrometry with a custom spectral library containing tau PTMs and Aβ isoforms, revealing downregulated mitochondrial/synaptic pathways and upregulated immune/metabolic processes, with larger effect sizes in early-onset AD (EOAD) versus late-onset AD (LOAD). It identified multiphosphorylated tau peptides (p-tau231/p-tau235 and p-tau231/p-tau235/p-tau237) as candidate biomarkers and detected Aβ in 45% of cognitively unimpaired elderly controls, accompanied by subtle AD-like proteomic signatures.

title: Tissue microenvironment dictates the state of human iPSC-derived endothelial cells of distinct developmental origin in 3D cardiac microtissues.
summary: The study shows that human iPSC-derived endothelial cells (ECs) from distinct developmental origins (cardiac mesoderm vs. paraxial mesoderm) acquire a similar intramyocardial, heart-specific identity when incorporated into 3D cardiac microtissues with cardiomyocytes and cardiac fibroblasts. While early EC gene expression reflects lineage origin, the cardiac microenvironment largely reprograms EC identity, demonstrating EC plasticity driven by tissue context rather than origin alone.

title: Pro-inflammatory response of human iPSC-derived intestinal epithelial monolayers towards microbial toxins LPS and nigericin.
summary: This study compared inflammatory responses of human iPSC-derived intestinal epithelial monolayers and differentiated Caco-2 monolayers to lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and nigericin. iPSC-derived IECs showed significant barrier disruption and robust IL-6, IL-8, and TNF-α induction, whereas Caco-2 cells showed minimal responses, indicating iPSC-derived IECs better emulate pro-inflammatory epithelial reactions in vitro.

title: Human platelet lysate standardization across three independent European blood establishments.
summary: This study standardized the manufacture of human platelet lysate (hPL) across three European blood establishments using a single-step, closed-system production set and compared national versus pooled international batches for biochemical composition and bioactivity. All hPL batches showed comparable quality metrics and supported HUVEC and MSC functions, with lower variability in pooled international batches, demonstrating feasibility of cross-border standardization.

title: Data on the cytotoxicity of surfactants used to increase the dispersion of micro- and nanoplastics.
summary: This Data in Brief article reports cytotoxicity profiles of five surfactants used to disperse micro- and nanoplastics—four synthetic (Triton X-100, Tween 80, sodium cholic acid, sodium hexametaphosphate) and one biosurfactant (DPPC)—on human BEAS-2B and Caco-2 cell lines using MTT, NR, and SRB assays. Synthetic surfactants caused dose-dependent decreases in cell viability (with Triton X-100 and Tween 80 most potent), whereas DPPC did not show dose-dependent toxicity, underscoring the need for dedicated surfactant controls in micro/nanoplastic toxicity studies.

title: Studies of post-partum placentas provide insights into the origin of structural chromosomal aberrations.
summary: This retrospective diagnostic study analyzed enzymatically separated cytotrophoblast and mesenchymal core from post-partum placentas to explain discrepancies between NIPT-detected structural chromosomal aberrations and fetal results. In 58% of 31 cases, the placental chorionic villi confirmed the NIPT structural aberration, and among these, 39% showed complex foeto-placental mosaicism, demonstrating that complex chromosomal rearrangements can persist into the mature placenta and sometimes the fetus.

title: Secretome Analysis of Human and Rat Pancreatic Islets Co-Cultured with Adipose-Derived Stromal Cells Reveals a Signature with Enhanced Regenerative Capacities.
summary: The study profiled the secretomes of human and rat pancreatic islets cultured alone or co-cultured with adipose-derived stromal cells (ASCs) under transplantation-relevant stressors (normoxia, cytokines, high glucose, hypoxia, and hypoxia+high glucose) using discovery proteomics and functional assays. Co-culture with ASCs remodeled the secretome toward pathways supporting energy metabolism, extracellular matrix organization, angiogenesis, and immune modulation, with condition-dependent increases in factors such as VEGF, PDGF, bFGF, collagen Iα1, IL-1α, and IL-10 that translated into enhanced angiogenesis, collagen deposition, and attenuation of alloimmunity in vitro.

title: Novel GelMA/GelMA-AEMA Hydrogel Blend with Enhanced Printability as a Carrier for iPSC-Derived Chondrocytes In Vitro.
summary: This study develops a GelMA/GelMA-AEMA hydrogel blend that exhibits enhanced flowability, yield-stress behavior, and strong shear-thinning for extrusion-based bioprinting while maintaining or improving biological performance with iPSC-derived chondrocytes. The blend prints smoother filaments than GelMA, supports robust cartilage matrix deposition, yields higher COL2A1/COL1A1 ratios, and achieves greater construct stiffness during culture, highlighting rheology-driven improvements in bioink design.

title: Detection of hepatitis B virus mRNA from single cell RNA sequencing data without prior knowledge.
summary: The study demonstrates that viral reads, specifically hepatitis B virus (HBV) mRNA, can be detected directly from single-cell RNA-seq data without prior viral reference inclusion or targeted amplification by leveraging PathSeq on unmapped reads. Applied to human liver scRNA-seq from chronic HBV patients, HBV transcripts were primarily found in hepatocytes and to a lesser extent in Kupffer cells in viraemic individuals, while functionally cured patients showed no detectable HBV mRNA.

title: Cellular Heterogeneity During Arterial Aging.
summary: This review synthesizes single-cell and spatial transcriptomic studies to map cellular heterogeneity and intercellular communication changes across the arterial wall during aging, highlighting recurrent programs of endothelial dysfunction, smooth muscle phenotypic modulation, fibroblast-driven extracellular matrix remodeling, immune activation, and senescence. It emphasizes limitations (inconsistent annotations, limited spatial/epigenetic resolution, and scarce functional validation) and recommends cross-species integration with spatial and epigenomic profiling to improve mechanistic insight and translational relevance.

title: Proteomics and tracer metabolomics link GAPDH ISGylation to glycolytic control.
summary: Using proteomics and 13C-glucose tracer metabolomics in human cell lines, the authors show that ISGylation extensively targets metabolic enzymes and suppresses glycolysis by creating a bottleneck at GAPDH. They validate that multisite ISGylation of GAPDH reduces its catalytic activity without disrupting tetramer assembly, positioning GAPDH as a central metabolic checkpoint for ISG15-mediated control of energy metabolism.

title: A dynamic gene regulatory code drives synaptic development of hippocampal granule cells.
crm_level_3: VIB Center for Brain & Disease Research
summary: This study reconstructs dynamic gene regulatory networks that drive the postnatal synaptic development of mouse hippocampal dentate gyrus granule cells by integrating single-cell transcriptomics, single-nucleus multiome, and ribosome-tagging datasets. Functional perturbations identify Bcl6 as a promoter of dendritic spine maturation and mossy fiber bouton refinement and Smad3 as a modulator of inhibitory synaptic transmission, and reveal a sequential program in which early repressor TFs delay activation of late synaptogenic networks.

title: Design, Synthesis, and Antibacterial Evaluation of Rifampicin-Siderophore Conjugates.
summary: The study designs and synthesizes rifampicin–siderophore conjugates to overcome Gram-negative outer-membrane permeability, discovering that an ester-linked chlorocatechol conjugate (compound 33) markedly enhances activity—up to 32-fold—against several Gram-negative pathogens. Structure–activity analysis shows triazole click linkers diminish activity, while short ester linkers and chlorocatechol moieties improve potency, with iron dependence and enterobactin competition indicating uptake via siderophore transport pathways.

title: Single cell transcriptomics of human kidney organoid endothelium reveals vessel growth processes and arterial maturation upon transplantation.
summary: The study profiles ~12,000 human endothelial cells from hiPSC-derived kidney organoids, showing that transplantation into chicken embryos preserves endothelium, drives angiogenic proliferation, and induces a vein-to-artery phenotypic shift with a fetal arterial/afferent arteriolar-like transcriptome. Transcriptional programs indicate hypoxia-driven glycolysis and laminar shear stress/Notch signaling with SOX7 upregulation as candidate drivers of arterial maturation upon perfusion.

title: The Dissemination of Rift Valley Fever Virus to the Eye and Sensory Neurons of Zebrafish Larvae Is Stat1-Dependent.
summary: This study establishes a zebrafish larva model for Rift Valley fever virus (RVFV) showing robust replication and in vivo imaging-based tropism to liver and sensory neurons (optic tectum and retina), while implicating Stat1 signaling in restricting viral dissemination. Pharmacologic JAK inhibition (ruxolitinib) or stat1a knockout markedly increased viral loads and vascular spread but eliminated dissemination to sensory neurons, and a nucleoside analog (2′-fluoro-2′-deoxycytidine) suppressed replication.

title: Astrocytes contribute to olanzapine-mediated reversal of kleefstra syndrome-associated neurodevelopmental regression.
summary: In an international cohort of 54 individuals with Kleefstra syndrome (EHMT1 haploinsufficiency), developmental regression during adolescence/young adulthood was common and 10 of 16 treated cases showed functional improvement with olanzapine. Preclinical iPSC-derived human neuron–astrocyte cocultures and Ehmt1+/– mouse tissues revealed astrocyte-driven network hyperactivity linked to elevated S100B; both olanzapine and S100B inhibition/knockdown normalized astrocytic Ca2+ responses and neuronal hyperactivity, implicating astrocytes and S100B as therapeutic targets.

title: Ancient and Recent Riverine Gene Flow Contributed to the Adaptive Radiation of Sailfin Silversides in Wallace's Dreampond.
summary: The study assembled a chromosome-scale reference genome for the riverine sailfin silverside Telmatherina bonti and generated whole-genome sequences for all Lake Matano Telmatherina species to resolve phylogenetic relationships and detect gene flow. Results show two monophyletic clades (roundfins and sharpfins) with mito-nuclear discordance and both ancient and ongoing introgression between riverine T. bonti and lacustrine sharpfins, including a detected recent hybrid and a spatial decline in allele sharing away from the river–lake interface.

title: Piezoelectric truss metamaterials: data-driven design and additive manufacturing.
summary: The authors introduce a generative machine learning framework to inverse-design piezoelectric truss metamaterials that exhibit customizable and unconventional anisotropic electromechanical responses, and they fabricate these designs via an in-gel direct-ink-writing (DIW) process using a PEGDA-based, lead-free piezo-ceramic composite. They demonstrate auxetic, unidirectional, and omnidirectional behaviors, report a >48% gain in specific hydrostatic piezoelectric coefficient over bulk PZT, and validate frequency-sensitive electromechanical performance in 3D-printed octet lattices.

title: A robust expression system reveals distinct gating mechanisms and calmodulin regulation of NaV1.9 channels.
summary: The study establishes a robust transient heterologous expression protocol that yields strong mouse NaV1.9 currents, enabling direct electrophysiological comparison with native mouse dorsal root ganglion neurons, and uses NaV1.9–NaV1.5 chimeras to uncover C‑tail regions controlling expression and gating. It shows calmodulin binds the NaV1.9 C‑tail with unusually weak affinity and identifies the pre‑IQ region as a key determinant of NaV1.9’s depolarized inactivation, while applying the system to known gain‑of‑function mutations that recapitulate disease phenotypes.

title: Metaproteomics in the One Health framework for unraveling microbial effectors in microbiomes.
summary: This opinion article outlines how metaproteomics can uncover microbial effectors (e.g., virulence factors, toxins, AMPs/NRPs, and phages) within the One Health framework linking human, animal, and environmental microbiomes. It reviews current workflows, analytical advances, and bioinformatics, highlights challenges in detecting low-abundance or non-canonical peptides, and proposes multi-omics and model systems to translate findings into clinical, agricultural, environmental, and biotechnological applications.

title: Highly potent antiviral drug candidates targeting SARS-CoV-2 nsp3 and nsp5.
summary: The study used structure-based virtual screening, click-chemistry fragment growth, and molecular dynamics to identify two small-molecule inhibitors of SARS‑CoV‑2 proteases nsp3 (Amb929) and nsp5 (Amb701). Amb929 showed strong antiviral efficacy with low cytotoxicity in Vero E6 cells and human airway epithelium cultures, outperforming Amb701, which exhibited moderate toxicity.

title: A new human in vitro model of cytotypic and testosterone-producing organoids derived from testicular tissue of transgender women.
summary: This study demonstrates that testicular tissue from transgender women can be used to generate human testicular organoids with bicompartmental architecture that produce testosterone over extended culture and respond to gonadotrophic stimulation, with transcriptomic profiles resembling prepubertal/pubertal testis. Success of organoid formation correlated with longer duration of gender-affirming hormone therapy, higher AMH expression in donor tubules, and lower peritubular myoid cell proportions, positioning trans tissue as an abundant, ethical source for human testis models in reproductive research and toxicology.

title: Enhanced Human Antigen-Specific B Cell Responses Using In Vitro 3D Tonsil Cultures Containing Stromal Cells.
crm_level_1: Amsterdam Institute for Immunology and Infectious Diseases
summary: This study develops a human 3D in vitro tonsil model that incorporates fibroblastic reticular cells (FRCs) within a synthetic PEG-4MAL hydrogel to better mimic germinal center-like environments and improve antigen-specific B cell responses compared to 2D cultures. The 3D FRC-supported system enhanced B and T cell survival, promoted follicle-like organization, increased antigen-specific B cells and antibody-secreting cells, reduced bystander activation, and worked similarly with autologous or allogeneic FRCs, supporting its use for mechanistic studies and vaccine/adjuvant screening.

title: Dysfunctional CD4 T cells in an oncovirus-specific TCR-transgenic in vivo model.
summary: This study introduces MolT-II, a TCR-transgenic mouse whose CD4 T cells specific for a Moloney MuLV class II epitope are intrinsically dysfunctional due to cross-reactivity with an endogenous AKV retroviral epitope, exhibiting reduced proliferation, cytokine production, and elevated inhibitory receptors. Antigen-specific vaccination combined with PD-L1, LAG-3, and CTLA-4 blockade restores CD4 T-cell function and enhances tumor control in vivo.

title: Targeting replication stress in neuroblastoma by exploiting the synergistic potential of second generation RRM2 and CHK1 inhibitors.
summary: This study shows that TAS1553, a small-molecule inhibitor that disrupts the RRM1–RRM2 interaction in ribonucleotide reductase, induces replication stress, DNA damage, and apoptosis in neuroblastoma and synergizes strongly with CHK1 inhibitors (prexasertib and the selective CHK1 inhibitor SRA737) in cell lines, tumoroids, sarcoma lines, and a zebrafish xenograft model. Transcriptomic profiling reveals induction of p53 and inflammatory pathways, suppression of MYC/MYCN and G2/M programs, and a selective downregulation of RNA splicing components, supporting TAS1553 as a next-generation RRM2 inhibitor for combination therapy.

title: Increased TMEM106B levels lead to lysosomal dysfunction which affects synaptic signaling and neuronal health.
summary: This study generated the first transgenic mouse model that stably overexpresses human TMEM106B, causing 4–8× increases in protein levels, and demonstrated lysosomal dysfunction, age-related downregulation of immediate early genes, altered hippocampal synaptic signaling, anxiety-like behavior at 12 months, and mild hippocampal neuronal loss by 21 months. The findings suggest that elevated TMEM106B impairs lysosomal and synaptic function, thereby reducing brain resilience during aging and increasing vulnerability to neurodegenerative mechanisms.

title: Loss of endothelial ZEB2 in mice attenuates steatosis early during metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
summary: This study shows that endothelial loss of ZEB2 in mice amplifies western-diet–induced capillarization and lipid-metabolism programs in liver sinusoidal endothelial cells (LSECs), enhances PPARα pathway activation, and ultimately reduces steatosis, liver injury, and hypo-vascularization during early MASLD. The findings reveal a context-dependent role for ZEB2 in liver disease, being disease-promoting in early steatosis while previously shown protective in fibrosis, partly via altered LSEC-LSEC communication.

title: Cell-based sialoglycan arrays for directly comparing influenza A virus receptor requirements for binding and infection.
summary: This study builds a HEK293 cell-based sialoglycan array by CRISPR/Cas9 glycoengineering and transient reconstitution of specific sialyltransferases, enabling direct, side‑by‑side comparison of influenza A virus receptor binding and productive infection across N-glycans, O-glycans, and glycosphingolipids. The authors show that all three glycoconjugate classes can independently support infection, and that H3N2 receptor use evolved over decades—shifting toward α2-6 sialic acid on multiple carriers with a later partial regain of α2-3 use—while revealing only a moderate correlation between binding and infection, implying post-attachment receptor requirements for entry.

title: Candida albicans Hxk1 influences expression of metabolic- and virulence-related genes
summary: This study shows that the N-acetylglucosamine kinase Hxk1 in Candida albicans broadly and indirectly modulates metabolic and virulence gene expression in a carbon source-dependent manner, as revealed by RNA-Seq and supported by CUT&RUN indicating Hxk1 does not directly bind promoters of differentially expressed genes. Deletion of HXK1 alters sterol intermediates and increases fluconazole susceptibility, elevates tolerance to oxidative stress via SOD4/5 upregulation, and increases toxicity toward gut epithelial cells, underscoring Hxk1’s multifaceted roles beyond GlcNAc phosphorylation.

title: Protocol to annotate dendritic cell maturation types in vivo making use of lipid nanoparticle-based approaches.
summary: This protocol describes how to steer and classify dendritic cell maturation along a homeostatic versus immunogenic spectrum in vivo using lipid nanoparticles, combining flow-cytometry marker panels with transcriptional profiling and an accompanying web tool. It details LNP formulation/characterization, in vivo delivery routes, uptake tracking, tissue processing, and DC phenotyping in mice, enabling standardized assessment of LNP immunogenicity and DC maturation states across tissues and conditions.

title: RIPK1 ablation in T cells results in spontaneous enteropathy and TNF-driven villus atrophy.
summary: The study shows that deleting RIPK1 in conventional αβ T cells (Ripk1ΔCD4) causes spontaneous small-intestinal pathology in mice, including duodenal villus atrophy, crypt hyperplasia, and small-intestinal elongation, driven by a T-cell imbalance with expansion of TNF-producing γδ T cells. Antibiotics reversed microbiome-dependent elongation and crypt hyperplasia but not villus atrophy, which was rescued by Tnfr1 deletion, while combined T cell–specific ablation of Ripk1 and Casp8 fully normalized pathology, demonstrating that RIPK1-mediated protection from caspase-8-dependent apoptosis in αβ T cells is essential for proximal small-intestinal homeostasis.

title: Citrullination and Deamidation in Type 1 Diabetes: Linking Beta Cell Stress to Neoantigen-Driven Autoimmunity.
summary: This review synthesizes evidence that beta-cell stress in type 1 diabetes activates calcium-dependent PAD (citrullination) and TGM2 (deamidation), generating neoepitopes that bind disease-risk HLA and are targeted by autoreactive T cells, thereby amplifying autoimmunity. It emphasizes distinct temporal regulation (PAD2 early, TGM2 later), incomplete central tolerance to PTM epitopes, and therapeutic opportunities in inhibiting these modifying enzymes.

title: Precision genome editing using combinatorial viral vector delivery of CRISPR-Cas9 nucleases and donor DNA constructs.
summary: The study presents a dual viral-vector genome editing platform that delivers high-specificity CRISPR-Cas9 via high-capacity adenoviral particles (AdVPs) and donor DNA via AAVs, enabling selection-free, precise knock-ins at safe-harbor and endogenous loci in human cells at up to ~90%+ frequencies. It shows that programmable nuclease-induced double-strand breaks enhance AAV transduction, self-complementary AAV does not necessarily outperform HR donors for precision, and high-fidelity Cas9 is critical to avoid off-target capture of defective AAV genomes.

title: Pharmacological HIF activation protects against diet-induced obesity, glucose intolerance, and skeletal dysfunction by exerting dual beneficial effects on energy metabolism and bone.
summary: In mice, systemic activation of hypoxia signaling with the HIF–prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor FG-4592 (Roxadustat) prevented high-fat diet–induced obesity, glucose intolerance, marrow adiposity, and skeletal vascular decline, while increasing energy expenditure and improving bone formation and fracture healing. Short- and long-term dosing stabilized HIF-1α in vitro and in vivo, preserved bone vasculature, normalized VEGF expression, and enhanced callus vascularization, culminating in improved metabolically compromised fracture repair.

title: Early Taurine Administration Decreases the Levels of Receptor-Interacting Serine/Threonine Protein Kinase 1 in the Duchenne Mouse Model mdx.
summary: This study tested early taurine supplementation (~4.6 g/kg from postnatal day 7 to 5.5 weeks) in the mdx mouse model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy and found a selective reduction of RIP1 protein levels in skeletal muscle, with no significant changes in RIP3 or autophagy markers (LC3 II/SQSTM1). Immunofluorescence showed diminished heterogeneous RIP1 staining in muscle fibers and fewer LC3 II–positive macrophages, supporting a taurine-associated dampening of necroptotic signaling without enhancing autophagy or mitophagy under these conditions.

title: Automated microinjection for zebrafish xenograft models.
summary: This study presents a machine-learning–guided automated microinjection robot that performs vascular, perivitelline space, and hindbrain ventricle injections in 2 dpf zebrafish larvae, achieving ~60% injection success and >70% survival—comparable to manual methods—while doubling throughput in fully automated mode. The system was validated across multiple labs using dyes, microspheres, TILs, human cancer cell lines, and patient-derived samples, demonstrating reproducibility, speed, and reduced operator training needs for zebrafish xenograft workflows.

title: Subcellular glycan-mannose receptor binding kinetics correlate with myeloid cell function.
summary: The study introduces Glyco-PAINT-APP, an automated single-molecule imaging and analysis pipeline that quantifies subcellular glycan–lectin binding kinetics on live primary myeloid cells and correlates these kinetics to functional outcomes. Using dendritic cells and macrophages, the authors show that mannose receptor (MR) binding heterogeneity predicts uptake and cross-presentation, with high on-membrane mobility inversely correlating with uptake and longer dwell-times positively correlating with cross-presentation, and they map MR-dependent binding changes during macrophage polarization.

title: Cameroonian blackflies (Diptera: Simuliidae) harbour a plethora of RNA viruses.
summary: The study performed viral particle-based metagenomic sequencing on 55 pools of adult blackflies collected in an onchocerciasis-endemic area of Cameroon and found over a thousand viral contigs, with a dominance of novel RNA viruses spanning many families, including some associated with human disease, but no close relatives of known neurotropic viruses. Phylogenetic and dinucleotide analyses suggested the detected flavivirus and rhabdoviruses are insect-specific, underscoring extensive blackfly virome diversity and the value of incorporating blackflies into zoonotic surveillance.

title: Forces in mechanically interlocked materials.
summary: This review surveys how mechanically interlocked molecules (rotaxanes, catenanes, knots) and their polymers respond to force, highlighting single-molecule force spectroscopy insights (forces, work, dynamics) and how topology governs mechanochemical reactivity. It further examines polymer mechanochemistry and mechanically interlocked polymer networks (slide-ring materials), detailing their pulley effect, viscoelastic behavior, force-sensing/actuation applications, and key challenges and outlook.

title: Statescope: an integrative deconvolution framework for discovering cell states in tumors.
summary: Statescope is a Bayesian multi-omic deconvolution framework that integrates DNA-derived malignant cell purity and models inter-sample variability to accurately infer cell fractions, cell type–specific gene expression, and discover cell states from bulk RNA-seq. It outperforms existing methods in benchmarks and, in applications to NSCLC and PDAC cohorts, identifies biologically and clinically relevant states, including signatures predictive of immunotherapy benefit in POPLAR/OAK trials.

title: Mapping functional non-coding variation in individual human genomes through haplotyping, multiomics, and deep learning.
summary: This study integrates whole-chromosome haplotyping (linked-reads + Hi-C), allele-specific ATAC-seq and TT-seq, and deep learning (ChromBPNet) to map functional non-coding variants in individual human lymphoblastoid genomes. It identifies hundreds of allele-specific regulatory events, links them to genes, validates motif disruptions driving TF binding differences, and discovers a rare OCT2 motif–disrupting variant that modulates PIK3R5 expression, demonstrating a generalizable framework for interpreting non-coding variation in personal genomes.

title: Murine vascular organoids are responsive and adaptable 3D systems with cellular heterogeneity and dynamic plasticity.
summary: The study establishes a robust protocol to generate murine blood vascular organoids (mBVOs) from embryonic stem cells, validates their structural and functional maturation in vitro and in vivo, and maps extensive endothelial, mesenchymal, and macrophage heterogeneity and plasticity by single-cell RNA sequencing. mBVOs respond to inflammatory cues and VEGF blockade and can be fused with glioblastoma spheroids to recapitulate distinct tumor–vessel interaction modes, underscoring their utility as adaptable vascular biology platforms.

title: Dietary Carrageenan Amplifies the Inflammatory Profile, but not Permeability, of Intestinal Epithelial Cells from Patients With Crohn's Disease.
summary: This study tested the effects of dietary carrageenan on epithelial permeability and inflammatory responses using Caco-2/HT29-MTX cocultures and organoid-derived monolayers from Crohn’s disease patients. Carrageenan did not alter permeability (TEER) but increased inflammatory gene expression and cytokine release, especially under pre-existing inflammatory conditions.

title: Profiling the Cellular Surfaceome by Furan-Based Protein Biotinylation.
summary: The study presents a furan-based, oxidation-activated biotinylation strategy (furan-biotin, FB1–FB6) to profile the cellular surfaceome with high specificity, demonstrating that FB1 most effectively labels and enriches plasma membrane proteins while reducing intracellular background compared to NHS-biotin. Using pull-downs and LC–MS/MS (DDA and DIA), the method captured extensive surfaceomes and distinguished between MCF-7 and MCF-10A cell lines, highlighting cancer-relevant receptor tyrosine kinases and adhesion networks.

title: A Tissue Section-Based Mid-Infrared Spectroscopical Analysis of Salivary Gland Tumors Based on Enzymatic Deglycosylation.
summary: This study evaluated attenuated total reflectance–Fourier transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy combined with enzymatic deglycosylation to classify salivary gland tumors (SGTs) using 155 human tissue sections, achieving 81.9% accuracy for tumor versus control discrimination but limited performance for benign versus malignant separation. Enzymatic removal of terminal sialic acid and fucose residues caused detectable mid-infrared spectral changes in glycan-associated regions, confirming glycosylation’s contribution to tumor-specific signatures.

title: Multiplexed bacteriocin synthesis to combat and prevent antimicrobial resistance.
summary: The study demonstrates rapid, multiplexed cell-free synthesis of bacteriocin cocktails, rationally combining peptides that use distinct envelope-entry pathways to enhance killing, broaden spectrum, and prevent resistance in Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria. Using optimized DNA devices, continuous-exchange cell-free expression, and disulfide-bond supplements, the authors produced potent cocktails verified by activity assays and proteomics, and showed in vivo efficacy in Galleria mellonella against multidrug-resistant E. coli isolates.

title: TIMS2Rescore: A Data Dependent Acquisition-Parallel Accumulation and Serial Fragmentation-Optimized Data-Driven Rescoring Pipeline Based on MS2Rescore.
summary: The study introduces TIMS2Rescore, a data-driven rescoring pipeline optimized for DDA-PASEF timsTOF data that integrates new timsTOF-specific MS2PIP spectrum prediction models and IM2Deep, a deep-learning predictor of peptide collisional cross section. By directly ingesting Bruker raw files and outputs from multiple search engines, the workflow significantly increases peptide and protein identifications across plasma proteomics, immunopeptidomics (HLA-I/II), and metaproteomics datasets while maintaining robust FDR control.

title: Is the time right for transplanting immature testicular tissue or cells to restore male fertility? Expert perspectives on clinical implementation of autotransplantation of cryopreserved testicular tissue or cells for fertility restoration.
summary: This expert opinion paper outlines the current status, opportunities, and challenges for clinical implementation of autotransplantation of cryopreserved immature testicular tissue (ITTT) and spermatogonial stem cell transplantation (SSCT) to restore fertility in male survivors of gonadotoxic therapies. It emphasizes patient selection, rigorous pre-transplant safety assessments (including malignancy risk), standardized preparation and transplant procedures, and long-term follow-up, while highlighting unresolved issues such as timing, safety, and efficacy that require coordinated international research and data sharing.

title: Extracellular Vesicles From Schistosoma mansoni Adult Worms Stimulate IL-10 Release by B Cells.
summary: The study shows that excretory/secretory (ES) products from Schistosoma mansoni adult worms, enriched in extracellular vesicles (EVs), induce IL-10 production by mouse splenic and human peripheral blood B cells. Proteomics of IL-10–inducing ES fractions revealed an enrichment of EV-associated proteins, and highly purified adult worm EVs interacted with B cells and were sufficient to stimulate IL-10 release, especially with CD40 co-stimulation.

title: Micro-computed tomography to visualize preserved vascular architecture in decellularized human vaginal tissue: explorative study.
summary: This study used contrast-enhanced micro-computed tomography to compare the 3D vascular architecture of native human vaginal wall tissue with chemically decellularized vaginal matrices from the same donors. Vascular density was preserved after decellularization, while connectivity decreased and average vessel thickness and length increased, indicating loss of small capillaries but preservation of larger vascular structures, supporting the matrix’s potential for recellularization and graft integration.

title: Synaptic deregulation of cholinergic projection neurons causes olfactory dysfunction across five fly Parkinsonism models.
crm_level_3: VIB-KU Leuven Center for Brain and Disease Research
summary: Across five knock-in Drosophila Parkinsonism models, single-cell RNA-seq revealed early, convergent synaptic deregulation in cholinergic olfactory projection neurons (OPNs), leading to hyposmia before dopaminergic motor defects; similar synaptic gene changes were observed in cholinergic neuron–rich regions from human PD brains. Restoring cholinergic function in fly OPNs or enhancing cholinergic signaling (e.g., nicotine) rescued later dopaminergic dysfunction in flies and improved activity deficits in LRRK2G2019S human iPSC-derived dopaminergic neurons.

title: RIM and MUNC13 membrane-binding domains are essential for neuropeptide secretion.
summary: In mouse primary neurons, MUNC13 is essential for dense-core vesicle neuropeptide secretion, while RIM’s N terminus maintains MUNC13 by preventing its proteasomal degradation; proteasome inhibition partially rescues secretion in RIM-deficient neurons. Unlike synaptic vesicle release, RIM C2B and MUNC13 C1–C2B membrane-binding domains are functionally redundant for DCV exocytosis, whereas the MUNC13 C2C lipid-binding domain is indispensable, revealing distinct mechanisms between SV and DCV exocytosis.

title: Networks in Aquatic Communities Collapse Upon Neonicotinoid-Induced Stress.
summary: Using 36 outdoor freshwater ditch mesocosms exposed to field-realistic thiacloprid pulses, the authors show that aquatic invertebrate co‑occurrence networks lose coherence and become indistinguishable from random assemblages as insecticide concentration increases. This network collapse coincides with sharp declines in ecosystem functioning, including reduced organic matter consumption and shifts in primary production, despite little change in local taxon richness.

title: Macronutrient-Based Predictive Modelling of Bioconversion Efficiency in Black Soldier Fly Larvae (Hermetia illucens) Through Artificial Substrates.
crm_level_1: Thomas More University of Applied Sciences
summary: The study optimized hydration and macronutrient composition of artificial substrates for rearing black soldier fly larvae and developed a response-surface model showing significant main, interaction, and quadratic effects of protein, fat, and carbohydrates on bioconversion efficiency. Validation with real side-stream mixtures confirmed predictive trends when accounting for protein source digestibility (e.g., feather meal), providing a practical tool to blend diverse organic wastes for improved larval performance.

title: Multiomics immune profiling of a patient-relevant orthotopic lung cancer model using SEPARATE-Seq.
crm_level_3: Dendritic Cell Biology and Cancer Immunotherapy
summary: This study introduces an orthotopic, dissectible mouse lung adenocarcinoma model (ORTHO) and a new single-cell method, SEPARATE-Seq, that partitions vascular versus intratissue immune cells, combined with spatial transcriptomics to map immune niches. The model mirrors key LUAD immune features (NK dysfunction, NAN/TAN neutrophil dichotomy, a lipid TAM ring at the tumor edge, and interferon-stimulated gene hubs) and shows clinically relevant responses to cisplatin plus anti–PD‑1.

title: Sperm cell empowerment: X-ray-guided magnetic fields for enhanced actuation and localization of cytocompatible biohybrid microrobots.
summary: The study demonstrates X-ray-guided magnetic actuation and localization of biohybrid microrobots made from clusters of iron oxide nanoparticle-coated bovine sperm cells, enabling real-time control and imaging in a human-scale reproductive tract phantom. It evaluates trade-offs among magnetic content, detectability, actuation performance, and cytocompatibility, showing effective imaging (X-ray fluoroscopy and ultrasound), robust magnetic response, and minimal cytotoxicity across nanoparticle concentrations of 1–3 mg/mL.

title: Combined Deletion of ZFP36L1 and ZFP36L2 Drives Superior Cytokine Production in T Cells at the Cost of Cell Fitness.
summary: In murine CD8+ T cells, combined deletion of the RNA-binding proteins ZFP36L1 and ZFP36L2 dramatically unleashes and prolongs TNF and IFNγ production during continuous stimulation but compromises cell fitness via altered IL-7/STAT5 signaling, increased apoptosis, and dysregulated cell-cycle progression. Despite heightened cytokine output in tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, double-deficient T cells fail to control tumor growth, indicating built-in safeguards that limit super-cytokine producers by impairing survival and proliferation.

title: Immunopeptidomics of cutaneous leishmaniasis patients reveals the natural antigenic landscape.
summary: This study profiled the naturally presented Leishmania aethiopica immunopeptidome directly from skin lesion biopsies of 27 Ethiopian cutaneous leishmaniasis patients and from in vitro infected THP-1 macrophages, identifying 333 MHC-I and 247 MHC-II epitopes from 398 parasite proteins with several shared, epitope-rich antigens (e.g., EF-2, Hsp70, Histone H2A). It further showed that widely used MHC-binding prediction tools missed 20–70% of experimentally observed epitopes, underscoring the value of mass spectrometry-based immunopeptidomics for vaccine antigen discovery.

title: Revisiting endothelial tropism of SARS-CoV-2 using a cell-specific hACE2 mouse model
summary: The authors generated a transgenic mouse model with endothelial-specific hACE2 expression (Cdh5-hACE2) to test whether endothelial-restricted SARS-CoV-2 entry alone causes disease and compared it to Krt18-hACE2 mice. Despite confirmed endothelial hACE2 and spike binding, Cdh5-hACE2 mice showed no clinical illness, viral replication, immune infiltration, or pathology in lung or brain after intratracheal or intravenous infection, indicating endothelial tropism alone is insufficient for productive infection and disease in vivo.

title: Preclinical assessment of splicing modulation therapy for ABCA4 variant c.768G>T in Stargardt disease.
summary: The study develops and preclinically evaluates antisense oligonucleotides to correct the ABCA4 c.768G>T splicing defect underlying Stargardt disease, identifying a lead 2'-O-methoxyethyl phosphorothioate AON (A7 21-mer) that restores approximately 50% of wild-type ABCA4 RNA and protein in patient-derived photoreceptor precursor cells and retinal organoids. Distribution, stability, off-targets, immunostimulation, and toxicity assessments in vitro and in mice showed favorable profiles, supporting further in vivo development.

title: A specific blend of prebiotics and postbiotics improved the gut microbiome of dogs with soft stools in the in vitro Simulator of the Canine Intestinal Microbial Ecosystem.
summary: Using the Simulator of the Canine Intestinal Microbial Ecosystem (SCIME), the authors tested a prebiotic/postbiotic blend (baobab fruit pulp, acacia gum, heat-killed Lactobacillus helveticus HA-122, and yeast fractions) on fecal microbiota from dogs with soft stools in proximal and distal colon reactors. Repeated dosing increased saccharolytic activity and beneficial taxa (e.g., Bifidobacterium, Prevotella), decreased Proteobacteria, and led to donor-dependent increases in short-chain fatty acids, indicating positive modulation of dysbiotic canine microbiomes in vitro.

title: Population-based, first-tier genomic newborn screening in the maternity ward.
summary: The BabyDetect pilot implemented first-tier genomic newborn screening using targeted next-generation sequencing of 405 genes for 165 treatable pediatric disorders in a Belgian maternity ward, enrolling 3,847 newborns with over 90% acceptance. In 18 months, 71 positive cases were identified (30 not detected by conventional screening), demonstrating feasibility and highlighting the need to integrate genomic with biochemical NBS while addressing challenges in variant interpretation, reporting, and confirmatory workflows.

title: Beyond one-size-fits-all: cancer biology shapes nanoparticle behavior.
summary: The study compares a single nanoparticle formulation (gold@mesoporous-silica with and without PEI) across four human cancer spheroid models (A549, KM12C, MCF7, HeLa) and finds an inverse relationship between cellular uptake and penetration depth: tumors with slower uptake allow deeper diffusion. Quantitative proteomics links these differences to tumor-specific expression of endocytic and ECM proteins, and removing PEI lowers uptake while enhancing penetration, arguing for tumor-tailored nanomedicine design.

title: Internal gene segments from a mouse-adapted influenza B virus confer increased pathogenicity to mice.
summary: The study generated a mouse-adapted influenza B virus by serially passaging a 2:6 reassortant (HA/NA from B/Washington/02/2019 on a B/Memphis/12/1997 backbone) through mouse lungs, yielding mutations across internal genes (notably in M and PA) that conferred high pathogenicity in mice. This mouse-adapted internal-gene backbone also increased pathogenicity when combined with HA/NA from B/Austria/1359417/2021, providing a tool to study IBV in mice without altering surface antigens.

title: Increased or decreased numbers of CpG dinucleotide motifs in the genome of influenza A virus do not affect in vitro virus phenotype
summary: The authors engineered influenza A viruses with genome-wide increases or decreases in CpG dinucleotide motifs using only synonymous, naturally occurring mutations while preserving predicted RNA secondary structures and overlapping ORFs. Across multiple independent rescues and assays in A549 and MDCK cells, altered CpG content did not change replication, plaque phenotype, or IFN-β induction, and introduced mutations remained stable over 10 serial passages, challenging CpG enrichment as a general attenuation strategy.

title: Global interfertility and heterosis in sugar kelp populations: a next step in sugar kelp breeding.
crm_level_1: NIOZ Royal Netherlands Institute for Sea Research
summary: This study demonstrates that Saccharina latissima (sugar kelp) genetic resources from across the globe are interfertile and that many interregional crosses exhibit significant heterosis for yield-related traits under common garden conditions. While hybrids showed wide morphological diversity and frequent performance gains, heterosis did not correlate with geographic distance, indicating global resources can enhance breeding without simple distance-based predictions.

title: The designer cytokine IC7Fc attenuates atherosclerosis development by targeting hyperlipidemia in mice.
summary: In APOE*3-Leiden.CETP mice, the designer cytokine IC7Fc markedly lowered plasma triglycerides and cholesterol by suppressing hepatic de novo lipogenesis, reducing APOB/VLDL production, and increasing bile acid synthesis, which together substantially reduced atherosclerotic lesion burden and inflammation. IC7Fc outperformed atorvastatin in limiting lesion area and necrosis without systemic cytokine changes, acting via hepatic pathways including HNF4α downregulation and altered bile acid transport/signaling.

title: Inactive ryanodine receptors sustain lysosomal availability for autophagy by promoting ER-lysosomal contact site formation.
summary: The study shows that ryanodine receptors (RyRs) physically interact with the lysosomal v-ATPase subunit ATP6v0a1 to form ER–lysosome contact sites, thereby suppressing RyR Ca2+ release, positioning lysosomes within the ER network, reducing lysosomal exocytosis, and increasing their availability for autophagic flux. Pharmacological RyR inhibition or ATP6v0a1 overexpression enhances ER–lysosome contacts and autophagy in human iPSC-derived cortical neurons and validates RyR–ATP6v0a1 complexes as dynamic ER–lysosomal tethers.

title: Development of simulated human milk ultrafiltrate (SHMUF) for analysis of native particles in human milk.
summary: The study designed and validated two simulated human milk ultrafiltrate media (SHMUF-Ca and SHMUF-pH) tailored to human milk serum to preserve native particles (casein micelles and extracellular vesicles) during dilution, benchmarking them against PBS, demineralized water, and bovine SMUF via optical transmittance. SHMUF-Ca maintained stable light scattering for at least 10 hours and outperformed other media, while freezing/thawing (-20 °C, 2–8 weeks) increased transmittance (indicative of particle loss), leading to recommendations to dilute with SHMUF-Ca and avoid freezing when possible.

title: Cellular Crosstalk Promotes Hepatic Progenitor Cell Proliferation and Stellate Cell Activation in 3D Co-culture.
summary: This study establishes a 3D Matrigel co-culture of mouse hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) and intrahepatic cholangiocyte organoids (ICOs) that reproduces key in vivo features of ductular reaction and fibrosis, namely enhanced progenitor proliferation and HSC activation. Transcriptomics and functional assays indicate these effects require close cell–cell contact and involve retinoic acid production (ALDH1A2) and Wnt signaling, with spatial transcriptomics of human liver explants supporting colocalized expression of co-culture–induced markers in fibrotic regions.

title: Identification of β-galactosidases along the secretory pathway of Nicotiana benthamiana that collectively hamper engineering of galactose-extended glycans on recombinant glycoproteins.
summary: This study identifies multiple endogenous β-galactosidases in Nicotiana benthamiana that remove terminal galactose from engineered N-glycans on recombinant glycoproteins, with NbBGAL3B and previously known NbBGAL8 emerging as principal contributors in vivo. The authors also present a practical Lewis X-based strategy that shields galactose in planta and enables efficient post-purification defucosylation to yield highly galactosylated N-glycans, improving plant-based production of tailored glycoproteins and vaccines.

title: Enhancing anti-tumor immunity through intratumoral combination therapy with amphiphilic conjugates of oxaliplatin and imidazoquinoline TLR7/8 agonist.
crm_level_3: VIB Center for Inflammation Research Ghent Belgium peter.vandenabeele@irc.vib-ugent.be
summary: This study develops and evaluates intratumoral combination therapy using amphiphilic PEG–cholesteryl conjugates of oxaliplatin (OxPt) and an imidazoquinoline TLR7/8 agonist (IMDQ) to enhance immunogenic cell death and local innate immune activation. Amphiphilic conjugates reduced systemic inflammation and more effectively eradicated primary and distal tumors than native drugs, inducing antigen-specific CD8+ T-cell responses, whereas a highly lipophilic IMDQ–OxPt–C18 conjugate underperformed due to poor solubility and limited in vivo activity.

title: Microfluidic Approaches to Pickering Emulsions and Foams: Strategies, Challenges, and Promising Applications.
summary: This review synthesizes recent advances in using microfluidic platforms to generate and study particle-stabilized emulsions and foams (Pickering systems), covering device materials/geometries, particle loading strategies, and on-chip analytical capabilities. It evaluates advantages, limitations, and application opportunities, and highlights future directions such as improved particle adsorption strategies, device parallelization for scale-up, and integration with analytical and actuation tools.

title: Modelling Atherosclerotic Plaque Cap Mechanics: Microcalcifications Reduce Mechanical Properties in Mesenchymal Stromal Cell-Based Model.
crm_level_1: Erasmus MC, University Medical Center Rotterdam
summary: This study develops a tissue-engineered model of the atherosclerotic fibrous cap using human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) that deposit a collagenous matrix and subsequently form microcalcifications, enabling direct assessment of cap biomechanics. Microcalcifications significantly reduced tissue stiffness and ultimate tensile stress in uniaxial testing, with the extent of calcification correlating with mechanical weakening, while collagen alignment and content remained comparable to controls.

title: Back to the roots: Uncovering ectomycorrhizal communities across three major African vegetation types.
summary: Using root-tip metabarcoding across Guineo-Congolian rainforest, Sudanian woodland, and Zambezian Miombo woodland, the study reveals distinct ectomycorrhizal (EcM) fungal communities dominated by Russulaceae and shows riparian forests act as corridors that facilitate movement of rainforest-associated taxa into woodlands. The authors also benchmark Species Hypothesis (SH) matching for Lactifluus against herbarium collections, finding high concordance and indicating strong influences of host specificity and edaphic factors on EcM community structure.

title: Warming from cold pools: A pathway for mesoscale organization to alter Earth's radiation budget.
summary: Large-eddy simulations of trade-wind shallow cumulus show that rain-evaporation-driven cold pools reduce clear-sky outgoing longwave radiation by moistening the cloud layer, producing a net top-of-atmosphere warming of 1.88 W/m² relative to simulations where rain evaporation cooling is homogenized to suppress cold pools. This warming arises because cold pools weaken mesoscale ascent and prevent extreme moisture self-aggregation and heavy precipitation, highlighting the need to represent mesoscale processes in kilometer-scale climate models to capture radiative budgets accurately.

title: Sec61 translocon inhibitor flavitransin blocks selectively dengue virus polyprotein insertion in the ER with pan-orthoflavivirus antiviral potency.
summary: This study identifies flavitransin, a Sec61 translocon inhibitor derived from CADA, as a potent, selective blocker of the first N‑terminal transmembrane signal of the dengue virus polyprotein, thereby preventing ER insertion, halting viral replication, and showing broad activity against orthoflaviviruses (DENV1–4, ZIKV, YFV) in human and insect systems. Resistance mapping implicates Sec61α mutations (notably A70V) in cellular desensitization, while dengue virus exhibits a high barrier to resistance under drug pressure, and activity extends to mosquito cells and an ex vivo Aedes aegypti midgut model.

title: Evaluating Mathematical Concordance Between Taxonomic and Functional Diversity Metrics in Benthic Macroinvertebrate Communities.
summary: The study assessed how taxonomic and functional diversity metrics align structurally for benthic macroinvertebrate communities along a fluvial habitat quality gradient in the Paute River Basin, Ecuador, using unsupervised clustering and the Measure of Concordance. Strong concordance was found between Shannon/Margalef and functional metrics (Rao, FDis, wFDc), while FRic and family richness showed weaker alignment; the Andean Biotic Index was highly responsive to habitat quality but less concordant with functional metrics, supporting the combined use of taxonomic and functional measures for biomonitoring.

title: Transient colonization with Blastocystis spp. after transmission via fecal microbiota transplantation.
summary: This study investigated transmission and persistence of Blastocystis spp. via fresh fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) in three adolescents with refractory IBS who received two nasoduodenal fresh-donor FMTs from a Blastocystis ST3–positive donor. Two initially negative recipients transiently acquired donor ST3 (clearing by 24–48 weeks), while a recipient carrying ST2 remained ST2-only; no serious FMT-related adverse events occurred, and culture experiments showed Blastocystis viability in fresh but not frozen preparations.

title: USP24 is a cross-reactive DUB targeting MOV10 to regulate IFN-I production.
summary: The study identifies USP24 as an ISG15 cross-reactive deubiquitinase that processes pro-ISG15 and deISGylates substrates, with proteomics revealing MOV10 as a specific USP24 target whose ISGylation enhances IFN-β production via interaction with IFIT3. USP24 loss increases ISGylation and IFN-β/ISG expression during cytosolic RNA sensing without altering canonical IFN-I signaling, positioning USP24 as a potential therapeutic target in antiviral and inflammatory contexts.

title: CellEKT: A Robust Chemical Proteomics Workflow to Profile Cellular Target Engagement of Kinase Inhibitors.
summary: The authors present CellEKT, a standardized chemical proteomics workflow that quantifies cellular target engagement of kinase inhibitors across endogenously expressed kinases using the covalent probe XO44 and two new broad-spectrum probes (ALX005/ALX011), expanding kinome coverage to about 48% (≈300+ kinases). The platform integrates optimized sample prep, on-bead proteolytic digestion, automated KNIME data analysis for IC50 fitting, and validation via phosphoproteomics and NanoBRET, enabling dose–response selectivity profiling of covalent and noncovalent inhibitors in human cell lines.

title: A human intestinal epithelial-mesenchyme-immune triple culture system for disease modelling.
summary: The authors developed a modular human intestinal triple co-culture model on transwell inserts that combines primary organoid-derived intestinal epithelial cells with intestinal fibroblasts and antigen-presenting cells (monocyte-derived dendritic cells and macrophages) from adult and foetal donors, reproducing ECM deposition, Paneth cell support, barrier longevity, and immune modulation. The system enabled inflammation modeling and viral studies (CMV, EV-A71, E11), and single-cell RNA-seq revealed epithelial differentiation states and fibroblast signaling, demonstrating improved physiological relevance compared to epithelial-only models.

title: Insights in Cellular and Molecular Signatures of the Small Intestinal Graft Posttransplantation: Successful, Recovered, and Rejected-A Case Series.
summary: This case series performed longitudinal single-cell RNA sequencing on ileal graft biopsies from three intestinal transplant recipients to map donor and recipient cell dynamics and relate them to clinical outcomes. It found rapid recipient immune repopulation in the rejected graft, incomplete T-cell depletion after rATG induction, and that epithelial apoptotic and interferon pathway activation preceded pathology-defined severe rejection, suggesting transcriptomic profiles may provide early prognostic signals.

title: Cross-species comparison reveals that Hmga1 reduces H3K27me3 levels to promote cardiomyocyte proliferation and cardiac regeneration.
summary: Cross-species spatial transcriptomics and functional genetics identify HMGA1 as a conserved regulator that lowers repressive H3K27me3 marks to reactivate developmental and metabolic programs, driving cardiomyocyte proliferation and regeneration. In zebrafish, hmga1a is required and sufficient for regeneration, and AAV-mediated HMGA1 delivery to adult mouse infarct border zones induces cardiomyocyte cell-cycle re-entry and improves cardiac function without adverse remodeling.

title: Asynchronous xylogenesis among and within tree species in the central Congo Basin.
summary: The study monitored cambial activity (xylogenesis) in 18 trees from six abundant species during the transition from dry to rainy season in the Yangambi rainforest, Democratic Republic of the Congo, using microcoring and epifluorescence microscopy. Results show pronounced inter- and intraspecific asynchrony in cambial phenology with weak coupling to leaf phenology and seasonal rainfall, implying no forest-wide dormant period and highlighting implications for linking ground growth measurements with eddy-covariance carbon fluxes.

title: A missing enzyme-rescue metabolite as cause of a rare skeletal dysplasia.
summary: This study identifies TGDS as a UDP-glucose 4,6-dehydratase that produces UDP-4-keto-6-deoxyglucose, an enzyme-rescue metabolite that reoxidizes the UXS1-bound cofactor to NAD+ and restores UXS1 activity when NAD+ is scarce in the ER/Golgi due to H6PD. Loss of TGDS in cells and mice reduces UDP-xylose and specific glycans (heparan sulfate and matriglycan), explaining Catel–Manzke syndrome via a functional UXS1 deficiency that can be rescued by supplying UDP-4-keto sugars or by modulating H6PD.

title: Nonfouling Coatings from Synthetic Intrinsically Disordered Proteins.
summary: The study optimizes a triblock, self-assembling protein brush (B-M-E) for nonfouling coatings on gold by screening synthetic intrinsically disordered polypeptides and identifies the EIDP3 sequence [(GAGAIP)3-(GAGEIP)]4 as a top performer, matching the protein resistance of tetraethylene glycol-terminated SAMs. These recombinantly produced brushes resist adsorption from human serum and significantly reduce E. coli adhesion for at least seven days, with performance validated by QCM-D, SPR, DLS, AFM, and CLSM.

title: Advancing diagnostics in suspected periprosthetic joint infections using synthetic synovial fluid and microcalorimetry.
summary: This study evaluated two alternative diagnostic approaches for suspected periprosthetic joint infection—culturing synovial fluid in synthetic synovial fluid (SSF2) and isothermal microcalorimetry (IMC)—and compared them with conventional culturing. SSF2 culture yielded the highest positivity rate and broader organism diversity, while IMC reduced time-to-detection (median ~16 hours), indicating these methods are complementary for improving diagnostic yield and speed.

title: Starch-based thickening in infant formula: in vitro study of behavior in the bottle and under gastric conditions.
summary: This in vitro study evaluated how starch-based thickening of infant formulas behaves in the bottle and under simulated gastric conditions, comparing a standard formula thickened with rice flour (SFRF) to a commercial pre-thickened potato-starch formula (IFPS). Rice flour produced higher in-bottle viscosities early but declined after ~20 minutes, while potato starch peaked around ~30 minutes with vigorous shaking; however, both lost most viscosity under simulated gastric conditions to levels comparable with standard formula, and added starch substantially increased caloric intake.

title: Protocol for synthesis and mechanical characterization of polyacrylamide hydrogels of varying stiffness for cell culture applications.
summary: This STAR Protocol details the fabrication of large, unattached polyacrylamide hydrogels with tunable stiffness, their bulk rheological characterization, and surface functionalization for 2D cell culture. It provides a standardized workflow from gel synthesis and microscale rheology to ECM coupling and downstream applications such as culturing KM12L4a colorectal cancer cells for secretome/cell collection and fluorescence imaging.

title: Envelope destabilization by AcrAB2NodT overexpression links antibiotic resistance to metal sensitivity in Caulobacter vibrioides.
crm_level_3: Research Unit in Biology of Microorganisms (URBM)
summary: In Caulobacter vibrioides, deletion of the repressor TipR causes constitutive overexpression of the AcrAB2NodT RND efflux pump, which destabilizes the cell envelope and depletes the proton motive force, lowering ATP and creating a collateral sensitivity to copper and other metals despite unchanged intracellular copper levels. Genetic or functional inactivation of the pump restores copper resistance, revealing a fitness trade-off that links antibiotic resistance to metal sensitivity and suggesting therapeutic strategies that exploit this metabolic burden.

title: Loss of DIAPH3 accelerates glioma genesis in mice.
summary: Using conditional mouse models, the authors show that loss of DIAPH3 on a Trp53-deficient background accelerates onset of high-grade diffuse gliomas, increases whole-chromosome aneuploidy and endogenous DNA damage, and shortens survival without altering tumor growth rate. Pre-tumor transcriptomics reveal cancer-related pathway changes, and glioma stem-like cells from double knockouts are more radioresistant—associated with Fgfr2 amplification—supporting a tumor-suppressor role for DIAPH3 and its impact on radiotherapy response.

title: Intradermal immunization with Plasmodium berghei late-arresting genetically attenuated sporozoites induces PD-L1 expression on regulatory macrophages and dendritic cells.
crm_level_3: Leiden University Centre for Infectious Diseases (LU-CID)
summary: This study compares immune responses to intradermal versus intravenous immunization with late-arresting genetically attenuated Plasmodium berghei sporozoites (GA2) in mice and finds that intradermal delivery yields fewer CD8+ tissue-resident memory T cells and reduced cytotoxic activation across organs. Intradermal immunization induces a regulatory myeloid phenotype with high PD-L1 and low CD86 in skin and draining lymph nodes, potentially suppressing T cell priming and contributing to reduced protection, suggesting optimization of intradermal delivery (e.g., lower volumes) may improve efficacy.

title: Assessing the Impact of Nutritional Stress on the Identification of Plastic-Associated Bacteria in Insect Gut Microbiota.
summary: The study tested whether plastic-only diets confound the identification of plastic-associated gut bacteria in Galleria mellonella and Tenebrio molitor by comparing polyurethane (PU) feeding with nutritionally complete, mixed, and starvation conditions using 16S rRNA profiling and culture-based isolation. Plastic-only microbiomes closely resembled starvation in both species (strongly in T. molitor), and isolates obtained from PU cultures also grew without an added carbon source, indicating that nutritional stress—not polymer presence—primarily drives observed bacterial enrichment under plastic diets.

title: In vivo 9.4 Tesla MRI of a patient with drug-resistant epilepsy: Technical report.
summary: This technical report describes the first in vivo 9.4 Tesla MRI examination of a patient with drug-resistant epilepsy, demonstrating markedly improved spatial resolution and anatomical delineation compared to 3T and 7T MRI but identifying no epileptogenic lesion. The study highlights benefits (enhanced visualization of hippocampal subfields and gray–white junctions) and challenges (B0/B1 inhomogeneity, SAR limits, anterior-inferior temporal signal dropouts), and calls for larger studies to establish diagnostic and therapeutic gains over 7T.

title: Peptide-Modified Lipid Nanoparticles Boost the Antitumor Efficacy of RNA Therapeutics.
summary: The authors engineered lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) by conjugating a CD44-targeting A6 peptide (AKPC) to cholesterol-PEG, enabling selective delivery of YAP/TAZ siRNA to CD44+ tumor cells. These AKPC-LNPs enhanced cellular uptake, gene silencing, apoptosis, and tumor suppression in breast cancer cell lines, zebrafish xenografts, prostate cancer PDX-derived organoids, and a PDX mouse model, outperforming unmodified MC3-LNPs while maintaining acceptable safety.

title: Animal-free alternatives for Matrigel in human iPSC-derived blood vessel organoid culture.
summary: This study replaces animal-derived Matrigel in human iPSC-derived blood vessel organoid workflows by using recombinant human Vitronectin for 2D iPSC culture and a fibrin-based hydrogel (fibrinogen + thrombin) for 3D differentiation. Across multiple iPSC lines, the Vitronectin–fibrin system supported organoid growth, vascular network formation, and endothelial sprouting comparable to Matrigel, improving reproducibility and xeno-free translational potential.

title: Rapid Volumetric Bioprinting Coupled with Dynamic Perfusion Enhances Human Hepatic Organoid Toxicity Testing.
summary: The study integrates rapid volumetric bioprinting with a custom continuous-perfusion bioreactor to culture human intrahepatic cholangiocyte organoid-derived hepatic constructs, which show enhanced hepatic maturation under flow. Under prolonged subtoxic acetaminophen exposure, perfused constructs exhibited greater injury marker release and metabolic decline than static controls, demonstrating improved sensitivity for hepatotoxicity testing.

title: Rational design of alternative treatment options for radioresistant rectal cancer using patient-derived organoids.
summary: Patient-derived rectal cancer organoids that were resistant to radiation showed enhanced DNA repair and antioxidant (glutathione) metabolism compared to sensitive organoids. Guided by transcriptomics and combination screens, the authors found that inhibiting GCLC (with BSO or genetic knockout) synergizes strongly with the oxidative stress inducer RRx-001 to eradicate radioresistant organoids, suggesting a potential alternative therapy for radioresistant rectal cancer.

title: Polymicrobial Sepsis-Induced Changes in Hepatic Stellate Cell Communication in Male C57BL/6J Mice.
summary: This study used cell type-specific bulk RNA-sequencing and computational ligand–receptor inference (CellChat, NicheNet) to map how polymicrobial sepsis (CLP) reorganizes intercellular communication among liver cells in male C57BL/6J mice. Hepatic stellate cells emerged as a central signaling hub after sepsis, broadcasting fibrogenic and chemotactic cues (e.g., Ccl7) that suppress hepatocyte metabolic programs and promote leukocyte infiltration, suggesting early fibrogenic priming of the liver microenvironment.

title: Adenocarcinoma of the small intestine cohort: prospectively collecting real-world data to improve care and quality of life for patients with a rare cancer.
summary: This article describes the nationwide AdenoCarcinoma of the Small Intestine (ACSI) cohort, a prospective subcohort of the Dutch PLCRC, established to integrate clinical, molecular, and patient-reported outcomes for small intestinal adenocarcinoma. By June 2025, 143 patients were enrolled; among the first 105, median age was 65, 57% had duodenal tumors, 27% presented with stage IV disease, 80% underwent primary resection, 42% received systemic therapy, and 28% had mismatch repair deficiency.

title: A tool to pulse-label yeast nuclear pore complexes in imaging and biochemical experiments.
summary: The authors present a rapid, tunable pulse-labeling strategy for yeast nuclear pore complexes using a high-affinity Nup84 nanobody fused to either mNeonGreen for live imaging or a ZZ tag for affinity purification. Short induction pulses label NPCs within minutes, allow tracking across cell divisions, and enable affinity pulldowns whose proteomic profiles match endogenous Nup84-ZZ baits, facilitating time-resolved NPC interactome analyses.

title: CRISPR activation screen uncovers MARCKSL1 as a gauge for extracellular vesicle secretion.
summary: A genome-wide CRISPR activation screen using CD63 surface display as a readout identifies MARCKSL1 as a key regulator that shifts extracellular vesicle (EV) output toward plasma membrane–derived vesicles and away from late endosome–plasma membrane fusion. Functional, imaging, and proteomic analyses show that MARCKSL1 boosts EV secretion, alters EV cargo, and collaborates with actin–membrane linkers (Radixin/Moesin) and SNARE-associated protein STXBP3 to control CD63 trafficking and EV biogenesis.

title: Influence of natural variations in eating rate and bolus properties on postprandial glucose and insulin responses in healthy adults.
summary: In a repeated-measures study of 33 healthy adults consuming a standardized mixed meal, natural differences in eating rate and oral processing (chews and oro-sensory exposure) were linked to higher early and late postprandial insulin (and C-peptide) responses among slower eaters, while total postprandial glucose did not differ significantly between groups. The findings suggest that slower eating enhances insulin dynamics—likely via extended chewing and sensory exposure—helping modulate glucose homeostasis without markedly altering overall glycemia in healthy individuals.

title: Profiling cytotoxicity of nanofractionated elapid snake venoms in human cell lines representing different tissues.
crm_level_3: Amsterdam Institute of Molecular and Life Sciences
summary: This study integrates nanofractionation analytics, high-throughput cellular cytotoxicity assays, and venomics to profile and identify cytotoxic components in elapid snake venoms across four human tissue-representative cell lines (kidney, liver, endothelial, skin). Three-finger toxins (3FTxs), phospholipases A2 (PLA2s), and Kunitz-type protease inhibitors were implicated in selective, cell type–specific cytotoxicity; crude Bungarus multicinctus showed cytotoxicity in liver and skin cells that was lost after RP-HPLC (likely denaturation) but recovered with size-exclusion chromatography-based fractionation.

title: A catheter-associated urinary tract infection mouse model to study bladder dysfunction and pain.
summary: The authors developed a female mouse suprapubic catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI) model using bioluminescent UPEC (UTI89-Lux) to longitudinally track infection, bladder function, inflammation, and pain. Compared with sham, sterile-catheter (CACON), and transurethral UTI controls, CAUTI mice showed sustained infection with catheter biofilms, increased suprapubic mechanical hypersensitivity, reduced bladder capacity, and decreased voiding efficiency, effects that were mitigated by antibiotic treatment.

title: Polymeric (Poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid)) Particles Entrapping Perfluorocarbons Are Stable for a Minimum of Six Years.
summary: This study demonstrates that lyophilized PLGA nanoparticles encapsulating perfluoro-15-crown-5-ether (PFCE) remain remarkably stable for at least six years when stored at −20 °C, with minimal changes in size, polydispersity, and PFCE content, and exhibit robustness through multiple freeze–thaw cycles.
