Using DLS, multi-angle DLS, 19F NMR, and TEM, the authors show the particles maintain integrity and performance, and remain stable up to 30 days at 4 °C and room temperature in water or serum-free medium, with expected behavior at 37 °C attributable to their multicore structure.

title: Serum heat inactivation diminishes ApoE-mediated uptake of D-Lin-MC3-DMA lipid nanoparticles.
summary: The study shows that heat inactivation of fetal calf serum (56 °C, 30 min) diminishes apolipoprotein E (ApoE)-dependent uptake and siRNA delivery of D-Lin-MC3-DMA lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), while C12-200 LNPs remain unaffected. Mechanistically, heat treatment denatures/aggregates ApoE, reducing its binding to MC3 LNPs and cellular uptake; adding recombinant ApoE rescues this effect, underscoring the importance of serum handling in in vitro LNP evaluations.

title: Current State-Of-Play of the EU Advanced Therapy Medicinal Product (ATMP) Field, With an Emphasis on Belgian Human Cell and Tissue Products.
summary: This review assesses the impact of the EU Advanced Therapy Medicinal Products (ATMP) regulation 15 years after implementation, finding that approvals are dominated by gene therapies, whose very high prices strain public reimbursement and limit patient access. It highlights how stringent Hospital Exemption (HE) frameworks—especially in Belgium—have contributed to the discontinuation of many previously available hospital-produced human cell and tissue products (HCTPs), leaving patients with fewer options.

title: The piRNA pathway mediates transcriptional silencing of LTR retrotransposons in ovaries and somatic tissues of Aedes mosquitoes.
summary: This study shows that the Aedes albopictus PIWI protein Piwi6 mediates transcriptional silencing of LTR retrotransposons, including a full-length endogenous retrovirus (AalERV1), by promoting H3K9me3 deposition and requiring an intrinsically disordered region for nuclear localization. Piwi6 knockout cells and in vivo knockdown mosquitoes exhibit strong upregulation of LTR elements and AalERV1, increased RNA Pol II occupancy, and rescue only with nuclear-localizing Piwi6, establishing a somatic nuclear arm of the piRNA pathway in mosquitoes.

title: Identifying colorectal cancer-specific vulnerabilities in the Wnt-driven long non-coding transcriptome.
crm_level_3: Center for Experimental and Molecular Medicine
summary: The study maps the Wnt/β-catenin-regulated long non-coding RNA landscape in colorectal cancer using GRO-seq and identifies essential lncRNAs via CRISPRi dropout screens, highlighting LINC02418 as a cancer-specific dependency that maintains MYC and stemness. Therapeutically, lipid nanoparticle-formulated siRNAs targeting LINC02418 suppress tumour growth in xenograft models, suggesting a cancer-selective RNAi approach to modulate Wnt-driven oncogenic programs.

title: RAPPID-M: A Mix-and-Measure Bioluminescent Sandwich Immunoassay Based on Generic Antibody-Binding Protein M.
summary: The study introduces RAPPID-M, a mix-and-measure bioluminescent sandwich immunoassay that uses a truncated protein M (pM440) to noncovalently bind antibodies and attach split NanoLuc fragments, eliminating the need for protein G photoconjugation. RAPPID-M shows lower background, improved dynamic range, sub-picomolar detection limits, and compatibility with mouse IgG1, Fab, and scFv fragments, while remaining stable over days and performing in buffered and serum-containing matrices.

title: The absence of Pitx3 results in postnatal loss of dopamine neurons and is associated with an increase in the pro-apoptotic Bcl2 factor Noxa and cleaved caspase 3.
summary: Using a Pitx3 knockout GFP knock-in mouse, the study shows that the loss of substantia nigra dopaminergic neurons occurs postnatally (around P3) rather than during embryogenesis and is associated with increased cleaved caspase-3 and upregulation of the pro-apoptotic BH3-only factor Noxa. Noxa overexpression induces apoptosis in dopaminergic MN9D cells, which can be mitigated by a Bax-inhibiting peptide, indicating a Noxa–Mcl1–Bax mitochondrial apoptosis pathway underlying neuron loss in the Pitx3-deficient model.

title: Nutritional c-Fos Induction Rewires Hepatic Metabolism and Can Promote Obesity-Associated Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
summary: This study shows that hepatic c-Fos is nutritionally and hormonally induced—rising with insulin during feeding and suppressed by glucagon—where persistent elevation rewires liver metabolism toward glycolysis, lipogenesis, and insulin resistance in obesity. In hepatocellular carcinoma, c-Fos correlates with activation of PI3K-Akt/MAPK pathways and supports proliferation and stress resistance, while its knockdown reduces growth and restores apoptotic sensitivity, positioning c-Fos as a metabolic–oncogenic integrator across the MASLD–HCC spectrum.

title: Pathogenesis of mtDNA point mutation m.10191T>C affecting complex I function is a multifactorial process leading to metabolic remodeling of mitochondria.
summary: This study investigates the pathogenic mtDNA mutation m.10191T>C (ND3S45P) in mitochondrial complex I and finds that while mutant mitochondria retain ~30–40% complex I activity and OXPHOS capacity, intact cells exhibit severely reduced respiration and a dramatically elevated NADH/NAD+ ratio. The authors propose that ND3S45P lowers the activation barrier for the complex I Active/Deactive transition, leading to a regulatory shutoff of NADH oxidation in cells; complexome profiling across cybrids, patient fibroblasts, and muscle biopsies reveals moderate remodeling but no alternate primary cause for NADH accumulation.

title: Engineering of induced pluripotent stem cells for the efficient development of non-alloreactive, hypoimmunogenic CD8αβ CAR-T cells.
summary: This study engineered human T cell-derived induced pluripotent stem cells (T-iPSCs) by knocking out TRAC and B2M and inserting a doxycycline-inducible CD38 CAR and an HLA-E single-chain trimer to generate non-alloreactive, hypoimmunogenic CAR-T cells. The approach produced functional TCR-negative CD8ab+ CAR-iT cells with in vitro and in vivo anti-tumor efficacy, though B2M disruption introduced genomic instability and reduced developmental efficiency and proliferative capacity.

title: The honey bee triad: a comprehensive catalogue of phages in the Apis mellifera gut microbiome.
summary: This study assembled 2,343 largely novel phage genomes from 450 virus-enriched gut samples of Apis mellifera collected across eight European countries, and defined a globally prevalent core set of 97 phages that predominantly exhibit temperate lifestyles and target honey bee core gut bacteria. The authors identified auxiliary metabolic genes, notably a phage-encoded PAPS reductase, whose abundance associated with agricultural land use, and validated ecological patterns across gut parts and geography, with absolute viral loads measured by flow cytometry corroborating metagenomic inferences.

title: Accelerating personalized medicine: miniaturized patient-derived organoid drug screening for predicting cancer treatment responses and beyond.
summary: The study develops and validates a miniaturized, automated patient-derived organoid (PDO) drug screening workflow using the Yamaha Cell Handler to seed as few as 5–10 PDOs per well, reducing input material by ~96% and shortening turnaround time. Optimized image-based CyQUANT viability readouts and YCH-based transfer produced drug response profiles in metastatic colorectal cancer PDOs that correlate with conventional assays and patient outcomes, supporting faster personalized treatment prediction.

title: Comparative Physiology and Genomics of Thermincola and Carboxydocella Strains and Description of Two Novel Isolates.
summary: Two new thermophilic carboxydotrophic bacteria were isolated from Azorean hot springs—AZ34E (Thermincola) and AZ29I (Carboxydocella)—and shown to grow by hydrogenogenic CO oxidation; comparative genomics indicates that all currently described Thermincola strains constitute a single species and most Carboxydocella (except C. manganica) likewise cluster as one species. Genomes of Thermincola and Carboxydocella encode four and six [Ni–Fe] CODH (cooS) copies, respectively, and a broader survey of Bacillota_B revealed widespread CODH genes, expanding the diversity of candidate CO oxidizers and prompting taxonomic synonymies for Thermincola ferriacetica with T. carboxydiphila and Carboxydocella sporoproducens with C. thermautotrophica.

title: An analytical toolbox to verify the presence, quantity and origin of recycled cotton fibres in textile garments.
summary: The study introduces an analytical toolbox that combines microscopy, fibre length distribution measurement, and viscosity-based degree of polymerisation (DP) analysis to verify the presence, quantity, and pre- vs post-consumer origin of mechanically recycled cotton in garments. Applied to lab-made and industry textiles, the toolbox qualitatively confirms recycled fibres, estimates recycled content within about ±10 percentage points, and uses DP thresholds to infer origin, supporting future standardization and integration with digital product passports.

title: The Proprotein Convertase BLI-4 Is Required for Axenic Dietary Restriction Mediated Longevity in Caenorhabditis elegans.
summary: This study shows that the proprotein convertase BLI-4, acting primarily in neurons, is required for the robust lifespan extension induced by axenic dietary restriction (ADR) in Caenorhabditis elegans, with isoforms b, f, i, and j redundantly supporting this effect while the d isoform mainly affects development. Quantitative proteomics under ADR identified downregulation of GOLG-2 upon bli-4 knockdown and demonstrated that golg-2 partially mediates ADR longevity, highlighting a BLI-4–Golgi axis specific to ADR and not other dietary restriction regimens.

title: Plasma proteomics identifies early markers of endothelial and inflammatory activation associated with dengue disease severity in children.
crm_level_3: Bijvoet Centre for Biomolecular Research and Utrecht Institute for Pharmaceutical Sciences
summary: This longitudinal plasma proteomics study of Cambodian children with post-primary DENV-2 infection profiled 296 plasma samples from 92 cases across disease phases and identified early endothelial and inflammatory activation signatures that distinguish subclinical from hospitalized cases and predict progression to severe dengue. Key early markers included PTX3 and VCAM1 for endothelial stress and complement regulators, while CLEC11A most strongly differentiated DF from DHF/DSS at hospital admission; machine-learning models achieved high accuracy in classifying disease phase and severity from acute-phase plasma proteomes.

title: Sequence simplification of antigen coding IVT mRNA allows accelerated synthetic DNA template generation and epitope immunogenicity validation.
summary: The study shows that antigen-encoding IVT mRNA can be simplified by removing stabilizing elements such as 5′ and 3′ UTRs and the poly-A tail without compromising antigen presentation, enabling faster and more flexible mRNA production for epitope validation. The authors introduce a one-oligonucleotide synthetic DNA template workflow that accelerates IVT-mRNA manufacturing, reduces dsRNA byproducts, and supports high-throughput immunogenicity screening using electroporation and LNP delivery in human APC/T cell systems.

title: B-cell abundance in perivascular cuffs associates with local lesion activity in multiple sclerosis.
summary: JSON parse error

title: Impedance flow cytometry for rapid quality assessment of protoplast cultures.
summary: The study demonstrates that impedance flow cytometry (IFC) provides rapid, label-free, and reproducible measurements of protoplast viability, size, and early division in Arabidopsis thaliana, Brassica napus, and Beta vulgaris. IFC-derived viability metrics correlate with traditional FDA staining and predict microcallus formation, enabling efficient quality control and optimization of plant protoplast culture workflows.

title: Understanding the Stability of Poorly Covered Pickering Emulsions Using on-Chip Microfluidics.
summary: The study uses an on-chip microfluidic platform to generate and analyze poorly covered Pickering emulsions, showing that droplets remain highly stable (≥12 h) at particle surface coverages below 3% due to crown-like particle bridges localized at droplet contact regions. Experiments and simulations reveal that hydrodynamic shear gradients drive particle accumulation at droplet poles, enabling mono-, bi-, or multilayer bridges that prevent coalescence despite sparse overall coverage.

title: Proteome-wide Ubiquitinome Profiling Reveals Substrate-specific Dynamics Within the USP7 Network.
summary: This study integrates proteome-wide ubiquitin remnant (K-ε-GG) profiling by DIA-MS with targeted and interaction proteomics to map USP7’s substrates and define how USP7 inhibition reshapes the ubiquitinome and proteome. The authors reveal that USP7’s deubiquitylating effects are highly substrate- and site-specific, differentially impacting stability of distinct targets (e.g., ncPRC1.6 versus ncPRC1.1 components), and provide a high-confidence USP7 interaction network connecting neurodevelopmental and tumor suppressor pathways.

title: Exploratory Assessment of Short-Term Antecedent Modeled Flow Memory in Shaping Macroinvertebrate Diversity: Integrating Satellite-Derived Precipitation and Rainfall-Runoff Modeling in a Remote Andean Micro-Catchment.
summary: The study integrates satellite-derived rainfall, rainfall–runoff modeling, and field sampling of benthic macroinvertebrates to assess how short-term antecedent streamflow conditions shape diversity in a pristine Andean micro-catchment in southern Ecuador. It finds that macroinvertebrate taxonomic diversity responds most strongly to cumulative flow over a nine-day window, with recession (negative flow changes) being the key hydrological driver and taxonomic metrics reacting more quickly than functional ones.

title: TD-NMR-Based Determination of the Entrapped Water Yield of Water-in-Oil-in-Water Double Emulsions: Influence of Xanthan Gum Addition.
summary: This study benchmarks three direct methods—analytical photocentrifugation, TD-NMR T2 relaxometry, and PFG-NMR diffusometry—for determining the entrapped water yield (EY) of water-in-oil-in-water double emulsions formulated with varying xanthan gum concentrations in the external phase. TD-NMR methods (T2 relaxometry and diffusometry) provided reliable EY values across viscosities, whereas analytical photocentrifugation overestimated EY in viscous systems due to incomplete cream/serum separation.

title: Pan-cancer single-cell atlases of mouse and human tumor-associated dendritic cells.
crm_level_3: Lab of Dendritic Cell Biology and Cancer Immunotherapy
summary: This study builds comprehensive pan-cancer single-cell RNA-seq atlases of tumor-associated dendritic cells (TADCs) from 14 mouse models and 10 human cancer types, resolving lineage-defined subsets (cDC1, cDC2A, cDC2B, DC3, pDC) and functional states (e.g., CCR7+, ISG, hypoxic, proliferative) and validating annotations using fate-mapping-derived signatures. The authors show that TADCs gain interferon-stimulated inflammatory profiles as tumors progress, identify tumor-driven reprogramming in lymph nodes, demonstrate moderate cross-species conservation, and associate specific human TADC states with patient outcomes.

title: Synaptic enrichment of pSer129 alpha-synuclein correlates with dopaminergic denervation in early-stage Parkinson's disease.
summary: In human post-mortem brains spanning Braak stages 0–6, multiplex immunofluorescence and confocal microscopy revealed early enrichment of pSer129 α-synuclein in putaminal dopaminergic synapses that correlates with dopaminergic terminal loss, while C-terminally truncated α-synuclein (CTT122) accumulates later and is associated with synaptic swelling. Synaptosomal AlphaLISA confirmed elevated pSer129 α-synuclein in PD putamen, and enrichment of pSer129/CTT122 in cortical glutamatergic terminals preceded cortical Lewy body pathology, supporting synapse-to-soma propagation.

title: Conceptualising and mapping polarisation trends in land systems.
summary: The paper conceptualizes land-system polarization as opposing, interconnected land-use trajectories and proposes a scalable, transferable framework and workflow for mapping it across spatial and temporal dimensions. Applied to EU crop production systems (2000–2012) using CAPRI data, the study shows that about 87% of NUTS-2 regions exhibit polarization across indicators of extent, intensity, composition, and spatial patterns, offering spatially explicit insights for policy and monitoring.

title: Survey on Ochratoxin A Occurrence in Cured Meat Products in The Netherlands.
summary: The study developed and in-house validated an LC-MS/MS method (LOQ 0.04 µg/kg; reporting limit 0.2 µg/kg) using methanol extraction and immunoaffinity cleanup to quantify ochratoxin A (OTA) in cured meats. Applying this method to 50 Dutch retail products, OTA was found in 40% of samples (12% ≥ 0.2 µg/kg) with one high outlier (79.8 µg/kg), indicating cured meats can contribute to low-level but recurring OTA exposure.

title: Land-Use Shapes Soil Fungal Communities and Functional Guilds in Tropical Forest Ecosystems.
summary: Using high-throughput ITS2 and SSU amplicon sequencing of tropical forest soils in southwestern Nigeria, the study found strong land-use effects on total fungal, saprotrophic, and plant pathogenic communities but not on arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF). Undisturbed forests harbored more unique specialist OTUs, whereas croplands were enriched in plant pathogens, and agroforestry likely buffered AMF communities by maintaining continuous host roots.

title: Tissue tropism and viral levels of Acheta domesticus densovirus throughout the house cricket production.
summary: This study quantified Acheta domesticus densovirus (AdDV) levels across house cricket developmental stages and tissues to infer transmission routes in mass-rearing conditions. AdDV levels increased from nymphs to adults, were higher in mated than unmated crickets, and were detected in all tissues—with particularly high levels in female gut and ovaries—supporting both horizontal and vertical transmission routes and informing strategies to establish virus-free breeding lines.

title: Combining AlphaFold with Focused Virtual Library Design in the Development of Novel CCR2 and CCR5 Antagonists.
summary: The study combined an AlphaFold-refined model of CCR5 with focused virtual library design and molecular docking to identify intracellular allosteric antagonists of CCR2 and CCR5. Eighteen pyrazinyl-sulfonamide analogues were synthesized, yielding three CCR2 binders (Ki = 1.3–6 μM) and one CCR5 antagonist (IC50 = 10.8 μM), with structure–activity relationships rationalized by docking and molecular dynamics simulations.

title: Red Yeast Rice Increases Bone Morphogenetic Protein-2 Expression and Enhances Fracture Healing Process in Delayed Union Models of Sprague-Dawley Rats: A Preclinical Study.
summary: In a Sprague-Dawley rat delayed-union femoral fracture model, oral red yeast rice (25 mg/kg) increased BMP-2 expression and improved histomorphometric indices of healing (reduced fibrous tissue, increased cartilage/woven bone) compared with controls at 2 and 4 weeks. The study suggests red yeast rice, a source of monacolin (lovastatin-like), may be a cost-effective adjunct to enhance fracture healing via BMP-2 upregulation.

title: Monitoring M-Protein, Therapeutic Antibodies, and Polyclonal Antibodies in a Multiparametric Mass Spectrometry Assay Provides Insight into Therapy Response Kinetics in Patients with Multiple Myeloma.
summary: This proof-of-concept study expands a bottom-up mass spectrometry (MS-MRD) assay to simultaneously quantify patient-specific M-proteins, multiple therapeutic antibodies (including bispecifics), and polyclonal immunoglobulin isotypes in a single run, enabling detailed monitoring of therapy response in multiple myeloma. Longitudinal analysis of sera (and CSF in one case) from four patients showed that the assay sensitively tracked M-protein dynamics, drug levels, and hypogammaglobulinemia, with teclistamab yielding the deepest responses in two patients and detection of both M-protein and bispecific antibodies in CSF.

title: Proteome selectivity profiling of photoaffinity probes derived from imidazopyrazine-kinase inhibitors.
summary: The study designs and synthesizes photoaffinity probes based on imidazopyrazine kinase inhibitors (KIRA6, acalabrutinib, and linsitinib) to profile proteome-wide selectivity and off-targets via chemical proteomics. Using UV-induced labeling in human cell lysates, click-enrichment, on-bead trypsin digestion, and LC-MS/MS, the authors show differing off-target landscapes among probes and attribute selectivity differences to the size, rigidity, and spatial arrangement of 1-position substituents, supported by molecular dynamics and docking analyses.

title: Identify structures underlying out-of-equilibrium reaction networks with random graph analysis.
summary: The authors present a general procedure that translates chemically designed reaction networks into directed, weighted species–species graphs, enabling analysis with network measures and random graph null models, and apply it to a known enzymatic (trypsin-based) oscillator. By integrating temporal simulations (ODEs) with graph metrics, they reveal when feedback interactions emerge during oscillations and provide open-source tools for broader analysis of out-of-equilibrium CRNs.

title: Dynamics of pesticide residues in soils during the growing season: a case study in peach orchards, east-central Portugal.
summary: This study monitored pesticide residues in topsoils of 18 peach orchards in east‑central Portugal over five time points in 2022 (270 samples), analyzing 37 compounds and finding 32 at least once, with glyphosate and AMPA most frequent and at highest concentrations. Measured soil concentrations generally exceeded EFSA-predicted values, indicating slower-than-expected decay and highlighting the potential for persistent background levels and the need for long-term, regionally calibrated monitoring and modeling.

title: A crucial role of the malate aspartate shuttle in metabolic reprogramming in TNF-induced SIRS.
summary: This study shows that tumor necrosis factor (TNF) downregulates the malate–aspartate shuttle (MAS) via HNF4α loss-of-function, leading to NAD+ and NADH depletion, impaired fatty acid β-oxidation, enhanced glycolysis, hyperlactatemia, and lethal vascular leakage in TNF-induced systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS). Using Slc25a13-/- (citrin-deficient) mice, the authors demonstrate that MAS dysfunction exacerbates metabolic dysregulation and mortality, identifying MAS/NAD+ homeostasis as a therapeutic target.

title: Single cell multiomics unravel the transcription networks controlling the different EMT tumor states.
summary: Using single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq multiomics in a mouse skin squamous cell carcinoma model, the study maps discrete EMT states and identifies Klf5 and Pitx1 as regulators of epithelial/early-hybrid states and Nfatc1 and Creb3l1 as regulators of late EMT. CRISPR loss-of-function shows Klf5 and Pitx1 are required to maintain early EMT states and for metastasis, while Nfatc1 and Creb3l1 drive progression to late EMT; regulatory patterns are partially conserved in mouse pancreatic cancer and human cancers.

title: Beneficial effects of the novel first-in-class compound DX243 on ischemic outcomes following in vitro and in vivo models of stroke.
summary: This study evaluates the neuroprotective efficacy of DX243, a first-in-class small molecule, across in vitro (oxygen-glucose deprivation and glutamate excitotoxicity) and in vivo (transient middle cerebral artery occlusion in C57BL/6J mice) stroke models. DX243 increased ATP levels and neuronal survival in vitro, reduced infarct volume, and preserved motor coordination in vivo, supporting its potential as a therapeutic for acute ischemic stroke.

title: Failing maternal-fetal tolerance in SLE (FaMaLE): a prospective cohort study for finding the molecular mechanisms behind pregnancy complications.
summary: The FaMaLE study is a single-centre prospective cohort investigating how failures in maternal–fetal tolerance contribute to pregnancy complications in women with SLE by longitudinally profiling blood and placental immune cell compositions. It provides a standardized protocol for collecting maternal blood and placental tissue, processing them for flow cytometry, and linking cellular phenotypes to disease activity and pregnancy outcomes.

title: Early Activation of Lung CD8+ T Cells After Immunization with Live Plasmodium berghei Malaria Sporozoites.
crm_level_3: Leiden University Centre for Infectious Diseases (LU-CID)
summary: In a mouse model immunized intravenously with late-arresting genetically attenuated Plasmodium berghei sporozoites, the lungs exhibited earlier and stronger CD8+ T-cell–driven responses than the liver, including marked increases in activated CD8+, double-negative, and γδ T cells, and higher Granzyme A and TNF expression. These findings indicate the lungs are a key site for early T-cell priming and activation following live sporozoite vaccination, with implications for optimizing whole-sporozoite vaccine strategies.

title: Integrating Rapid Evaporative Ionization Mass Spectrometry Classification with Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption Ionization Mass Spectrometry Imaging and Liquid Chromatography-Tandem Mass Spectrometry to Unveil Glioblastoma Overall Survival Prediction.
summary: This study integrates rapid evaporative ionization mass spectrometry (REIMS), matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry imaging (MALDI-MSI), and LC-MS/MS proteomics to predict overall survival in IDH-wild type glioblastoma from intraoperative lipidomic profiles. REIMS-based PCA/LDA models classified short-term vs prolonged survival with high training accuracy and moderate external validation, MALDI-MSI localized discriminating lipids to tumor regions, and LMD-guided proteomics revealed survival-associated pathways including myelination and integrin signaling.

title: Major human schistosome species express different glycans with immunological and diagnostic implications.
crm_level_3: Leiden University Center for Infectious Diseases
summary: This study maps the glycan repertoire of Schistosoma haematobium across cercariae, adult worms, and eggs, revealing major differences from S. mansoni, including a trihexosyl glycosphingolipid (GSL) core, distinct fucosylation patterns, and abundant glucuronic acid (GlcA)-containing (acidic) GSLs. Functional glycan microarrays show that sera from S. haematobium–infected individuals preferentially recognize acidic egg GSL glycans, highlighting species-specific immunogenic targets with diagnostic potential.

title: Sourdough starter culture and breadmaking process impact wholemeal bread characteristics associated with starch digestibility.
summary: The study investigated how defined sourdough starter cultures and short (100 min) versus long (510 min) breadmaking processes affect wholemeal wheat bread characteristics linked to starch digestibility, and assessed starch digestion using the static INFOGEST 2.0 in vitro protocol. While sourdoughs and longer fermentations markedly altered bread pH, titratable acidity, specific volume, and water-extractable arabinoxylan, all breads showed rapid in vitro starch digestion reaching a plateau by 30 minutes, with only slight, non-significant increases in resistant starch in long-fermented sourdough breads, indicating further work is needed to optimize fermentation for health benefits.

title: Candida albicans and Staphylococcus aureus reciprocally promote their virulence factor secretion and pro-inflammatory effects.
crm_level_3: Molecular Biology and Microbial Food Safety
summary: This study shows that co-culturing Candida albicans and Staphylococcus aureus increases secretion of multiple cytolytic, proteolytic, and lipolytic virulence factors and augments non-extracellular virulence factors, enhancing fungal invasion, immune evasion, and bacterial toxin production (partly via pH maintenance). Secretomes from co-cultures induce stronger pro-inflammatory transcriptional responses in human THP-1-derived macrophages (e.g., TNF, NFκB, TLR signaling) and greater cytotoxicity to oral epithelial cells than monocultures, offering mechanistic insight into heightened morbidity during co-infection.

title: Pre-formation loading of extracellular vesicles with exogenous molecules using photoporation.
summary: The study demonstrates that photoporation of producer HEK293T cells can pre-load extracellular vesicles (EVs) with exogenous macromolecules while preserving EV secretion, size, charge, and tetraspanin profiles. Targeted anti-EGFP nanobodies yielded higher EV loading (up to 53% AF647+ EVs; ~18% double-labeled EGFP-AF647 EVs) than non-targeted dextran (~12% AF647+ EVs; ~3% double-labeled), highlighting the advantage of active targeting during pre-formation loading.

title: Proximity-enhanced cysteine-histidine crosslinking for elucidating intrinsically disordered and other protein complexes.
summary: The study introduces a proximity-enhanced, dual-electrophile histidine-trap crosslinker (maleimide–cyclohexenone) that enables selective Cys–His crosslinking to stabilize and probe protein complexes involving intrinsically disordered partners of 14-3-3, with mechanism and SAR validated by crystallography, intact MS, and peptide panels. Applying this approach to full-length hyperphosphorylated Tau revealed a cryptic 14-3-3 binding site at pSer356 and, via an equilibrium model, demonstrated its functional relevance at cellular concentrations, prompting a re-evaluation of 14-3-3/Tau interaction mechanisms.

title: Structure-in-Void Quasi-Bound State in the Continuum Metasurface for Deeply Subwavelength Nanostructure Metrology.
crm_level_3: Physics of Information in Matter and Center for Nanophotonics
summary: The paper introduces a structure-in-void quasi-BIC dielectric metasurface that enables optical readout of deeply subwavelength feature widths (critical dimensions) by embedding sub-10 nm gratings inside the void of a meta-atom and tracking Fano resonance shifts. Simulations predict ~40.5 nm resonance shift per 1 nm CD change at ~7 nm features with 1.8 nm linewidth (Q≈805), while experiments on larger CDs validate the concept and show the shifts map to an effective refractive index of the structured void with a sensitivity of 262 nm/RIU and FOM≈146.

title: Medicinal plant use in a context of coloniality: Congolese perspectives on lost and preserved healing traditions in Belgium.
summary: This qualitative study explores how coloniality shapes medicinal plant use, knowledge transmission, and healthcare choices among people of Congolese descent living in Belgium. Through reflexive thematic analysis of in-person, semi-structured interviews, the authors show that experiences of racism, distrust of Western pharmaceuticals, religious tensions, and acculturation pressures influence both the preservation and abandonment of plant-based healing practices in a postcolonial context.

title: Growth Propagation of Liquid Spawn on Non-Woven Hemp Mats to Inform Digital Biofabrication of Mycelium-Based Composites.
summary: This study evaluates liquid spawn as a precise inoculation method for digitally biofabricating mycelium-based composites by characterizing the growth kinetics of Ganoderma lucidum and Pleurotus ostreatus on non-woven hemp mats under different media (YPD, CYM), static vs. shaking precultures, and dilution regimes. Results show that CYM and shaking precultures generally accelerate coverage, lower dilutions promote faster and fuller colonization, and liquid spawn enables controlled, mold-free deposition suitable for digital fabrication workflows.

title: NLRP3 Inflammasome Inhibition by the Novel Bispecific Antibody InflamAb Attenuates Atherosclerosis in Apolipoprotein E-Deficient Mice.
summary: This study develops and tests InflamAb, a bispecific antibody that uses IL-1R1 for cellular entry to inhibit the intracellular NLRP3 inflammasome, thereby suppressing IL-1β production. In Apoe-/- mice, InflamAb reduced atherosclerotic plaque development and decreased macrophage and necrotic core content, and in established lesions it improved stability markers without altering systemic leukocyte counts or cholesterol.

title: Nanoparticle accumulation and penetration in 3D tumor models: the effect of size, shape, and surface charge.
summary: This study systematically evaluates how gold nanoparticle size, shape, and surface charge affect uptake in A549 cell monolayers and accumulation/penetration in 3D tumor spheroids using two-photon/confocal microscopy and a custom penetration analysis algorithm. Larger and spherical nanoparticles showed higher cellular uptake but poorer penetration than smaller ones, negatively charged particles accumulated and penetrated slightly better than neutral/positive ones, and spheres outperformed rods in both accumulation and penetration.

title: Rumen metabolic environment of dairy cows varying in susceptibility of subacute ruminal acidosis modifies in vitro bacterial composition and fermentation.
summary: This study tested how sterile ruminal supernatant from dairy cows differing in susceptibility to subacute ruminal acidosis (SARA) alters in vitro fermentation and bacterial communities. Supernatant from unsusceptible cows increased total volatile fatty acids and lactate and supported higher relative abundances of Firmicutes and cellulolytic taxa, whereas supernatant from susceptible cows increased Prevotella, with effects generally consistent across pH 6.8 and 5.8 (though fermentation was limited at pH 5.8).

title: iDeepLC: Chemical Structure Information Yields Improved Retention Time Prediction of Peptides with Unseen Modifications.
summary: The study introduces iDeepLC, an enhanced deep learning model for peptide LC retention time prediction that augments DeepLC with chemical structural information via the MolLogP descriptor derived from SMILES using RDKit. iDeepLC matches DeepLC on unmodified peptides while improving generalization and accuracy for unseen modifications and amino acids, and is released as open-source software.

title: Biphasic CAPA-IVM Improves Equine Oocyte Quality and Subsequent Embryo Development Without Inducing Genetic Aberrations.
summary: This study tested a CNP-based biphasic CAPA-IVM in horses and found that a short pre-maturation (6 h) significantly increased oocyte maturation, cleavage, and blastocyst rates after ICSI without elevating chromosomal abnormalities, while a long pre-maturation (24 h) improved maturation but showed aging morphology and reduced developmental outcomes. Single-oocyte proteomics showed broadly similar proteomes between short CAPA-IVM and standard IVM with enrichment of cytoskeleton and ribosome-related pathways, calcium oscillations remained largely irregular, and blastocysts displayed high euploidy across conditions.

title: Impact of Acute and Sub-Acute Gluten Exposure on Gastrointestinal Symptoms and Psychological Responses in Non-Coeliac Gluten Sensitivity: A Randomised Crossover Study.
summary: In a single-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled crossover trial, 16 individuals with non-coeliac gluten sensitivity (NCGS) and 20 healthy controls received acute (16 g) and sub-acute (5 days, 16 g/day) gluten challenges versus placebo to assess psychological, gastrointestinal, and biological responses. NCGS participants showed higher baseline negative affect, greater acute fatigue, and higher sub-acute GI symptoms, but effects were not gluten-specific and no changes were observed in intestinal permeability, hsCRP, or cortisol, suggesting prominent nocebo and psychological contributions rather than gluten-driven mechanisms.

title: Cellular and molecular landscapes of inflammation in anterior cruciate ligament rupture patients are independent on concurrent meniscal injury.
summary: This study compared inflammatory cellular and molecular profiles, as well as patient-reported outcomes, between anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) rupture patients with and without concurrent meniscal injury. Across synovium, synovial fluid, and blood, no significant differences were found in histology, immune cell composition, synovial gene expression, or serum/synovial fluid-induced pathway activation, and postoperative outcomes improved in both groups with only subtle differences, while synovial inflammation decreased with time since injury.

title: Cell cycle arrest enhances CD8+ T cell effector function by potentiating glucose metabolism and IL-2 signaling.
summary: The study shows that transiently arresting the cell cycle of activated CD8+ T cells (with HU, CDK inhibitors or topotecan) uncouples proliferation from differentiation and imprints a high-energy metabolic state (enhanced glycolysis and cholesterol biosynthesis) alongside elevated IL-2/STAT5 signaling, which together drive rapid expansion and superior effector function upon release. This metabolic priming improves tumor control and synergizes with checkpoint blockade, adoptive transfer, and therapeutic vaccination, with parallel metabolic changes observed in patient biopsies after ribociclib.

title: Targeting the DNA damage response prevents regrowth of colorectal peritoneal metastasis-derived organoids following treatment with mitomycin C.
summary: This study shows that inhibiting the DNA damage response, especially ATR inhibition with berzosertib, prevents regrowth of colorectal peritoneal metastasis-derived organoids after mitomycin C (MMC) treatment, including when MMC is applied for 90 minutes to model HIPEC. Multiple DDR inhibitors (ATR, CHK1, WEE1) combined with MMC synergistically eradicated organoids across diverse histopathological subtypes, supporting evaluation of adjuvant DDR inhibition post-CRS/HIPEC to reduce recurrence.

title: Carbon upshift in Lactococcus cremoris elicits immediate initiation of proteome-wide adaptation, coinciding with growth acceleration and pyruvate dissipation switching
summary: This study examined how Lactococcus cremoris rapidly reprograms its proteome after a sudden shift from galactose to glucose, showing immediate growth acceleration and proteome-wide adaptation that largely proceeds via halted production and dilution-by-growth of redundant proteins. A notable exception is the active degradation of several 4Fe-4S–dependent proteins, including the pyruvate formate lyase activator (PflA), which facilitates a rapid switch from mixed-acid to homolactic fermentation by reorienting pyruvate dissipation.

title: The Neurolipid Atlas: a lipidomics resource for neurodegenerative diseases.
crm_level_3: Center for Neurogenomics and Cognitive Research
summary: This study introduces the Neurolipid Atlas, an open-access data commons and browser for standardized neurolipidomics, and shows that iPSC-derived neurons, astrocytes, and microglia recapitulate in vivo brain lipotypes. Using multiomics, the authors demonstrate that APOE4 drives cholesterol ester accumulation in human astrocytes, suppressing interferon/MHC I–immunoproteasome pathways, while human AD brain tissue also exhibits increased neutral lipids, particularly cholesterol esters.

title: Disruption of tRNA threonylation triggers RIG-I mediated anti-tumour immune response.
summary: Loss of the tRNA t6A-modifying enzyme OSGEP disrupts ANN codon decoding, induces proteotoxic stress and HRI-dependent stress granule formation, and activates RIG-I to drive strong T cell–mediated anti-tumor immunity in melanoma. An OSGEP/t6A-linked gene signature correlates with T-cell infiltration and improved survival in melanoma patients, positioning t6A modulation as a therapeutic lever for immunologically ‘cold’ tumors.

title: Non-thermal plasma as promising anti-cancer therapy against bladder cancer by inducing DNA damage and cell cycle arrest.
summary: This study evaluates plasma-activated solution (PAS), generated by non-thermal plasma irradiation of PBS, as an anti-cancer treatment for human bladder cancer cells, demonstrating that PAS induces intracellular ROS, DNA damage, and G1 cell-cycle arrest/senescence. Phosphoproteomics revealed activation of DNA damage checkpoint signaling, and combining PAS with mitomycin C produced synergistic cytotoxicity, highlighting PAS’s potential for clinical combination therapy.

title: Endocytosis of the damage-associated molecular pattern receptor PEPR1 is BAK1-dependent.
summary: This study shows that the damage-associated molecular pattern receptor PEPR1 requires the co-receptor BAK1, specifically phosphorylation of BAK1’s C-terminal tail and PEPR1’s own kinase activity, to undergo ligand-triggered, clathrin-mediated endocytosis in Arabidopsis. Using partially functional GFP-tagged BAK1 insertion variants, the authors demonstrate that PEPR1 and BAK1 are co-internalized upon Pep1 treatment, and that in vitro PEPR1 can trans-phosphorylate BAK1 but not vice versa, linking BAK1 phosphocode to both immune signaling and receptor trafficking.

title: Proteome-Wide Profiling of Olaparib Interactors Using a Biotinylated Photoaffinity Probe.
summary: The authors synthesized a biotinylated diazirine photoaffinity probe based on olaparib that eliminates the need for copper-catalyzed reporter conjugation, and used it to profile direct protein interactors in HeLa whole-cell lysates by quantitative proteomics. The probe enriched PARP1/2 and other ARTDs and uncovered additional interactors such as CDK8/19, with specificity verified by UV-dependent crosslinking, competition with unlabeled olaparib, and western blot validation.

title: HIV-1 envelope trimer vaccine induces sex-associated differences in antibody responses: a phase 1 clinical trial.
summary: In a phase 1 trial of an MPLA-adjuvanted HIV-1 ConM SOSIP.v7 trimer vaccine in HIV-negative adults, the regimen was safe and elicited robust strain-specific binding and autologous neutralizing antibodies, with markedly higher neutralization titers in female-born participants than males. Despite stronger serologic responses in females, males showed higher somatic hypermutation in vaccine-specific memory B cells, and female-derived PBMCs secreted more IL-6 to MPLA, suggesting innate sex-associated differences may underlie divergent antibody outcomes.

title: Metagenomics Study of the Commercial Tomato Virome Focused on Virus Species of Epidemiological Interest.
summary: This study applied a virus-like particle (VLP) enrichment metagenomics workflow (NetoVIR) and the ViPER bioinformatics pipeline to 101 tomato plant samples from 13 countries, identifying 43 viral species with PepMV, ToBRFV, and STV as most prevalent and generating genomes for phylogenetic analyses. The work highlights low intra-genotype diversity for PepMV, ToBRFV, and STV, documents sporadic detections of ToTV, ToFBV, and CMV, and finds no association between STV detection and symptom presence, thereby refining understanding of the commercial tomato virome and its epidemiologically important members.

title: A goatpox but not sheeppox heterologous live attenuated vaccines provide complete protection against lumpy skin disease in cattle under experimental conditions.
summary: Using a standardized vaccination/challenge model in cattle, the study compared four sheeppox-based and one goatpox-based heterologous live attenuated vaccines against lumpy skin disease virus (LSDV). All sheeppox vaccines failed to fully protect (with nodules, viremia and organ viral genomes detected), whereas the goatpox vaccine Caprivac provided complete protection and induced humoral and cellular responses comparable to homologous LSDV vaccines.

title: Decolonial knowledge in Practice: a mestiza reflection on sentipensar in indigenous Nasa epistemologies.
summary: This article explores the Nasa concept of sentipensar—an embodied, relational way of knowing that integrates feeling, thinking, ritual, territory, and collective decision-making—and shows how it animates Indigenous governance and everyday practices in northern Cauca, Colombia. Drawing on participatory action research with the Guardia Indígena, it argues that sentipensar is a decolonial epistemology made visible through territorial patrols, rituals, the tulpa, and assemblies, challenging Western epistemic dualisms and centering the body as a first territory of knowledge.

title: Beyond growth: comparative impact of plastics and natural particles on EPS dynamics and aggregation in Rhodomonas Salina.
summary: This study examined how virgin and weathered PET micro/nanoplastics and the natural particle kaolin affect growth, extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), and aggregation in a Rhodomonas salina algae-bacteria consortium. Weathered PET and kaolin caused stronger growth inhibition and larger increases in bound EPS and aggregate number/size than virgin PET, indicating particle properties (e.g., surface chemistry, hydrophilicity) rather than material identity primarily drive stress responses and EPS-mediated aggregation.

title: Monitoring trace minerals and heavy metals in liver of free-living large herbivores in the Netherlands.
summary: This study measured trace minerals and heavy metals in liver samples from free-living Heck cattle, Konik horses, and red deer in the Oostvaardersplassen (Netherlands) over 2003–2023 to establish species-specific reference intervals and assess temporal, seasonal, and age-related trends. Using ICP-MS, the authors found distinct species profiles (e.g., higher copper in red deer, higher iron and lead in horses), general declines over time in iron and lead, and reference intervals that differ from livestock standards, underscoring the need for context-specific baselines in wildlife health monitoring.

title: Benchmarking of computational demultiplexing methods for single-nucleus RNA sequencing data.
summary: This study benchmarks genetic demultiplexing tools (Vireo, Souporcell, Freemuxlet, scSplit) for single-nucleus RNA-seq, comparing SNP sources (SNP arrays and matched bulk RNA-seq via BCFtools, FreeBayes, cellSNP) across simulated pools of 2, 4, and 6 samples with varying doublet rates, and validating with sex-linked genes. Vireo consistently achieved the best accuracy and speed, accuracy declined with increasing doublets, and the authors provide an implementation pipeline (including mixed-species demultiplexing) that improves doublet detection and cell annotation in human heart snRNA-seq data.

title: RNA-associated glycoconjugates highlight potential ambiguities in glycoRNA analysis.
summary: This study shows that non-RNA N-glycoconjugates co-purify with RNA and can mimic reported properties of glycoRNA, leading to apparent RNase sensitivity artifacts that depend on silica column cleanup conditions. The authors demonstrate that these glycoconjugates are RNase-resistant yet are lost during silica-based purification after RNase digestion, propose simple controls to distinguish true glycoRNA from co-isolated glycoconjugates, and reveal that increased alcohol or exogenous RNA rescues silica capture of the glycoconjugates.

title: Hypersensitivity to Excipients in Drugs: An EAACI Position Paper.
summary: This EAACI position paper reviews the evidence for immediate and delayed drug hypersensitivity reactions caused by excipients such as polyethylene glycol (PEG), polysorbates, poloxamers, gelatin, methylcelluloses, povidone, mannitol, and certain preservatives, and provides consensus-based recommendations for recognition, diagnosis, and management. It emphasizes targeted skin testing, selective use of in vitro assays (BAT, sIgE), careful consideration of drug provocation testing, and practical avoidance strategies, highlighting unmet needs in standardization, access to pure excipients, and labeling harmonization.

title: A Modified Sample Preparation Protocol for High-Efficiency Lab-on-a-Disk-Based Separation and Single-Image Quantification of Soil-Transmitted Helminth Parasite Eggs in Stool.
summary: This study refines the sample preparation workflow for a lab-on-a-disk (SIMPAQ) device to improve capture and single-image quantification of soil-transmitted helminth (STH) eggs in stool. By adding targeted washing steps, switching to a finer first filter, reducing stool input, and using a surfactant-enriched flotation solution, the authors substantially reduced egg loss and debris, boosting Field-of-View capture efficiency from ~31% (reported previously) to ~74% for eggs and enabling clearer, single-image counts at low egg loads.

title: AAV-mediated long-term TBX18 expression causes cardiac fibrosis and fails to induce pacemaker activity in rodents.
summary: In rodent models, long-term AAV-mediated expression of TBX18 caused severe cardiac fibrosis at high levels and, when reduced to nonfibrogenic levels, suppressed working myocardial genes without inducing a pacemaker program or functional pacing, whereas AAV-Hcn2 produced robust ectopic ventricular pacing in the presence of isoproterenol. These findings indicate TBX18 is neither sufficient nor necessary for pacemaker induction under noncytotoxic expression, while Hcn2 remains a viable candidate for biological pacemaker development.

title: Protocol to generate a 3D atherogenesis-on-chip model for studying endothelial-macrophage crosstalk in atherogenesis.
summary: This STAR Protocol describes building a 3D atherogenesis-on-chip model on the Emulate dual-channel perfusion platform that co-cultures human aortic endothelial cells with PBMC-derived macrophages embedded in a collagen-I gel to study endothelial–macrophage crosstalk. It details chip activation/coating, cell seeding and IL-1β stimulation, monocyte isolation, collagen gel embedding, organ-chip culture and sampling, and downstream analyses (immunofluorescence, flow cytometry, qPCR, secretome profiling), including an IL1R knockdown perturbation in endothelial cells.

title: A comparative study of organoid-derived and cell line-derived intestinal epithelial models.
summary: This study directly compares human duodenum organoid-derived epithelial monolayers with Caco-2/HT29 (9:1) coculture monolayers grown on Transwells, assessing structure, barrier function, and secretome under matched conditions. Both models formed polarized, tight barriers with similar TEER, but organoids showed lower Lucifer Yellow permeability, villus/crypt-like features, uniform MUC2 distribution, and higher basolateral EGF secretion, whereas the cell line model had longer/denser microvilli and higher apical VEGF secretion.

title: Spatial Omics Technologies in Glioblastoma Research: Principles, Applications, and Best Practices.
crm_level_3: Translational Cell and Tissue Research Unit
summary: This review synthesizes recent advances in spatial omics applied to human glioblastoma, comparing platforms (transcriptomic, proteomic, and multi-omic), cohort designs, and key biological insights into spatially organized tumor ecosystems, immune architecture, and treatment-induced remodeling. It outlines limitations in current studies and proposes best practices and a roadmap for standardization, multimodal integration, and clinical translation of spatial biomarkers in precision neuro-oncology.

title: Predicting the developmental toxicity of 8-methyl-benzo[a]pyrene (BaP) by physiologically based kinetic (PBK) modeling-facilitated reverse dosimetry and read-across from BaP.
summary: This study developed and validated a physiologically based kinetic (PBK) model for 8‑methyl‑benzo[a]pyrene (8‑MBaP) in rats using read‑across from benzo[a]pyrene (BaP) and reverse dosimetry of in vitro mouse embryonic stem cell test (mEST) data for its active metabolite 3‑OH‑8‑MBaP. The model predicted an in vivo developmental toxicity ED50 for 8‑MBaP of 10.5 mg/kg bw (single oral dose), about 1.3-fold lower than BaP, and reproduced time-course blood concentrations for parent compounds and their 3‑OH metabolites against literature and new rat kinetic data.

title: Discovery of microbial glycoside hydrolases via enrichment and metaproteomics.
summary: The study combines microbial enrichment under acidic, thermophilic conditions with metagenomics and metaproteomics to discover pullulan-degrading glycoside hydrolases from complex environmental communities. Enrichments (57°C, pH 4.5) selected Alicyclobacillus as dominant, and metaproteomics narrowed thousands of genes to a handful of secreted GH13 candidates absent from the inoculum, indicating an extracellular AmyA-like and intracellular CdaA-like two-step pullulan degradation pathway.

title: Usutu virus NS4A induces autophagy and is targeted by the selective autophagy receptor p62/SQSTM1 for degradation.
summary: The study maps the host interactome of Usutu virus (USUV) NS4A using TurboID-based proximity labeling and mass spectrometry, revealing enrichment of autophagy-related proteins and showing that NS4A induces autophagosomes. The selective autophagy receptor p62/SQSTM1 binds NS4A and promotes its autophagic degradation, and p62 knockdown enhances USUV replication, indicating an antiviral role for p62, while general modulation of canonical autophagy had little effect on virus replication.

title: Protocol for functional screening of CFTR-targeted genetic therapies in patient-derived organoids using DETECTOR deep-learning-based analysis.
summary: This STAR Protocol describes a medium‑throughput workflow to functionally screen CFTR-targeted gene editing or addition strategies in patient-derived intestinal organoids, using a deep-learning tool called DETECTOR to automatically quantify forskolin-induced swelling (FIS) phenotypes. It details wet‑lab steps for organoid dissociation, lentiviral delivery, culture and imaging, as well as software setup, use of pretrained models, and guidance for retraining DETECTOR’s counting and swelling detection models on custom datasets.

title: Protocol for imaging-based quantification of RNAPII clearance during transcription-coupled DNA repair.
summary: This STAR Protocols article presents an imaging-based method to quantify clearance of elongating RNA polymerase II (RNAPII) from sites of localized UV-C–induced DNA damage in adherent human cells, enabling assessment of transcription-coupled DNA repair (TCR) efficiency. It details UV damage induction, DRB treatment to restrict analysis to pre-elongating RNAPII, immunofluorescent detection of CPDs and RNAPII-S2P, and ImageJ-based quantification, with example outcomes showing TCR factor dependence (e.g., CSB/CSA).

title: Freeze-Drying in Sucrose Followed by Cryomilling Enables the Formulation of sa-mRNA-LNP Powders for Inhalation.
summary: The study demonstrates that self-amplifying mRNA lipid nanoparticles (sa-mRNA–LNPs) can be stabilized by freeze-drying in 20% sucrose to maintain functionality for at least 8 weeks at 4 °C, while liquid formulations remain stable only at −20 to −80 °C. Subsequent cryomilling of the lyophilized cake with 4 wt-% leucine yields respirable dry powders that retain ~60% functional activity and exhibit suitable aerosol performance for deep-lung delivery using a Cyclops dry powder inhaler (MMAD ≈ 4.13 µm).

title: Structural Insights Into Complement Inhibition: Visualizing Distinct Binding Modes of C4b-Binding Protein Complexes With C4b and SAP.
crm_level_3: Bijvoet Center for Biomolecular Research and Utrecht Institute for Pharmaceutical Sciences
summary: This study uses an integrative structural proteomics approach—mass photometry, high-speed AFM, and cross-linking mass spectrometry—to define how human C4b-binding protein (C4BP) engages complement C4b and serum amyloid P component (SAP). It reveals two distinct modes: C4b binds via the distal CCP1–4 domains of a single C4BPα ‘leg’ allowing multiple C4b per C4BP, whereas SAP binds 1:1 to the entire spider-like C4BP assembly primarily through the oligomerization core, with CCP8 and CCP1 wrapping around the SAP pentamer’s faces, explaining potential crosstalk that dampens C4BP’s C4b-cofactor activity when SAP is bound.

title: Cuts or carcasses? Diet form affects fecal microbial and animal fiber fractions in a large carnivore, the Asiatic lion.
summary: This study tested how different raw diet forms (meat on bone vs. carcasses with or without skin/hair) affect fecal microbiota and fecal characteristics in zoo-housed Asiatic lions. Carcasses with skin/hair increased fecal particle size and animal fiber excretion and shifted the microbiome (e.g., decreased Proteobacteria and increased Actinobacteria and Fusobacteria), while fecal ash, calcium, and phosphorus patterns suggested lower bone intake on skin-on carcasses.

title: Interest of inulin in obesity: comparison of the prebiotic effect of edible-food sources versus purified inulin from chicory root.
summary: In high-fat diet-fed mice, equal fructan doses delivered as purified chicory inulin or as lyophilized scorzonera both shifted gut microbiota (notably increasing Bifidobacterium and reducing Desulfovibrionaceae) and reduced food intake, but they produced distinct physiological effects. Chicory inulin lowered hepatic lipids and triglycerides, while scorzonera enhanced intestinal antimicrobial peptides, immunity markers, and crypt depth, and increased Akkermansia while decreasing Bacteroides.

title: Sodium chloride enhances suberization in seminal roots but does not affect cutinized leaf barriers in cultivated and wild barley.
summary: The study compared a cultivated barley cultivar (Scarlett) and a wild accession (Pakistan) under hydroponic NaCl stress (80, 180, 280 mM) and found that leaf cuticular barriers were largely unaffected while roots showed pronounced increases in endodermal suberization, especially at the root tip. No exodermis formed in either genotype, the wild accession did not outperform the cultivar, and the authors suggest targeting exodermis formation as a potential breeding strategy for improved salt tolerance.

title: The nucleus as a mechanobiological hub in muscle aging.
summary: This review synthesizes evidence that the nucleus functions as a central mechanobiological hub in skeletal muscle, integrating forces from the extracellular matrix and cytoskeleton via the LINC complex and nuclear lamina to influence gene regulation, and argues that age-related remodeling of these systems contributes to sarcopenia. It surveys alterations in ECM stiffness and organization, non-sarcomeric cytoskeleton (microtubules and desmin), LINC components, and lamins in rodents and humans, highlighting nuclear fragility and impaired mechanotransduction in aged muscle and proposing research directions and exercise as a potential countermeasure.

title: Separating Myths From Facts About Bread and Health.
summary: This perspective article reviews scientific evidence on the health impacts of different breads (white factory-produced, wholemeal/wholegrain, sourdough) and the implications of classifying pre-packaged breads as ultra-processed foods. It concludes that while wholegrain breads generally provide additional benefits due to fiber and associated micronutrients, white bread is not intrinsically unhealthy, additives used in factory breads are regulated and generally safe, and fortification policies make white bread an important, affordable contributor to nutrient intake within a balanced diet.

title: Expression, purification, and biophysical characterization of liquid-liquid phase separation of full-length hnRNPA2B1.
summary: The authors present a denaturant-free workflow to express and purify full-length human hnRNPA2B1 using a SUMO tag, high-salt buffers, TEV cleavage, and high-pH storage to obtain highly pure, nucleic-acid–low protein. The purified hnRNPA2B1 undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation under near-physiological conditions and matures into amorphous aggregates, enabling robust biophysical characterization of LLPS and aggregation.

title: Gemistocytic tumor cells programmed for glial scarring characterize T cell confinement in IDH-mutant astrocytoma.
summary: This study shows that in IDH‑mutant astrocytoma, T cells are largely confined to perivascular cuffs that are surrounded by gemistocytic tumor cells (GTCs) and immune‑reactive tumor‑associated macrophages (TAMs), forming networks that mimic glial scarring. Integrative bulk, single‑nucleus, and spatial RNA/protein profiling identifies GTCs as a distinct astrocyte‑like tumor cell subpopulation engaging TAMs via pathways such as SPP1–CD44 and IL‑1β–IL1R1, linking GTC abundance to immune cell recruitment and T‑cell exclusion.

title: Irrationality and transcendence questions in the 'poor man's adèle ring'.
summary: The paper studies arithmetic properties in the 'poor man's adèle ring' A and proves that the element formed by Schur’s q-Fibonacci numbers, (Fp(q)) over primes p, is A-transcendental for every integer q > 1. The authors leverage Rosen’s characterization of A-algebraic elements, congruence properties of q-Fibonacci numbers, and prime-counting arguments to derive a contradiction to algebraicity, thereby removing prior assumptions such as square-free q and GRH.

title: Exploring Neutrophil Heterogeneity and Plasticity in Health and Disease.
summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on neutrophil development, heterogeneity, and plasticity, spanning their ontogeny from bone marrow progenitors to diverse functional and transcriptional states in blood and tissues. It highlights context-dependent neutrophil reprogramming in health and disease (e.g., infection, autoimmunity, cancer), discusses density- and function-based subsets, and outlines emerging therapeutic targets informed by single-cell and mechanistic studies.

title: Loss of TRPV4 is insufficient to promote repair in a spinal cord injury contusion model.
summary: Using conditional and bone marrow chimera mouse models, the authors tested whether loss of TRPV4 in phagocytes improves recovery after contusive spinal cord injury and found no benefit in locomotor recovery, microgliosis, lesion size, or scar formation. Robust engraftment of donor phagocytes was achieved, but neither phagocyte-specific nor whole-body TRPV4 deficiency improved outcomes, suggesting TRPV4’s role in SCI repair is non-essential or compensated by other pathways.

title: Blood and tissue correlates of steroid non-response in checkpoint inhibition-induced immune-related adverse events.
summary: This multi-omics study of immune checkpoint inhibitor-related adverse events, enriched for gastrointestinal toxicities, compared blood and colonic tissue from steroid responders and non-responders to identify correlates of steroid response. It found trends toward elevated type 1/17-skewed CD8+ T cells and cytokines before steroids and persistent T-cell activation after steroids in non-responders, while responders showed early decreases in tissue lymphocyte infiltration, suggesting rapid steroid effects and implicating enhanced type 1/17 immunity in non-response.

title: Epigenomic preconditioning of peripheral monocytes determines their transcriptional response to the tumor microenvironment.
summary: Using a murine Lewis lung carcinoma model, the study shows that distal tumors epigenetically precondition peripheral Ly6Chi monocytes, remodeling promoters and enhancers to repress interferon-responsive programs and prime pro‑inflammatory/pro‑tumoral pathways. Integrated RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, CUT&Run (H3K4me3) and CUT&Tag (H3K4me1, H3K27ac) reveal peripheral enhancer/promoter changes that persist or enable subsequent gene activation after tumor infiltration, implicating IL-1–linked systemic signals and TF motifs such as IRF, C/EBP, AP-1 and STAT.

title: CISD2 ensures adequate ER-mitochondrial coupling, critically supporting mitochondrial function in neurons.
summary: This study shows that the ER–mitochondria tethering protein CISD2 directly interacts with IP3R1 and is essential for maintaining ER–mitochondrial contact sites and Ca2+ transfer, with loss of CISD2 reducing ER-to-mitochondria Ca2+ coupling in both HeLa cells and human iPSC-derived cortical neurons. While HeLa cells tolerate CISD2 loss with minimal metabolic defects, CISD2-deficient neurons exhibit severely blunted glutamate-evoked Ca2+ signals, impaired mitochondrial respiration and membrane potential, elevated autophagic flux, and heightened apoptosis sensitivity.

title: NEOadjuvant Dendritic cell therapy added to first line standard of care in advanced epithelial Ovarian Cancer (NEODOC): protocol of a first-in-human, exploratory, single-centre phase I/II trial in the Netherlands.
summary: JSON parse error

title: Aedes aegypti mosquitoes from Burkina Faso can transmit the chikungunya virus and Zika virus of the African lineage, but not the Zika virus of the Asian lineage.
summary: This study evaluated the vector competence of Aedes aegypti from urban and peri-urban Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, to transmit chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and Zika virus (ZIKV) of African and Asian lineages. Both mosquito populations transmitted CHIKV and African-lineage ZIKV (with CHIKV transmission being dose-dependent), but failed to transmit Asian-lineage ZIKV, underscoring the need for arbovirus surveillance in the region.

title: Impact of sanitary conditions and dietary amino acids on behaviour and brain monoamine levels in piglets.
summary: In a 2×2 factorial experiment, pair-housed female piglets were kept under high vs. low sanitary conditions and fed either an indispensable amino acid (IAA)-deficient diet or given a choice between IAA-deficient and IAA-enriched diets, to assess effects on behavior, blood tryptophan/serotonin, and brain monoamines. Low sanitary conditions lowered plasma tryptophan, platelet serotonin, and multiple brain monoamines (hippocampus and prefrontal cortex) and reduced play behavior, while dietary choice modestly increased plasma tryptophan and reduced damaging behavior but did not mitigate the sanitary-condition effects on brain neurochemistry, likely due to low intake of the AA-enriched diet.

title: A BAC-guided haplotype assembly pipeline increases the resolution of the virus resistance locus CMD2 in cassava.
summary: This study presents a BAC-guided haplotype assembly pipeline that uses ONT ultra‑long reads, BAC sequencing, and optical mapping to improve the assembly of the repeat‑rich CMD2 virus-resistance locus in cassava cultivars 60444 and TME3. The approach restored marker order, resolved two CMD2 haplotypes with higher synteny and contiguity than prior assemblies, and identified 81 putative resistance genes (31 newly detected) within CMD2.

title: Shifting community assembly mechanisms in soil eukaryotes over successional time and their implications for restoration.
summary: The study analyzed how selection, dispersal, and drift shape soil eukaryote (fungi, protists, and animals) communities across a chronosequence from croplands to 6–155-year-old planted forests in Estonia using ITS and CO1 amplicon sequencing. Selection generally structured fungi and protists, dispersal increased in importance with forest age for ectomycorrhizal and saprotrophic fungi and protist omnivores, and drift dominated low-abundance groups—findings used to propose process- and group-specific restoration strategies.

title: Natural Strategies to Preserve Alcohol-Free Beer: Phenolamide Dimers with Anti-Yeast Potential.
summary: The study developed chemo-enzymatic routes to generate dimers of hydroxycinnamic acid derivatives (including poacic acid and hydroxycinnamoylagmatine dimers) and evaluated their anti-yeast activity against Saccharomyces cerevisiae subsp. diastaticus relevant to alcohol-free beer preservation. While monomers and most dimers were inactive, hordatine-like HCAgm dimers (CouAgm-4-O-7′/3-8′-DCouAgm and FerAgm-4-O-7′/3-8′-DFerAgm) and a poacic-acid-derived agmatine amide inhibited wild yeast in beer, highlighting that amidation and oxidative coupling can enhance antiyeast activity; natural barley rootlet dimer pools, however, showed no inhibition, likely due to stereochemical differences, and no activity was seen against L. brevis or tested molds.

title: Single-cell co-mapping reveals relationship between chromatin state and gene expression in early zebrafish development.
crm_level_1: Hubrecht Institute-KNAW (Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences)
summary: This study applies whole-organism T-ChIC to co-map histone modifications (H3K27me3, H3K4me1) and full-length transcriptomes in thousands of single cells from zebrafish embryos (4–24 hpf), revealing that chromatin and transcriptional states are initially weakly coupled and become progressively aligned during development. The authors identify promoter-anchored cis-spreading of H3K27me3 associated with gene silencing and lineage-specific demethylation, and use an interpretable model combining TF expression and chromatin to classify TFs as activators or repressors, highlighting epigenetically regulated factors.

title: The use of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma 2D and 3D models to evaluate NDV infection, replication and induced cell death.
summary: This study compares Newcastle Disease Virus (NDV) infection, replication, and induced cell death across human pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) monolayers, spheroids, and patient-derived organoids (PDOs), showing that 3D morphology strongly limits viral spread, especially to inner layers of spheroids and dense PDOs, while cystic PDOs display variable but often higher susceptibility. The authors conclude that PDOs, which better reflect patient genetics, may be preferable to identify markers of oncolytic response, whereas spheroids and dense PDOs are useful to study infection and spread in 3D contexts.

title: Proteomics- and BRET- screens identify SPRY2 as a Ras effector that impacts its membrane organization.
summary: Using TurboID proximity proteomics combined with BRET-based functional screening, the study identified eight K-Ras G-domain interactors and prioritized APLP2 and SPRY2 for validation. APLP2 associates with K-Ras indirectly via C-Raf, whereas SPRY2—especially its C-terminal fragment—binds active Ras at the plasma membrane in an inhibitor- and lipidation-dependent manner, oligomerizes (including with SPRY4), and likely blocks effector access to dampen MAPK signaling and promote C2C12 differentiation.

title: Decoding bull fertility in vitro: a proteomics exploration from sperm to blastocyst.
summary: This study assessed four Holstein–Friesian bulls for in vitro fertilization outcomes and linked bull-specific proteomic signatures from sperm, early embryos, and blastocysts to polyspermy and embryo quality. Despite similar blastocyst rates, a bull with high polyspermy produced lower-quality blastocysts, and proteomic differences were most pronounced at the blastocyst stage, highlighting the need to screen bulls for polyspermy in IVP programs.

title: One-step induction of human GABAergic neurons promotes presynaptic development & synapse maturation.
summary: The study presents a single-step PiggyBac transposon system co-expressing Ascl1 and Dlx2 that robustly produces pure human iPSC-derived GABAergic neurons, outperforming lentiviral methods which yield mixed neurotransmitter identities. Multi-omics and electrophysiology show synaptic maturation driven primarily by upregulation of presynaptic gene sets, and the neurons integrate with NGN2 excitatory neurons to form defined excitation/inhibition networks.

title: Multivalent Atezolizumab-Liposome Conjugates as Active Immunotherapeutic Platforms for Enhanced PD-L1 Blockade in Melanoma.
summary: The study engineered multivalent atezolizumab-conjugated liposomes and showed that higher antibody density increased binding avidity, cell-surface retention, and 3D spheroid penetration, resulting in superior PD-L1 blockade versus free antibody. Using human melanoma cell lines and PBMC co-cultures, the liposomal format improved apparent kinetic affinity (higher kon, lower koff) while maintaining immunomodulatory activity comparable to free atezolizumab.

title: DNA damage-associated vesicle production in Stenotrophomonas maltophilia is mediated by the maltocin endolysin
summary: DNA damage in Stenotrophomonas maltophilia induces the maltocin endolysin (LysSM), triggering explosive cell lysis and robust vesicle production; deleting mal reduces cell lysis, biofilm formation, and vesiculation. Fluorescence and cryo-EM show vesicles are predominantly single-layered explosive OMVs with fewer O-IMVs and putative cytoplasmic vesicles, and LysSM rapidly accumulates at cell poles upon genotoxic stress.

title: Cerebrospinal fluid proteomic analysis of long-term antihypertensive treatment with amlodipine and atenolol in hypertensive rats.
summary: This study used GeLC-MS/MS proteomics of cerebrospinal fluid from spontaneously hypertensive rats treated long-term with amlodipine or atenolol, compared with normotensive Wistar Kyoto controls, to assess how hypertension and antihypertensive class affect the CSF proteome. Hypertension was associated with pathways related to CNS development, inflammation, and coagulation, while amlodipine predominantly altered gas transport proteins (e.g., CA2, HBA1, HBB) and atenolol modulated complement/coagulation components (e.g., CFH, KNG1, APOE, AHSG), indicating drug class-specific CSF proteomic fingerprints.

title: Microbiota-derived indole metabolites inhibit rotavirus infection in vitro and in vivo and in human infants.
crm_level_1: Amsterdam Institute for Global Health and Development
summary: Across adult challenge, human intestinal enteroid, mouse, and infant datasets, microbiota-derived indole metabolites—particularly indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) and indole-3-propionic acid (IPA)—were associated with reduced rotavirus replication and shedding via aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) signaling. IAA inhibited human rotavirus in enteroids, the AhR agonist indole-3-carbinol lowered murine rotavirus shedding in vivo, and RV-infected Zambian infants had reduced fecal indole metabolites compared to healthy controls.

title: Potential of Proteomics in Forensic Phenotyping: A Focus on Biological Sex Estimation.
summary: This study evaluates the feasibility of using LC–MS/MS proteomics and machine learning to estimate biological sex from human whole blood, identifying key peptide markers (notably from pregnancy zone protein and ceruloplasmin) and achieving high cross-validated accuracy. However, performance degraded on mock, case-like samples due to batch effects and real-world variability, leading the authors to recommend focusing forensic proteomics on source attribution and event timelines rather than phenotypic donor profiling.

title: Addressing hurdles in cultured meat by exploring reduced myogenesis after bovine myoblast expansion.
summary: Primary bovine myoblasts from fetal and adult Belgian Blue cattle can be extensively expanded in vitro (several adult lines surpassing 60–100 doublings with normal karyotypes), but their myogenic differentiation capacity (fusion index) drops sharply and is largely lost by ~25 doublings. Transcriptomic and proteomic comparisons between high- and low-fusing cells revealed broad downregulation of myogenesis, DNA replication/repair, calcium signaling and cytoskeletal pathways in low-fusing cells, suggesting targets (e.g., HEY1, LIMK2, oxytocin/Ca2+ signaling, replication stress mitigation) to preserve or restore fusion.

title: Blood proteome profiling for biomarker discovery in broilers with necrotic enteritis.
summary: The study profiled the blood plasma proteome of broiler chickens with necrotic enteritis using two LC–MS/MS strategies—nano-DDA and Evo-DIA—and found high agreement but greater data completeness with Evo-DIA. Fifteen proteins were differentially expressed in both workflows, and three candidates (CFD, HPS5, MASP2) were validated by ELISA and PRM, with pathway analysis indicating strong activation of humoral and complement-mediated immune responses in diseased birds.

title: FUTURE-AI: international consensus guideline for trustworthy and deployable artificial intelligence in healthcare.
summary: This BMJ paper presents FUTURE-AI, an international consensus guideline for trustworthy and deployable AI in healthcare, built around six principles—fairness, universality, traceability, usability, robustness, and explainability. Developed by 117 experts from 50 countries using a modified Delphi process, it delivers 30 best-practice recommendations and step-by-step operational guidance spanning the full AI lifecycle from design to deployment and monitoring.

title: Antagonistic effects of amino acids support abiotic nano-environments in clay.
summary: The study shows that mixtures of amino acids with differing clay-interaction strengths create antagonistic effects that generate and sustain diverse abiotic nano-environments within Ca-montmorillonite. Strongly interacting proteinogenic amino acids (lysine, arginine) intercalate and stabilize clay layers, while γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) induces partial exfoliation, layer distortion, and nanocavity formation, with both effects coexisting under mixture conditions.

title: Preclinical evaluation of [11C]CHDI-009R for quantification of mutant huntingtin aggregates.
summary: [11C]CHDI-009R, a PET radioligand with high affinity for mutant huntingtin (mHTT) aggregates, showed high in vivo metabolic stability, robust genotype separation in zQ175DN mice, and excellent test-retest reliability, enabling quantification of mHTT aggregates at both 9 and 3 months. These preclinical data support advancing [11C]CHDI-009R to clinical evaluation for imaging cerebral mHTT aggregates.

title: Redox-modulated ERK dynamics support wound-dependent tissue formation during early planarian regeneration.
summary: This study shows that amputation-induced redox signals establish wound orientation-dependent ERK activation gradients that guide early patterning and regeneration in planarians, with higher ERK activity and ROS (superoxide and H2O2) at anterior-facing wounds. MEK/ERK perturbation revealed fragment position- and wound orientation-specific outcomes, uncovered an egr-4–MKP feedback that sustains ERK activation, and demonstrated functional interplay between MAPK-ERK and Wnt/β-catenin pathways during axis re-establishment.

title: Metatranscriptomes of activated sludge microbiomes from saline wastewater treatment plant.
summary: This data descriptor provides 32 metatranscriptomes from the facultative zone of a saline wastewater treatment plant in the Netherlands collected between 2014 and 2017, coupled with extensive process and water quality data. The study details sampling, RNA/cDNA workflows, Illumina MiSeq sequencing, and two bioinformatics pipelines (Kraken2/Bracken and SAMSA2) with technical, in-silico, and ecological validation, and deposits all raw reads and process data in public repositories.

title: How to improve the potential of microalgal biostimulants for abiotic stress mitigation in plants?
summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on microalgal biostimulants for mitigating plant abiotic stresses—drought, salinity, and heat—highlighting how cultivation conditions, extraction strategies, and application methods shape efficacy and modes of action.
