It finds drought tolerance benefits are consistently linked to enhanced photosynthesis, stomatal regulation, osmoprotectants and antioxidants, salt-stress outcomes are highly species- and context-dependent, heat stress remains underexplored, and identifies diversity, practical, and research gaps for future work.

title: Turbulent mixing controls fixation of growing antagonistic populations.
summary: The paper uses numerical simulations of a reaction–diffusion model coupled to 2D incompressible turbulent advection to study fixation in two antagonistic, growing populations, revealing that the Damköhler number (ratio of reproduction to flow timescales) controls which strain fixes by modulating a flow-modified nucleation threshold. An analytical model that combines early-time domain growth with a single mixing timescale quantitatively predicts critical fractions for fixation and fixation times, showing that turbulence elevates nucleation thresholds and that antagonism suppresses mixing by depleting interfaces.

title: The differential effect of Interferon-gamma on acute kidney injury and parasitemia in experimental malaria.
summary: In C57BL/6 mouse models of malaria, IFN-γ deficiency had opposing effects on parasitemia and kidney injury: it reduced parasitemia and protected against MAKI and MA-ARDS in Plasmodium berghei NK65 infections, but increased parasitemia and exacerbated renal injury (including hyaline casts) in P. chabaudi AS infections. IFN-γ drove renal CXCL10 expression in both models without altering TNF-α, indicating that its impact on kidney pathology is largely mediated via its model-dependent effects on parasitemia.

title: Tumor budding and poorly differentiated clusters as a biological continuum in colorectal cancer invasion and prognosis.
summary: This study integrates AI-based detection on H&E slides with spatial transcriptomics and immunohistochemistry to show a biological continuum between poorly differentiated clusters (PDCs) and tumor budding (TB) at the invasive margin of colorectal cancer, with TB exhibiting greater invasive potential. In a cohort of 1,134 Stage I–III CRC resections, nearly 400,000 small clusters/cells were quantified (2-celled clusters most abundant), and combined TB+PDC scoring improved prognostic stratification over either alone, while GeoMx DSP revealed ECM and invasion-associated gene upregulation from pushing borders to PDC to TB regions.

title: Targeting macrophages in liver fibrosis.
crm_level_3: Myeloid Cell Biology in Tissue Damage and Inflammation
summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on the heterogeneity, plasticity, and roles of hepatic macrophages in liver fibrosis across human and animal studies, emphasizing the dynamic balance between pro-fibrotic and pro-resolution programs. It evaluates therapeutic strategies targeting macrophages—including recruitment blockade, in situ reprogramming, and emerging cell-based therapies—highlighting opportunities, translational challenges, and the need for precise, temporally informed interventions.

title: A recursive enzymatic competition network capable of multitask molecular information processing.
summary: The authors present a scalable protease-based enzymatic reaction network that leverages recursive substrate competition to perform reservoir computing, enabling non-linear classification, sensing, and decision-making from peptide, pH, temperature, and light inputs. Enzymes immobilized on hydrogel beads in a temperature-controlled continuous stirred tank reactor produced complex peptide fragments read out by mass spectrometry, achieving tasks such as temperature sensing (25–55 °C, ~1.3 °C accuracy) and light-pulse periodicity discrimination (2–8 min).

title: Blood vessels as primary site of rejection in murine lung transplantation.
summary: Using a murine orthotopic left lung transplantation model with daily immunosuppression, the study maps spatiotemporal rejection dynamics and shows that endothelial cells in blood vessels are the early and primary targets of alloimmune injury, leading to perivascular inflammation, endothelial activation/loss, and subsequent bronchovascular fibrosis. Multicolor flow cytometry, in vivo/ex vivo micro-CT, and spatial proteomics converge to demonstrate a vascular-centered process that precedes and likely drives chronic graft dysfunction, reframing lung rejection as vessel-focused rather than airway-centric.

title: TRAINSPOTTER: profiling nascent protein N-termini indicative of bacterial translation initiation via deformylation-assisted N-terminomics.
summary: The study introduces TRAINSPOTTER, a deformylation-assisted N-terminomics workflow that uses peptide deformylase-mediated hydrophilic shifts and COFRADIC chromatography to selectively isolate nascent, initiation-derived N-termini, thereby mapping bacterial translation initiation sites with amino-acid resolution. Applied to Escherichia coli, the method identified over 1,000 TIS-indicative N-termini (including many alternative starts) and was validated by pulse SILAC, complementing and refining ribosome profiling datasets.

title: Mapping spatial organization of in vitro neuronal networks using high-content imaging.
summary: The study presents a high-content confocal imaging and automated analysis pipeline to reconstruct and quantify entire in vitro neuronal networks from primary mouse cortical, hippocampal, and cerebellar cultures, enabling spatial mapping of thousands of cells per well. The authors reveal a preferred short-range inter-neuronal spacing and small cluster formation, and extract subcellular features such as nuclear size and axon initial segment number, orientation, and length across whole-well datasets.

title: Foamy microglia link oxylipins to disease progression in multiple sclerosis.
summary: This study identifies a distinct population of foamy, GPNMB-positive microglia/macrophages in human multiple sclerosis white-matter lesions that exhibit disrupted lipid metabolism and elevated oxylipins, and links their presence to faster disease progression. Integrated lipidomics, transcriptomics, proteomics and chemical proteomics highlighted monoacylglycerol lipase (MAGL) as an active, targetable enzyme in foamy lesions; its inhibition promoted lesion recovery and reduced microgliosis in a mouse demyelination model, while CSF oxylipins correlated with foamy lesion burden.

title: Stressostat cultivation of Lactococcus lactis improves lactate stress resistance through mutations in RNA polymerase.
summary: Adaptive laboratory evolution using stressostat cultivation generated Lactococcus lactis isolates with enhanced resistance to high lactate, driven by mutations in RNA polymerase β (rpoB) and β′ (rpoC) that reprogrammed proteomes and improved osmotic stress tolerance. Multi-omics and growth assays revealed that lactate primarily imposes osmotic stress, with RNAP mutations elevating arginine deiminase pathway activity and altering osmoregulatory and cell-wall responses, yielding improved growth under high lactate/salt (and occasional trade-offs).

title: Repeated ionizing radiation exposure induces TRIP13 expression, conferring radioresistance in lung cancer cells.
summary: Repeated ionizing radiation elevates TRIP13 expression in non-small cell lung cancer cells, enhancing homologous recombination–mediated DNA repair and conferring radioresistance; manipulating TRIP13 (overexpression, knockout, or inhibition) correspondingly alters radiation sensitivity and DNA repair protein levels. Patient data show high TRIP13 expression correlates with poorer post-radiation survival, and TRIP13 inhibition reduces RAD51/NBS1 in resistant cells, highlighting TRIP13 as a potential therapeutic target.

title: Dietary Fiber and Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Obesity Management: Converging Mechanisms, Interactions, and Strategies for Durable Weight Control.
crm_level_3: Centre for Healthy eating & Food innovation (HeFi)
summary: This narrative review examines how GLP-1 receptor agonists and dietary fibers converge and differ in regulating appetite, metabolism, gut physiology, microbiota, and immunity for obesity management, highlighting GLP-1RA efficacy and limitations (GI adverse effects, cost, dependence) versus fibers’ modest but broad, durable benefits. It proposes conceptual combined and sequential strategies (e.g., fiber-first, GLP-1RA-first with fiber maintenance) and calls for trials testing specific fiber chemistries with GLP-1RAs including microbiome and immune endpoints to optimize long-term outcomes and reduce reliance on pharmacotherapy.

title: In vivo models to study gastrointestinal Salmonella infections.
summary: This review synthesizes current in vivo models used to study gastrointestinal infection by non-typhoidal Salmonella, spanning invertebrates (Caenorhabditis elegans) to vertebrates (zebrafish, chicken, mouse, cattle, pig), and compares their immune systems, gastrointestinal anatomy, infection dynamics, and practical considerations. It emphasizes that no single model fully recapitulates human infection and advocates a complementary, multi-model approach balancing mechanistic insight, ecological relevance, throughput, ethics, and logistics.

title: The C-terminal tail of Cf resistance proteins determines the intensity of the effector-triggered hypersensitive response-related cell death.
summary: This study shows that the short cytoplasmic C-terminal tail of tomato Cf receptor-like proteins determines the intensity of effector-triggered hypersensitive response-related cell death by modulating their association with the co-receptor SOBIR1. Domain swaps, tail truncations, and chimeras with Ve tails reveal that a full-length, Cf-4/9-type tail is required to elicit strong cell death without altering early ROS or MAPK responses, and that Cf-4/9 recruit larger SOBIR1 pools than Cf-2/5.

title: Precise targeting of HIV broadly neutralizing antibody precursors in humans.
summary: In a randomized, double-blind phase 1 trial, a germline-targeting, native-like HIV Env trimer (BG505 SOSIP.v4.1-GT1.1) adjuvanted with AS01B safely primed broadly neutralizing antibody (bnAb) precursors in humans, inducing high-frequency VRC01-class, CD4bs-specific memory B cells and eliciting monoclonal antibodies structurally and functionally similar to VRC01. These responses showed substantial affinity maturation, partial accommodation of key CD4bs glycans (notably N276), and low-level neutralization of select viruses, providing proof-of-concept for precise bnAb-precursor targeting and a foundation for shaping/polishing boosts.

title: Farm conditions shape microbial communities and their association with methane intensity in dairy cattle: insights from the rumen microbiome at the community level.
summary: Across 17 Dutch dairy farms, rumen fluid from 212 cows was profiled by 16S rRNA sequencing and linked to individual methane intensity measured with GreenFeed, showing that diet (especially fresh grass) and lactation stage strongly shaped both microbiota and methane intensity. Despite a balanced comparison of low vs high emitters, only limited and inconsistent taxonomic differences were detected (e.g., Lachnospiraceae common to both; Rikenellaceae/Ruminococcaceae enriched in low and Oscillospiraceae in high emitters), underscoring the difficulty of finding stable microbial markers under real-world variability.

title: Melatonin suppresses cancer cell proliferation, DNA repair and expression of the oncogene TRIP13.
summary: This study shows that melatonin suppresses proliferation and DNA repair in non-small cell lung cancer cell lines by downregulating the oncogene TRIP13 via the MTNR1B (MT2) receptor, leading to reduced RAD51 and XRCC5 levels and impaired homologous recombination and non-homologous end-joining. Combining melatonin with the TRIP13 inhibitor DCZ0415 produced additive anti-proliferative effects, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy for NSCLC.

title: Tryptophan metabolites profile predict remission with dietary therapy in pediatric Crohn's disease.
summary: This diagnostic accuracy study in 26 children with mild-to-moderate Crohn’s disease found that baseline fecal tryptophan metabolite profiles, particularly elevated kynurenine and specific metabolite ratios (e.g., serotonin/kynurenine, quinolinic acid/kynurenine), strongly predict remission at Week 6 with Crohn’s disease exclusion diet plus partial enteral nutrition or exclusive enteral nutrition. Liquid chromatography–quadrupole mass spectrometry revealed that kynurenine alone achieved AUCs up to 0.97, suggesting baseline fecal tryptophan markers could personalize dietary therapy.

title: Preclinical evaluation of glycan-targeting monoclonal antibodies for bimodal near-infrared fluorescence and photoacoustic imaging of gastrointestinal cancers.
summary: This preclinical study evaluates two glycan-targeting monoclonal antibody tracers, CH88.2-800CW (anti-Lea/c/x) and CH129-800CW (anti-sdi-Lea), for bimodal near-infrared fluorescence and photoacoustic imaging of gastrointestinal cancers. The tracers specifically delineated orthotopic colon and pancreatic tumors in mice with high tumor-to-background ratios and low off-target organ signal, supported by immunohistochemical evidence of target expression in human gastric and colorectal cancers.

title: Impact of asundexian on a panel of coagulation assays.
crm_level_3: Clinical Pharmacology and Toxicology Research Unit
summary: This in vitro study evaluated how the oral FXIa inhibitor asundexian (0–2000 ng/mL) affects a comprehensive panel of coagulation assays using human pooled platelet-poor plasma and whole blood. Asundexian variably prolonged aPTT and intrinsic one-stage factor assays, reduced thrombin generation at low tissue factor or ellagic acid triggers, modestly affected ROTEM INTEM and ACT assays, and had no meaningful effect on PT, extrinsic factor assays, fibrinogen, protein C/S, reptilase time, ecarin assay, or dRVVT-based lupus anticoagulant testing, highlighting reagent-dependent impacts and the need for further clinical validation.

title: Stored L-PRF membranes: safety, morphology, tensile properties, and cell viability-an in vitro pilot study.
summary: This in vitro pilot study assessed whether leukocyte- and platelet-rich fibrin (L-PRF) membranes stored at 4°C in their own exudate for up to 4 weeks maintain safety, structure, mechanics, and cell viability. While no consistent bacterial contamination and largely preserved tensile properties were observed, leukocyte viability declined markedly over time, indicating potential loss of biological functionality with storage.

title: Host-specificity and therapeutic potential of novel Escherichia coli-targeting bacteriophages for bovine mastitis control.
summary: Eight Escherichia coli bacteriophages were isolated and characterized for controlling bovine mastitis, with evaluations of pH/temperature stability, activity in raw/HT/UHT milk, host range, and receptor-binding proteins. Phages were broadly stable and reduced bacterial loads in milk (often below detection, with some regrowth), and specificity was chiefly linked to long tail fiber variability, supporting cocktail/high-MOI strategies while highlighting resistance risks.

title: Investigating the role of stable flies (Stomoxys calcitrans) and biting midges of the genus Culicoides as potential mechanical vectors of African swine fever virus in Lithuania, Poland and Romania.
summary: JSON parse error

title: Dual targeting of CD155/TIGIT and PD-L1/PD-1 immune checkpoints potentiates NK cell-mediated cytotoxicity in medulloblastoma.
summary: The study shows that medulloblastoma (MB) tumor cells express the immune checkpoint ligand CD155 while infiltrating immune cells express TIGIT, and that MB cells can upregulate PD-L1 in response to NK cell-derived interferon-γ. Blocking TIGIT (Tiragolumab) and PD-1/PD-L1 (Durvalumab), especially in combination, enhances primary NK-cell activation and cytotoxicity against MB cell lines and patient-derived xenograft organoids, suggesting a translatable immunotherapeutic strategy for SHH and Group 3 MB.

title: Limited value of Nanopore adaptive sampling in a long-read metagenomic profiling workflow of clinical sputum samples.
summary: This study evaluated Oxford Nanopore adaptive sampling (NAS) on R10.4.1 flowcells for long-read metagenomic profiling of human clinical sputum and found at best ~3.1× bacterial enrichment but severe, rapid pore loss that reduced total sequencing yield by ~80%. Despite extensive troubleshooting (altered library prep, higher loading, multiple washes, RNase treatment), the authors could not identify the cause of pore loss, ruled out NAS and underloading, and concluded that NAS utility is constrained by sample characteristics and unresolved pore degradation issues.

title: Effect of curcumin on the gut microbiota of patients with ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease and healthy participants.
summary: In an open-label study of 29 men with ulcerative colitis or Crohn’s disease in remission and healthy volunteers, 6 g/day curcumin for 8 weeks produced only transient shifts in gut microbiota composition at 4 weeks that returned to baseline by 8 weeks, with no significant changes in alpha diversity or clinical/biochemical parameters. Curcumin was well tolerated, showed very low plasma levels but extremely high fecal levels, and did not induce durable microbiota modulation.

title: LolA and LolB are conserved in Bacteroidota and are crucial for gliding motility and Type IX secretion.
crm_level_3: Research Unit in Biology of Microorganisms (URBM)
summary: The study identifies LolB homologs in the Bacteroidota phylum and shows that multiple LolA/LolB pairs coexist and are functionally specialized, with LolA1 and LolB1 in Flavobacterium johnsoniae required for gliding motility and Type IX secretion. Despite these roles, F. johnsoniae lacking all LolA/LolB proteins remains viable and can still surface-localize lipoproteins, indicating an alternative lipoprotein transport pathway distinct from the canonical Lol system and non-interchangeability with Escherichia coli Lol components.

title: Moisture Content Estimation of Porous Building Stones using Hyperspectral Imaging.
summary: The study presents a SWIR hyperspectral imaging dataset of 36 specimens from six porous building materials (five stones and a red brick) across controlled moisture levels, using the NRAL method to generate pixel-wise moisture maps. Validation against gravimetric measurements and petrographic thin sections shows strong agreement (RMSE 1–2 g/g × 100), revealing material-specific moisture distribution patterns tied to pore structure and texture.

title: Depletion of TP53 in Human Pluripotent Stem Cells Triggers Malignant-Like Behavior.
summary: Using CRISPR/Cas9 to deplete TP53 in human pluripotent stem cells (hESC H9 and hiPSC LU07), the authors found that despite minimal changes in pluripotency and global transcriptomics, TP53 loss induces malignant-like traits, including enhanced clonogenicity, anchorage-independent growth, and increased resistance to cisplatin and gemcitabine. These findings, benchmarked against human germ cell tumor lines (NCCIT, 2102Ep), highlight safety risks of undetected TP53-depleting mutations in hPSCs intended for clinical applications.

title: Patient-Derived 3D Bioprinted Cardiac Organoid Constructs Reveal Key Pathological Features of Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
summary: This study develops human 3D cardiac organoids and bioprinted cardiac organoid constructs from DMD patient-derived hiPSCs, isogenic-corrected lines, and healthy controls, showing that DMD models recapitulate increased cell death, oxidative stress (NOX4/NADPH), calcium handling defects, stiffness, and fibrosis. Embedding organoids in a 7% alginate–5% gelatin hydrogel via bioprinting enhanced structural organization (e.g., Cx43) but accentuated dystrophic phenotypes (apoptosis, dysregulated cardiac/fibrotic markers), providing a scalable platform for disease modeling and therapeutic screening.

title: Protocol to generate human monocyte-derived macrophages in the absence of exogenous proteases and protease inhibitors to study proteolysis.
summary: This protocol describes how to generate human monocyte-derived macrophages from PBMCs and culture them under conditions free of exogenous proteases and protease inhibitors by switching to a defined replacement serum for the final 24 hours. It details monocyte isolation, macrophage differentiation and activation into M(M-CSF), M(LPS/IFN-γ), or M(IL-4), followed by collection of supernatants and cell lysates for protease activity and content analyses.

title: Integrated multi-omics of feces, plasma and urine can describe and differentiate pediatric active Crohn's Disease from remission.
summary: This study integrated fecal microbiome (bacteria and fungi), fecal proteome, and metabolomes from feces, plasma, and urine in 58 pediatric Crohn’s disease patients to distinguish active disease from remission using a machine learning model (AUC 0.80). The integrated analysis identified fecal bacteria and metabolites as most discriminative and implicated purine metabolism—independent of thiopurine use—as a key pathway associated with remission, with interactome links among microbes, metabolites, and proteins across compartments.

title: Endothelial Features Along the Pulmonary Vascular Tree in Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension: Distinctive or Shared Facets?
summary: This study compared endothelial features along large versus (sub)-segmental pulmonary arterial lesions from CTEPH patients and found distinct in situ VEGF-A/VEGFR2 expression patterns but similar in vitro angiogenic and barrier functions of isolated PAECs. Recanalizing vessels in distal lesions comprised both COL15A1-positive and -negative endothelial cells, suggesting contributions from systemic and pulmonary circulations to lesion recanalization.

title: Identification of an anti-inflammatory action of exosome release in P2Y4 loss-mediated cardioprotection.
summary: This study shows that loss of the mouse P2Y4 nucleotide receptor enhances the release of anti-inflammatory plasma exosomes enriched in PD-L1 and adiponectin, which promote M2c macrophage polarization and reduce post‑myocardial infarction fibrosis and T‑cell infiltration. Pharmacologic inhibition of exosome biogenesis with GW4869 abrogated these protective effects and normalized plasma PD-L1 levels, implicating exosomal PD-L1/adiponectin as key mediators of P2Y4 loss–mediated cardioprotection.

title: Half-Pipe Melt Electrowritten Scaffolds Support Engineering of an Immunocompetent Hydrogel-Embedded Intestine-on-a-Chip.
summary: The study presents a melt electrowritten (MEW) half‑pipe scaffold-based, immunocompetent intestine‑on‑a‑chip that supports a Caco‑2 epithelial monolayer interfaced with hydrogel‑embedded monocyte‑derived dendritic cells and downstream T‑cell co‑culture. Compared to Transwell-like systems, the chip achieved comparable barrier integrity with higher metabolic and brush-border activity, and upon stimulation, food allergens caused modest effects whereas toxin A plus LPS disrupted barrier function and biased immune readouts toward type 1 responses, with ovalbumin trends suggesting type 2/regulatory shifts.

title: Proteome and Secretome Profiling of the Melanoma-Induced Transition Toward Immune Incompetent Dendritic Cells Reveals Enhanced IDO1, Cathepsin, and Legumain Activity.
summary: Using LC-MS/MS proteomics and the nascent-secretome labeling method THRONCAT, the authors profiled human cDC2s transitioning to tumor-induced DC3s and found 157 proteomic changes, including upregulated IDO1 and legumain, and a newly synthesized secretome enriched in cathepsins and TGFβI. Enzymatic activities (IDO1, legumain, cysteine cathepsins) were validated in vitro and in patient samples, revealing particularly high cathepsin activity in tumor-associated DC3s.

title: Targeting the Lipid Metabolism Proteins FASN and GPAM in Alveolar Type II Cells Decreases Lung Metastasis.
summary: Spatial metabolomics and transcriptomics of human and mouse lungs show that breast cancer lung metastases stimulate proliferation and SREBP-1–driven lipid synthesis (FASN, GPAM) in neighboring alveolar type II (AT2) cells, enriching surfactant lipids around lesions. Genetic deletion of Fasn in AT2 cells or systemic inhibition of GPAM/FASN reduces lung palmitate-rich lipids and markedly impairs metastasis growth in mice without evident lung toxicity.

title: Composition and liquid-to-solid maturation of protein aggregates contribute to bacterial dormancy development and recovery.
summary: This study shows that in Escherichia coli, protein aggregation precedes and drives dormancy by progressively sequestering energy-production proteins, leading to ATP depletion and persistence, and that continued maturation from liquid-like condensates to solid-like aggregates limits recovery and marks transition to the VBNC state. Disaggregation and regrowth depend primarily on DnaK, and aggregate structure—not lower energy—explains the reduced recoverability of VBNC cells.

title: Site-specific profiling of structure and function of Igµ B cell receptor glycans.
summary: The study profiles site-specific N-glycosylation at all four conserved sites (N46, N209, N272, N279) of human Igμ B cell receptors from primary naive and memory B cells and compares them to serum IgM and to matched BCR vs secreted IgM produced by a Ramos cell line. Glycosylation patterns are highly conserved between naive and memory B cells and differ from serum IgM mainly by higher sialylation and lower bisection on BCRs; functionally, individual glycans are not required for surface expression, internalization, or early signaling, though the N209 glycan supports optimal antigen binding, likely by stabilizing BCR structure.

title: In-depth plasma N-glycoproteome profiling using narrow-window data-independent acquisition on the Orbitrap Astral mass spectrometer.
crm_level_3: Bijvoet Centre for Biomolecular Research and Utrecht Institute for Pharmaceutical Sciences
summary: The study develops a narrow-window DIA workflow (nGlycoDIA) on the Orbitrap Astral mass spectrometer to enable fast, in-depth profiling of the human plasma N-glycoproteome, achieving over 3000 unique glycoPSMs from 181 glycoproteins in 40 minutes and maintaining high coverage with 10–20 minute gradients. By optimizing the MS1 m/z range (955–1655), 3 Th isolation windows, and ~30% NCE, the method detects very low-abundance glycoproteins (including cytokines) across ~7 orders of magnitude, with and without cotton-HILIC glycopeptide enrichment.

title: Surface Plasmon Resonance as a Potential Diagnostic Tool for the Detection of CXC Chemokine Receptor 4 (CXCR4) on Extracellular Vesicles.
summary: The study develops a standardized, label-free surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assay on a Biacore T200 to detect and profile CXCR4 on extracellular vesicles (EVs) using tetraspanin (CD9, CD63, CD81) and CXCR4 antibodies, achieving limits of detection around 1.6–2.0 × 10^8 particles/mL with high repeatability and chip regenerability. EVs isolated from seven human cell lines exhibited distinct SPR molecular fingerprints whose CXCR4 signals correlated with parental cell CXCR4 expression by flow cytometry, and EV detection was demonstrated both in purified fractions and directly in complex media, with single-EV colocalization benchmarking by SP-IRIS (ExoView).

title: Loss of STARD7 Triggers Metabolic Reprogramming and Cell Cycle Arrest in Breast Cancer.
summary: The study shows that loss of the lipid transfer protein STARD7 in breast cancer induces metabolic reprogramming with elevated S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) and carnitine derivatives, leading to increased H3K27me3, repression of cell-cycle genes, G1 arrest, and impaired ERα and EGFR signaling, alongside altered mitochondria–ER contacts, endosomal trafficking, autophagy, and ciliogenesis. STARD7 is overexpressed in breast cancers and is required to sustain proliferation by maintaining mitochondrial lipid transfer and signaling pathways.

title: Induced ubiquitination of the partially disordered estrogen receptor alpha via a 14-3-3 directed molecular glue-PROTAC.
summary: The study develops molecular glue-PROTACs (MGPROTACs) by covalently linking a 14-3-3/ERα molecular glue (FC-NAc) to a VHL ligand to recruit VHL to a 14-3-3/ERα complex, enabling cooperative complex formation and induced ubiquitination. Linker length and chemistry governed cooperativity and site-selective ubiquitination, with cryo-EM revealing a de novo VHL–14-3-3ζ interface; MGPROTACs drove robust in vitro ubiquitination of both ERα(LBD_F) and 14-3-3ζ, although cellular degradation of ERα was not observed despite increased complex engagement in MCF-7 cells.

title: PRC2 loss impairs small cell lung cancer tumorigenesis and enhances sensitivity to G9a/GLP inhibition.
summary: The study shows that loss of the PRC2 structural component EED blocks small cell lung cancer (SCLC) tumorigenesis, whereas enzymatic inhibition of EZH2 alone does not impede tumor growth. Prolonged EZH2 inhibition reprograms neuroendocrine SCLC cells to become vulnerable to G9a/GLP inhibition by inducing oxidative stress, leading to improved outcomes in xenograft models when the drugs are combined.

title: Polypept(o)ide-Based Core-Shell Bottlebrush Polymers: A Versatile Platform for Drug Encapsulation.
crm_level_3: Leiden Academic Center for Drug Research (LACDR)
summary: The study reports the controlled synthesis of polypept(o)ide core–shell bottlebrush polymers via a grafting-from strategy using poly-lysine backbones and pGlu(OBn)-b-pSar side chains, yielding well-defined nanoparticles (Rh 17–70 nm, Mw 1.32–4.0 MDa) characterized by SEC, NMR, DLS/SLS, AFM, and FCS. As a drug delivery proof-of-concept, Dasatinib was encapsulated (≈9–10% loading) with sustained release up to 72 h and effective reduction of U-87 MG glioblastoma cell viability comparable to free drug in vitro.

title: Association of tear fluid glutathione synthetase and glutathione levels with amyloid positivity.
summary: This study profiled the tear fluid proteome from 60 human participants across cognitive stages and amyloid PET status, identifying 703 proteins and highlighting glutathione synthetase (GSS) and glutathione (GSH) as elevated in amyloid PET–positive individuals. Using these tear biomarkers as pre-screeners could reduce the need for PET scans by up to 75%, suggesting tear fluid as a promising non-invasive source for Alzheimer’s disease biomarker screening.

title: Quantitative protein analysis and glycan profiling of umbilical cord plasma and corresponding maternal plasma samples.
summary: This study developed a targeted SRM-based mass spectrometry assay to quantify 19 acute-phase proteins and 7 immunoglobulins in plasma and combined it with high-throughput total plasma N-glycome profiling on matched umbilical cord and maternal plasma (n=98 pairs). Neonatal plasma showed broadly lower protein levels except for elevated alpha-2-macroglobulin, and its glycome was dominated by core-fucosylated di‑antennary glycans, whereas maternal plasma exhibited higher abundances of branched, highly sialylated glycans.

title: Widespread Fab-arm exchange affects all endogenous serum IgG4.
crm_level_3: Bijvoet Center for Biomolecular Research and Utrecht Institute for Pharmaceutical Sciences
summary: This study develops an LC-MS workflow to profile endogenous human serum IgG4 at clonal resolution and demonstrates that Fab-arm exchange (FAE) is widespread and effectively affects all serum IgG4 clones. As a result, IgG4 forms a massively expanded repertoire of bispecific entities; intact Fab2 profiles become too complex to resolve by LC-MS unless reduced to Lc and Fd fragments, and FAE appears stochastic and even across clones with ~78% covalently linked (Fab2) versus ~22% non-covalently linked (Fab) species in serum.

title: EMT-associated bias in the Parsortix® system observed with pancreatic cancer cell lines.
summary: JSON parse error

title: TRPV4 Deficiency Shifts Mitochondrial Dynamics Toward a Fragmented Morphology in Primary Microglia.
summary: Using primary murine microglia and BMDMs, the authors show that loss of TRPV4 shifts mitochondrial dynamics toward a fragmented, less complex network, increases pDrp1 (Ser616) recruitment, and redistributes mitochondria further from the nucleus without altering baseline oxidative metabolism. Acute TRPV4 inhibition did not induce fragmentation but increased non-mitochondrial respiration and enhanced glycolytic reserve and ATP-linked respiration primarily in Trpv4 knockout cells, suggesting chronic versus acute TRPV4 loss have distinct effects.

title: H-ferritin nanoparticle-mediated antibody delivery across the blood-brain barrier.
summary: This study demonstrates that human H-ferritin (HFn) nanoparticles chemically conjugated to an anti-BACE1 monoclonal antibody (1A11) can cross the blood-brain barrier via transferrin receptor 1-mediated transcytosis and reduce brain Aβ1−40 levels in humanized TfR1 knock-in mice after intravenous administration. The 1A11-HFn conjugates retained binding to both BACE1 and human TfR1, showed intact nanocage structure, achieved higher brain exposure than unconjugated antibody at day 1, and produced a transient pharmacodynamic effect consistent with their pharmacokinetics.

title: Comparative lipidomics of iPSC-derived microglia protocols reveal lipid droplet and immune differences mediated by media composition.
crm_level_1: VU Amsterdam, Amsterdam University Medical Center
summary: The study compares lipidomes of human iPSC-derived microglia generated by embryoid body (EB) and induced transcription factor (iTF) protocols and finds markedly elevated triglycerides and lipid droplets in iTF microglia driven by the absence of B-27 supplement. Supplementation with B-27 or its component L-carnitine lowers triglycerides, reduces lipid droplets, and shifts iTF microglia toward a more homeostatic and immune-responsive state, highlighting that maturation media composition, rather than induction method, dictates major lipidomic differences.

title: Cytoskeletal dynamics and mitochondrial rearrangements drive cell fate upon antibody-induced complement activation in DLBCL.
summary: Using DLBCL models and patient samples, the study shows that mitochondrial damage and reactive oxygen species drive antibody-induced complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC), while resistance arises via mitochondrial rearrangements (increased fusion, reduced mitophagy) and decreased actin dynamics, particularly at mitochondria. Pharmacologic promotion of actin polymerization restores CDC sensitivity, and cytoskeleton-related gene expression correlates with ex vivo CDC and improved survival in R-CHOP–treated patients.

title: Follicular fluid-derived small extracellular vesicles during individual in vitro maturation improve blastocyst development.
summary: This study tested follicular fluid-derived small extracellular vesicles (FF-sEVs) added during bovine oocyte in vitro maturation in group versus fully individual culture systems. While higher FF-sEV doses impaired outcomes in group culture, a low dose (6.5 μg/mL) in individual maturation significantly improved day 8 blastocyst rates, total and inner cell mass cell numbers, and reduced apoptosis, indicating context- and dose-dependent benefits of FF-sEVs.

title: Diversity of the Ixodes ricinus Microbiome Across Belgian Ecoregions and Its Association with Pathogen and Symbiont Presence.
summary: This study characterized the microbiome and pathogen/symbiont prevalence of Ixodes ricinus nymphs across three Belgian ecoregions using qPCR and Oxford Nanopore 16S rRNA sequencing. It revealed strong geographic differences in microbiome composition and pathogen prevalence, pathogen–microbiota associations (notably with Rickettsia helvetica), and ecoregion-specific microbiome network robustness and structure.

title: Colchicine Alleviates Non-Atherosclerotic Vascular Aging by Targeting Endothelial Dysfunction and Inflammatory Status.
crm_level_1: Erasmus MC, University Medical Center Rotterdam
summary: In a smooth muscle–specific ERCC1 knockout mouse model of DNA damage–driven, non-atherosclerotic vascular aging, chronic low-dose colchicine reduced arterial stiffness, preserved elastin architecture, and improved endothelium-dependent vasorelaxation without altering systemic cytokines. Mechanistically, colchicine acutely promoted vasorelaxation via NO–cGMP and β-adrenergic pathways and chronically lowered local vascular iNOS, COX-2, and MAPK-p38 signaling, thereby sustaining endothelial NO signaling and vascular compliance.

title: The effect of substrate and product transfer between polydisperse microdroplets on biological high-throughput screens.
summary: Using biosensor strains in polydisperse water-in-oil emulsions, the authors show that small amphiphilic molecules such as ethanol and weak acids can transfer between droplets—ethanol partitions into fluorinated oils and enables unintended growth in neighboring droplets, while weak acids lower pH—whereas sugars like glucose do not transfer. They quantify oil- and surfactant-dependent effects (FC40 reduces but does not eliminate ethanol crosstalk) and provide practical recommendations to validate compartmentalization in droplet-based high-throughput screens.

title: Randomized phase I trial outcomes show safe and sustainable inhibition of classical and lectin complement pathways by empasiprubart.
summary: This study elucidates the crystal structure of the anti-C2 monoclonal antibody empasiprubart bound to the CCP2 domain of complement C2, revealing a Ca2+-mediated binding interface that underpins its selectivity and mechanism. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase I trial in 78 healthy participants showed that intravenous empasiprubart causes sustained, dose-dependent reductions in free C2 and inhibition of the classical and lectin pathways, with a long elimination half-life (70–88 days) and an acceptable safety profile.

title: Cytoskeletal control in adult microglia is essential to restore neurodevelopmental synaptic and cognitive deficits.
summary: The study shows that disrupting the scaffold protein DISC1 in microglia skews actin dynamics toward filopodia, driving excessive synaptic protein uptake, reduced excitatory synaptic connectivity in hippocampal CA1, and spatial memory deficits in mice. Replacing adult DISC1-deficient microglia with wild-type bone marrow–derived microglia-like cells restores synaptic function and rescues cognitive performance, highlighting microglial cytoskeletal remodeling as a therapeutic target in neurodevelopmental disorders.

title: Development of Reliable and High-Throughput Human Biomimetic Cartilage and Bone Models to Explore Senescence and Personalized Osteoarthritis Treatment Options.
summary: This study establishes human biomimetic osteochondral explant and high-throughput cartilage organoid models to induce and dissect senescence phenotypes relevant to osteoarthritis using ionizing radiation and hyperphysiological mechanical loading. Irradiation primarily induced a p21/p53 cell cycle arrest signature, mechanical loading elicited a SASP response, and their combination produced a complementary profile; a 96-well organoid model recapitulated the irradiation-induced arrest, enabling scalable screening of anti-senescence therapeutics.

title: Association Between Abnormal DNA Methylation and Altered Transcriptome in Muscle Five Years After Critical Illness.
summary: This study found widespread abnormal DNA methylation in skeletal muscle biopsies taken 5 years after critical illness, which correlated strongly with previously observed long-term RNA expression changes linked to reduced muscle strength. The aberrant methylation affected genes and pathways related to muscle contraction, vascular development, and signaling, and was associated with risk factors including age, sex, ICU exposure to glucocorticoids, benzodiazepines, early parenteral nutrition, and certain medications at follow-up.

title: From spheroids to organoids: next-generation models for CAR-T cell therapy research in solid tumors.
summary: This review discusses the evolution of CAR-T cell therapy and emphasizes the need for physiologically relevant models beyond traditional 2D cultures to advance CAR-T efficacy in solid tumors. It compares 2D, 3D spheroid/organoid, microfluidic/organ-on-chip, bioprinting, and patient-derived tumor slice approaches, and outlines how integrating these systems with murine models can better predict clinical outcomes by recapitulating tumor microenvironmental barriers and immune interactions.

title: A vaccine central in A(H5) influenza antigenic space confers broad immunity.
summary: The study created a high-resolution, three-dimensional antigenic map of H5 influenza haemagglutinin and used it to rationally design antigenically central vaccine antigens that elicit broad cross-reactive antibody responses. In ferrets, a central HA antigen (AC-Anhui) induced broader, more central antibody profiles and provided protection comparable to homologous vaccines against heterologous H5N1 and H5N6 challenges.

title: Iodine increases pulmonary type I interferon responses and decreases covid-19 disease severity: Results from an open label randomized clinical trial.
summary: In a single-center, open-label randomized clinical trial, adding oral iodine (12.5 mg/day for 8 days) to standard care for hospitalized COVID-19 patients did not significantly reduce mortality or ICU admissions, though an exploratory analysis suggested shorter ICU stays in the iodine group. In vitro, iodine (Lugol’s solution) enhanced poly(I:C)-induced type I interferon responses (IFNβ, IFIT1, MX1) in human lung epithelial Calu-3 cells, indicating a potential mechanistic basis for improved antiviral immunity.

title: Plant-based proteins for infant formula: findings and recommendations from the ILSI Europe workshop.
summary: This review summarizes findings from the ILSI Europe workshop on plant-based proteins for infant formula, assessing current approvals (soy, hydrolyzed rice), emerging candidates (pea, lentil, faba bean), and the interplay of nutritional adequacy, allergenicity, processing, sustainability, and regulatory issues. It recommends prioritizing a few promising proteins, developing robust extraction and antinutrient mitigation processes, advancing in vitro digestion models and clinical studies, and using integrated environmental-nutritional assessments (n-LCA) to guide sustainable product development.

title: Selective Lysine Ubiquitination Using Activated Phenol Esters.
summary: The study introduces a water-soluble activated phenol ester of ubiquitin (2,4-dichloro-6-sulfonic acid phenol ester) that enables rapid, selective lysine ubiquitination of peptides and proteins under alkaline conditions, while showing reduced regioselectivity and slower N-terminal modification at neutral pH. Using model peptides, orthogonally protected ubiquitin variants, and the ubiquitin-like protein FUBI, the authors demonstrate efficient lysine conjugation and confirm site-specific K–GG linkages by LC–MS/MS, offering a practical alternative to thiolysine-based native chemical ligation.

title: Polypept(o)ide Based Biodegradable Cylindrical Polymer Brushes: Controlling Size, Shape, Surface Functionality, and Stability.
crm_level_3: Leiden Academic Center for Drug Research (LACDR)
summary: The study reports a grafting-from synthesis of polypept(o)ide-based cylindrical polymer brushes using poly-L-lysine backbones to initiate ring-opening polymerization of sarcosine N-carboxyanhydride, yielding azide-capped polysarcosine side chains with tunable size, aspect ratio, and high grafting densities. These brushes are thermally stable in PBS, biodegradable upon exposure to Streptomyces griseus protease, resist protein adsorption in human serum, exhibit low cell association and cytotoxicity, and circulate up to three days in zebrafish embryos.

title: Biological tissue engineering for Fontan failure using decellularized extracellular matrix: a systematic review.
summary: This systematic review synthesizes 58 human-scale (porcine/human) studies on decellularization and 13 on recellularization of cardiac extracellular matrix to assess their suitability as contractile scaffolds for a future biological Fontan conduit. Most decellularization studies achieved high DNA removal and preserved ECM architecture, while recellularization with human cardiomyocyte-like cells yielded viable, organized, and spontaneously contracting constructs, though with sub-physiological function, highlighting the need for standardized protocols, improved maturation, and integration of vascular/supportive cells.

title: Plasma Extracellular Vesicles Contain Protein Biomarkers for Capturing Stages of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Preliminary Exploratory Study.
summary: This exploratory study profiled proteins in plasma-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) from 70 patients with MASLD to identify non-invasive biomarkers associated with steatosis, steatohepatitis (MASH), and fibrosis, and related them to MRI-based liver metrics. EV proteins H4C1, OIT3, and ANPEP increased and CCDC25 and KLHL41 decreased with advanced steatosis; GP1BA was higher in MASH; and C7 was elevated with advanced fibrosis and correlated with MRE-derived stiffness, supporting EV proteins as candidate biomarkers pending validation in larger cohorts.

title: Heart Failure Impacts Endothelial Cell Responses to Cardiac Surgery on Cardiopulmonary Bypass.
summary: This study compared endothelial cell (EC) activation and ex vivo EC responses in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) versus non-HF patients undergoing cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), measuring plasma ANG2, vWF, sP-selectin, and CD138 and profiling EC morphology and mitochondrial function after exposure to patient plasma. HFrEF patients had higher baseline ANG2/vWF and a dampened postoperative vWF rise; ECs exposed to HFrEF plasma appeared more activated at baseline, while post-CPB plasma from both groups induced pronounced mitochondrial fragmentation and functional changes, and a smaller ΔvWF (T4–T3) correlated with higher noradrenaline dose/duration, implicating pre-existing EC/mitochondrial dysfunction in postoperative hemodynamic instability.

title: Label-free quantitative shotgun analysis of bis(monoacylglycero)phosphate lipids.
summary: The study presents a label-free shotgun lipidomics method that selectively quantifies bis(monoacylglycero)phosphate (BMP) lipids by leveraging collision-induced dissociation of sodiated ions to distinguish BMP from isomeric phosphatidylglycerol (PG), integrated into the Lipidyzer/SLA workflow with isotope correction. Validated in K-562 cells with robust analytical performance (LOQ 0.12 µM), the method revealed characteristic BMP accumulation—especially 22:6-containing species—in bone marrow–derived macrophages from NPC1 cKO mice.

title: Inhibition of TBK1/IKKε mediated RIPK1 phosphorylation sensitizes tumors to immune cell killing.
crm_level_3: Bijvoet Center for Biomolecular Research and Utrecht Institute for Pharmaceutical Sciences
summary: The study shows that inhibiting TBK1/IKKε-mediated phosphorylation of RIPK1 at Ser25 disables a pro-survival checkpoint in TNF/TNFR1 signaling, promoting RIPK1 activation (pS166) and sensitizing tumor cells to cytotoxic CD8 T and NK cell killing. Sensitization correlates with reduced recruitment of non-canonical IKKs (TBK1/IKKε) to the TNFR1 complex across multiple perturbations, and direct TBK1/IKKε knockouts increase immune cell cytotoxicity, suggesting a tractable strategy to enhance immunotherapy efficacy.

title: TRIM33 loss reduces androgen receptor transcriptional output and H2BK120 ubiquitination.
summary: The study identifies TRIM33 as a conserved androgen receptor (AR) co-regulator that co-occupies AR-bound chromatin and is required for full transcriptional output of a subset of AR target genes in prostate cancer cells. Contrary to prior reports, TRIM33 loss does not alter AR protein stability but is associated with locus-specific reductions in H2BK120 ubiquitination, implicating a transcriptional mechanism rather than proteasomal regulation.

title: Application of Lacticaseibacillus paracasei and Tetragenococcus halophilus as adjunct starter cultures in Gouda cheese production.
crm_level_3: Faculty of Sciences and Bioengineering Sciences
summary: This study evaluated two adjunct starter cultures, Lacticaseibacillus paracasei LP46 and the halophilic Tetragenococcus halophilus TH63, in pilot-scale Gouda cheese production using multiple primary starter mixtures and assessed their microbiological dynamics, metabolite profiles, and sensory impact over 32 weeks. Both adjuncts became abundant and modulated metabolite profiles (e.g., increased acetoin; TH63 increased total amino acids by 55%), but triangle tests found no consistent sensory differences versus controls, while LP46 increased cadaverine to low, sub-toxic levels.

title: Two-year Results of Bronchoscopic Lung Volume Reduction Using One-Way Endobronchial Valves: Real-World Single Center Data.
summary: This single-center, real-world cohort study followed COPD patients undergoing bronchoscopic lung volume reduction with Zephyr endobronchial valves for up to two years and found significant improvements in FEV1, RV, 6MWD, mMRC, SGRQ at one year, with sustained benefits in RV, mMRC, and BODE index at two years. Composite response rates were 86% at one year and 71% at two years, with a pneumothorax rate of 11.4% and a multidisciplinary pathway enabling step-up to surgery when needed.

title: Ultrapotent SARS coronavirus-neutralizing single-domain antibodies that clamp the spike at its base.
summary: The study identifies and structurally characterizes single-domain antibodies (VHHs) that bind a conserved, quaternary epitope in the membrane-proximal HR2 coiled-coil of the SARS-CoV spike S2 subunit, locking HR2 in its prefusion state and thereby blocking membrane fusion. A humanized Fc-fused lead VHH exhibits picomolar-to-low nanomolar neutralization across diverse SARS-CoV-2 variants, and provides strong prophylactic and therapeutic protection in K18-hACE2 mice and Syrian hamsters, with escape mutations severely compromising viral fitness.

title: Calciprotein particle-activated endothelial cells aggravate smooth muscle cell calcification via paracrine signalling.
summary: This study shows that endothelial cells activated by calciprotein particles (CPP2) promote vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) calcification via paracrine signaling, increasing pro-calcification gene expression in VSMCs. Secretome proteomics identified 76 differentially expressed proteins (notably ECM remodeling and oxidative stress pathways) in CPP2-activated endothelial cells, and clinical data linked higher circulating CPP counts to elevated soluble VCAM-1 in humans.

title: Transfer learning in DeepLC improves LC retention time prediction across substantially different modifications and setups.
summary: The study shows that applying transfer learning to DeepLC substantially improves peptide LC retention time prediction across diverse chromatographic setups and peptide modifications compared to calibration or training new models from scratch. Across 474 public datasets and focused tests on TMPP-labeled peptides and basic-pH LC runs, transfer learning achieved lower errors with fewer training peptides and generalized to unseen modifications and markedly different LC conditions.

title: Rab10 regulates neuropeptide release by maintaining Ca2+ homeostasis and protein synthesis.
summary: This study shows that Rab10 is essential for dense core vesicle (DCV) exocytosis in mature mouse hippocampal neurons by maintaining endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ homeostasis and sustaining protein synthesis, without affecting synaptic vesicle exocytosis. Rab10 depletion reduces SERCA2 levels, depletes ER Ca2+, slows ER refilling, lowers activity-evoked Ca2+ signals, dysregulates ribosomal proteins and protein synthesis, and these DCV release defects are largely rescued by leucine supplementation.

title: Natural deep eutectic solvents as a sustainable alternative for multi-class pesticide extraction in food safety analysis.
summary: This study demonstrates that natural deep eutectic solvents, particularly a thymol:menthol (1:1) mixture, can serve as green, effective extraction media for multi-class pesticide residue analysis in food matrices (orange, spinach, wheat) prior to LC-MS/MS, with optimization and validation across 313 pesticides. The approach yielded acceptable recoveries and matrix effects, outperformed conventional and miniaturized QuEChERS in greenness metrics, preserved NADES structure post-extraction (confirmed by NMR), and performed satisfactorily in a proficiency test.

title: Combinations of approved oral nucleoside analogues confer potent suppression of alphaviruses in vitro and in vivo.
summary: The study evaluates combinations of approved oral nucleoside analogues—molnupiravir (MPV), sofosbuvir (SOF), and favipiravir (FAV)—against multiple alphaviruses in human cell lines and a chikungunya virus (CHIKV) mouse model, finding additive to synergistic antiviral effects in vitro and improved outcomes in vivo. In CHIKV-infected AG129 mice, MPV reduced swelling and viremia dose-dependently, and the MPV+SOF combination further lowered infectious titers and swelling while reducing MPV-associated viral mutational burden compared to higher-dose MPV monotherapy.

title: A pharmacokinetic study and critical reappraisal of curcumin formulations enhancing bioavailability.
summary: In a randomized crossover study of nine healthy males, the authors compared multiple commercial curcumin formulations and quantified unconjugated versus conjugated curcuminoids in plasma, urine, and feces using LC-MS/MS. Unconjugated curcumin remained extremely low across all products (even with high doses and piperine), with NovaSOL yielding the highest but still sub-therapeutic levels, while fecal recovery suggested poor absorption for most formulations and highlighted that bioavailability claims based on conjugates are misleading.

title: Multiomics for Risk Stratification in Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease.
summary: This review synthesizes how multiomics—including genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics/epitranscriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and radiomics—can enhance risk stratification for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, comparing their performance and limitations against traditional clinical scores. It highlights opportunities (e.g., polygenic risk scores and proteomic panels) and challenges (data heterogeneity, standardization, cost, ethical issues), and underscores the role of AI/ML for integrating multi-layer data into clinically actionable tools.

title: Human microglial transitions at the Aβ-tau inflection point associate with divergent pathways to dementia and resilience.
crm_level_3: VIB Center for Brain & Disease Research
summary: Using spatial transcriptomics, single-nucleus RNA sequencing, and in situ hybridization on human superior frontal cortex from octogenarians and centenarians, the study identifies a microglial inflection point where responses shift from Aβ-associated early plaque-induced genes (PIGs) to tau-associated late, antigen-presenting PIG programs. Resilient trajectories differ: octogenarians without dementia do not transition to late PIGs, whereas centenarians show late PIG activation uncoupled from tau, positioning microglial state transitions at the Aβ–tau interface as potential therapeutic targets.

title: CellCousin2: an optimized system for partial ablation and tracing of regenerative lineages.
summary: The study presents CellCousin2, a zebrafish liver lineage-tracing and mosaic ablation system that combines a dual-controlled DHFR-CreER (DDCreER) to minimize background recombination with NTR2.0 to enable effective ablation at tenfold lower metronidazole doses. CellCousin2 achieves high recombination with low leakiness and durable labeling, allowing precise long-term tracking of spared and de novo hepatocytes during regeneration while reducing off-target toxicity.

title: Mapping the spread of fluoroquinolone resistance: continued presence of non-susceptible Escherichia coli in broilers.
summary: In a longitudinal study of 29 Belgian broiler farms, fluoroquinolone (FQ) non-susceptible Escherichia coli were widespread in day-old chicks (79.3% of farms) and the farm environment (48.3%), and persisted in flocks through to slaughter even without on-farm FQ use; total antimicrobial use showed a positive but modest association with the proportion of FQ non-susceptible E. coli at the end of production. Whole-genome sequencing revealed persistence of identical FQ non-susceptible strains from day 0 to day 36, frequent multidrug resistance, and a mix of QRDR mutations and qnr genes underpinning FQ non-susceptibility.

title: Intensification of Palmaria palmata protein biorefinery using multifrequency ultrasonication and enzymes.
summary: This study optimizes protein and R-phycoerythrin extraction from the red seaweed Palmaria palmata using low-frequency ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE, 40 kHz) and a novel enzyme-assisted high-frequency ultrasonication (EAUE, 578–1148 kHz) via design of experiments and response surface methodology. While both approaches reached similar R-phycoerythrin yields (2.6 mg/gdw), total protein extraction efficiency increased from 13.6% (UAE) to 36.0% under EAUE with Viscozyme L, evidencing a synergistic effect between mild high-frequency acoustic irradiation and enzymatic hydrolysis.

title: Microbial protein-derived bioplastics from renewable substrates: pathways, challenges, and applications in a circular economy.
crm_level_1: Center for Advanced Process Technology for Urban Resource Recovery (CAPTURE)
crm_level_3: Center for Advanced Process Technology for Urban Resource Recovery (CAPTURE)
summary: This review synthesizes pathways, processing strategies, and market/regulatory considerations for turning microbial protein-rich biomass into protein-based bioplastics, highlighting advantages (e.g., oxygen barrier performance, biodegradability) and constraints (e.g., mechanical properties, variability, cost). It emphasizes co-valorization strategies with other microbial polymers (notably PHA), whole-biomass processing, and scalable wet/dry processing (e.g., extrusion) to improve environmental and economic sustainability within a circular economy.

title: Cytokine-Induced Barrier Dysfunction and Lipid Signaling in a Gut-On-Chip Model.
crm_level_3: Leiden Academic Centre for Drug Research
summary: This study uses a gut-on-chip (OrganoPlate) model of human Caco-2 intestinal epithelial tubules to show that apical exposure to proinflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IFN-γ) impairs barrier integrity (reduced TEER), increases cell death (DRAQ7), and triggers actin remodeling, with media composition (serum-free vs complete EMEM) shaping lipid signaling responses. Targeted LC–MS/MS profiling revealed apical increases in prostaglandins—especially under serum-free conditions—and distinct compartmental patterns of eicosanoids and bile acids, highlighting spatial and medium-dependent lipid mediator dynamics during inflammation.

title: Combining co-introduction with patch-size optimization as a novel strategy to maximize seagrass restoration.
crm_level_1: NIOZ Royal Netherlands Institute for Sea Research
summary: This study tested a large-scale seagrass restoration strategy that combines intraspecific facilitation (larger patch size) with interspecific facilitation (co-introduction of the epiphyte-grazing snail Littorina littorea) for Zostera marina in Lake Grevelingen. Co-introduction consistently boosted seagrass performance and winter survival (up to 20× more shoots where snails persisted), while larger patches improved outcomes only at hydrodynamically exposed sites and reduced success at sheltered sites due to algal smothering.

title: Exposure to processing from ultraprocessed diets and in feeding studies.
summary: This short communication advocates treating food processing as a quantifiable dietary exposure rather than a categorical label, introducing the Food Processing Levels–Processed Food Intake (FPL-PFI) framework and its exposure metrics (PFIN, PFIE, and PFINRF). Reanalysis of controlled feeding studies and a UPF-aligned model diet shows wide heterogeneity and overlap in processing exposure across UPF and non-UPF diets, supporting the design and interpretation of interventions that explicitly vary processing history while aligning with IAFNS guiding principles.

title: Proof of Concept for a Controlled Raman-Compatible Skin-Mimicking Hydrogel Substrate for Chemical Imaging Technique Development.
summary: This study develops a standardized, skin-mimicking dried agarose–gelatine hydrogel loaded with diphenhydramine hydrochloride as a controlled substrate to optimize Surface-Enhanced Raman Chemical Imaging (SER-CI) nanoparticle deposition and imaging performance. The matrix shows protein-like Raman fingerprints similar to reconstructed human epidermis, highly uniform analyte distribution and repeatable drying kinetics, and it enables evaluation of nanoparticle deposition methods, with spray-coating outperforming drop-casting for homogeneous AgNP coverage and SERS response.

title: FGF9 treatment reduces off-target chondrocytes from iPSC-derived kidney organoids.
summary: The study shows that extending fibroblast growth factor 9 (FGF9) supplementation by one week in human iPSC-derived kidney organoids markedly reduces off-target cartilage formation without compromising renal structures. FGF9-treated organoids also display reduced EMT markers, increased vessel-like structures, and improved functional readouts, enabling longer culture periods and higher-quality organoids for research applications.

title: Deciphering shared molecular dysregulation across Parkinson's disease variants using a multi-modal network-based data integration and analysis.
summary: The study builds a Parkinson’s Disease Knowledge Graph (PD-KG) by integrating high-content imaging and RNA-seq data from monogenic PD midbrain organoids (LRRK2-G2019S, SNCA triplication, GBA-N370S, MIRO1-R272Q) with public databases, and adds a new single-cell RNA-seq dataset from idiopathic PD (IPD) organoids. Analyses reveal shared dysregulation in ROBO signaling and cytoskeleton/axonogenesis pathways—especially in glial cells—and stratify IPD samples relative to monogenic forms, suggesting convergent mechanisms and drug repurposing opportunities.

title: X-chromosome upregulation operates on a gene-by-gene basis at RNA and protein levels.
summary: This study shows that mouse pluripotent stem cells compensate for loss or silencing of specific X-chromosome segments by upregulating the corresponding genes in trans at both RNA and protein levels, and that similar transcriptional compensation can occur on autosomes when one allele is silenced. The authors find no evidence for a single X-chromosome upregulation center; instead, dosage compensation operates on a gene-by-gene basis and involves histone modification changes and multi-layered regulation.

title: A pair of congenic mice for imaging of transplants by positron emission tomography using anti-transferrin receptor nanobodies.
summary: This study develops species-specific anti-transferrin receptor nanobody PET tracers (VHH123 for mouse TfR, VHH188 for human TfR) and a congenic mouse system (TfR humanized knock-in) to non-invasively track genetically unmodified transplanted cells in vivo. The authors compare 89Zr-, 64Cu-, and covalent 18F-labeling, show chelated 89Zr/64Cu are released after endocytosis, and demonstrate tracking of bone marrow transplants, B16.F10 lung metastases, and placental TfR, with CNS accumulation detected by gamma counting but not PET.

title: Elucidating the role of human skeletal muscles in the pathogenesis of enterovirus D68 infection.
summary: The study shows that enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) productively infects human iPSC-derived skeletal muscle in both 2D myotubes and 3D tissue-engineered muscles, causing cell death, structural damage, and loss of contractile force. Infection is largely mediated by sialic acids, and in 3D tissues leads to depletion of satellite cells and failure of muscle regeneration, suggesting skeletal muscle as an extra-respiratory replication site contributing to EV-D68–associated muscle weakness.

title: Ischemic and non-ischemic myocardial injuries at autopsy- an overview for forensic pathologists.
summary: This review synthesizes the mechanisms, histopathology, ancillary diagnostics, and medicolegal implications of ischemic and non‑ischemic myocardial injuries encountered at autopsy, proposing a stepwise approach to differentiate myocardial infarction (types 1–5) from other injuries. It stresses careful clinicopathologic correlation using histology, immunohistochemistry, nitroblue tetrazolium staining, postmortem imaging, and troponin assays, while recognizing pitfalls from agonal changes and resuscitation artifacts.

title: Ionic regulation of thylakoid membrane architecture: Mg2+-driven destacking and restacking visualized.
summary: The study combines pulse-amplitude modulation fluorometry, 77 K fluorescence spectroscopy, expansion microscopy, and transmission electron microscopy to show that Mg2+ concentration controls reversible destacking and restacking of Arabidopsis thylakoid membranes, thereby regulating lateral segregation of PSI and PSII. Even under Mg2+-depleted conditions thylakoids retain loose grana-like domains, and reintroduction of Mg2+ drives structural reorganization and restacking, offering a mechanistic view of ion-dependent architectural control of photosynthetic membranes.

title: Analysis of trade-offs of post-sorting plastic packaging.
summary: This study compares source-separated (PMD) and post-sorted (PoSo) plastic packaging waste processed on the same MRF line, finding similar target-polymer bale purities but consistently higher contamination (moisture/dirt, VOCs, halogens, and metals including Pb and Cd) in PoSo streams. A cluster-based EU27+3 and US model shows that expanding post-sorting can substantially increase available recycling feedstock, but with a quality penalty that necessitates more intensive washing and may constrain high-grade mechanical recycling.

title: Nixtamalization of Maize to Reduce Mycotoxin Exposure: A Human Biomonitoring Intervention Study in Soweto, South Africa.
summary: This intervention study in Soweto evaluated nixtamalization (alkaline cooking) of visibly moldy maize and showed 89–100% reductions for several mycotoxins in maize (e.g., FB1/FB2 ~95%, ZEN 89%, DON and AFB1 to below detection), while a human biomonitoring arm (n=40) found urinary mycotoxin biomarker levels after consuming nixtamalized maize were not significantly different from those after control maize. The results support nixtamalization as an effective, affordable food safety strategy and demonstrate the utility of human biomonitoring to assess intervention impact on internal exposure.

title: Autologous fecal microbiota capsules are safe and potentially preserve beta-cell function in individuals with type 1 diabetes.
summary: In an open-label pilot study of 10 adults with type 1 diabetes, daily autologous lyophilized fecal microbiota capsules (a-LFMCs) taken for 3 months were safe, well tolerated, and associated with stabilization of mixed-meal–stimulated C-peptide compared to a decline during the prior 3-month run-in period. The study also details an aerobic, GMP-like workflow to produce enteric-coated lyophilized capsules from participants’ own stool, demonstrated long-term viability at −80 °C, and observed post-treatment changes in duodenal gene expression consistent with immune and barrier modulation.

title: Pyocyanin produced by Pseudomonas aeruginosa creates legacy effects that promote antibiotic resistance evolution in enterococci
summary: The study shows that transient exposure of enterococci to Pseudomonas aeruginosa-conditioned medium—specifically its phenazine pyocyanin—induces a lasting increase in antibiotic efflux and tolerance, which markedly elevates the evolvability of resistance to rifampicin and nalidixic acid. Using evolvability assays, tolerance and efflux measurements, whole-genome sequencing, and transcriptomics, the authors link pyocyanin-induced efflux upregulation (e.g., MacB/FtsX-like transporters) to enhanced survival and selection of resistance mutations in Enterococcus faecium and E. faecalis.

title: T cell responses in repeated controlled human schistosome infection compared to natural exposure.
crm_level_3: Leiden University Center for Infectious Diseases
summary: In a repeated controlled human Schistosoma mansoni infection model, CD4+ T cell responses developed as a mixed Th1/Th2/regulatory profile predominantly against adult worm antigens, with greater activation when volunteers inadvertently received sequential male–female–male cercarial exposures. These responses broadly mirrored adult-worm–specific immunity in naturally exposed Ugandan participants, while endemic individuals showed muted egg responses and higher cercarial (Th17) signals, highlighting context-dependent immunoregulation during reinfection.

title: Probiotic Potential of Lactic Acid Bacteria Isolated from Moroccan Traditional Food Products.
summary: This study isolated and identified five lactic acid bacteria from Moroccan traditional fermented foods and evaluated their probiotic potential through acid/bile tolerance, antimicrobial activity, surface hydrophobicity, emulsifying capacity, organic acid production, and safety assays. Lactiplantibacillus plantarum, Lacticaseibacillus casei, and Enterococcus durans showed strong survival under gastrointestinal-like stress, notable antimicrobial effects (largely acid-mediated), robust organic acid production (particularly L. plantarum), and no hemolytic activity with generally favorable antibiotic susceptibility profiles, supporting their potential as feed additives.

title: Gut microbiota composition differences are associated with geographic location and age in malaria-endemic regions of Rwanda.
summary: This cross-sectional study of 169 Rwandan participants across three malaria-endemic provinces used 16S rRNA gene sequencing to show that gut microbiota composition differed by geography and age, but not by malaria or soil-transmitted helminth infection status. Lower dietary fibre and protein intake in the Western province likely contributed to its distinct microbiota profiles, while preschool children had significantly lower alpha diversity than older groups.

title: The fecal metabolome and microbiome are altered in dogs with idiopathic epilepsy compared to healthy dogs.
summary: This study compared the fecal metabolome and microbiome of healthy dogs and dogs with idiopathic epilepsy (drug‑resistant vs mild phenotype) using UHPLC‑HRMS and 16S rRNA sequencing under a standardized diet. Drug‑resistant dogs showed proinflammatory signatures (elevated histamine/1‑methylhistamine and Escherichia‑Shigella), while mild‑phenotype dogs showed features linked to anti‑inflammatory/epithelial benefits (higher serotonin and Blautia hominis), implicating the microbiota‑gut‑brain axis in epilepsy.

title: Awakening of the RuMP cycle for partial methylotrophy in the thermophile Parageobacillus thermoglucosidasius.
summary: The authors engineered and evolved the thermophile Parageobacillus thermoglucosidasius to achieve partial methylotrophy via the native RuMP cycle, without introducing heterologous enzymes, enabling methanol-dependent co-assimilation with ribose. Whole-genome sequencing and proteomics revealed activation of a native methanol dehydrogenase (AdhT) and strong upregulation of HxlAB, with 13C labeling confirming ~17% of biomass derived from methanol in the best strain (PTM1).

title: STAG2-truncating variants reveal a mosaic STAG2 inactivation pattern and compensatory mechanisms involving cohesin complex remodeling.
summary: This study reports six females with germline STAG2-truncating variants and shows that many somatic tissues, especially skin fibroblasts, display skewed X-chromosome inactivation favoring the mutant allele, leading to loss of STAG2 and a proliferative advantage of STAG2-negative cells without overt cohesion or DNA repair defects. The authors find compensatory remodeling of cohesin, with increased STAG1 and ectopic expression of germline STAG3 forming a chimeric cohesin complex, providing a mechanistic basis for phenotypic variability in STAG2-associated cohesinopathies.

title: Single-Domain Antibodies That Specifically Recognize Intact Capsids of Multiple Foot-and-Mouth Disease Serotype O Strains.
summary: The study identifies four new single-domain antibodies (VHHs)—M907F, M910F, M912F, and M916F—that bind specifically to intact (146S) capsids of multiple Foot-and-Mouth Disease Virus (FMDV) serotype O strains, enabling sensitive and broadly reactive ELISAs for vaccine quality control. These VHHs target a conserved capsid site, show high 146S specificity across diverse serotype O topotypes, and achieve low detection limits (down to 0.7–5.9 ng/mL), outperforming many prior strain-specific reagents.

title: Probiotic Bifidobacterium bifidum strains desialylate MUC13 and increase intestinal epithelial barrier function.
summary: This study shows that two probiotic Bifidobacterium bifidum strains (W23 and W28), but not the type strain DSM 20456, desialylate the extracellular domain of the transmembrane mucin MUC13 on human intestinal epithelial cells and significantly enhance epithelial barrier function. The strain-specific effects are linked to high constitutive sialidase activity, efficient colonization of a secreted mucus layer, and increased transepithelial electrical resistance, with sialidase inhibition blocking MUC13 modification.

title: Detection of chimeric alpha-defensin transcripts and peptides in mouse Paneth cells.
summary: Using 148 bulk RNA-seq datasets from FACS-purified mouse Paneth cells and proteomics from a His-tagged Defa30 mouse line, the authors identify widespread but low-abundance chimeric alpha-defensin transcripts and confirm corresponding chimeric peptides in vivo. Synthetic chimeric peptides display antibacterial activity comparable to or exceeding parental defensins, and the authors propose stochastic or unfolded protein response-related mechanisms for their generation.

title: Fasting boosts breast cancer therapy efficacy via glucocorticoid activation.
summary: This study shows that periodic fasting enhances the efficacy of endocrine therapy in ERα-positive breast cancer by activating glucocorticoid receptor (GR) and progesterone receptor (PR) programs, while repressing AP-1-driven enhancers, leading to reduced tumor proliferation. Mechanistically, fasting elevates circulating cortisol/corticosterone and progesterone, increases GR/PR chromatin binding and transcriptional activity, and these benefits are phenocopied by dexamethasone administration; GR knockout abrogates the fasting–tamoxifen synergy, and patient data on fasting-mimicking diets corroborate increased GR/PR activity with reduced proliferation signatures.

title: Beyond Molecular Weight: Peptide Characteristics Influencing the Sensitivity of Retention to Changes in Organic Solvent in Reversed-Phase Chromatography.
summary: The study measured retention sensitivity (S values) for 18 structurally diverse peptides under isocratic RP-UPLC conditions and used multivariate and machine-learning approaches to identify key peptide descriptors that govern S beyond molecular weight. A simple predictive model based on six descriptors (CH2R2 count, rotatable bond fraction, lysine frequency, phenol/enol/carboxyl group count, GRAVY index, and isoelectric point) accurately forecasts S values and outperforms prior formulas on a diverse peptide set.

title: Human and viral chemokines differentially modulate G protein signaling, β-arrestin recruitment and chemotaxis mediated by the viral G protein-coupled receptor ORF74.
summary: This study systematically profiles how human and viral chemokines interact with the Kaposi’s sarcoma-associated herpesvirus GPCR ORF74, showing that ELR+ CXC chemokines (CXCL1-3, CXCL5-8) act as agonists for calcium mobilization, β-arrestin recruitment, and ORF74-dependent chemotaxis, while CXCL10, CXCL12, CCL1 and vCCL2 act as antagonists or inverse agonists in specific pathways. The authors also demonstrate constitutive β-arrestin recruitment by ORF74 and show that ORF74 co-expression modulates CXCL12–CXCR4-mediated migration, highlighting complex ligand- and pathway-specific regulation.

title: Expanding the human proteome with microproteins and peptideins.
crm_level_3: Princess Máxima Center for Pediatric Oncology
summary: The TransCODE Consortium integrated large-scale proteomics and HLA immunopeptidomics (PeptideAtlas builds) across 7,264 non-canonical ORFs, detecting ~2.5% in tryptic proteomes and ~24.6% in HLA-I datasets, and introduced the term “peptideins” for confidently detected microproteins lacking established physiological function. They established stringent annotation workflows, created the ORBL evolutionary metric, validated select cases with targeted PRM and CRISPR screens (including elevating a GMCL1 uORF to protein-coding status and identifying an essential OLMALINC peptidein), and released resources via GENCODE and PeptideAtlas.

title: Variable A-type lamin expression in Merkel cell carcinoma cell lines and its association with nuclear integrity.
summary: This study compares A- and B-type lamin expression and nuclear envelope (NE) integrity between MCPyV-positive (non-adherent) and MCPyV-negative (adherent) Merkel cell carcinoma cell lines using immunofluorescence, Western blotting, qPCR, and live-cell imaging. MCPyV-positive cells exhibit markedly lower A-type lamin and higher B-type lamin levels and undergo irreversible NE ruptures leading to cell death, whereas MCPyV-negative cells show higher A-type lamin levels, frequent but repairable NE ruptures, and nuclear morphology abnormalities with local accumulations of lamin C and emerin.

title: Unraveling the immunosuppressive role of Elastase B produced by cystic fibrosis isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in an organotypic 3D lung epithelial cell model.
summary: Using clinical Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates grown in a cystic fibrosis-mimicking medium and an organotypic 3D A549 lung epithelial model, the authors show that proteolytically active isolates degrade cytokines and suppress epithelial inflammatory responses. Proteomics of bacterial supernatants identified 79 proteases with extracellular proteases (especially Elastase B/LasB) strongly upregulated in active isolates, and lasB mutants confirmed LasB’s major role in degrading MCP-1, IL-1β, GM-CSF, and IL-6, although multiple proteases likely contribute.

title: Enterovirus-like particles encapsidate RNA and exhibit decreased stability due to lack of maturation.
summary: Using baculovirus-expressed enterovirus A71 and coxsackievirus A6 virus-like particles (VLPs), the authors show that insect-cell–produced enterovirus VLPs can encapsidate RNA fragments containing viral protein-coding sequences, yet lack maturation (no VP0 cleavage and no pocket factor).
