Atomic force microscopy reveals VLPs are mechanically more fragile than virions, indicating decreased stability arises primarily from absent maturation rather than the presence of RNA.

title: Blood vessel-resident macrophages safeguard blood and vessel integrity in zebrafish.
summary: The study identifies a distinct population of intravascular macrophages in zebrafish, termed blood vessel-resident macrophages (bMΦs), which patrol the bloodstream, remove foreign particles and unfit cells, and act as first responders to endothelial injury, with conserved counterparts detected in mice. bMΦs arise directly from endothelial cells through a runx1-independent endothelial-to-macrophage transition (EMacT) and function independently of csf1r, revealing a new macrophage origin and mechanism safeguarding blood and vessel integrity.

title: Localization of human UBE3A isoform 3 is highly sensitive to amino acid substitutions at p.Met21 position.
summary: The study revisits the subcellular localization of human UBE3A isoform 3 (hUBE3A-Iso3) and shows that, contrary to prior conclusions, wild-type hUBE3A-Iso3 predominantly localizes to the cytosol, similar to its mouse ortholog mUBE3A-Iso2. It further demonstrates that amino acid substitutions at hUBE3A-Iso3 position p.Met21 (e.g., Met21Ala or Met21Thr) shift the protein toward the nucleus, explaining earlier discrepancies and highlighting N-terminal sensitivity in determining localization.

title: A Synovium-on-Chip Platform to Study Multicellular Interactions in Arthritis.
summary: This study presents a compartmentalized synovium-on-chip featuring a 2-µm-thick porous PDMS membrane that supports co-culture of human fibroblast-like synoviocytes, THP-1-derived macrophages, and HUVECs, enabling direct cell migration and interactions that drive endothelial lumen remodeling and angiogenic responses. Upon TNF-α stimulation, the model exhibits robust inflammatory readouts (e.g., IL-6, IL-8, CCL2, GM-CSF) and increased endothelial ICAM-1, providing a human-relevant platform to interrogate synovial crosstalk in arthritis.

title: Process intensification of cultivated meat production through microcarrier addition strategy optimisation.
summary: This study optimizes microcarrier-based expansion of bovine satellite cells in serum-free media by defining seeding conditions and a confluence-triggered microcarrier addition strategy that sustains exponential growth and maximizes fold-increase. The authors identify an optimal confluence window (15,000–25,000 cells/cm2) for adding microcarriers, validate high expansion ratios (up to 10), and successfully scale the process to a 3 L stirred-tank bioreactor.

title: Infrapatellar fat pad as a source of biomarkers and therapeutic target for knee osteoarthritis.
summary: This review evaluates the infrapatellar fat pad (IPFP) as a source of diagnostic/prognostic biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets for knee osteoarthritis, synthesizing 61 studies spanning imaging, biochemical, and molecular evidence. It highlights MRI-based IPFP signal intensity alterations linked to inflammation, fibrosis, pain, and structural degeneration, and consistently elevated molecular markers such as IL-6, adiponectin, FABP4, and lysophosphatidylcholines, advocating combined imaging–biochemical approaches for earlier detection and better patient stratification.

title: Mucosal B Cell Expansion and Maturation Contribute to Colitis Pathogenesis.
summary: Single-cell RNA-sequencing of human colonic biopsies revealed an enrichment of naive B cells with a more mature phenotype in inflamed ulcerative colitis mucosa, with predicted ligand–receptor interactions primarily between naive B cells and CD4+ T cell subsets. In a SCID transfer colitis model, co-transfer of naive B cells with CD45RBhigh T cells—especially at a 1T:2B ratio—exacerbated disease severity and increased IgG, implicating maturing naive B cells in colitis pathogenesis.

title: Usutu virus-induced meningoencephalitis in immunocompetent mice is characterized by the recruitment of mononuclear cells and a proinflammatory T helper 1 response
summary: The study establishes an intracranial Usutu virus (USUV) infection model in immunocompetent adult C57BL/6 mice that produces lethal meningoencephalitis characterized by robust leukocyte infiltration, microgliosis without detectable neuronal loss, and a pronounced Th1-skewed inflammatory response peaking at day 6 post-infection. Viral replication is confined to the CNS, and flow cytometry plus cytokine profiling reveal recruitment/activation of macrophages, neutrophils, and CD4/CD8 T cells with elevated T-bet and proinflammatory chemokines/cytokines (e.g., CXCL9/10, IFN-γ, CCL2/3/4/5, IL-6).

title: MIRO1 mutation leads to metabolic maladaptation resulting in Parkinson's disease-associated dopaminergic neuron loss.
summary: Using patient-specific iPSC-derived midbrain organoids carrying the MIRO1 (RHOT1) p.R272Q mutation, the study combines single-cell RNA sequencing and multi-cell metabolic modeling to show an altered dopaminergic neuron developmental trajectory, mitochondrial dysfunction, and disrupted neuron–astrocyte metabolic crosstalk. Flux analyses predict increased glycolysis and lactate shuttling with reduced TCA/OXPHOS activity, and experiments confirm decreased mitochondrial membrane potential and elevated ROS, suggesting metabolic maladaptation underlies selective dopaminergic neuron loss.

title: Molecular mechanisms of transhydrogenase activity and allosteric regulation in eukaryotic type II PHGDH Ser33.
summary: This study elucidates the structural and mechanistic basis of transhydrogenase activity and serine-mediated allosteric regulation in the eukaryotic type II PHGDH Ser33 from Saccharomyces cerevisiae. High-resolution crystal structures, mutational analyses, enzyme kinetics, molecular dynamics, and phylogenetics reveal how an NADH-locked cofactor site, a Type II-specific CXC motif, and a fungal-specific N-terminal extension coordinate substrate recognition, internal NAD+/NADH cycling with α-ketoglutarate reduction to D-2-hydroxyglutarate, and negative feedback by L-serine.

title: The Medicago truncatula lncRNA ENOD40 is a mediator of microRNA169-controlled NF-YA activity in nodule initiation.
summary: This study shows that the conserved box2 region of the plant lncRNA ENOD40 acts as a miR169 target mimic to relieve repression of NF-YA1, thereby enabling root nodule initiation in the model legume Medicago truncatula. Genetic complementation, transient luciferase assays, and expression analyses demonstrate that box2-mediated mimicry elevates NF-YA1 mRNA levels, rescuing nodule initiation defects in ENOD40 double mutants.

title: Year-long, multiple-timepoint field studies show the importance of spatiotemporal dynamics and microbial functions in agricultural soil microbiomes
summary: In a year-long, multi-depth, multi-plot field study across two agricultural fields, the authors combined metabarcoding, PLFA, and metatranscriptomics to show that temporal and spatial dynamics outweigh compost and biochar amendments in shaping soil bacterial and fungal communities and their activity. Functional gene expression varied strongly with season (particularly in topsoil), while organic amendments affected fewer than 2% of ASVs and had negligible effects on functional profiles.

title: Delivering cytokine mRNA to secondary lymphoid organs for robust cancer immunotherapy.
crm_level_3: Internal Medicine and Radboud Center for Infectious Diseases (RCI)
summary: The study introduces apolipoprotein nanoparticles (aNPs) that deliver cytokine-encoding mRNA to monocytes in secondary lymphoid organs, enabling sustained in situ cytokine production (e.g., IL-2, IFN-γ) and robust anti-tumor effects in multiple mouse models while minimizing hepatocyte translation. The platform shows spleen/lymph node tropism by PET, translates functionally in non-human primates, performs ex vivo on patient monocytes, and is supported by scalable, stable manufacturing enabling long-term storage.

title: Cytoplasmic inheritance: The transmission of plastid and mitochondrial genomes across cells and generations.
summary: This topical review synthesizes mechanisms governing cytoplasmic inheritance of plastid and mitochondrial genomes in plants and algae, emphasizing vegetative segregation and a spectrum of uniparental to biparental transmission patterns shaped by organelle exclusion, genome degradation, cytoplasmic stripping, sperm dimorphism, selective replication, organelle positioning, and developmental bottlenecks. It highlights recent genetic findings (e.g., DPD1, M20, Otu2p) and emerging tools that enable deeper study and potential manipulation of cytoplasmic inheritance for plant breeding.

title: Encapsulating volatiles by spray drying: The choice of dextrose equivalent influences d-limonene retention via skin formation and particle morphology.
summary: This study investigated how the dextrose equivalent (DE) of maltodextrin affects retention of d-limonene during spray drying of pea-protein-stabilized oil-in-water emulsions, keeping solids (20 wt%), oil (6 wt%), and process conditions constant. Contrary to the hypothesis that lower DE (earlier skin formation) would improve retention, lower DE produced more porous, dented particles with higher surface oil and larger internal cavities, resulting in reduced d-limonene retention due to morphology-driven losses.

title: Protein phosphatase 2 phosphatase activator (PTPA) promotes oncogene-induced senescence and carboplatin response in human malignant pleural mesothelioma cells.
summary: This study shows that heterozygous loss of PPP2R4 (PTPA), a PP2A activator, is frequent in malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM) and correlates with worse overall survival, while re-expression of PTPA in PTPA-low MPM cells increases PP2A activity, triggers oncogene-induced senescence via KSR1/MEK/ERK and p53/p21 pathways, and reduces tumor cell growth. PTPA re-expression also sensitizes MPM cells to carboplatin, suggesting that preventing oncogene-induced senescence through PTPA loss may contribute to mesothelial transformation and chemoresistance.

title: Filter-Aided Extracellular Vesicle Enrichment (FAEVEr) for Proteomics.
summary: This study introduces FAEVEr, a filter-aided extracellular vesicle enrichment workflow using 300 kDa MWCO ultrafiltration and Tween-20 washes to remove non-EV proteins, followed by on-filter SDS lysis and S-Trap-based proteomic preparation, yielding cleaner and more reproducible EV proteomes than ultracentrifugation. The method was validated with recombinant EVs and applied to conditioned media, bovine serum, human plasma, and urine, and it revealed that serum deprivation markedly alters the EV proteome of MCF7 cells.

title: A Quantitative Printability Framework for Programmable Assembly of Pre-Vascular Patterns via Laser-Induced Forward Transfer.
summary: This study establishes a quantitative printability framework for laser-induced forward transfer (LIFT) bioprinting to deterministically micropattern pre-vascular cell arrays with high viability and spatial fidelity. By mapping laser, distance, ink volume, and viscosity into a single printability score and leveraging Poisson-based cell loading control, the authors demonstrate tunable endothelial morphogenesis and stable HUVEC–BM-hMSC co-patterned microvascular-like networks across tailored hydrogel receivers.

title: Equine monocyte-derived macrophages revisited: isolation and comprehensive characterization of pro- versus anti-inflammatory polarisation.
summary: The study establishes a robust, reproducible workflow to isolate equine peripheral blood CD172a+ monocytes, differentiate them into macrophages, and polarize them toward pro- (IFN-γ/LPS) or anti-inflammatory (IL-4) phenotypes, with comprehensive characterization at morphological, transcript, protein, and secretome levels. Conditioned media from these polarized macrophages altered proliferation and gene expression of equine tendon cells, supporting the platform’s utility for modeling inflammation and repair in translational equine systems.

title: From bats to humans: uncovering ISG15 as a new resistance factor in type 1 diabetes.
summary: The study identifies ISG15 as a key antiviral resistance factor enriched in human pancreatic alpha cells, showing that alpha cells share bat-like antiviral gene programs and greater intrinsic resistance compared to beta cells. ISG15 knockdown heightens IFNα-driven inflammatory responses, apoptosis, and coxsackievirus B1 replication in human islet models, while ISG15 overexpression protects beta cells, suggesting a convergent antiviral strategy and a potential therapeutic target in type 1 diabetes.

title: Non-polio enteroviruses compromise the electrophysiology of a human iPSC-derived neural network.
summary: Using human iPSC-derived neural co-cultures (Ngn2-induced excitatory neurons with astrocytes) and micro-electrode arrays, the authors compared EV-D68 and EV-A71 replication, tropism, and functional impact on neural networks. EV-D68 (especially A2/2018) preferentially infected neurons and caused rapid, sustained suppression of spontaneous and network activity, whereas EV-A71 infected neurons and astrocytes equally yet produced less consistent functional impairment; notably, EV-D68 B3/2019 released little infectious progeny but still spread and reduced neurotransmission, indicating virus-specific neurofunctional effects not strictly correlated with replication efficiency.

title: Postmortem muscle proteomics reveals breed specific responses to environmental enrichment and broiler meat quality.
summary: This study used mass spectrometry-based proteomics to compare how slower-growing (Hubbard S757N) and faster-growing (Hubbard JA787) broilers reared with or without environmental enrichment differ in muscle biology, performance, and meat quality. Slower-growing broilers showed stronger cytoskeletal and detoxification profiles and benefited from enrichment (enhanced immune/metabolic resilience and improved meat composition), whereas faster-growing birds emphasized anabolic pathways, accumulated more intramuscular fat, and exhibited reduced breast yield under enrichment, likely due to elevated proteasome activity.

title: Identification of RNF114 as ADPr-Ub reader through non-hydrolysable ubiquitinated ADP-ribose.
summary: The authors synthesized a non‑hydrolysable ADP‑ribose–ubiquitin (ADPr‑Ub) probe and used it to identify RNF114 as a high‑affinity reader of the hybrid ADPr‑Ub modification. They show that RNF114 recognizes ADPr‑Ub via its tandem ZnF2+ZnF3 and UIM domains and uniquely elongates it with K11‑linked ubiquitin chains, promoting recruitment to DNA damage sites.

title: Albumin Restores Endothelial Cell Mitochondrial Morphology in Patients With Decompensated Cirrhosis.
summary: This ex vivo study shows that plasma from patients with decompensated cirrhosis and hypoalbuminemia induces endothelial cell mitochondrial fragmentation and elevated respiration, and that adding albumin restores mitochondrial morphology and normalizes respiration without increasing ROS. Albumin did not mitigate EC activation by individual factors (LPS, TNFα, bilirubin), suggesting its primary effect is direct modulation of mitochondrial function rather than neutralization of specific mediators.

title: Triple-negative breast cancer modifies the systemic immune landscape and alters neutrophil functionality.
summary: In a comprehensive analysis of fresh peripheral blood from patients with triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) and healthy donors, metastatic TNBC was associated with reduced circulating T cells, dendritic cells, and differentiated B cells, alongside disease-driven increases in classical monocytes and neutrophils. Neutrophils from TNBC patients showed enhanced migration, elevated granule proteins, and greater ROS production, while Vδ1 γδ T cells produced more IL-17; some alterations appeared already in earlier TNBC stages and reductions in T cells/DCs were linked to prior chemotherapy.

title: Brain Pericytes and Wnt/β-Catenin Signaling Induce Functional Blood-Brain Barrier Phenotype in Human iPSC-Derived Model.
summary: The authors present a human iPSC-derived blood–brain barrier model in which naïve endothelial cells acquire a bona fide brain microvascular endothelial cell phenotype by co-culture with isogenic brain pericytes and transient activation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling, yielding tight junctions, lower permeability, functional P-glycoprotein efflux, and appropriately attenuated inflammatory responses. Bulk RNA-seq shows that pericyte cues and Wnt activation synergize through ETS1, SMAD3/4, and PPARγ networks, and the approach is validated in a self-organized 3D microvascular chip, providing a translational platform for drug screening and disease modeling.

title: Cardiovirus-Mediated PKR inhibition results from nucleocytoplasmic trafficking disruption.
summary: This study shows that cardioviruses inhibit PKR by disrupting nucleocytoplasmic trafficking through the viral leader (L) protein, which retargets RSK kinases to nuclear pore FG-nucleoporins, opening the NPC and relocalizing factors. Disruption of trafficking drives PKR sequestration to nucleoli where it remains inactive, and causes nuclear RNA-binding proteins to diffuse into the cytosol, likely competing with PKR for dsRNA and further preventing its activation.

title: Mucosal administration of lipid nanoparticles containing self-amplifying mRNA induces local uptake and expression in a pig model as a potential vaccination platform against STIs.
summary: This study evaluates mucosal delivery of self-amplifying mRNA encapsulated in lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) in pigs, showing that formulations retain potency after spraying and exposure to porcine mucus, but not a human cervicovaginal simulant. In vivo, intranasal/vaginal injection yielded uptake and expression at mucosa and draining lymph nodes, whereas mucosal spraying produced transient expression only in the vaginal mucosa (lost by day 4), with minimal differences between two LNP formulations.

title: Cytoplasmic lattices are megadalton storage complexes in mammalian oocytes.
summary: Using cryo-EM single-particle analysis at ~4.2 Å resolution and AI-guided model fitting, the authors determine that mammalian oocyte cytoplasmic lattices (CPLs) are megadalton assemblies built from at least 13 proteins, including PADI6 rings, subcortical maternal complex components, unpolymerized α/β-tubulin dimers, and ubiquitination factors such as UHRF1, UBE2, and FBXW adapters. The structures reveal how PADI6 and SCMC scaffold CPL architecture to stockpile essential maternal proteins, providing a molecular mechanism linking CPL disruption to infertility and early developmental defects.

title: Regional comparison of efficacy and safety for vilobelimab in critically ill, invasively mechanically ventilated COVID-19 patients.
summary: This regional analysis of the PANAMO phase 3 double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial assessed vilobelimab (anti-C5a monoclonal antibody) in critically ill, invasively mechanically ventilated COVID-19 patients and found a significant reduction in 28- and 60-day all-cause mortality in western Europe, with neutral results in South America and a trend toward benefit in South Africa/Russia. The variation was attributed partly to an age imbalance (notably a younger placebo group in Brazil) and potential differences in standard of care, while safety was generally favorable and comparable across regions.

title: Dysregulation of Inositol Polyphosphate 5-Phosphatase OCRL in Alzheimer's Disease: Implications for Autophagy Dysfunction.
summary: The study shows that the inositol polyphosphate 5-phosphatase OCRL is abnormally redistributed in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) brains, being depleted from RIPA-soluble fractions and enriched in insoluble fractions, correlating with Beclin1 and accumulating in plaque-associated dystrophic neurites in both human AD and 5XFAD mouse brains. Overexpression of OCRL in a HEK tau FRET biosensor reduced tau seeding induced by AD-derived sarkosyl-insoluble tau, suggesting OCRL dysregulation contributes to autophagy defects and tau pathology despite unchanged OCRL/BECN1 RNA levels and no detectable OCRL PTM shifts by 2D Western blotting.

title: Potential of ultrasonication to produce low-salt surimi from blue mussel (Mytilus edulis) meat.
summary: This study evaluates high-intensity ultrasonication (HIUS) as a non-thermal strategy to produce low-salt surimi from blue mussel (Mytilus edulis) meat by systematically varying NaCl (1–3%), sonication amplitude (20–90%), and time (5–60 min). HIUS significantly increased protein solubility, reduced particle size, altered secondary structure (more intermolecular β-sheets), improved water-holding capacity and whiteness, while excessive sonication at high salt weakened gels, demonstrating a practical route to lower-sodium mussel surimi with optimized processing conditions.

title: Branched tetrameric lactoferricin peptides modified with diaminopropionic acid exhibit potent antimicrobial and wound-healing activities.
summary: The study engineered branched tetrameric lactoferricin derivatives and identified a diaminopropionic acid–modified variant (LBT-1) with superior broad-spectrum antimicrobial, antifungal, immunomodulatory, and pro-regenerative activities compared to the parent tetramer (LBT). LBT-1 rapidly kills MRSA and MDR A. baumannii, neutralizes LPS-induced inflammation, enhances macrophage bacterial clearance and angiogenesis, and significantly reduces MRSA burden in an ex vivo human skin wound model.

title: The role of finite strain kinematics in the natural fibre reinforcement of peat and other soft organic soils.
summary: The study combines tensile testing and dynamic image analysis of peat fibres with a finite‑strain numerical framework to quantify how natural fibre networks reinforce peat under large deformations. It shows that fibre strength and stiffness are size‑dependent and stochastic, introduces a 3D supershape-based orientation distribution, and demonstrates that fibre reorientation and volumetric changes, together with strain history, control anisotropic reinforcement and match triaxial test observations.

title: Elevated IL-6, IL-10, and IFN-γ levels in fatal elephant endotheliotropic herpesvirus - hemorrhagic disease cases suggest an excessive proinflammatory cytokine response contributes to pathogenesis.
summary: This study measured cytokine mRNA in blood and tissues from 11 EEHV hemorrhagic disease (EEHV-HD) cases and 12 controls, finding significantly elevated IFN-γ, IL-6, and IL-10 (and reduced IL-2) associated with high viral loads in heart and liver, consistent with a pathogen-induced cytokine storm. The authors propose that excessive proinflammatory responses contribute to EEHV-HD pathogenesis and suggest evaluating anti-inflammatory therapies, such as glucocorticoids, to improve outcomes.

title: Protein flexibility drives sugar rotation and high substrate promiscuity in a GDP-sugar 4-epimerase.
summary: This study elucidates how protein flexibility in the Pyrococcus horikoshii GDP-sugar 4-epimerase (PhGal4E_1) drives sugar-ring rotation and underpins its broad substrate promiscuity. X-ray structures (holo and GDP-L-fucose Michaelis complex), docking, and 500-ns MD simulations reveal a dynamic hydrogen-bond network (involving P80, H182, R83, N174) that modulates phosphate and sugar positioning, with mutagenesis confirming their essential roles in catalysis.

title: Proliferative Cell Targeting and Epithelial Cell Turnover Fuels Hepatitis E Virus Replication in Human Intestinal Enteroids.
summary: This study establishes a human intestinal enteroid (HIE) model for hepatitis E virus (HEV) showing limited replication after direct infection of 3D/2D cultures but robust, sustained replication and release of highly infectious nonenveloped virions when HIEs are electroporated with capped HEV RNA. HEV predominantly targets proliferative stem/progenitor cells while also infecting enterocytes, goblet, and enteroendocrine cells, supporting the gut as an HEV reservoir contributing to fecal shedding.

title: Using muscle homing peptide CyPep10 to deliver phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomers in the mdx mouse.
summary: The study evaluated the muscle-homing peptide CyPep10 (CP10) conjugated to phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomers (PMOs) in mdx mice and found that CP10 increased PMO concentrations in muscle but did not enhance exon skipping or dystrophin restoration compared with naked PMO. A linear double conjugate combining CP10 with a cell-penetrating peptide (CPP) modestly improved exon skipping, dystrophin restoration, and histopathology versus PMO alone, with no adverse effects on liver/kidney markers.

title: A single-cell and spatial wheat root atlas with cross-species annotations delineates conserved tissue-specific marker genes and regulators.
summary: This study presents a single-cell RNA-seq atlas of soil-grown wheat (Triticum aestivum) root apical meristems, with cluster identities assigned by a cross-species orthology-based pipeline and validated using untargeted spatial transcriptomics (STOmics Stereo-seq). The resource identifies conserved tissue-specific marker genes and predicts cell type-specific gene regulatory networks across wheat, rice, maize, and Arabidopsis.

title: Echinacoside reduces intracellular c-di-GMP levels and potentiates tobramycin activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilm aggregates.
summary: This study identifies the diguanylate cyclase SiaD as essential for Pseudomonas aeruginosa auto-aggregation in a cystic fibrosis-like environment and uses virtual screening to discover echinacoside as a putative SiaD inhibitor that lowers intracellular c-di-GMP and reduces aggregate size. Echinacoside synergistically enhances tobramycin activity against P. aeruginosa aggregates in SCFM2, on 3-D human A549 lung epithelial cells, and in murine lungs, highlighting its potential as an adjunctive anti-biofilm therapy.

title: UBE3A promotes foam cell formation and counters remyelination by targeting ABCA1 for proteasomal degradation.
summary: The study demonstrates that the E3 ubiquitin ligase UBE3A ubiquitinates and targets the cholesterol efflux transporter ABCA1 for proteasomal degradation in myelin-laden macrophages, driving foam cell formation and an inflammatory phenotype that impairs remyelination. Genetic loss of UBE3A stabilizes ABCA1, enhances cholesterol efflux, reduces lipid accumulation and inflammation, improves remyelination ex vivo and in vivo, and is regulated by TIP30, which retains UBE3A in the cytoplasm via importin β-dependent nuclear import inhibition.

title: Base barrier cells provide compartmentalization of choroid plexus, brain and CSF.
summary: This study identifies choroid plexus base barrier cells (BBCs), a fibroblast population at the choroid plexus–brain attachment that forms tight and adherens junctions to compartmentalize the choroid plexus stroma, brain parenchyma, and cerebrospinal fluid, and shows they are conserved in mouse and human. Through scRNA-seq, lineage tracing, high-resolution imaging, and tracer assays, the authors demonstrate BBCs arise from meningeal mesenchyme, restrict small-molecule and immune-cell movement under homeostasis, and become permeable during systemic inflammation.

title: Dietary fructo-oligosaccharides dose-dependently modulate the microbiome and suppress type 2 lung inflammation in a murine model of house dust mite-induced allergic asthma.
summary: In a murine model of house dust mite-induced allergic asthma, dietary fructo-oligosaccharides (FOS) modulated the gut microbiome and dose-dependently attenuated lung type 2 immunity, with 10% FOS reducing pulmonary Th2 cells, Th2/Th1 ratios, and BALF IL-13/CCL22 despite unchanged eosinophilic inflammation. High-dose FOS increased fecal Prevotellaceae and was associated with higher serum acetate and reduced type 2 markers, underscoring dose-specific microbiome-metabolite-immune interactions along the gut–lung axis.

title: Neutrophils as critical orchestrators of chronic inflammation.
summary: This narrative review synthesizes current knowledge on how neutrophils orchestrate chronic inflammation through effector functions (ROS, degranulation, NETs, programmed cell death) and cross‑talk with endothelial cells, platelets, monocytes/macrophages, and adaptive immunity. It maps neutrophil contributions across major immune-driven diseases (rheumatoid arthritis, atherosclerosis, inflammatory bowel disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, COPD, and fibrotic disorders), highlighting mechanistic pathways and potential therapeutic implications.

title: Origin and development of uniparental and polyploid blastomeres.
summary: By haplotyping 118 early bovine blastomeres and profiling 446 single-cell transcriptomes, the study shows that heterogoneic division—segregation of entire parental genomes into different blastomeres—occurs in both multipolar and, more rarely, bipolar first cleavages, generating uniparental and polyploid cells alongside normal diploid cells. Whole‑genome abnormal cells exhibit impaired development linked to stress responses during embryonic genome activation, yet some still reach blastocyst stage, suggesting that haplotype-based screening alongside PGT-A could improve IVF outcomes.

title: Cyanobacterial Argonautes and Cas4 family nucleases cooperate to interfere with invading DNA.
summary: This study shows that cyanobacterial long-A prokaryotic Argonaute proteins (pAgos) partner with a co-encoded Cas4-family nuclease (ACE1) to enhance DNA interference against plasmids and bacteriophages. Structural, biochemical, and in vivo analyses reveal that ACE1 is an ssDNA endonuclease that trims or generates siDNA guides and forms a heterodimeric complex with pAgo, boosting pAgo-mediated immunity in E. coli.

title: CARD14 signaling in intestinal epithelial cells induces intestinal inflammation and intestinal transit delay.
summary: This study shows that activating a psoriasis-associated gain-of-function CARD14(E138A) mutant specifically in intestinal epithelial cells (IEC) of mice induces mild intestinal inflammation and markedly delays intestinal transit without epithelial damage. Mechanistically, CARD14 signaling decreases Paneth cell antimicrobial peptide expression, alters the microbiota, and heightens susceptibility to Citrobacter rodentium infection; these effects require the MALT1 scaffold function but not its protease activity and appear linked to microbiome-dependent epithelial–neuronal communication rather than enteric neuron loss.

title: Transient ER stress cell-autonomously promotes beta cell cycling in mice.
summary: In mice, transient endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress induced by beta cell-specific overexpression of sFLT1 or GFP triggers a subsequent increase in beta cell proliferation upon stress relief, independent of islet revascularization, with accompanying shifts in UPR signaling and beta cell maturity markers. Brief in vitro ER stress (thapsigargin or tunicamycin) followed by washout similarly increased beta cell cycling—potentiated by high glucose—and coincided with elevated mTORC1 signaling rather than Akt activation.

title: HMOS 2'FL and 3FL prevent house dust mite induced proinflammatory cytokine release in vitro and decrease specific IgE production in a murine allergic asthma model.
summary: This study developed a human in vitro airway mucosal coculture model (Calu-3 bronchial epithelial cells with monocyte-derived dendritic cells and naïve T cells) to examine HDM-induced type 2 immunity and tested the immunomodulatory effects of human milk oligosaccharides 2′-fucosyllactose (2’FL) and 3-fucosyllactose (3FL). Both HMOS prevented HDM-induced epithelial/DC activation and shifted downstream T cell responses away from type 2 in vitro, and in vivo dietary 1% 2’FL or 0.5% 3FL reduced HDM-specific IgE in a murine asthma model without significantly reducing airway inflammation.

title: Dracaena trifasciata (Prain) Mabb leaf extract protects MIN6 pancreas-derived beta cells against the diabetic toxin streptozotocin: role of the NF-κB pathway.
summary: This study shows that a methanolic leaf extract of Dracaena (Sansevieria) trifasciata protects mouse pancreatic beta-cell line MIN6 from streptozotocin-induced cytotoxicity, an effect that depends on an intact NF-κB pathway. However, the extract induces pro-inflammatory gene expression in macrophage-like RAW cells and, in the presence of TNF-α or NF-κB blockade (MG132), loses its protective effect on MIN6 cells.

title: In vitro fermentation potential of undigested dietary protein.
summary: This study quantified the in vitro fermentation potential of undigested protein entering the hindgut by incubating pooled ileal digesta from pigs fed seven plant protein sources with porcine fecal inoculum and continuously recording gas production. Fermentation kinetics and a new standardized gas production potential (SGPpro) metric revealed large source-dependent differences, with maize germ meal showing the highest hindgut fermentation potential and soybean meal the lowest, influenced by nitrogen solubility and molecular mass distribution.

title: Synaptic signatures and disease vulnerabilities of layer 5 pyramidal neurons.
crm_level_3: VIB Center for Brain & Disease Research
summary: The study uses an optimized in vivo proximity biotinylation strategy (TurboID fused to PSD95 or Homer1) to profile the excitatory postsynaptic proteomes of genetically defined layer 5 intratelencephalic (IT) and pyramidal tract (PT) neurons in mouse somatosensory cortex. Data-independent LC-MS/MS reveals distinct synaptic protein signatures and a marked enrichment of autism risk genes in IT neuron postsynaptic proteomes, indicating differential disease vulnerability between IT and PT neurons.

title: Synthesis and Characterization of Curcumin-Polycaprolactone Block Copolymers for Biomedical Applications.
summary: The authors synthesized a curcumin–polycaprolactone (MCP) block copolymer by ring-opening polymerization of ε-caprolactone initiated from maleic anhydride–modified curcumin, and characterized it by FTIR, 1H NMR, UV–Vis, and DSC. MCP was processable by electrospinning, 3D printing, and molding, showed UV-blocking, antioxidant activity, biocompatibility and enhanced fibroblast migration, and—when incorporated with Cu or Fe into PVA films—displayed selective anti-Pseudomonas activity without systemic or contact toxicity in Galleria mellonella.

title: Suspension cultivation of mosquito cell lines for the production of the mosquito-borne flavivirus Usutu virus in a stirred-tank bioreactor.
summary: This study adapts Aedes albopictus C6/36 and U4.4 mosquito cell lines to serum-free, chemically defined EX-CELL medium for suspension growth, achieving high cell densities in shake flasks and, for C6/36, in a stirred-tank bioreactor. As a proof-of-concept, C6/36 cells in a 500 mL STR produced high Usutu virus titers (>3.6×10^8 TCID50/mL), matching adherent cultures and demonstrating a scalable serum-free platform for mosquito-borne virus production.

title: Mesenchymal stem cells suppress NF-κB and ERK signalling while enhancing chemotaxis in CD4+ T cells.
summary: The study shows that umbilical cord–derived mesenchymal stem cells (UC‑MSCs) modulate TCR-activated human CD4+ T cells by suppressing NF-κB and ERK signaling while enhancing expression of chemotaxis and adhesion genes, promoting a resting memory-like phenotype. RNA-seq and phospho-flow cytometry identified upregulation of inhibitory regulators (e.g., TNIP1, NFKBIA, DUSP5) and reduced phosphorylation of p65 and ERK1/2 (but not p38), with increased chemokines (CXCL9/10/11, CCL5/20) in co-cultured T cells.

title: Lipocalin 2 deficiency impacts angiogenesis after ischemia in vivo and in vitro.
summary: This study identifies lipocalin 2 (LCN2) as a pro-angiogenic factor upregulated after hind limb ischemia and shows that Lcn2 deficiency impairs angiogenesis in vivo (reduced capillary density/size) and ex vivo (decreased aortic ring sprouting), and diminishes human microvascular endothelial cell migration and tube formation in vitro. Despite these angiogenic effects, arteriogenesis, collateral density, and overall blood flow recovery after ischemia were unchanged in Lcn2 knockout mice compared with wild-type controls.

title: Human brain prefrontal cortex proteomics identifies compromised energy metabolism and neuronal function in Schizophrenia.
summary: This study performed deep, DIA-based proteomics on laser-capture microdissected dorsal prefrontal cortex layers (1–3 and 4–6) from 47 schizophrenia cases and 49 controls, identifying 387 differentially expressed proteins with highly concordant effects across layers. Findings indicate downregulation of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, ribosomes, and proteasome, with upregulation of kinases and small GTPase regulators, enrichment of genetic risk signals (GWAS/pQTL), and convergence with snRNA-seq, pointing to energy deficits impacting synaptic and neuronal functions in schizophrenia.

title: Protocol for insulin dosing during expansion and maturation of human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes.
summary: This STAR Protocol provides a workflow to control proliferation versus maturation of human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes by tuning insulin levels alongside Wnt/β-catenin signaling. It details differentiation, lactate-based purification, replating, cryopreservation/thawing, expansion with high insulin plus CHIR99021, and maturation via insulin withdrawal or low-dose insulin to boost metabolism without reactivating the cell cycle.

title: Axonal Eif5a hypusination controls local translation and mitigates defects in FUS-ALS.
crm_level_3: VIB-KU Leuven Center for Brain & Disease Research
summary: Using spatial transcriptomics and single-molecule smFISH, the study maps subcellular RNA profiles of adult mouse motor neuron somas and sciatic nerve axons, revealing robust enrichment of translation machinery in mature axons and axon-type–specific RNA signatures. ALS-linked FUS mutations reduce axonal hypusinated Eif5a and impair local translation, which is rescued by axon-targeted spermidine in neurons and improves phenotypes in FUS and TDP-43 Drosophila models, suggesting a therapeutic avenue via restoring Eif5a hypusination.

title: Predicting therapeutic responses in metastatic colorectal cancer through personalized functional profiling of patient-derived spheroids.
summary: This study develops and validates a personalized functional profiling platform using patient-derived spheroids from metastatic colorectal cancer to screen 42 drugs and standard-of-care regimens, showing that spheroids preserve histopathological and genomic fidelity to parental tumors and that ex vivo anti-EGFR responses correlate with clinical outcomes. Anti-VEGFR agents showed limited activity ex vivo, cryopreserved spheroids performed comparably to fresh, and combined genomic and functional data highlighted candidates for ERBB2/ERBB3-targeted therapy while underscoring areas for workflow refinement to enhance clinical applicability.

title: An oncolytic herpesvirus expressing a CXCR4 antagonist interferes with glioblastoma cells' stemness features and migration.
summary: The authors engineered an oncolytic HSV-1 (Δγ34.5/ΔUL39/ΔICP47) that expresses and secretes a CXCR4 antagonist (CXCL12 P2G-HA), which antagonizes CXCR4 signaling and reduces stemness marker expression, self‑renewal, and migration of human patient‑derived glioblastoma stem‑like cells (GSCs) in vitro. In an orthotopic xenograft model, intratumoral oHSV/P2G decreased tumor growth and markedly limited GBM cell migration toward the corpus callosum, although overall tumor control was similar to unarmed oHSV in immunodeficient mice.

title: Usambarensine from Strychnos usambarensis: Revisiting a Bis-Indole Alkaloid for Antiviral Repositioning.
crm_level_3: University of Liège Faculty of Medicine
summary: The study isolated and characterized the bis-indole alkaloid usambarensine from Strychnos usambarensis and demonstrated its selective antiviral activity against coronaviruses (SARS-CoV-2, SARS-CoV-1, MERS-CoV) in Vero E6 cells, achieving up to ~4 log10 reductions in viral RNA. Data suggest interference with an early coronavirus entry/fusion process, motivating mechanistic studies and structure–activity optimization to develop usambarensine as a coronavirus entry inhibitor scaffold.

title: Tributyrin (CoreBiome®) enhances butyrate levels and modulates the gut microbiota, barrier function, and immune response in vitro.
summary: This in vitro study evaluated the stability and colonic delivery of tributyrin (CoreBiome) and its effects on the human gut microbiome, barrier function, and immune responses using SHIME reactors and Caco-2/THP1 co-cultures. Over half of tributyrin survived upper GI transit, increased colonic butyrate, shifted microbial composition (e.g., enriching Bifidobacterium spp. and Akkermansia muciniphila), improved barrier integrity, and modulated cytokines (increased IL-10, decreased TNF-α).

title: Characterization of Extracellular Vesicles from Streptococcus thermophilus 065 and Their Potential to Modulate the Immune Response.
summary: This study isolated and characterized extracellular vesicles (EVs) produced by Streptococcus thermophilus 065 during growth, showing EVs enriched in membrane-associated transporters, glycolytic and ribosomal proteins, and prophage-derived proteins, with mitomycin C induction amplifying phage protein expression and EV release. EVs and producer cells differentially modulated cytokine and chemokine release from human PBMCs, indicating EVs’ potential as postbiotics for immune modulation.

title: Osteoarthritic chondrocytes exert higher contractile forces and exhibit enhanced protrusive activity when cultured in 3D degradable hydrogels.
summary: The study compares active force generation by human osteoarthritic (OA) versus non-OA articular chondrocytes using 2D and 3D traction force microscopy and shows that OA cells exert significantly higher contractile forces only in 3D degradable PEG hydrogels, not on 2D non-degradable substrates. This enhanced 3D contractility coincides with increased protrusive activity, higher actomyosin content/coupling, and altered adhesion/matrix protein localization in OA chondrocytes, underscoring the importance of 3D degradable environments for revealing OA-specific mechanobiology.

title: Policy principles for sustainable and just land systems.
summary: This article proposes eight guiding principles for designing land-system policies that are both sustainable and just, structured along a heuristic policy cycle: recognitional justice, political strategy, multiple goals, addressing systemic issues, integrative scope, co-development, clear and monitorable targets, and diagnostic/adaptive capacities. Applying these principles to land-based climate mitigation and biodiversity-friendly agriculture, the authors show how narrow, top-down agenda setting leads to misalignment and weak outcomes, while policy mixes like Brazil’s PPCDAm and Kenya’s agroecology strategies illustrate more aligned, politically feasible pathways that integrate multiple goals, co-development, and adaptive monitoring.

title: A Metagenomic Survey of Virological Hazards in Market-Ready Oysters.
summary: This study used hybridization capture-based viral metagenomics to survey vertebrate viral nucleic acids in 144 market-ready oyster batches from the Dutch market (2015–2021) and demonstrated linear, sensitive detection of norovirus alongside identification of fifteen human-associated viral species, including norovirus, sapovirus, adeno-associated dependoparvoviruses, Aichi viruses, and others. The workflow showed sensitivity down to 5–14 genome copies for norovirus spikes, and results were partially verified by (RT-)dPCR and subtyping, underscoring metagenomics’ utility for hazard identification in shellfish while noting low viral loads and the need for infectivity assessment and improved reference databases.

title: Gut bacterium Intestinimonas butyriciproducens improves host metabolic health: evidence from cohort and animal intervention studies.
summary: This study links the abundance of the gut bacterium Intestinimonas butyriciproducens and its fructoselysine-to-butyrate metabolic pathway to improved metabolic markers in humans, and demonstrates in mice that oral supplementation with I. butyriciproducens GL3 reduces weight gain, adiposity, inflammation, and fasting glucose while increasing cecal and plasma short-chain fatty acids. The findings support I. butyriciproducens as a candidate microbiota-based therapy for metabolic disease by converting dietary fructoselysine into beneficial butyrate and acetate.

title: A Pilot-Scale Evaluation of Duckweed Cultivation for Pig Manure Treatment and Feed Production.
summary: This pilot-scale study evaluated three outdoor duckweed (Lemna ×japonica) systems treating pig-manure-derived wastewaters over a full temperate growing season, achieving up to ~8.6 t dry biomass/ha/year and ~3.3 t protein/ha/year with nitrogen and phosphorus removals of ~1.2 g N/m²/d and ~0.13 g P/m²/d when fertilized with diluted liquid fraction and nitrification–denitrification effluent. Growth ceased after ~100–140 days due to rising pH and salinity, while harvested duckweed showed a high-protein, balanced amino-acid profile suitable for broilers and promising energy/protein values for ruminants, though high ash/fibre may limit inclusion in monogastrics; constructed-wetland effluent alone caused poor growth due to high EC.

title: Urban heat Islands shape epiphytic communities of lichens and bryophytes.
summary: In a survey of 303 Tilia street trees across Amsterdam, Leiden, and Rotterdam, the authors showed that epiphytic lichen diversity peaks at intermediate urban heat island (UHI) levels while bryophyte diversity increases with UHI, and that biodiversity rises with tree age. They identified 23 biological indicators (lichens, bryophytes, an alga, and total coverage) for distinct UHI zones, with microclimate sensor data (temperature, relative humidity, vapour-pressure deficit) corroborating macro-scale UHI patterns.

title: Characterization of the brain lipidome associated with frontotemporal lobar degeneration MAPT P301S mutation.
summary: This study profiled brain lipids and sterols in MAPT P301S (PS19) tau transgenic mice and found that the mutation increases diglycerides, hexosylceramides, lactosylceramides, and unsaturated phosphatidylethanolamines while decreasing triglycerides—especially those containing monounsaturated fatty acids—without baseline changes in cholesterol. With increasing hippocampal pTau accumulation, neutral storage lipids (cholesteryl esters and triglycerides) rise and cholesterol synthesis/turnover (lanosterol, desmosterol, lathosterol, and 24S-hydroxycholesterol) declines, indicating distinct lipidomic signatures for MAPT mutation and pTau load.

title: Cracking rare disorders: a new minimally invasive RNA-seq protocol.
summary: The study presents a minimally invasive RNA-seq workflow using short-term cultured peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) with and without cycloheximide to unmask nonsense-mediated decay, enabling robust detection of aberrant splicing relevant to Mendelian neurodevelopmental disorders. Applied to 46 patients, the approach identified splicing defects in 6 of 9 targeted splice-variant cases and enabled reclassification of 7 variants, while global analyses (FRASER, OUTRIDER, MAE) supported findings but yielded no additional diagnoses, and a practical diagnostic decision tree is provided.

title: Enabling next-generation engineered TCR-T therapies based on high-throughput TCR discovery from diagnostic tumor biopsies.
crm_level_1: Neogene Therapeutics, A member of the AstraZeneca Group
summary: This study presents a pan-HLA, functional-genetic screening platform that enables high-throughput discovery of tumor-reactive, neoantigen-specific TCRs directly from diagnostic, fresh-frozen tumor biopsies (including core-needle specimens) without requiring viable TIL. By combining tumor mutation/TCR repertoire profiling, synthetic combinatorial TCR and tandem minigene antigen libraries, engineered autologous B-cell antigen presentation, and sensitive activation-based enrichment, the platform identifies both class I and class II TCRs across multiple solid cancers, enabling next-generation, multi-specific TCR-T therapies.

title: Saponin-based adjuvant uptake and induction of antigen cross-presentation by CD11b+ dendritic cells and macrophages.
summary: The study fluorescently labeled saponin-based adjuvants (ISCOMs) with SP-DiIC18(3) and showed that they are preferentially taken up by CD11b+ dendritic cells and macrophages via clathrin-mediated endocytosis, inducing lipid bodies and endosomal antigen translocation to the cytosol. These events enable efficient cross-presentation not only by dendritic cells but also by bone marrow-derived macrophages, leading to robust CD8+ T cell activation and IFN-γ production, highlighting macrophages as contributors to SBA-driven cellular immunity.

title: PD-L1 directed bispecific Vδ2-T cell engager combines lysis of PD-L1 expressing tumor cells with PD-1 immune checkpoint inhibition and modulation of the tumor immune microenvironment.
summary: The authors engineered a bispecific Vδ2 T-cell engager (PD-L1xVδ2 bsTCE) that binds PD-L1 and Vγ9Vδ2 T cells, simultaneously blocking PD-1/PD-L1 and redirecting Vγ9Vδ2 T cells to kill PD-L1+ tumor and myeloid cells. Across melanoma and RCC cell lines, patient-derived tumor suspensions, and 3D spheroids, the bsTCE activated Vγ9Vδ2 T cells, enhanced infiltration and tumor lysis, and shifted the tumor immune microenvironment toward a more proinflammatory, dendritic cell–rich state.

title: Optimization of Sugar-Derivatives Mixtures for Stabilizing Polyclonal Immunoglobulin G in Spray-Dried Inhalable Powders During Processing and Long-Term Storage.
summary: This study used a mixture design of experiments to evaluate D‑mannitol, D‑sucrose, and dextran 10 kDa, alone and in combination, as stabilizers of bovine polyclonal IgG during spray‑drying and 10‑month storage, finding that the binary D‑mannitol/dextran (MD) mixture minimized low‑ and high‑order aggregates at both time points. All dry powders were largely amorphous with suitable glass transition temperatures and showed good aerosol performance (fine particle fraction up to 71% for the MSD ternary blend), with MD offering the best balance of protein integrity, powder stability, and inhalation efficiency.

title: A robust method for assessing mitochondrial function in healthy and diseased frozen cardiac tissue.
summary: This study develops a high-resolution respirometry method, Tailored Substrate-Inhibitor Titration (TSIT), to assess complex I and II mitochondrial respiratory capacities from frozen cardiac tissue using the Oroboros O2k, enabling multi-step substrate/inhibitor measurements in a single run. TSIT reproduces atrial–ventricular differences seen in fresh tissue, detects dysfunction in aging, Ndufs4−/−, ischemia–reperfusion, and NZO+HFD mouse models, and identifies reduced complex II capacity in human pathological hearts; blue-native electrophoresis reveals coupling between ETC supercomplexes and TCA-cycle enzyme citrate synthase, supporting feasibility in frozen samples.

title: Adaptive radiofrequency shimming in MRI using reconfigurable dielectric materials.
summary: This study introduces a reconfigurable high-permittivity dielectric array with PIN diode-controlled interconnections to adaptively modulate the transmit B1+ field in MRI, enabling cost-effective shimming without modifying scanner hardware. Electromagnetic simulations and 3T phantom experiments showed localized, translatable B1+ modulation up to ~11% at 15 mm depth (measurable to ~95 mm), with performance dependent on dielectric permittivity and wiring configuration.

title: Mitochondria-Targeted Antioxidants Prevent Tachypacing-Induced Contractile Dysfunction in In Vitro Cardiomyocyte and In Vivo Drosophila Models of Atrial Fibrillation.
summary: The study shows that tachypacing induces contractile dysfunction, mitochondrial impairment, and oxidative damage in rat inducible immortalized atrial myocytes (iAMs) and increases arrhythmogenesis and mitochondrial ROS in Drosophila, and that mitochondria-targeted antioxidants MitoTEMPO and Sul-238 prevent these effects. Genetic manipulation demonstrated a causal role for mitochondrial oxidative stress, as SOD2 knockdown worsened dysfunction and arrhythmia while SOD2 overexpression rescued tachypacing-induced phenotypes, highlighting mitochondria-targeted antioxidants as potential therapies for atrial fibrillation.

title: TamL is a Key Player of the Outer Membrane Homeostasis in Bacteroidota.
crm_level_3: Research Unit in Biology of Microorganisms (URBM)
summary: This study shows that the TamA-like lipoprotein TamL and the inner-membrane AsmA-like protein TamB are essential for outer membrane homeostasis in Bacteroidota, using Flavobacterium johnsoniae and Capnocytophaga canimorsus as models. TamL depletion compromises outer membrane integrity, increases release of large OMVs, alters the outer membrane proteome (notably elevating lipoproteins without a global loss of β-barrel proteins), has limited impact on bulk lipids, and reveals a physical interaction with TamB, indicating a TAM-like function distinct from Proteobacteria.
