title: Sex differences in the association between long-term ambient particulate air pollution and the intestinal microbiome composition of children.
summary: In a cohort of 412 Belgian children aged 4–12 years, long-term exposure to particulate air pollution (black carbon, PM2.5, coarse PM, PM10) was associated with sex-specific differences in gut microbiome diversity and composition, with boys showing reduced richness and Shannon diversity and girls showing non-significant positive trends. Differential abundance analyses identified several taxa with opposite associations by sex, highlighting boys as potentially more vulnerable to microbiome diversity loss from particulate exposure.

title: Antiparasitic triterpenic ester and ursolic acid lipid nanocapsule design, cytotoxicity, and permeability evaluation for oral delivery.
summary: This study designed and evaluated lipid nanocapsules (LNCs) to improve the solubility, intestinal permeability, and antiparasitic activity of highly lipophilic triterpenes (ursolic acid, a natural triterpenic ester mixture 8TTE, and a semi-synthetic derivative UAOPP) for potential oral delivery. LNCs were non-toxic to Caco-2 cells up to 2 mg/mL, increased Caco-2 permeability up to 2.68-fold for triterpenic esters (shifting them to moderately absorbed), preserved epithelial integrity compared to free drugs, and enhanced in vitro antitrypanosomal activity of UAOPP while showing limited added benefit for UA due to intrinsic potency constraints and blank LNC effects in antiplasmodial assays.

title: RNA-Binding Proteome-Wide Analysis Reveals Rice RNA-Binding Proteins Enriched After Sobemovirus Rice Yellow Mottle Virus Infection.
crm_level_3: Institute of Botany and Microbiology KU Leuven Leuven Belgium
summary: This study used a silica-based acidic phase separation (SAPS) workflow coupled with UV crosslinking and LC–MS/MS to profile RNA-binding proteome changes in rice leaves following infection with Sobemovirus Rice yellow mottle virus (RYMV). They identified 13 non-viral host RBPs with altered abundance/activity (11 enriched, 2 reduced) and three viral RBPs enriched upon infection, highlighting potential susceptibility factors for resistance breeding.

title: Exopolysaccharides of Lactobacillus crispatus mediate key balancing interactions with the vaginal mucosa.
summary: This study identifies a conserved exopolysaccharide (EPS) biosynthetic locus in Lactobacillus crispatus and demonstrates that the priming glycosyltransferase gene epsE is a key regulator of EPS production that modulates host immune responses at the vaginal mucosa. An epsE knockout reduced capsular sugars, altered adhesion and biofilm phenotypes, and shifted epithelial and immune biomarker profiles (by Olink profiling) in monolayer and 3D vaginal models, with several biomarkers validated in human vaginal swabs.

title: CFAP20 salvages arrested RNAPII from the path of co-directional replisomes.
summary: This study identifies CFAP20 as a nuclear factor that prevents transcription–replication conflicts by salvaging arrested RNAPII at promoter-proximal, co-directional encounters, thereby limiting R-loop accumulation, abnormal fork acceleration, reduced origin firing, and PRIMPOL-dependent ssDNA gaps. Genetic and genomic analyses show that CFAP20 loss causes Mediator-driven transcription stress localized at promoters near replication origins, and that co-depleting Mediator or removing R-loop–engaged RNAPII restores normal replication dynamics and genome stability.

title: Wall shear stress modulates metabolic pathways in endothelial cells.
summary: The study shows that laminar wall shear stress (15 dyn/cm2) reprograms endothelial cell metabolism away from glycolysis toward glutamine-driven anaplerosis, as demonstrated by RNA-seq and 13C tracer metabolomics. Inhibiting glutamate dehydrogenase under shear stress disrupts cytoskeletal integrity and cell–cell junctions, underscoring the necessity of glutamine metabolism for endothelial fitness under flow.

title: Quantifying protein digestion kinetics of feed ingredients using a modified in vitro incubation assay.
summary: The study develops and applies a modified two-step enzymatic in vitro assay to quantify kinetics of nitrogen solubilization and hydrolysis in feed ingredients, incorporating a gastric pH shift (from 4 to 2) and an optional brush-border enzyme step. Tested on rapeseed meal, fish meal, peas, barley, and zein, the assay showed most nitrogen becomes soluble during the gastric phase—especially after lowering pH—fish meal had the fastest solubilization and low–molecular-weight nitrogen appearance, and adding Flavourzyme or rat intestinal acetone powders did not further increase hydrolysis.

title: Transcriptomic profiling of unmethylated full mutation carriers implicates TET3 in FMR1 CGG repeat expansion methylation dynamics in fragile X syndrome.
summary: The study profiles transcriptomes of fibroblasts from two rare unmethylated full mutation (UFM) FMR1 carriers, a fragile X syndrome (FXS) patient, and a control, identifying a robust ~80% downregulation of TET3 in UFM cells and implicating TET3 in the establishment of methylation at the expanded FMR1 CGG repeat. Whole-genome sequencing revealed rare TET3 variants (including a shared 3′UTR SNP) without a definitive cis-acting cause, while developmental and cross-species analyses suggest regulatory differences in TET3 expression that align with human-specific methylation timing at FMR1.

title: Synergistic antibacterial effect of CATH-2 and D-amino acids against mastitis causing gram-positive bacteria.
summary: This study shows that the antimicrobial peptide CATH-2 synergizes strongly with positively charged D-amino acids, especially D-arginine and D-lysine, to inhibit and kill Gram-positive mastitis-causing bacteria, notably Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus uberis, including multidrug-resistant isolates. The combination was effective in LB and raw milk without detectable toxicity to bovine mammary epithelial cells, suggesting a promising intramammary alternative to antibiotics for mastitis treatment.

title: An exploration of markers of microvascular dysfunction in kidney transplant recipients randomized to belatacept: no clinical impact of CNIs on endothelial function.
summary: This randomized conversion study assessed endothelial dysfunction biomarkers, circulating microRNAs, and an endothelial cell morphology assay in kidney transplant recipients switched from calcineurin inhibitors to belatacept versus those maintained on calcineurin inhibitors. No significant differences were observed in Ang-1/Ang-2, soluble thrombomodulin, P-selectin, or miRNA profiles between groups, and although high-dose tacrolimus or cyclosporine altered endothelial cell morphology in vitro, patient plasma did not produce treatment-specific morphological changes, suggesting minimal clinical impact of CNIs on endothelial function at contemporary dosing.

title: Doubling dolutegravir dosage reduces the viral reservoir in ART-treated people with HIV.
summary: This randomized phase 2 clinical trial tested antiretroviral therapy intensification by doubling dolutegravir (DTG) dosage in ART-suppressed adults with HIV and found significant reductions in multiple peripheral blood HIV reservoir markers (total HIV DNA, intact HIV DNA, cell-associated unspliced RNA, and US RNA/total DNA) in the intensified group compared to controls. Intensification modestly reduced T-cell activation/exhaustion markers without measurable effects on systemic or tissue inflammation, while DTG concentrations doubled in plasma and increased in rectal tissue, suggesting the pre-intensification regimen was not fully suppressive.

title: Global relationships between body size and urban affinity across more than 30,000 plant and animal species.
summary: This global synthesis quantified urban tolerance for over 30,000 plant and animal species using GBIF occurrence records and VIIRS night-time lights, introducing Species Urbanness Distributions that show many urban avoiders and few exploiters worldwide. Bayesian analyses across 17,722 species found heterogeneous links between body size and urban tolerance—generally positive in plants and variable in animals—highlighting that body size alone cannot explain urban filtering patterns.

title: Numerical analysis of a multiproduct biorefinery on a chip: Exploiting acoustic waves to process the microalgae Tisochrysis lutea.
summary: The study measures acoustic properties of the marine microalga Tisochrysis lutea and its chloroplasts using a neutrally buoyant state method, then uses these data to model an acoustofluidic ‘biorefinery-on-a-chip’ that harvests cells and fractionates intracellular components via acoustophoresis. Simulations show high-efficiency size-based harvesting and component separation (lipid droplets, chloroplasts, nuclei, starch granules), while composition-only separations are challenging but may be improved with dynamic acoustic fields.

title: A transpupillary approach for crosslinking Guinea pig sclera using WST11 and near-infrared light.
crm_level_1: MERLN Institute for Technology-Inspired Regenerative Medicine
summary: This study optimized a transpupillary near‑infrared (753 nm) WST11-with-dextran (WST-D) crosslinking approach to strengthen guinea pig sclera, showing that 10% dextran limits photosensitizer penetration to the sclera and that ex vivo parameters of WST-D incubation for 30 minutes followed by 10 mW/cm2 NIR for 30 minutes maximized thermal stabilization (ΔT50 up to ~6.8°C). Applying these parameters in vivo via sub-Tenon or retrobulbar WST-D delivery and transpupillary NIR illumination significantly increased scleral thermal stability in both equatorial and posterior regions, with stronger effects in older animals.

title: Integrated multi-omics identifies distinct macrophage alterations during progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis.
summary: This study integrates single-nucleus RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics (GeoMx, CosMx), and multiplex spatial proteomics (COMET, MILAN) on human liver to chart macrophage remodeling across MASLD progression. It reveals depletion of Kupffer cells and expansion of spatially contextualized, antigen-presenting and metabolically adaptive GPNMB+ macrophages (MetMacs) supported by IL32-producing hepatocytes, with markers that stratify disease activity and correlate with circulating proteins (GPNMB, CD163, MSR1).

title: Carbon Emissions From Fires in Eastern Siberian Larch Forests.
summary: This study quantified carbon emissions from 41 burned plots in Cajander larch forests in eastern Siberia and found mean combustion of 3.20 kg C m−2, with 78% originating from organic soil layers, comparable to North American boreal fires. Combustion was most strongly driven by pre-fire organic soil depth, stand attributes, and fire weather, and a spatial model (adjusted R2 ≈ 0.47) extrapolated emissions across two large fire scars.

title: Engineered protein nanoclusters reduce liver fibrosis and hepatocellular carcinoma in mice models.
summary: This study engineers a consensus tetratricopeptide repeat-based protein (C390) that stabilizes gold nanoclusters (C390-AuNC) to inhibit Hsp90, thereby attenuating TGF-β signaling and demonstrating dual anti-fibrotic and anti-tumor efficacy in murine models of acute liver fibrosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In CCl4-induced fibrosis, C390-AuNC reduced profibrotic markers and promoted collagen degradation, while in DEN+CCl4-induced HCC, it lowered oncogenic markers and tumor burden with favorable biodistribution and safety after intraperitoneal administration.

title: De novo H3.3K27M-altered diffuse midline glioma in human brainstem organoids to dissect GD2 CAR T cell function.
crm_level_3: Princess Máxima Center for Pediatric Oncology
summary: The authors develop FGF4-guided human brainstem organoids enriched for pontine/medulla glial lineages and generate de novo H3.3K27M TP53/PDGFRA-altered diffuse midline glioma that recapitulates infiltrative growth and patient-like cellular states. Using this model, they profile prolonged GD2 CAR T cell therapy, reveal effector and exhausted states, demonstrate selection of potent but short-lived NCAM1+ effectors, and show that integrated microglia acquire DMG-specific immunosuppressive phenotypes that increase CAR T exhaustion and reduce tumor control.

title: Reannotation of cancer mutations based on expressed RNA transcripts reveals functional non-coding mutations in melanoma.
summary: By reannotating cancer mutations to the transcripts actually expressed in melanoma, the authors show that many clusters previously labeled as coding are in fact non-coding promoter mutations, including an IRF3/BCL2L12 promoter cluster that lowers IRF3, BCL2L12, and TP53 expression and correlates with poorer immunotherapy response. They introduce a simple Salmon+VEP workflow to annotate mutations relative to expressed transcripts and find that 22% of significant melanoma mutation clusters are non-coding, underscoring the need to integrate DNA- and RNA-seq for accurate mutation interpretation.

title: A robust cell-based infection model for Rhinovirus C research and antiviral drug discovery.
summary: The authors developed a robust, high-content imaging-based, high-throughput screening platform for Rhinovirus C using a genetically stable fluorescent reporter virus (RV-C15a-mGL) and phenotypically selected HeLa clones expressing CDHR3C529Y. The system showed strong assay performance (Z′ > 0.75) in 96- and 384-well formats, was adaptable to multiple RV-C types and RV-A/B, and enabled discovery of known and novel RV-C inhibitors in a 10,240-compound pilot screen.

title: Integrated omics reveal a unique antibacterial mechanism of action for the small molecule HSI#6.
summary: This study uses integrated transcriptomics, proteomics, and functional assays to define the antibacterial mechanism of HSI#6, a rapid, broad-spectrum bacteriostatic small molecule that induces a distinctive envelope-stress–centered response with global stress reprogramming, aligning closest to membrane-active ionophores yet remaining mechanistically unique. Adaptive laboratory evolution and whole-genome sequencing uncovered recurrent topA and regulatory mutations conferring limited tolerance without true resistance, and a naturally resistant EPEC strain showed minimal omics responses, indicating low resistance potential and specificity of action.

title: Performance comparison of streptavidin magnetic beads for epcam expressing cancer cell lines for circulating tumor cell (CTC) enrichment in a flow-through immunomagnetic system.
summary: This study compared eight commercially available streptavidin-coated magnetic beads for EpCAM-targeted capture of circulating tumor cell surrogates in a flow-through immunomagnetic system using a Halbach magnet array. Beads around 100–150 nm performed best, with MojoSort Streptavidin Nanobeads providing the strongest balance of capture efficiency and purity, though further reduction of leukocyte co-capture is needed for large-volume applications such as diagnostic leukapheresis.

title: A novel accessible in vitro model of proliferative vitreoretinal diseases shows facilitated epithelial mesenchymal transition through aquaporin-1.
summary: The study establishes an accessible in vitro model of proliferative vitreoretinal disease (PVD) using nicotinamide-differentiated ARPE-19 cells subjected to TNF-α and TGF-β (TNT) to induce EMT, and shows that Aquaporin-1 (AQP1) overexpression enhances EMT-associated transcriptomic changes and cell migration. The AQP1 TNT N− condition most closely matches human PVD membranes at the transcriptomic level, implicating AQP1 in facilitating EMT, β-catenin translocation, and modest upregulation of MMP2.

title: Quorum sensing in Saccharomyces cerevisiae brewing strains: effects of 2-phenylethanol on proteomic, lipidomic, and metabolomic profile.
crm_level_3: Centre for Food and Microbial Technology (CLMT)
summary: Three industrial Saccharomyces cerevisiae brewing strains were grown on nitrogen-limited (SLAD) or nitrogen-sufficient (SHAD) agar with or without 200 μM 2‑phenylethanol (2‑PE) and analyzed by proteomics, lipidomics, and metabolomics to assess quorum-sensing effects. Nitrogen limitation consistently reduced ribosome-associated proteins, while 2‑PE effects were strain-specific and more evident in lipidomic/metabolomic profiles, indicating that 2‑PE’s impact on industrial ale yeasts is not universal.

title: Cholangiocytes contribute to hepatocyte regeneration after partial liver injury during growth spurt in zebrafish.
summary: During a rapid growth phase in zebrafish, partial hepatocyte loss triggers robust cholangiocyte-to-hepatocyte transdifferentiation, yielding de novo hepatocytes even when spared hepatocytes remain. Using genetic ablation, partial hepatectomy, single-cell RNA-seq, and lineage tracing, the study shows that active mTORC1 in uninjured growing livers primes cholangiocyte plasticity, and Notch inhibition is sufficient to induce de novo hepatocytes.

title: Recent advances in the application of microbiota transplantation in chickens.
summary: This review synthesizes recent advances in microbiota transplantation (MT) in chickens, covering sources (feces, intestinal contents, fermented inocula, litter), donor selection, preparation and delivery methods, mechanisms of engraftment, and documented effects on performance, behavior, gut barrier and immunity, metabolism, and disease resistance. It also highlights practical challenges and safety considerations (e.g., standardization, anaerobic handling, pathogen screening) and outlines future directions for scaling and optimizing MT in poultry production.

title: Reduced contribution of sulfur to the mass extinction associated with the Chicxulub impact event.
crm_level_3: Atomic and Mass Spectrometry-A&MS research unit
summary: This study empirically estimates the amount of sulfur released by the Chicxulub impact by measuring sulfur concentrations and isotopic compositions in target rocks and globally distributed K–Pg boundary deposits, then applying isotope-dilution mass balance. The result, 67 ± 39 Gt S, is about five times lower than the most recent numerical estimate, implying a milder, shorter impact winter than previously modeled.

title: Extreme MetaboHealth scores in three cohort studies associate with plasma protein markers for inflammation and cholesterol transport.
summary: In three Dutch cohorts, individuals at the extremes of an NMR-based MetaboHealth score showed broad plasma proteome and cytokine differences linking high scores (poorer health) to elevated inflammatory proteins (e.g., CRP, LBP, IL-6, GDF15, MIG) and low scores to higher HDL remodeling/cholesterol transport proteins (e.g., APOA1/2/4, TETN). Twin analyses indicated the MetaboHealth score is moderately heritable (h2≈0.4), and many protein associations persisted within monozygotic twin pairs, suggesting substantial non-genetic contributions alongside some genetically influenced components (e.g., weaker APOA1/2 signals in twins).

title: Characterization of human CD34+ HSPC-derived neutrophils with limited myeloid-derived immunosuppressive cell activity.
summary: The authors developed a serum-free SL-II culture system to generate mature, functional neutrophils from human CD34+ HSPCs that closely resemble blood polymorphonuclear neutrophils (PMNs) in phenotype, transcriptome, proteome, and antimicrobial/ADCC functions. Despite these similarities, the cultured neutrophils lacked myeloid-derived suppressor cell (MDSC) activity, which correlated with a distinct deficit in specific and gelatinase granule proteins rather than canonical MDSC marker expression differences.

title: Systematic comparison of temporal hepatotoxicant-induced gene network responses across 3 liver test systems.
summary: This study compared time- and concentration-resolved transcriptomic responses to ketoconazole, diclofenac, and nitrofurantoin across three human liver models (primary human hepatocytes, hiPSC-derived hepatocyte-like cells, and HepG2), mapping time-responsive genes onto TXG-MAPr co-expression modules. It identified conserved core stress programs (ER stress/ATF4, oxidative stress/NRF2, heat shock/HSF1) and found several modules with reproducible transcriptomic points of departure across systems, supporting network-based endpoints for hepatotoxicity assessment.

title: PPARα-mediated lipid metabolism reprogramming supports anti-EGFR therapy resistance in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
summary: The study shows that acquired resistance to anti-EGFR therapy (cetuximab) in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is driven by a PPARα-dependent reprogramming toward increased fatty acid uptake and oxidation via CD36 and CPT1A, without major changes in glycolysis. Pharmacologic or genetic inhibition of CPT1A or PPARα selectively impairs resistant cells and resensitizes 3D spheroids and xenograft/PDX models to anti-EGFR therapy, and a PPARα-related gene signature correlates with poor response and survival in HNSCC patients.

title: Correction of pathogenic mitochondrial DNA in patient-derived disease models using mitochondrial base editors.
summary: The study demonstrates efficient creation and correction of mitochondrial DNA mutations in primary human cells using DdCBE base editors, modeling disease (m.15150G>A in MT-CYB) in liver organoids and correcting a pathogenic variant (m.4291T>C in MT-TI) in patient-derived fibroblasts to restore mitochondrial membrane potential. It further shows that delivering DdCBE as modRNA, including via lipid nanoparticles, improves editing efficiency and viability relative to DNA plasmids, with limited nuclear off-targets and mitochondrial off-targets correlating with on-target activity.

title: Machine learning with label-free Raman microscopy to investigate ferroptosis in comparison with apoptosis and necroptosis.
summary: This study uses label-free Raman microscopy combined with machine learning (support vector machines) to distinguish regulated cell death modalities—apoptosis, ferroptosis, and necroptosis—in the murine fibroblast line L929sAhFas, with direct SVMs on normalized spectra achieving 73% per-spectrum (≈78% per-cell) accuracy. Peak analysis revealed general RCD-associated bands and modality-specific changes (e.g., decreases at 853 and 939 cm−1 in ferroptosis), while necroptosis showed no unique peaks.

title: Monocyte-hitchhiking system for the targeted delivery of paclitaxel-loaded PLGA nanoparticles to glioblastoma in mice.
crm_level_3: Translational Cell and Tissue Research Unit
summary: The study develops a monocyte-hitchhiking system in which bone marrow–derived monocytes (BMDMs) are surface-conjugated via biotin–streptavidin to paclitaxel-loaded biotin-PEG-PLGA nanoparticles, enabling enhanced blood–brain barrier crossing and targeted accumulation in glioblastoma (GBM) in mice. Paclitaxel was identified as the most selective agent for GBM in vitro, nanoparticle conjugation did not impair BMDM transmigration, and in vivo imaging and intravital microscopy showed significantly higher brain tumor delivery versus free nanoparticles.

title: Hypoxia Induces a Mitotic Survival Advantage After Radiotherapy in Head and Neck Cancer Cells.
summary: Using a hypoxia fate-mapping system in HPV-positive and HPV-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) models, the authors show that post-hypoxic cells drive regrowth after radiotherapy and are intrinsically more radioresistant, exhibiting fewer radiation-induced mitotic defects and a checkpoint-reliant phenotype. Targeting mitotic checkpoint regulators (ATR, CHK1/2) restored radiosensitivity in post-hypoxic cells, indicating mitotic survival advantage as a key mechanism of hypoxia-associated radiotherapy resistance.

title: Incorporation of iPSCs together with TERT-immortalized keratinocytes and fibroblasts into reconstructed human gingiva enhances phenotype of gingival epithelium.
summary: The study shows that incorporating undifferentiated human iPSCs into the collagen–fibrin hydrogel of a reconstructed human gingiva (RhG) model composed of TERT-immortalized gingival keratinocytes and fibroblasts induces greater keratinocyte proliferation, epithelial thickening, and spontaneous rete ridge formation, yielding a phenotype closer to native gingiva. iPSCs underwent early apoptosis (by ~1–2 weeks air-exposed culture), correlating with transient boosts in epithelial proliferation and differentiation marker normalization, after which histological differences versus standard RhG diminished.

title: circTGFBR2(3-6) acts as an assembly platform for RNA-binding protein IGF2BP3 and TGFBR1 mRNA to enhance breast cancer cell plasticity.
crm_level_3: Oncode Institute and Department of Cell and Chemical Biology
summary: This study identifies a circular RNA, circTGFBR2(3-6), as a cytoplasmic scaffold that enhances TGF-β/SMAD signaling and promotes epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT), migration, extravasation, stemness, and chemoresistance in breast cancer cells. Mechanistically, circTGFBR2(3-6) binds IGF2BP3 and m6A-modified TGFBR1 mRNA to stabilize TGFBR1, thereby augmenting receptor-level signaling; disrupting IGF2BP3 or the m6A site diminishes these effects.

title: Biologics for bone regeneration: advances in cell, protein, gene, and mRNA therapies.
crm_level_1: MERLN Institute for Technology-Inspired Regenerative Medicine
summary: This review synthesizes advances in biologic therapies for bone regeneration, covering protein therapies (e.g., BMPs, monoclonal antibodies), gene and mRNA (cmRNA) strategies, small molecules, peptides, and cell- and platelet-based approaches, and their integration with biomaterials. It highlights mechanisms, benefits, limitations, clinical evidence, and potential applications in difficult-to-heal fractures and disease contexts like osteoporosis, rickets/osteomalacia, Paget’s disease, osteogenesis imperfecta, and tumor-related bone defects.

title: Novel Insights into Emx2 and Dmrta2 Cooperation during Cortex Development and Evidence for Dmrta2 Function in the Choroid Plexus.
summary: This study investigates how the transcription factors Emx2 and Dmrta2 cooperate during mouse cortical development, combining bulk RNA-seq and ChIP-seq to show they share few but key direct targets (e.g., Pax6, Gsx2/Nkx2.1 loci) and identifying Ldb1 as a cofactor that Emx2 recruits to activate or repress downstream genes. It also shows that while Emx2 suppresses choroid plexus development, Dmrta2 is required for choroid plexus function; conditional loss of Dmrta2 in the cortical hem/choroid plexus does not block specification but leads to postnatal hydrocephalus with apical membrane protrusions in choroid plexus epithelium.

title: Salmonella stress response systems as targets for anti-virulence strategies.
summary: This study systematically interrogates the roles of major stress response systems in Salmonella Typhimurium (RpoS, RpoE, RecA, and others) across virulence- and tolerance-associated phenotypes, identifying RpoS, RpoE, and RecA as key regulators of biofilm formation, antibiotic tolerance/persistence, mutation rate, epithelial invasion, and macrophage survival. It further evaluates chemical inhibitors and shows that the RecA inhibitor BRITE-338,733 suppresses the SOS response and reduces ciprofloxacin tolerance and persistence, whereas epigallocatechin gallate (RpoS) and batimastat (RpoE) showed no significant effects under the tested conditions.

title: Peritoneal resident macrophages constitute an immunosuppressive environment in peritoneal metastasized colorectal cancer.
summary: This study maps the human peritoneal immune system and shows that peritoneal-resident macrophages (VSIG4+ C1Q+ and SPP1+ subsets) form a constitutively immunosuppressive niche that fuels peritoneal metastases in colorectal cancer. Depleting macrophages via anti-CSF1R combined with anti-PD1 reduced tumor burden and improved survival in a mouse PM-CRC model, highlighting PRMs as therapeutic targets.

title: Loss of the E3 ubiquitin ligase MARCHF6 alters hepatic lipid metabolism and drives spontaneous hepatosteatosis.
summary: This study shows that loss of the ER-associated E3 ubiquitin ligase MARCHF6 in mice, particularly in hepatocytes, causes spontaneous hepatic triglyceride and cholesteryl ester accumulation by stabilizing squalene epoxidase, activating SREBP1-driven lipogenesis, and enhancing lipoprotein clearance, without changes in caloric intake. Lipidomics, flux tracing, and human primary hepatocyte experiments indicate a shift toward polyunsaturated, long-chain neutral lipids and NADPH-demanding de novo lipogenesis; pharmacologic pentose phosphate pathway inhibition reduces lipid accumulation, and human MASLD/MASH datasets show reduced hepatic MARCHF6 with increased lipogenic gene expression.

title: Tripotent Lgr5 stem cells in the posterior tongue generate lingual, taste, and salivary gland lineages.
crm_level_3: The Princess Maxima Center for Pediatric Oncology
summary: This study maps the cellular composition of the posterior mouse tongue and shows that a single Lgr5+ stem cell is tripotent, generating taste bud cells, von Ebner salivary gland cells, and non-taste lingual epithelium. Using single-cell RNA sequencing, clonal organoids, and in vivo multicolor lineage tracing, the authors delineate lineage trajectories and identify Foxe1 as a regulator of fate decisions, whose loss skews differentiation toward progenitor states and alters taste cell subtype balance.

title: Structure of a pH-sensitive pentameric ligand-gated ion channel from the Sarcoptes scabies mite.
summary: The study reports cryo-EM structures of a pH-sensitive chloride channel from the Sarcoptes scabiei mite (SsCl) in closed (pH 6.5), desensitized (pH 9), and ivermectin-bound states, revealing an hourglass-shaped desensitized pore and pH-dependent ivermectin modulation. Structural and functional analyses identify histidine/glutamate residues in a binding-like extracellular region that contribute to pH sensing and gating, informing mechanisms of ivermectin action and antiparasitic target design.

title: Human biomonitoring of mycotoxins: key challenges and future directions.

title: Surface-Associated Proteins on Extracellular Vesicles Remodel the Tumor Microenvironment by Potentiating TGF-β Signaling in a Contact-Dependent Manner.
crm_level_3: Oncode Institute and Department of Cell and Chemical Biology
summary: TGF-β activation of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) increases extracellular vesicle (EV) surface-associated proteins such as TSG6 and THBS1, which dock to CD44 and promote clustering with TGF-β receptors to potentiate TGF-β/SMAD signaling in recipient cells. This contact-dependent mechanism enhances CAF activation and suppresses CD8+ T cell cytotoxicity, thereby promoting tumor progression.

title: Saccharomyces cerevisiae reduces vulvovaginal candidiasis severity through modulation of fungal pathogenicity and inflammatory responses.
summary: This study identifies a Saccharomyces cerevisiae strain (Sc3458) that reduces Candida albicans virulence and dampens host inflammatory responses, thereby ameliorating vulvovaginal candidiasis in vitro and in a murine model. Mechanistically, Sc3458 constrains C. albicans growth, adhesion, hyphal morphogenesis, and biofilm formation via contact- and metabolism-dependent interactions, reprograms fungal and epithelial transcriptional responses, and enhances neutrophil antifungal activity while limiting hyperinflammation, resulting in lower fungal burden and reduced IL-1-driven responses in vivo.

title: Integrative epigenetic and transcriptomic profiling of whole blood and fibroblasts in Hao-Fountain syndrome.
summary: This study integrated genome-wide DNA methylation, RNA sequencing, and cis eQTM analyses in whole blood (n=9) and patient-derived skin fibroblasts (n=4) from individuals with USP7-related Hao–Fountain syndrome to map regulatory consequences of USP7 haploinsufficiency. Blood reproduced the established hypermethylation episignature with a small set of DMRs and eQTMs, whereas fibroblasts showed coherent methylation–expression changes (notably in the HOXB cluster) and strong enrichment of DMRs in PRC1.1-associated chromatin (BCOR/H2AK119ub1), highlighting marked tissue specificity of regulatory effects.

title: Experimental glycopeptide antibiotic EVG7 prevents recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection by sparing members of the Lachnospiraceae family.
summary: The study evaluates the experimental glycopeptide antibiotic EVG7 as a CDI therapy, showing it is 8–16× more potent in vitro against clinical Clostridioides difficile isolates than vancomycin and, in a validated mouse model, low-dose oral EVG7 (0.04 mg/mL) prevents recurrence better than a 10× higher vancomycin dose. Microbiome analyses indicate EVG7 preserves Lachnospiraceae, taxa associated with protection against C. difficile colonization, thereby supporting reduced relapse.

title: Culturomics of the pig tonsil microbiome identifies new species and an untapped source of novel antimicrobials.
summary: This study defined the core palatine tonsil microbiota of healthy piglets across 11 European farms and built a culturomics-derived collection of 518 bacterial isolates spanning 23 genera, capturing ~39% of taxa detected by 16S profiling. Genome mining and in vitro antagonism assays identified two novel species and multiple biosynthetic gene clusters, including a Corynebacterium kozikiae strain producing a heat- and protease-stable flavucin-like lanthipeptide that inhibits Streptococcus suis and Staphylococcus aureus in vitro.

title: CREsted: modeling genomic and synthetic cell-type-specific enhancers across tissues and species.
crm_level_1: VIB Center for AI and Computational Biology
summary: The authors introduce CREsted, a Python framework that trains sequence-to-function models on scATAC-seq to decode and design cell-type-specific enhancers, with modules for preprocessing, modeling, attribution-based motif discovery, and synthetic enhancer design. They demonstrate applications across mouse cortex, human PBMCs, cancer cell lines and glioma biopsies, and zebrafish development, showing improved enhancer prediction over baselines, cross-species generalization, and in vivo validation of designed enhancers in zebrafish embryos.

title: Size- and polymer-dependent toxicity of amorphous environmentally relevant micro- and nanoplastics in human bronchial epithelial cells.
summary: This study evaluated size- and polymer-dependent toxicity of amorphous micro- and nanoplastics (PVC, PP with talc filler, and PA) in human BEAS-2B bronchial epithelial cells, measuring cytotoxicity, inflammation, oxidative stress, and NF-κB/AP-1 activation. PA nanoplastics (<1 μm) caused dose-dependent cytotoxicity and NF-κB–mediated IL-8 release with SOD2 upregulation, PP/talc increased IL-8 likely due to talc, while PVC and all leachates showed no significant toxicity under the tested conditions.

title: The cellular activating protein-1 cFos regulates influenza A virus replication.
summary: The study shows that the AP-1 subunit cFos is strongly induced by influenza A virus infection and acts as a proviral factor: cFos knockdown reduces viral replication across human and avian IAV strains, increases apoptosis, elevates IFN-β mRNA, and diminishes late viral transcripts and proteins (e.g., NA and M2). Evidence points to a nuclear role of cFos (rather than its ER lipid-synthesis role) in supporting IAV replication, potentially by modulating innate immunity and facilitating viral transcription.

title: Pseudorabies virus infection triggers pUL46-mediated phosphorylation of connexin-43 and closure of gap junctions to promote intercellular virus spread.
summary: This study shows that pseudorabies virus (PRV) uses its tegument protein pUL46 to activate ERK1/2, leading to phosphorylation of connexin-43 (Cx43), closure of gap junctions, and suppression of gap junctional intercellular communication (GJIC), which enhances cell-to-cell viral spread. PRV lacking pUL46 fails to phosphorylate Cx43 or inhibit GJIC, reduces intercellular spread, and this defect is rescued by pharmacological inhibition of GJIC or STING, implicating gap junction–mediated antiviral signaling in restricting spread.

title: A Longitudinal 3D Live-Cell Imaging Platform to Uncover AAV Vector-Host Dynamics at Single-Cell Resolution.
summary: The study presents a longitudinal 3D live-cell imaging and automated analysis pipeline to quantify rAAV2 trafficking, nuclear entry, and transgene expression at single-cell resolution from 4–12 h post-transduction. It reveals dose-dependent improvements in cytoplasmic trafficking and nuclear accumulation, cell-cycle–dependent facilitation of trafficking and expression (particularly with S/G2 progression), and distinct, impaired nuclear accumulation of empty capsids compared to genome-containing vectors.

title: Heat Treatment and Storage of Frass From Black Soldier Fly Larvae and Yellow Mealworm Production: Compliance With EU Regulation on Microbiological Quality and Safety.
summary: This study evaluated heat treatments (50–80°C for 15–90 min) and storage effects on the microbiological safety of frass from black soldier fly larvae (BSFL) and yellow mealworms (YM) to assess compliance with EU Regulation 2021/1925. The reference process (70°C for 60 min) consistently met EU criteria by reducing E. coli below 1000 cfu/g and eliminating Salmonella (even when inoculated), whereas milder treatments sufficed for BSFL but not always for YM, and storage up to 2 weeks at 4°C or ~26–28°C did not increase bacterial counts, supporting tailored processing based on initial load and frass properties.

title: Identification of DksA as a novel pro-inflammatory mediator of Pseudomonas aeruginosa under conditions mimicking chronic cystic fibrosis lung infection.
summary: The study identifies the transcriptional regulator DksA as a novel pro-inflammatory mediator produced by Pseudomonas aeruginosa under conditions mimicking chronic cystic fibrosis lung infection, using SCFM2 culture and a 3D human lung epithelial model to screen cell-free supernatants. Comparative proteomics and PA14 transposon mutants implicated DksA in driving IL-8 responses, and analysis of CF sputum transcriptomes showed high in vivo expression of dksA, supporting its relevance to persistent airway inflammation.

title: Alkaline pH-Driven Metabolic Plasticity of Lactococcus lactis FM03.
summary: This study investigates how alkaline pH (6, 7, 8) affects metabolism, growth, and morphology of Lactococcus lactis FM03 in lactose-limited chemostats, finding an earlier and stronger shift to homolactic fermentation at pH 8 that lowers ATP yield and biomass despite unchanged maintenance energy and maximum ATP-based yield. Proteomics shows pH-dependent downregulation (up to ~13.5-fold) of mixed-acid pathway enzymes, while cells become more spherical with a reduced surface-to-volume ratio, suggesting constrained substrate uptake and reduced maximal growth at high pH.

title: Loss of the lysosomal lipid flippase ATP10B leads to progressive dopaminergic neurodegeneration and parkinsonian motor deficits.
summary: This study shows that loss of the lysosomal lipid flippase ATP10B causes progressive degeneration of nigrostriatal dopaminergic neurons, reduced striatal dopamine transporter binding, and parkinsonian motor deficits in rats, and reduces survival of human iPSC-derived midbrain dopaminergic neurons. ATP10B knockdown alters lysosomal marker number and size in dopaminergic neurons, indicating lysosomal dysfunction as a contributor to neurodegeneration.

title: The MIR-NAT MAPT-AS1 does not regulate Tau expression in human neurons.
summary: This study characterizes the long non-coding RNA MAPT-AS1 in human brain and neuronal models, confirming its neuronal, predominantly cytoplasmic expression, but finds that altering MAPT-AS1 levels does not change MAPT mRNA or Tau protein. Using siRNAs, antisense oligonucleotides, and lentiviral overexpression in neuroblastoma cells and human iPSC-derived neurons, the authors conclude MAPT-AS1 does not regulate Tau expression and is unlikely to be a viable therapeutic target for Tau lowering in tauopathies.

title: Iron deficiency induces maturation-dependent loss of pancreatic β-cells.
summary: This study identifies a maturation-dependent requirement for iron in pancreatic β-cells, showing that immature mouse and human β-cells rely on TFRC-mediated iron uptake for mitochondrial function and survival, whereas mature β-cells become resilient to iron depletion. Genetic loss of Tfrc in β-cells causes glycolytic reprogramming, p53-mediated apoptosis, β-cell loss, and diabetes, which is fully prevented by iron supplementation, and similar stage-dependent effects are observed in human EndoC-βH1 cells, donor islets, and iPSC-derived β-cells.

title: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy in mismatch-repair-proficient colon cancers.
summary: In the phase II NICHE platform trial, 31 patients with early-stage mismatch-repair-proficient colon cancer received neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab (± celecoxib), yielding a 26% response rate (20% major pathological response) despite uniformly low tumor mutational burden; ctDNA clearance strongly associated with response, while higher chromosomal instability, proliferation signatures, TCF1 expression, and increased Ki-67+ cancer and CD8+ T cells characterized responders. Celecoxib did not enhance efficacy or immunomodulation, and non-response correlated with inflamed-fibrotic/TGFβ-high stromal features, suggesting biomarkers for selection and stromal-targeting strategies for resistant tumors.

title: The Peptonizer2000: Bringing Confidence to Metaproteomics.
summary: The study introduces Peptonizer2000, a peptide-centric Bayesian workflow that integrates peptide scores from any search engine with Unipept peptide-to-taxon links to compute calibrated probability scores for taxonomic identifications in metaproteomics. Validated on lab-assembled mock communities, human fecal, ocean, and soil microbiomes, it improves specificity and confidence over simple peptide-count methods and supports both DDA and DIA inputs.

title: iPSC-Derived Liver Organoids as a Tool to Study Medium Chain Acyl-CoA Dehydrogenase Deficiency.
summary: This study established human iPSC-derived hepatic organoids (EHOs) and their matured counterparts (Mat-EHOs) from fibroblasts of MCADD patients and controls, demonstrating that patient organoids recapitulate hallmark biochemical features of MCADD, including accumulation of medium-chain acylcarnitines and elevated C8/C10 ratios. Mat-EHOs showed increased peroxisomal markers and transcriptomic changes in TCA and CoA-related genes (notably NUDT7 upregulation), supporting their utility to investigate patient-specific pathophysiology and compensatory mechanisms in MCADD.

title: Chromatin dynamics of the Klf4 locus in mouse pluripotent cells.
summary: Using the ANCHOR3 DNA labeling system and live-cell single-locus tracking, the authors measured chromatin dynamics at multiple positions across the mouse Klf4 locus in naïve mESCs and differentiated EpiLCs and found similar, subdiffusive motion across cis-regulatory and control regions regardless of Klf4 transcriptional status. They observed notably faster mobility at the neighboring housekeeping gene Rad23b promoter, challenging a universal role for active transcription in increasing local chromatin mobility.

title: CD70 recruitment to the immunological synapse is dependent on CD20 in B cells.
summary: This study identifies CD70 as a binding partner of CD20 on human B cells and shows that CD20 is required for recruiting CD70 to the immunological synapse, enabling efficient B–T cell synapse formation. Loss of CD20 impairs synapse formation, diminishes T cell activation and cytokine secretion, and CD20 overexpression stabilizes CD70 at the B cell surface.

title: Syntenin inhibition impairs stroma-tumor communication in multiple myeloma and improves bortezomib treatment efficiency.
summary: The study shows that syntenin, highly expressed in inflammatory bone marrow stromal cells (BMSCs), orchestrates pro-tumoral stromal secretomes and small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) that drive multiple myeloma (MM) survival and bortezomib resistance via STAT3, MAPK, and AKT–mTOR pathways. Genetic knockout or pharmacologic inhibition of syntenin (SyntOFF) reduces IL-6 and specific sEV cargo loading, enhances bortezomib-induced MM cell death ex vivo, and significantly lowers tumor burden in vivo in the 5TGM1 model when combined with bortezomib.

title: Low-dose chronic exposure to hemin and kynurenine enhances metabolic adaptation in a colorectal cancer cell model.
summary: This study shows that chronic low-dose exposure of colorectal cancer HCT116 spheroids to hemin and kynurenine, alone or combined, induces distinct and complementary metabolic adaptations that enhance flexibility under nutrient stress. Combined hemin+kynurenine exposure particularly maintained energy production during glucose deprivation by leveraging pyruvate and lipid metabolism with increased lipid storage, linking red meat–derived metabolites to colorectal cancer metabolic plasticity.

title: Actin and vimentin jointly control cell viscoelasticity and compression stiffening
summary: This study uses a custom single-cell rheometer to show that actin and vimentin contribute comparably to the linear stiffness and compression-induced stiffening of mouse embryonic fibroblasts, while actin more strongly governs energy dissipation. Using oscillatory compression and strain ramps, plus genetic (vimentin knockout) and pharmacological (cytochalasin D, blebbistatin) perturbations and enucleation, the authors demonstrate that compression stiffening originates from the cytoskeleton rather than the nucleus and that prestress modulates stiffening behavior.

title: Integrated multi-omics mapping of mitochondrial dysfunction and substrate preference in Barth syndrome cardiac tissue.
summary: This study applied an integrated metabolomics, lipidomics, and proteomics workflow to left-ventricular cardiac tissue from five pediatric Barth syndrome patients versus 24 non-failing donors, confirming hallmark cardiolipin remodeling defects, severe mitochondrial respiratory chain perturbations, and a substrate shift away from fatty acid oxidation toward glycolysis. The data also revealed accumulation of heart-failure–associated lipids and pronounced inter-individual variability, especially between transplanted and autopsy samples.

title: Glycoproteomics analysis of complement factor H and its complement-regulatory function during Streptococcus pneumoniae-associated hemolytic uremic syndrome.
summary: This study profiled N-glycosylation of complement factor H (FH) in four children with Streptococcus pneumoniae-associated hemolytic uremic syndrome (SP-HUS) and found extensive acute-phase trimming of FH glycans beyond desialylation, including loss of galactose and GlcNAc, with partial normalization in remission. Despite these glycan changes, FH retained normal complement-regulatory activity in C3b cofactor and sheep erythrocyte hemolysis assays, and the authors show that previously reported functional impairments likely resulted from residual neuraminidase activity rather than loss of FH function.

title: Organoids as powerful models of endometrium epithelium in transcriptomic, cellular and functional mimicry.
summary: This review synthesizes recent advances in modeling the human endometrium with a focus on epithelial organoids that recapitulate hormone-driven cycling, cellular diversity, and transcriptomic programs across the menstrual phases, including the window of implantation. It integrates single-cell datasets, highlights ion-channel biology, and surveys applications from disease modeling (endometrial cancer, endometriosis, adenomyosis, Asherman’s syndrome) to embryo-adhesion assays, assembloids, organ-on-chip platforms, and prospects for personalized and regenerative medicine.

title: A CHD8-TRRAP axis facilitates MYC and E2F target gene regulation in human neural stem cells.
summary: The study identifies the TRRAP complex as a prominent interactor of the chromatin remodeler CHD8 in human neural stem cells and shows that CHD8 and TRRAP co-occupy promoters of MYC and E2F target genes. Knockdown of CHD8 or TRRAP downregulates MYC/E2F target programs and reduces S-phase entry, linking CHD8-TRRAP to cell-cycle control in neural stem cells.

title: Respiratory viruses induce ferroptosis-like features in lung epithelial cells.
summary: This study compares ferroptosis-like responses induced by influenza A virus H1N1 and human adenovirus type C5 in human lung epithelial A549 and BEAS-2B cells, showing both viruses elevate lipid peroxidation and remodel mitochondrial networks. H1N1 increases ferritin expression, whereas HAdV-C5 elevates lipid peroxidation without altering ferritin, with ferrostatin-1 only partially suppressing lipid peroxidation at later infection stages.

title: Understanding the impact of oat groat heat treatment on its protein extractability.
crm_level_3: Food Chemistry and Biochemistry and Leuven Food Science and Nutrition Research Centre (LFoRCe)
summary: This study shows that industrial kilning of oat groats markedly reduces protein extractability compared to non- and lab-scale heat treatments, without pronounced denaturation detectable by DSC. Instead, reduced extractability arises from increased protein aggregation via non-covalent interactions and disulfide bonds and shifts in secondary structure (lower α-helix/random coil, higher β-sheet), with stronger effects in outer (bran) tissues under industrial conditions.

title: In vitro and in vivo validation studies of optimized iron oxide nanoparticles carrying targeting ligands for a new therapeutic strategy in head and neck cancers.
summary: The study develops dendronized iron oxide nanoparticles (IONPs) functionalized with either cRGD or an EGFR-targeting peptide (P22) and shows that P22-conjugation markedly enhances nanoparticle uptake in head and neck cancer (HNC) cell lines and trends toward greater tumor accumulation in vivo by MRI. Biodistribution studies in mice revealed rapid liver and kidney T2 contrast and sustained liver/bone marrow signal changes, with ICP-AES confirming organ iron content and no overt toxicity over one month.

title: Phosphoproteomics distinguishes disease-specific mechanisms for human phospholamban cardiomyopathy reversible by RNA therapy.
summary: The study integrates global proteomics and phosphoproteomics of human PLN p.Arg14del (R14Δ/+) myocardium with CRISPR-engineered human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes to reveal a distinct phosphorylation signature affecting cytoskeletal and contractile pathways that differentiates PLN cardiomyopathy from other dilated cardiomyopathies. PLN-targeted antisense RNA therapy reduced PLN expression, reversed many disease-associated phosphosites, diminished PLN/LC3 aggregates, and improved calcium handling and contractile kinetics in human iPSC-cardiomyocytes.

title: Plasmodium falciparum stomatin-like protein forms a putative complex with a metalloprotease in distinct mitochondrial loci.
summary: This study shows that the Plasmodium falciparum stomatin-like protein (STOML) is important for efficient asexual blood-stage growth, localizes to puncta at mitochondrial branch ends and branch points, and forms a large complex with the mitochondrial metalloprotease FtsH. Structural modeling suggests STOML oligomerizes into a barrel-like scaffold reminiscent of bacterial HflK/C that may regulate FtsH accessibility, while STOML knockout does not alter drug sensitivity to respiratory chain inhibitors or gametocyte development.

title: Winning the battle of intestinal peace with Bacillus-a multifaceted approach to animal health, immunity, and future applications in monogastric livestock production.
summary: This review synthesizes evidence on the use of spore-forming Bacillus probiotics in monogastric livestock (poultry and swine), detailing how they enhance gut health, immunity, performance, and sustainability via microbiota modulation, bioactive metabolite production, and gut barrier reinforcement. It also outlines delivery strategies (feed, water, in ovo, spray), discusses extra-intestinal axes (gut–liver/lung/brain), and highlights research gaps including standardization, in vitro–in vivo translation, and the need for reliable biomarkers.

title: MLX phosphorylation stabilizes the ChREBP-MLX heterotetramer on tandem E-boxes to control carbohydrate and lipid metabolism.
summary: The study shows that phosphorylation of MLX by CK2 and GSK3 on conserved residues stabilizes the ChREBP–MLX heterotetramer on tandem E-box (ChoRE) elements, enabling transcription of carbohydrate and lipid metabolic genes, while glucose-6-phosphate accumulation inhibits this phosphorylation and tetramer formation. Genetic, biochemical, and physiological evidence across mammalian cells, mouse adipose tissue, and Drosophila demonstrates that this phosphorylation is essential for sugar tolerance and lipid storage, revealing a feedback mechanism linking sugar flux to ChREBP–MLX activity.

title: Polarization contrast neutron imaging enables operando visualization of iron plating in redox flow batteries.
summary: The study introduces polarization contrast neutron imaging to visualize, in operando, metallic iron plating/stripping and hydrogen evolution in all-iron redox flow batteries, enabling spatially and temporally resolved tracking of these phase-change processes. It reveals preferential iron deposition near the membrane due to non-uniform current distribution, strong dependencies on pH and flow-field architecture, and shows that convective flow improves electrode utilization and gas management compared to diffusion-dominated designs.

title: Turning off methylglyoxal stress: an alternative approach to inhibit MDSC expansion and metastasis in triple-negative breast cancer.
summary: This study shows that methylglyoxal (MG) stress promotes an immunosuppressive microenvironment in triple-negative breast cancer by expanding granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (g-MDSCs), enhancing NF-κB signaling, GM-CSF expression, and metastasis. Targeting MG with the scavenger carnosine combined with anti–PD-1 therapy reduces g-MDSCs and lung metastases in resistant mouse models, and an MG gene signature correlates with MDSC markers and immunotherapy resistance in patient datasets.

title: Tumour-reactive heterotypic CD8 T cell clusters from clinical samples.
summary: The study demonstrates that heterotypic clusters of CD8+ T cells with tumor cells and/or antigen-presenting cells can be isolated from 21/21 human melanoma metastases and that these clustered T cells exhibit increased exhaustion, clonal expansion, and tumor-reactive gene signatures. T cells expanded from clusters showed markedly enhanced ex vivo killing and improved in vivo control of patient-derived melanoma compared to singlet T cells, and the RNA signature of clustered T cells predicted response to TIL therapy.

title: Lipid nanoparticles as a tool to dissect dendritic cell maturation pathways.
summary: This study uses lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) to delineate homeostatic versus immunogenic maturation pathways in dendritic cells, developing flow cytometry and transcriptional markers that reliably distinguish these states. They show that empty or peptide-loaded LNPs induce homeostatic maturation, while TLR ligand- or mRNA-loaded LNPs drive immunogenic programs that differentially shape CD4 and CD8 T cell outcomes, indicating vaccine adjuvanticity stems from cargo rather than lipids.

title: RANKL blockade inhibits cancer growth through reversing the tolerogenic profile of tumor-infiltrating (plasmacytoid) dendritic cells.
summary: This study shows that blocking RANKL markedly inhibits primary tumor growth and lung metastasis in multiple syngeneic triple‑negative breast cancer (TNBC) mouse models by reprogramming the tumor immune microenvironment, specifically reducing Treg cells and activating dendritic cells and plasmacytoid dendritic cells via mTOR pathway inhibition. RANKL blockade synergized with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (doxorubicin or paclitaxel) but not with anti‑PD‑1 therapy, highlighting RANKL as a promising immunotherapeutic target.

title: The unfolded protein sensor IRE1 is essential for homeostatic dendritic cell maturation.
summary: This study identifies the ER stress sensor IRE1 as a critical regulator of homeostatic maturation in conventional type 1 dendritic cells (cDC1s), activated by lipid influx from apoptotic cell uptake rather than classical unfolded protein stress. IRE1 promotes cholesterol efflux by RIDD-mediated degradation of miR-92a-1 to stabilize Abcg1; loss of IRE1 impairs cDC1 maturation and survival, elevates cholesterol, and reduces cross-priming, which can be rescued by blocking miRNA biogenesis or enforcing cholesterol efflux with reconstituted HDL.

title: Deciphering HTLV-1-associated Lung Pathology through Integrated in vitro and Multi-cohort Multi-omics Analysis: Inflammation, Monocyte Recruitment and Differentiation Triggered by HTLV-1-exposed Alveolar Epithelial Cells.
summary: The study shows that HTLV-1-exposed human alveolar epithelial A549 cells activate NF-κB-dependent inflammatory programs, upregulate CCL2 and CSF-1, and drive monocyte chemotaxis and differentiation, modeling key features of HTLV-1-associated pulmonary inflammation. Multi-cohort, multi-omics comparisons (bulk/single-cell transcriptomics and GWAS) validate overlap with HAM/TSP and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis signatures, highlighting monocyte/macrophage pathways as central to lung pathology.

title: TGFβ signaling in cancer-associated fibroblasts drives a hepatic gp130-dependent pro-metastatic inflammatory program in colorectal cancer.
summary: The study shows that TGFβ signaling in colorectal cancer-associated fibroblasts induces IL-6 family cytokines (notably IL-6 and IL-11), which activate gp130-dependent JAK/STAT signaling in hepatocytes to upregulate neutrophil chemoattractants such as SAA1 and CXCL5, thereby promoting neutrophil recruitment and a pro-metastatic hepatic niche characteristic of CMS4 colorectal cancer. This stromal–hepatic axis was validated using human CAFs, hepatocyte models, a neutrophil migration assay, a CMS4-like murine model, and was functionally abrogated by gp130/JAK inhibition.

title: Activation of a FOXO3-induced cell cycle arrest regulates ferroptosis.
summary: The authors show that activating FOXO3 in non-transformed human hTERT-RPE-1 cells protects against ferroptosis by inducing a p27-dependent G1 arrest and coordinately decreasing cellular hydrogen peroxide, iron uptake (via TFR1), and lipid-metabolism factors (ACSL4, PEX5), thereby limiting lipid peroxidation. They further demonstrate that cell-cycle arrest alone is insufficient for ferroptosis resistance in this system; robust protection requires FOXO3-driven control of redox and iron metabolism in addition to cell-cycle effects.

title: Blueberries Reduce Palm Oil-Induced Metabolic Endotoxemia in an In Vitro Human Intestinal-Immune Cell Model.
summary: This study used a human Caco-2 intestinal epithelial–THP1-Lucia macrophage co-culture model to show that digested palm oil facilitates LPS translocation and enhances NF-κB activation, while digested blueberries and blackberries (and to a lesser extent bananas) attenuate this effect. Multi-omics and functional assays indicate berries reduce chylomicron secretion and downregulate genes involved in clathrin-mediated transcytosis, suggesting fruit-rich diets may mitigate metabolic endotoxemia by limiting lipid-driven LPS transport.

title: Identification of the cellular factor KLF16 as a novel epigenetic repressor of HIV-1 transcription.
summary: This study identifies the transcription factor KLF16 as a novel epigenetic repressor of HIV-1, showing that it binds the HIV-1 5′LTR Sp1 sites, competes with Sp1, and recruits Sin3A/HDAC1 and HP1α/Suv39H1 to enforce a repressive chromatin state. KLF16 depletion reactivates latent HIV-1 in T-lymphoid and myeloid models and primary CD4+ T cells, while all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) reactivates HIV-1 in myeloid cells in part by downregulating KLF16.

title: Fast growth and high-titer bioproduction from renewable formate via metal-dependent formate dehydrogenase in Escherichia coli.
summary: The study installs and tunes a fast, oxygen‑tolerant, metal‑dependent formate dehydrogenase (from Cupriavidus necator) in a reductive glycine pathway E. coli to achieve rapid formatotrophic growth with a ~4.4 h doubling time. Using electrochemically CO2‑derived formate and lignin‑derived, formate‑rich acid streams, the engineered strain produces up to 3.8 g/L mevalonate and also makes isoprenol, advancing a sustainable formate‑based bioproduction platform.

title: Identification of the cellular transcription factor KLF16 as a novel repressive epigenetic repressor of HIV-1 transcription.
summary: This study identifies the transcription factor KLF16 as a novel repressor of HIV‑1 by directly binding the HIV‑1 5′LTR at Sp1 sites, competing with Sp1, and recruiting Sin3A/HDAC1 and HP1α/SUV39H1 to establish a repressive chromatin state. KLF16 depletion reactivates latent HIV‑1 in T‑lymphoid and myeloid models and in primary CD4+ T cells, while all‑trans retinoic acid (ATRA) downregulates KLF16 and contributes to HIV‑1 reactivation in myeloid cells.

title: Bioartificial Hearts, Assist Devices, and Myocardium: New Developments.
summary: This systematic review synthesizes advances from 2014–2024 in bioartificial hearts (BAHs), engineered myocardium (constructs and patches), and biohybrid ventricular assist devices, assessing model maturity, performance, and clinical readiness. While BAHs and whole-tissue constructs remain far from clinically meaningful hemodynamic and electrophysiological function, cardiac patches have reached early clinical use with mixed and largely paracrine-driven benefits, and significant gaps persist in vascularization, electrical integration, and biocompatibility.

title: Induction of cardiac fibulin-4 protects against pressure overload-induced cardiac hypertrophy and heart failure.
summary: This study shows that fibulin-4 is induced in the myocardium during pressure overload and is essential for maintaining cardiac structure and function, independent of aortic valve pathology. Mice with reduced fibulin-4 exhibit aggravated hypertrophy, fibrosis, contractile dysfunction, and mortality after transverse aortic constriction, and fibulin-4 knockdown in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes increases cell size and stress gene expression, highlighting a primary cardiac role for fibulin-4 in ECM remodeling and myocyte contractility under stress.

title: Profiling histone post-translational modifications to identify signatures of epigenetic drug response in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
summary: This study uses mass spectrometry-based profiling of histone post-translational modifications (hPTMs) to identify baseline epigenetic signatures associated with sensitivity to epigenetic drugs and anthracyclines in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL). While distinct hPTM–drug sensitivity relationships were found in 21 T-ALL cell lines, these signatures did not translate to T-ALL patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models, highlighting model-dependent epigenetic covariation and underscoring the importance of model selection for predictive biomarker development.

title: Nature-inspired platform nanotechnology for RNA delivery to myeloid cells and their bone marrow progenitors.
summary: The study introduces an apolipoprotein-based nanoparticle (aNP) platform inspired by lipoproteins that encapsulates siRNA, ASO, or mRNA in a stable core and delivers them efficiently to myeloid cells and haematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) in mouse bone marrow. Through a 72-formulation library screen, in vivo selection, and a lead candidate (aNP18), the platform achieved gene regulation in immune and progenitor cells, demonstrated therapeutic CCR2 silencing effects in a tumour model, and enabled splice-switching and mRNA expression with favorable biodistribution and tolerability.

title: Development of a Hybrid NIR-II Thermometer Suitable for Drug Release.
summary: The study reports a hybrid nanothermometer-drug carrier composed of a solid SiO2 core, a mesoporous PMO shell (BTEB/APTES), and surface-decorated LiLuF4:Nd3+,Yb3+ nanoparticles that enables ratiometric NIR-II thermometry and pH-responsive doxorubicin (DOX) release. The material shows modest thermometric sensitivity in aqueous/PBS media, good biocompatibility in NHDFs, effective DOX loading and accelerated acidic release, and dose-dependent cytotoxicity in HeLa cells, highlighting theranostic potential while noting limitations in acidic/PBS-phantom calibration stability.

title: Molecular basis of 60 years of antigenic evolution of human influenza A(H3N2) virus neuraminidase.
summary: The study quantified and mapped 60 years of antigenic evolution of human influenza A(H3N2)/A(H2N2) neuraminidase (N2) using neuraminidase inhibition ELLA titers and antigenic cartography across >300 viruses and 24 ferret antisera, showing that NA drift is gradual and often discordant with HA. It identified multiple amino acid substitutions—particularly around the NA active site and lateral side—whose cumulative effects (changes in charge, volume, and hydropathy) drive NA antigenic evolution, informing NA-focused surveillance and vaccine design.

title: Fundamental aspects of sucrose metabolism reveal a trophic link between Rhodospirillum rubrum and Rhodobacter capsulatus
summary: This study compares sucrose, glucose, and fructose metabolism in two purple non-sulfur bacteria, Rhodospirillum rubrum and Rhodobacter capsulatus, revealing that Rh. capsulatus can hydrolyze and use sucrose while Rs. rubrum cannot unless in co-culture. Co-cultivation creates a trophic link whereby Rh. capsulatus ferments sugars to organic acids that Rs. rubrum re-assimilates, improving carbon yield and scaling successfully to a photobioreactor.
