title: Toward the Treatment of Glioblastoma Tumors Using Photoactivated Chemotherapy: In Vitro Evaluation of Efficacy and Safety.
summary: This study evaluates ruthenium-based photoactivated chemotherapy (PACT) prodrugs in glioblastoma U-87MG cells and neuron-like SH-SY5Y cells, identifying [3](PF6)2 as a light-activated compound with improved anticancer efficacy (PI≈3.5) in GBM while showing reduced or reversed toxicity in SH-SY5Y upon green light exposure. Light-activated [3](PF6)2 markedly increased intracellular Ca2+ in SH-SY5Y cells, and docking suggested possible interaction with AMPA receptors, indicating promise for GBM treatment with attention to neuro-safety and calcium signaling.

title: A workflow integrating organ-on-chip culture and correlative 3D light and electron microscopy for microtissue analysis.
summary: The study presents a practical workflow that integrates organ-on-chip culture with longitudinal live fluorescence imaging and correlative 3D electron microscopy via high-pressure freezing to analyze microtissues at multiple scales. Demonstrated on an hMSC-derived bone-on-a-chip, the pipeline enables fluorescence-guided targeting for FIB/SEM and Raman characterization while supporting fluid flow and mechanical compression to model physiologic cues.

title: Distinct stromal cell populations define the B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia microenvironment.
crm_level_3: Princess Máxima Center for Pediatric Oncology
summary: This study maps the pediatric B-ALL bone marrow microenvironment at single-cell resolution and identifies two major stromal MSC populations—early mesenchymal progenitors and adipogenic progenitors—along with osteogenic-lineage cells detected by spatial transcriptomics. Functionally, adipogenic progenitors uniquely support leukemic cells via IL-7 and VCAM1 signaling and are enriched at relapse, while B-ALL cells drive a contact-dependent adipogenic skew in MSCs, highlighting stromal niche heterogeneity as a contributor to leukemic survival and chemoresistance.

title: NAD-dependent dehydrogenases enable efficient growth of Paracoccus denitrificans on the PET monomer ethylene glycol.
summary: The study identifies and characterizes an NAD-dependent alcohol dehydrogenase (EtgB) and aldehyde dehydrogenase (EtgA) in Paracoccus denitrificans that together enable efficient growth on the PET monomer ethylene glycol, under control of the activator EtgR. Structural (cryo-EM) and functional analyses, along with adaptive laboratory evolution, show increased EtgB/EtgA production accelerates ethylene glycol growth, and that the etg gene cluster is widespread across bacteria.

title: BDH2-driven lysosome-to-mitochondria iron transfer shapes ferroptosis vulnerability of the melanoma cell states.
summary: This study identifies BDH2 as a critical effector of lysosome-to-mitochondria Fe(II) transfer at mitochondria–lysosome contacts in melanoma, where it produces the siderophore 2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid (2,5-DHBA) to support mitochondrial bioenergetics, maintain lysosomal acidification, and stabilize contact formation. Loss of BDH2 in mesenchymal-like melanoma causes lysosomal iron sequestration and ferroptosis vulnerability, which can be mitigated by BDH2 re-expression or 2,5-DHBA, including improved metastatic seeding in vivo.

title: Modulation of immunoglobulin G oligomerization by variable domain glycans: A mechanism to regulate complement activation.
summary: This study shows that variable domain glycans (VDGs) on IgG inhibit classical complement activation by impeding IgG oligomerization into hexamers, thereby reducing C1q recruitment. Using glycoengineered human monoclonal antibodies, biochemical assays, and cryo-electron tomography, the authors demonstrate fewer, less-ordered IgG–C1 complexes and diminished complement-mediated membrane lysis when VDGs are present, revealing a regulatory mechanism that diversifies antibody effector function.

title: Long-term multi-meta-omics resolves the ecophysiological controls of seasonal N2O emissions during wastewater treatment.
summary: This study combined nearly two years of metagenome-resolved metaproteomics, ex situ kinetics, and full-scale operation data from a wastewater treatment plant to resolve the mechanistic drivers of seasonal nitrous oxide emissions. It shows that an oxygen- and temperature-driven imbalance between ammonia- and nitrite-oxidizing bacteria leads to nitrite build-up and overexpression of nitrifier denitrification (notably NirK), identifying dissolved oxygen control as the key lever to mitigate N2O peaks.

title: Protocol for generation of a 3D humanized lung-tumor-on-a-chip model of immune-hot and immune-cold microenvironments.
summary: This protocol describes a fully humanized lung tumor-on-a-chip model using Emulate’s Chip-S1 to recreate immune-hot (H2009) and immune-cold (A549) tumor microenvironments with human lung microvascular endothelial cells and perfused human PBMCs under controlled flow. It details setup, perfusion, imaging, immune infiltration analyses (IF, flow cytometry), and secretome profiling, and provides troubleshooting and limitations for reproducing dynamic endothelium–immune–tumor interactions.

title: CIP2A mediates mitotic recruitment of SLX4/MUS81/XPF to resolve replication stress-induced DNA lesions.
summary: This study shows that the mitotic CIP2A–TOPBP1 complex forms large filamentous and loop-like structures at sites of under-replicated DNA and recruits the SMX tri-nuclease complex (SLX4, MUS81, XPF–ERCC1) to process replication stress–induced DNA lesions, while being dispensable for mitotic DNA synthesis (MiDAS). The unstructured C-terminal tail of CIP2A is essential for higher-order structure formation and SMX recruitment; its loss increases genome instability and is synthetically lethal in BRCA2-deficient cells, with SLX4 loss phenocopying CIP2A loss in BRCA-deficient contexts.

title: High-resolution multi-omics enhances prediction and detection of smORF-encoded proteins in the human gut microbiome.
summary: This study introduces a high-resolution multi-omics workflow that integrates smORF prediction into sample-specific metaproteomic databases and leverages next-generation Orbitrap Astral mass spectrometry to detect small open reading frame-encoded proteins (SEPs) in human gut microbiomes without size-based enrichment. Applying the pipeline to healthy human stool samples yielded over 3.7 million non-redundant predicted smORFs and 25,233 detected SEPs, substantially expanding the experimentally supported small-protein landscape and aligning their taxonomic and functional profiles with the broader metaproteome.

title: Co-trimoxazole-induced reproductive toxicity and placental-barrier disruption: impact on cell-cell junctions and ERK signaling pathway.
summary: This study shows that co-trimoxazole (sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim) causes reproductive toxicity in pregnant mice and disrupts placental barrier function in vitro by altering tight/adherens junction gene expression, reducing TEER, increasing FITC-dextran permeability, activating ERK1/2, and suppressing IL-6. Findings indicate potential risks to placental integrity and fetal outcomes during CTX exposure, warranting careful risk-benefit evaluation in pregnancy.

title: Native long-read RNA sequencing of human monocytes reveals activation-induced alternative splicing toward functional isoforms.
summary: The study uses Oxford Nanopore native RNA sequencing to profile full-length isoforms in primary human monocytes before and after LPS activation, identifying over 24,000 isoforms with many novel variants and widespread activation-induced isoform switching. Activation favors longer, coding-competent isoforms with fewer retained introns, which correlate with increased translation and protein abundance, highlighting alternative splicing as a functional regulator of monocyte activation.

title: Constitutive activity of an atypical chemokine receptor revealed by inverse agonistic nanobodies.
summary: This study identifies inverse agonistic nanobodies (VUN700 and VUN702) that suppress the constitutive activity of the atypical chemokine receptor ACKR3, reducing basal β-arrestin engagement, inhibiting constitutive internalization, and slowing non-chemotactic cancer cell motility. Hydrogen–deuterium exchange mass spectrometry and solution NMR show these nanobodies stabilize a more inactive receptor conformation than a neutral antagonist nanobody (VUN701), providing mechanistic insight and potential therapeutic strategies for ACKR3-driven pathophysiology.

title: Akkermansia muciniphila MucT harnesses dietary polyphenols as xenosiderophores for enhanced iron uptake.
summary: The study shows that Akkermansia muciniphila MucT exploits dietary proanthocyanidins (PACs) as xenosiderophores to import iron, upregulating a ferric catecholate ABC transporter (YclNOPQ), lipocalins, and ferrous iron transporters (Feo) and thereby restoring growth in iron-depleted conditions when supplied with iron-loaded PACs. Integrative proteomics/transcriptomics and iron-depletion assays implicate Fur and a DtxR-like regulator in coordinating these iron-acquisition systems, providing a mechanistic basis for PAC-driven enrichment of A. muciniphila and potential competitive advantages over pathogens.

title: Tractable mouse TNBC models capture the heterogeneous tumor immune microenvironment and adaptation to PD-L1 blockade.
summary: The study characterizes nine intraductal, syngeneic mouse triple-negative breast cancer models that span ‘hot’ to ‘cold’ tumor immune microenvironments and recapitulate growth, metastasis, and immune heterogeneity. Despite high PD-L1, both 4T1-hot and 4T1-cold models were resistant to PD-L1 blockade, adapting via increased CXCL10+ tumor-associated macrophages (cold) and cancer-associated fibroblasts (hot), highlighting cell-type–specific resistance mechanisms and therapeutic targets.

title: A model of Notch signalling control of angiogenesis: Evidence of a role for Notch ligand heterodimerization.
summary: This study combines biochemical experiments and mathematical modeling to show that JAG1 and DLL4 can form heterodimers that block DLL4-driven cis-inhibition of Notch1, while DLL4 (but not JAG1) efficiently trans-activates Notch1, thereby explaining the opposing roles of these ligands in angiogenic sprouting. The resulting model reproduces tip/stalk patterning in angiogenesis and predicts that DLL4–JAG1 heterodimerization together with ligand-specific affinities for Notch1 are critical determinants of endothelial cell fate.

title: Ethnomedicinal documentation, phytochemical characterization, and biological evaluation of the traditional medicinal plants from Swat region of Pakistan.
summary: This study documents ethnomedicinal uses, phytochemical profiles, TLC fingerprints, and a broad antimicrobial, antibiofilm, and cytotoxicity evaluation of 85 extracts from 17 traditional medicinal plants collected in the Swat region of Pakistan. Many extracts, especially ethanol extracts, showed substantial activity against planktonic bacteria and fungi and against biofilms (notably Staphylococcus aureus and Candida albicans) with generally low cytotoxicity, highlighting plants such as Juglans regia, Punica granatum, Artemisia maritima, Aesculus indica, Thymus linearis, Dysphania ambrosioides, and Nasturtium officinale as promising for further drug discovery work.

title: Ferroptosis inhibition protects against α-synuclein-related neuronal cell death.
summary: This study links α-synuclein pathology in Parkinson’s disease to increased ferroptosis vulnerability by showing reduced ferritin and ferroportin in α-syn-positive dopaminergic neurons, ferroptosis-related transcriptomic changes in substantia nigra, and enhanced neuronal death when α-syn fibrils are combined with the GPX4 inhibitor RSL3. Ferroptosis inhibition with ferrostatin-1 (but not deferoxamine) protected mouse primary cortical neurons and human LUHMES dopaminergic neurons, and iron chelation reduced α-syn inclusions in C. elegans, supporting ferroptosis as a therapeutic target, albeit with cell- and model-dependent effects.

title: The complexome contextualizes proteomics data to fingerprint biological states and highlight perturbed functional modules in disease.
summary: This study introduces a complexome-centered framework and software (ComplexomeProfiler) that overlays proteomics measurements onto curated protein complexes to fingerprint biological states and detect perturbed functional modules. Benchmarking across human tissues (PaxDb) and analyzing proteomes from patient-derived fibroblasts with inborn errors of metabolism revealed consistent remodeling of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and broader mitochondrial machinery, providing mechanistic insights into disease states.

title: Cryo-EM analysis of the Bacillus thuringiensis extrasporal matrix identifies F-ENA as a widespread family of endospore appendages across the Firmicutes phylum
summary: This study identifies and structurally characterizes a new family of endospore appendages (F-ENA) across Firmicutes, showing that Bacillus thuringiensis spores display flexible DUF4183-based pili tethered to the exosporium by a collagen-like F-Anchor and capped by a collagen-like F-BclA fibrillum. Using cryo-EM, crystallography and AlphaFold modeling, the authors define F-ENA architecture and assembly, document variants in Paenibacillus and Clostridia, and show F-ENA contributes to spore clustering.

title: The lipid transfer protein STARD7 controls intestinal tumor development in a context-dependent manner.
summary: This study shows that loss of the phosphatidylcholine transfer protein STARD7 in intestinal epithelial cells causes mitochondrial stress, elevated ROS, and mTORC1/ATF4-driven metabolic reprogramming, notably upregulating serine biosynthesis. Functionally, STARD7 deficiency reduces inflammation-driven (AOM/DSS) colon tumors but accelerates Wnt-driven tumor initiation in Apc+/Min mice via increased mutation burden and a microbiota shift, and these tumors are highly sensitive to mTORC1 inhibition (rapamycin).

title: Inhibitor-based modulation of huntingtin aggregation mechanisms mitigates fibril-induced cellular stress.
summary: This study shows that sub-stoichiometric curcumin modulates huntingtin exon 1 (HttEx1) aggregation by prolonging the nucleation lag phase and yielding narrower amyloid fibril polymorphs with altered morphology and dynamics. These curcumin-induced fibrils provoke reduced cellular stress in neuronal models, with structural changes supported by TEM, SAXS, and solid-state NMR consistent with differences in polyglutamine core organization and flanking-domain dynamics.

title: Dual NIR-I excitation and emission-based thermometry and pH-responsive drug delivery using NaYF4:Yb,Er@SiO2-folic acid conjugates.
summary: The authors synthesize cuboidal NaYF4:Yb,Er upconverting particles, coat them with mesoporous silica, conjugate folic acid, and load doxorubicin to create a theranostic platform that enables dual NIR-I excitation/emission ratiometric thermometry and pH-responsive drug delivery. They demonstrate stable temperature sensing in water and through chicken breast tissue under 975/940 nm excitation, quantify DOX loading/release and cytotoxicity, and show preferential anticancer effects in HeLa cells while maintaining good biocompatibility in NHDFs.

title: A group 1 hemagglutinin stem vaccine elicits broad humoral responses against influenza in phase 1/2a study.
summary: This randomized, double-blind Phase 1/2a trial tested a soluble trimeric group 1 hemagglutinin stem protein (INFLUENZA G1 mHA) in healthy adults, showing it was well tolerated and induced markedly higher, broader, and durable binding, neutralizing, and ADCC antibody responses than a standard quadrivalent seasonal influenza vaccine. Vaccinee sera conferred significant protection in a stringent H5N1 passive-transfer mouse challenge, supporting the HA-stem approach as a component toward a universal influenza vaccine.

title: Characterizing the Fate of Anti-CS1 Nanobody Displaying Extracellular Vesicles in Multiple Myeloma.
summary: The study engineered HEK293-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) to display anti-CS1 nanobodies to target multiple myeloma (MM) and evaluated their biodistribution and cellular uptake in vitro and in vivo. While α-CS1 EVs enhanced uptake by CS1+ myeloma cells in vitro, in vivo they showed only modest bone marrow retention with increased off-target accumulation (notably liver and lungs) and no improved specificity for MM cells in diseased mice, indicating further optimization is required for targeted EV delivery in MM.

title: Intestinal tuft cell subtypes represent successive stages of maturation driven by crypt-villus signaling gradients.
summary: This study shows that intestinal tuft-1 and tuft-2 cells are not distinct endpoints but successive post-mitotic maturation states along the crypt–villus axis, with chemosensory capacity increasing during maturation. Using mouse small-intestinal organoids with subtype-specific reporters, the authors demonstrate that IL-4/IL-13 generate new Nrep+ tuft-1 cells, while villus-like cues (notably BMPs and cholinergic signaling) drive their progression to Chat+/Folr1+ tuft-2 cells, enabling functional assays of mature tuft cells.

title: Macrophage-augmented intestinal organoids model virus-host interactions in enteric viral diseases and facilitate therapeutic development.
summary: This study develops macrophage-augmented intestinal organoids (MaugOs) by integrating human macrophages with primary human intestinal organoids to model enteric virus–host interactions, showing differential antiviral and inflammatory responses to echoviruses, rotavirus, OC43, and SARS-CoV-2. The authors demonstrate that acetate potently suppresses NLRP3-driven inflammation and that combining the antiviral nirmatrelvir with either budesonide or acetate concurrently reduces viral replication and inflammatory responses in MaugOs.

title: Pharmacological CLK inhibition disrupts SR protein function and RNA splicing blocking cell growth and migration in TNBC.
summary: This study demonstrates that the CLK inhibitor T-025 disrupts SR protein function and RNA splicing, leading to impaired proliferation, G1–S arrest with increased 4N DNA content and aneuploidy, and reduced migration in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) cell lines. Mechanistically, T-025 causes SR factors (notably SRSF7) to accumulate and interact within nuclear speckles, alters SRSF7’s interactome, and reprograms alternative splicing across genes governing cell division and migration.

title: Cryo-EM identifies F-ENA of Bacillus thuringiensis as a widespread family of endospore appendages across Firmicutes.
summary: This study identifies and structurally characterizes a new family of endospore appendages, F-ENA, across Firmicutes, showing they are DUF4183-based, C3-symmetric pili tethered to the exosporium via a collagen-like F-Anchor and capped by a collagen-like tip fibrillum (F-BclA). Using cryo-EM, X-ray crystallography, and proteomics, the authors reveal F-ENA promotes spore clustering, is widespread in Bacilli and Clostridia, and exhibits subgroup-specific neck domains that modulate filament architecture.

title: Epithelial Cell Mechanoresponse to Matrix Viscoelasticity and Confinement Within Micropatterned Viscoelastic Hydrogels.
summary: The authors developed micropatterned viscoelastic polyacrylamide hydrogels with independently tunable stiffness and stress relaxation to mimic the mechanical evolution of breast tissue from soft viscoelastic to stiff elastic states, and showed that viscoelasticity differentially regulates epithelial cell spreading, focal adhesions, YAP nuclear localization, and migration depending on initial stiffness. Spatial confinement on 1D fibronectin lines altered these viscoelasticity-driven responses, enhancing or suppressing migration via changes in actin retrograde flow and adhesion dynamics, and generally blunting viscoelastic effects under confinement on soft matrices.

title: Co-translational protein aggregation and ribosome stalling as a broad-spectrum antibacterial mechanism.
crm_level_1: VIB Center for Brain and Disease Research
crm_level_3: VIB Center for Brain and Disease Research
summary: The study introduces an aggregation‑prone peptide (P33) that penetrates bacteria without disrupting membranes, induces co‑translational aggregation of nascent polypeptides, traps stalled ribosomes and cognate mRNAs in inclusion bodies, and thereby kills a broad spectrum of ESKAPE pathogens, including in biofilms and in mouse infection models. Multi-omics and imaging show inclusion bodies enriched for ribosomal components and outer membrane proteins, while inhibition of translation (erythromycin) abrogates aggregation and lethality, supporting a mechanism of ribosome stalling via nascent chain aggregation.

title: Illuminating Rembrandt's Chiaroscuro in The Night Watch: the painting process of Van Ruytenburch's costume.
summary: Using noninvasive chemical imaging (MA-XRF, MA-XRPD, and RIS), microscopy, and targeted micro-sampling, the study maps Rembrandt’s pigment choices and layer structure to explain the chiaroscuro rendering of Lieutenant Van Ruytenburch’s costume in The Night Watch. It reveals systematic pigment groupings (e.g., lead white and lead–tin yellow impastos, smalt-enriched underpaints, arsenic-based pigments for golden reflections) and documents degradation products (mimetite, palmierite, weddellite) that now mute the original light–shadow effects and inform conservation strategy.

title: Evidence That Dmrta2 Acts through Repression of Pax6 in Cortical Patterning and Identification of a Mutation Impairing DNA Recognition Associated with Microcephaly in Human.
summary: This study demonstrates that Dmrta2 represses Pax6 to control cortical patterning and cooperate with Pax6 to maintain dorsal telencephalic identity, with genetic interactions shown by double mutant and double overexpression mouse models. Mechanistically, Dmrta2 represses Pax6 E60 enhancer activity in a DNA-binding dependent manner, recruits NuRD components (HDAC1/2, MBD3) potentially via Zfp423, and a human DMRTA2 p.Arg116Pro mutation that abolishes DNA binding is associated with microcephaly and corpus callosum agenesis.

title: The Escherichia coli replication initiator DnaA is titrated on the chromosome.
summary: This study combines genome-wide motif analysis and live-cell single-particle tracking to show that Escherichia coli chromosomes enrich high-affinity DnaA-binding sites near oriC and titrate DnaA in a growth rate-dependent manner, keeping a large fraction of DnaA DNA-bound especially during slow growth. Deleting datA, DARS1, and DARS2 reduces chromosomal titration capacity in slow growth, increases DnaA mobility, and leads to premature re-initiation events, indicating that titration stabilizes replication initiation by limiting free DnaA after initiation.

title: Traction Force Microscopy for Viscoelastic Substrates: A Semi-Analytical Method.
summary: The study introduces a semi-analytical, time-resolved viscoelastic traction force microscopy (veTFM) method that generalizes standard 2D elastic TFM to linear Generalized Maxwell substrates, enabling fast, Fourier–Laplace-based inversion of interfacial displacements to tractions while accounting for dissipation and finite thickness. Validated against analytical and FEM solutions and applied to human cardiomyocytes, mammary epithelial cells, and dermal fibroblasts on linear-polyacrylamide and alginate hydrogels, veTFM shows when elastic limits suffice and reveals that traction magnitudes scale primarily with total substrate dissipation, with timescale matching determining whether cells engage elastic or viscoelastic regimes.

title: A coronavirus assembly inhibitor that targets the viral membrane protein.
summary: This study reports the discovery of CIM-834, a small-molecule inhibitor that targets the coronavirus membrane (M) protein and blocks the conformational switch required for virion assembly, thereby potently inhibiting SARS-CoV-2 (multiple variants) and SARS-CoV in cells and in vivo. Structural, biochemical, and electron microscopy data show CIM-834 binds and stabilizes the short form of M, abolishing particle assembly, reducing lung viral titers in SCID mice and Syrian hamsters, and preventing transmission in hamsters.

title: WEE1 inhibitors trigger GCN2-mediated activation of the integrated stress response.
summary: The study shows that clinically used WEE1 inhibitors (AZD1775 and Debio 0123) activate the GCN2-dependent integrated stress response (ISR), causing global translational attenuation and that loss of ISR components (GCN2/GCN1/ATF4) reduces WEE1i cytotoxicity without preventing WEE1i-induced DNA damage or checkpoint override. ISR activation appears to be an off-target effect common to multiple WEE1 inhibitors and occurs in primary human PBMCs; importantly, low-dose WEE1 inhibition combined with PKMYT1 inhibition maintains antitumor synergy without inducing the ISR.

title: Recombinant Proteins: A Molecular Tool to Understand Marine Adhesion and to Advance Biomaterials.
summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on recombinant proteins that mimic marine invertebrate adhesives (mussels, scallops, barnacles, tubeworms, ascidians, sea anemones, sea stars), covering their identification, recombinant production across host systems, functional characterization, hybrid protein design, and translation into biomaterials. It highlights production hurdles (PTMs, inclusion bodies), enzymatic post-processing (tyrosinase), domain-focused truncations, and the creation of coacervates, hydrogels, fibers, and coatings for biomedical applications.

title: Clathrin-independent endocytosis and retrograde transport in cancer cells tune immune synapse organization and CD8 T cell response.
summary: This study identifies ICAM1 as a new cargo of Endophilin A3–mediated clathrin‑independent endocytosis in cancer cells and shows that, together with ALCAM, it undergoes retromer‑dependent retrograde transport to the trans‑Golgi network before polarized delivery to the immune synapse. Disrupting EndoA3 or retromer reduces CD8 T‑cell cytokine production but increases lytic activity and enlarges immune synapses, indicating altered synapse organization and a shift toward more transient, serial killing interactions.

title: In silico analysis of patient specific coagulation and flow effects on fibrin clot formation.
summary: This study presents a unified, assay-calibrated in silico framework that links patient-specific thrombin generation (TG) data to multi-dimensional coagulation simulations under flow in patient-specific vascular geometries. The model, validated against thrombodynamics (TD) outcomes, shows how plasma composition, tissue factor (TF) exposure, and hemodynamics jointly modulate fibrin formation, enabling individualized assessment of thrombotic potential.

title: Enhancer-driven cell type comparison reveals similarities between the mammalian and bird pallium.
crm_level_1: VIB Center for AI & Computational Biology
summary: The study generated single-cell multiome and spatial transcriptomics datasets of the chicken telencephalon and trained cross-species deep learning models on cell type–specific accessible chromatin to decode enhancer codes that define cell identities. They found highly conserved enhancer codes across birds and mammals for non-neuronal and GABAergic neurons, while excitatory neurons showed mixed 1:many correspondences, and validated predicted enhancers in vitro (MPRA) and in vivo (AAV reporter assays).

title: Reprogramming the EnvZ-OmpR two-component system confers ethanol tolerance in Escherichia coli by stabilizing the outer membrane and altering ferric homeostasis.
crm_level_3: Centre of Microbial and Plant Genetics (Department of Molecular and Microbial Systems)
summary: This study shows that a single EnvZ periplasmic-domain mutation (L116P) in Escherichia coli reprograms the EnvZ-OmpR two‑component system into a kinase-dominant state, stabilizing the outer membrane by elevating total OmpC/OmpF porin abundance and decreasing ferric uptake via repression of enterobactin biosynthesis and ferric transport. The mutation confers strong ethanol tolerance and boosts ethanol production rates, with TolC and LpcA essential for the tolerant phenotype, while providing no cross-tolerance to n-propanol or n-butanol.

title: Leveraging Targeted Protein Degradation for G Protein-Coupled Receptors: The Development of CCR2 Molecular Degraders.
summary: The study develops and validates the first small-molecule molecular degraders of the GPCR CCR2 by tethering an intracellular allosteric CCR2 ligand to E3 ligase recruiters, identifying CRBN-recruiting compounds (notably LUF7996) that induce potent, sustained CCR2 degradation. Mechanistic profiling shows degradation proceeds via a lysosomal pathway (not proteasomal), and the lead degrader inhibits CCR2-dependent monocyte migration in THP-1 cells, establishing a workflow to expand GPCR-targeted degradation.

title: Peptidomimetic Phenoxymethyl Ketone Warheads as Potent Dual-Mode Inhibitors against SARS-CoV-2 Mpro and Cathepsin.
summary: This study reports a library of peptidomimetic phenoxymethyl ketone (PMK) inhibitors that act dually on SARS‑CoV‑2 main protease (Mpro) and host cathepsins (hCTSL/hCTSB), showing nanomolar biochemical potency, robust cellular antiviral activity, and broad-spectrum efficacy against SARS‑CoV and MERS‑CoV. Lead compound 1 demonstrated favorable in vivo plasma exposure in Syrian golden hamsters (with ritonavir coadministration), while ADME profiling highlighted fast hepatic clearance mitigated by CYP3A4 inhibition, supporting advancement to in vivo efficacy studies.

title: Pre-assembly of biomolecular condensate seeds drives RSV replication.
summary: This study reveals that respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) nucleates its viral factories (biomolecular condensates) from infecting viral ribonucleoproteins (vRNPs) that already carry pre-assembled protein interaction networks, termed pre-replication centres (PRCs). Using live single-vRNP imaging tools, the authors show PRCs are enriched for P and L, highly transcriptionally active, recruit viral proteins efficiently, and thus seed rapid viral factory formation, explaining infection heterogeneity by virion-to-virion variation in PRC content.
